#1,415
I Played This Game for You

[Serafall Leviathan]

"Well, that's gonna be fun," she commented before taking a gulp from her bottle of water. In front of her, Joshua chuckled to himself, unaware of just how "fun" what he'd said would be. Fun for her, that was for sure, fun for him, and it'd be even more fun for Ravel, she'd bet. He wasn't wrong about any of that, but what he was wrong about was… a few things in regards to his plan.

Alas, Serafall had given up dealing with that side of her partner, just as she knew Yasaka and Gabriel had. He had gotten a little better, but that'd be about it, she supposed. There were worse things for him to be, especially when he had all that power at the tip of his fingers. The fact that Joshua managed to still be a paragon of goodness after everything had to be studied, really.

"That aside… Are we done here?" he commented, looking to the side where the director and co. were looking over the last scene they'd shot. "I think that scene was good." Margalo chose that moment to chirp something on his shoulder and Serafall could only look at the two fondly as they shared one of those brief but significant moments. Those moments in which Joshua and his familiars would share a split second glance and a million thoughts, warm smile on his face and soft features on their everything.

Like a moment before, when Domino Mask and Sussie had absolutely terrified a poor actor during their scene.

"I think it was good too, but you know they have their own opinions sometimes," she replied when the moment was over, even though her own smile remained. That kind side was a very endearing thing about Joshua, that was for sure. Just as meaningful as his ability to care and his generosity. "Can I just say? I'm liking these peaceful chapters, easier enemies, bonding moments."

"Lots of bonding moments," Joshua pointed out eyebrows raised and his lips tugging upwards, amused. He had noticed that there were a lot more romantic moments between Magical Girl Levia-tan and Domino Mask, apparently. He had also – correctly at that – deduced that she was the person behind those. Unfortunately for him, he had no proof.

"I'm sure I don't know what you're talking about," she said, making no effort to hide things anyway. Because, what'd be the point? Besides, again, he had no way of proving that it was her.

Knowing a lost battle when he saw one, Joshua left it at that with a shake of his head.

"Anyway, I like it too," he told her, his smile turning into a grin. "So, provided we are done, any plans?" he asked and Serafall had a suggestion to go somewhere at the tip of her tongue. Alas, she was good at reading people, and that meant she definitely noticed how off Joshua seemed. Not that it was a new thing those days.

Infinite magic and then… whatever the fuck it was that Heaven's System was trying to pull on him, both things had left him off balance and he wasn't recovering. Joshua's tolerance for supernatural bullshit seemed to have reached its peak. Not even he could normalize what had happened around him, not with one, but two instances of madness at that.

Worse even, he still had to continue working on Ophis' Silence, keep being a father to a bunch of girls – and familiars – and keeping up with Yasaka, Gabriel and Serafall herself. She felt bad for that last one, but in her defense, Joshua was doing that to himself in that regard. The three of them were doing their best to support him, to make things easier by playing things down like they were no big deal. They hoped it'd make it easier to deal with for him, and it worked… but it only worked so much, unfortunately.

"I feel like just going home. You know, get some snacks, something to drink and do nothing for a bit," she said and she was immensely proud of the relief and gratitude that she saw in his expression, his eyes. Joshua really needed to stop overworking himself, and if she could use her dates to help with that, all the better. Besides, it was nice to just cuddle at home. Even if she hadn't felt like doing that herself – which she did –, she would have suggested that anyway, because Joshua put up with his own things that he didn't want to do for her sake.

"That sounds like the best idea I've heard in a while," he said, sighing exaggeratedly and making her smile. "Your home or mine though?" he asked and she paused.

Sometimes, she forgot that no, she didn't live at the place he shared with Yasaka – not even the youkai herself counted it as fully hers anymore –, and it was a little silly that she did. She mostly went back to her own place, after all. Maybe her own mansion or maybe her family's, – more often than not the latter, since she didn't like how empty her house felt, even with her few peerage members around. They were not the sociable kind, funnily enough – but the fact of the matter remained that she did go there. Nothing against her parents, but it didn't feel the same. It was her parents's place, not hers. The mansion was so empty it didn't feel like it was anyone's, and maybe that was why Serafall had never bothered trying to make it hers.

"It's been a while since we've seen your family, right? I mean, Sona comes around for training sometimes, but that's about it," Joshua commented, breaking her out of her thoughts with a smile that drew her attention straight to him.

"It has," she acknowledged with a nod, smiling a little wider. Yes, that was a great idea. Besides, it was adorable to see Joshua just be nice to Sona and watching the poor girl not knowing what to do with her feelings for the man. Alas, she had no chance. She'd been thrown in the Childzone together with Rias forever ago, after all.

Too bad for Sona, but more for Serafall, she supposed.

Which was good, because there were already way too many people to share Joshua's time with.


[}-o-{]
​

[Yasaka]

"It'd been a while since I saw that one," she commented, bringing her cup of tea to her lips. Beside her, Joshua smiled fondly in the same way that she probably was, his eyes locked off to the side just like hers were. There was their daughter – it soothed something in Yasaka's soul to think that, always, because apparently she was more like Kunou than she thought –, playing against Ravel with the illusion chess set that Joshua had made what felt like a lifetime before.

The card game was a lot more popular those days, what with constant chances and improvements, but Kunou had felt a little nostalgic, apparently. That and Ravel and Koneko probably had felt a little left out, since they hadn't really been there for the completion of that particular project. Morag had been there, even if she hadn't been able to play. The woman-spider, however, didn't seem too bothered by that fact, nor did she seem to care what they played. She just liked the opportunity to play against her sisters.

She was adorable like that, after all.

"It had, yes," Joshua confirmed, taking a sip of his own cup. "Makes me think about making some other game," he commented idly. "Maybe I should."

"Aren't you making that flying game Kunou was talking about before?" Yasaka asked with a raised eyebrow. Her daughter seemed very excited about that one, after all. She had rambled a few times to her already.

"Yes and no. I just made the flying part, the game part will be on Kunou and maybe the others," Joshua answered with a shrug. "I could help with that, sure, but I think it'll be better if it's entirely her project, or their project, whatever. Having something to work on will be good for her. I think," he added, that last part coming out a little unsure, like he did sometimes when he was trying to be a good father.

Not that he was wrong, at all, but he was usually more unsure when he tried as opposed to the confidence and ease he showed when he didn't. It was very amusing to see, for Yasaka. She almost wanted to tell him not to try and just do what came naturally, but she knew that'd just make him second-guess everything he did thereafter and nobody wanted that.

Even less so those days, what with how uncomfortable he seemed to be with his new… situation.

"So, yeah, maybe some other thing," he said, and Yasaka noticed the way his eyes grew tired, almost dull. Because he was probably thinking about all the other things he needed to work on, none of which could even remotely be considered something fun or relaxing for him. For as much as he liked to tinker with his spells, the pressure of importance took that away from him.

It was cruel, the way life seemed to have taken something Joshua loved and made him hate it.

"Maybe once I finish a project or two," the man added, turning down towards where he had a notebook laying on the table. There, he started working again, scribbling down something and erasing something else. He tried to play it off, like it was no big deal, but Yasaka had eyes and she knew how to use them. Beyond that, she was also one of the, if not the, best senjutsu users in the world. He had no chance to fool her.

She saw the way his body was always the smallest bit tense, the way his emotions would dampen when he got lost in thought, the way he seemed to have to push himself to work some more. She could sense the weariness bleeding into his life energy, like a sickly color spreading on clear water. Concerning, ever so concerning to see any of those things in the man she loved, but Yasaka couldn't do anything. For all her power – political or otherwise –, she could do nothing. Because the things Joshua faced, nobody could help him with.

After even his attempt at reaching out to a similar-minded individual had failed, what chance did she have.

"You're worried," Joshua said, and she blinked at him. He hadn't looked up from whatever he was writing down. "You haven't touched the tea in a bit. You haven't even moved, pretty sure. And you're not looking at the girls playing."

"That is… correct," she admitted slowly, almost changing her mind before she did. In the end though, Joshua was right, and for all that he lacked the social skills Yasaka – and his other two partners – had, he wasn't stupid. "You worry me, Joshua."

"I know," he replied with a self-deprecating smile. That was why she hadn't said anything. That's what she had been trying to avoid. "And I'm sorry. I don't think I can do anything to help with that," he said and she hated how defeated he sounded while saying that, how full of shame and hopelessness. Joshua, of all people, shouldn't feel any of those things, not with all that he did and all that he was. Yet because he was who he was, he did.

Perhaps that was what Heaven or Yahweh – somehow – had seen in him, someone that cared too much for others and too little for himself.

Someone that wouldn't do what most would if given power over things that shouldn't be handled carelessly.

"Joshua, you don't have to be sorry for any of this. None of it is your fault," she said, feeling like she'd said similar things a hundred times. If she always saw his shoulders relax and his expression soften like she did then and there, then she'd say them a million more. Just for good measure, however, she reached with her own life energy towards him, helping filter out the poison that his own mind brought to his life energy. "You do what you can, and we do what we can. You can't help your worries, just like I can't help mine."

"But here you are, helping me with mine."

"And you've helped me with mine plenty," she replied almost immediately, because that was the whole truth. Once upon a time, it'd been Joshua that helped her. If anything, she was just returning the favor. "I love you," she added, because that never failed to bring his mood up, simple man that he was.

Maybe she was a simple woman too though, because-

"I love you too."

-it never failed to bring her mood up when he said those words too.


[}-o-{]
​

[Dion Fortune]

"Do we know what he wants?" George asked, looking like he was fearing Death itself to come through the doors to their room, the Stars Room, as the rest of House of Water had started calling it. Not an inappropriate name, really, considering they had basically done whatever they wanted with it. There were desks arranged around the place, shelves lined the walls full of books and more things spread all over. "Because I'm not going to lie, I'm scared."

So were all of them, really.

Davis had called them all through Meredith – Well, all but Aika, who'd gotten a call of her own – to meet him at the room, just like they had called him when they'd finally finished gathering the information on the Dimensional Gap. He also hadn't mentioned what he was calling them for. The most optimistic view they could muster was that he wanted to give them an apprentices-only lecture of some kind…

But he could also have called them to do what he did best and further indebt them to him, because the man seemed to drive some kind of sick pleasure out of that. Dion herself had learned a lot about how to make sure she always had a favor from someone in any eventuality from the man. She'd done her best to put it all to use and she'd had very good results. She had a web of magicians now, all of which she could call in a pinch if need be to work in combination with her own Coven Magic.

Very useful indirect lesson, that one.

Dion hadn't gone too overboard though, because she was no Joshua Davis and because she had more mercy than he did. She knew how it was to be on the other side, so she tried not to push people too much. If she didn't, she might have pushed people away from doing business with her.

She wasn't, after all, the best of the best like her mentor was. She couldn't just expect people to come her way regardless of what she did like Davis could. Dion needed to make friends, make people like her… but also have just enough debt there for her to call on them if necessary.

She had to manage a delicate balancing act where Davis just… didn't.

"He said something about repaying what you did with the information you gave him, the other day," Aika said and all of them flinched. That'd been what they'd been fearing. Was that what was going to happen? Because Dion felt a part of her die inside just thinking about it.

Ruthless, truly ruthless.

"I'm sure he won't," Meredith mumbled, but not even she seemed to believe what came out of her mouth. If anything, she looked like she was pondering the merits of jumping out the window and making a run for it. Tempting idea, Dion would admit, but they were all under Davis' spells already in House of Water. There was no escape for them. Their fates were sealed and there was nothing to do but to accept it.

So, that's how they waited. Like people on death row, they sat there, in silence. They couldn't even muster more conversation, too busy thinking about what they might do if their fears and Aika's words proved true. Was there any idea they might have missed that'd help them get out of the debt they were being buried under? Was their fate to eternally serve Davis until, hopefully, they were finally freed of the burden?

There were worse people to be indebted to like that, for sure, but Dion couldn't help but feel helpless all the same.

That's what she found herself thinking when the door finally opened.

"Oh good, everyone's here already," Davis said as he stepped in, as if any of them would dare to be late. The last one to arrive had been Levi and he'd been half an hour early. "Why do you all look so pale? Everything alright? Are you working too much?" he asked, concerned, and it was kind of… bizarre how he didn't even realize what he did.

Ravel, behind him, was far less oblivious to the situation, if the roll of eyes was any indication.

"Do I have to call Agnes and-?"

"There's no need for that, Professor Davis," Karin said, softly but quickly, before things could get out of hand. "We stayed late working on some projects last night, that's all."

"Y-Yeah, just lost track of time," Levi jumped on that lifeline immediately and latched onto it like the desperate man that he was. Not that the rest of them were any better, really.

"George and I got a little distracted talking about a spell combination," Dion added and Pickingill was quick to follow that up.

"We were considering a job, you see?"

"Huh?... That so?" Davis asked, looking between them curiously. Meredith and Aika nodded their agreement easily, not any more eager for more debt than the rest of them. "Well, I can't fault you for that. That'd make me a hypocrite," the man said with a chuckle. "Anyway, I guess I can make this quick then, so you can all go to sleep or something," he added casually.

Dion was really not liking the smile on the Phenex devil's face, however.

It spoke of terrible things in their future, but-

"So, you see, you can help me with something," Davis said and she could have sighed in relief at that. George did sigh, actually, and Meredith didn't look further behind. "I have duties to my pantheon, the Egyptians, if you didn't know." As if they could not know about that. They'd personally gathered as much information about him as they could. Not a small amount coming from Ravel Phenex herself in the time when Davis wasn't around. "Now, I can't do much by myself, however. That's why I called you all here. You're going to help me carry out my duties."

"... And how can we do that?" Dion risked asking, not seeing where he was going, exactly.

"You see, I have to spread the good word, as it were. Improve the Egyptian pantheon's reputation." Well, she guessed they could take jobs in his name. That'd indirectly work in the Egyptians' favor, right, so- "And that's why I'm going to use the fantastic power of delegation. You're all going to get your own blessings, you're all going to act on behalf of myself and the pantheon."

There was a pause and a stretched out silence after that.

'Did… did he say blessings? As in… Divine blessings?' she wondered, slowly turning to look at her fellow Stars to make sure she hadn't heard wrong. Pale faces and sweaty foreheads told her that no, she'd heard perfectly well.

"So, who wants to go first?" Joshua asked, as if he weren't putting another nail in their coffin.


[}-o-{]
​

[Joshua Davis]

Despite what some people might think, there was only so much that Joshua could remain ignorant about a topic. Which is why he knew why there was some dread in his apprentices as he moved towards them, towards Meredith who would be the first one. He knew they were dreading whatever perceived debt they were about to incur.

The truth of the matter was that they really were doing him a favor here, blessing or no blessing. He wasn't doing enough for the Egyptians as it was, and this would go a long way to making up for all the pantheon had done for him. No matter what they thought, he'd told Ravel in no uncertain terms that this wasn't going to add to whatever they owed him.

Ravel seemed certain that they wouldn't see it that way… and Joshua reluctantly agreed.

"Ready?" he asked, tilting his head as he looked at Meredith. She looked like she wanted to do anything but nod, but that's what she did in the end. Because she probably thought she didn't have a choice… and she didn't, but it was for her own good. No matter how they saw it, he really was taking away from their debt. Maybe one day they'd believe him when he said that.

That was a problem for the future, however.

As it was, Joshua just reached out, placing his hand on her forehead and letting one of the gods at the back of his mind move through him and to her. Like the lioness she was and the domains she governed, Sekhmet moved violently, destructively, in a way that was almost painful but not quite. Like it should be painful, but it ended up being only uncomfortable.

So, that was the first agent, Sekhmet's chosen. Very fitting, considering the goddess was supposed to be the protector of Pharaohs and Meredith was his only combatant apprentice. That and the fact that she'd be the one he called on if he needed some help combat-wise. Like with the vampire situation, for example.

"Next…" he said slowly as he stepped aside. Where she stood, Meredith seemed to look at herself, flexing her fingers as if feeling her body for the first time. It was an experience, having a god's power for the first time, so he wasn't too surprised. His own experiences had been kind of minor, until he started channeling, but since they were only getting the one god, that might make it more meaningful than his own blessings had been. Either way, he stepped in front of Aika. "Close your eyes," he warned in that one instance and the girl didn't hesitate at all.

Soon afterwards, Irer moved through him, much more gently than Sekhmet had before. Personification of sight that she was, the goddess was likely to help Aika with her magic a great deal. Selfishly, Joshua hoped that'd mean she'd make more progress in the stuff he needed, but if it didn't… Well, it wasn't like he was banking on that.

"Careful if you decide to open your eyes, Aika," he added absently before stepping aside once more. "Come on, don't be shy," he urged a moment later when George almost seemed to want to step away as Joshua turned towards him. "I promise they are nice," he reassured, as if that were the problem.

Imhotep was, admittedly, borderline gentle when he moved through Joshua, he noted to himself, a little amused. He remembered that particular name from a movie and… Well, that didn't matter. What mattered was that the healer god would pair incredibly well with George. Maybe that'd push him into a level that could be useful further down the line. He was hoping it would. Maybe Georg would have the key to better deal with soul recoveries…

"You're really making me feel self-conscious here, guys," he thought out loud, watching Karin, Dion and Levi stiffen. The first was the bravest, proving why Morag had taken a liking to her by stepping forward, shoulders squared. One would think she was going to war, honestly. "No need to look so tense," he commented with a raised eyebrow even as he reached with his hand.

Renenutet was an agricultural goddess, and that was only… tangentially related to Karin's Nature Magic, at best. The deity had been eager when offered the chance though, and Joshua thought that mattered more than compatibility, really. There were also not that many generally nature oriented gods in the pantheon, by the looks of it. Most of them tended to focus on one or two aspects of it rather than its entirety.

He wondered how that'd work out for both his Star and the goddess, however.

"And then there were two…" he mused idly, not missing a bit as he approached the last of his students. With no hesitation, feeling how the others were already coming down from the high of their blessings, he moved to bless the last two. He wanted to be there in case they had any questions or needed help with something.

The second to last was Dion, who was chosen by Hesat. He wasn't too sure what she was goddess of, truth be told, but there was something maternal to her, which made him think she might be a goddess of motherhood or some such. She always enjoyed when he spent time with his daughters, that was for sure.

Why she'd chosen Dion was a mystery, but he suspected it was because, in a way, Coven Magic could be considered a motherly magic. A magic that took weaker spells and made them stronger, nurtured them, raised them. It commanded its own way of respect and deference, but softly, caringly.

"... A deity chose me?" Levi asked when Joshua turned towards him at last, as if he were surprised that he did. Was he expecting to be left out? And Joshua thought he was oblivious. Hadn't he directly stated that he was part of the whole deal?

"Sure did." In a way, his was actually the most surprising and at the same time the most expected. It'd certainly be a shock to Levi himself though. Because if he thought no deity would choose him, then being picked by someone as notorious as Thoth would be quite something, surely. God of knowledge, writing, scribes and tuition though, Thoth couldn't have been more perfect for Levi if he tried. Although, it was the other way around, right?

"That's that," he announced, clapping his hands and stepping back a little. "Now… any questions?" he asked. He pretended not to hear Ravel stifling a giggle behind him while the Stars stared at him with wide eyes. "I'll take that as a yes," he commented idly, but that was to be expected.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,422
Champions Aren't Born, We're Built

[Karin]

She felt… the same and different and more, all at the same time.

She could feel Renenutet at the back of her mind, whispering things without words. Telling her about nature and plants and their ground and animals and their instincts and how to handle them. Every time her mind wandered to a spell, the goddess would point things out, things Karin could do with them, things Renenutet could help with, things Karin could do better. Most of all, however, Renenutet would tell her about the things she'd no longer need magic for.

Her blessing alone would be more than enough to make things happen, to make plants grow, to make cattle healthy, to look over fields and make sure resources were never scarce. Renenutet whispered tempting things, encouraging things, and Karin could do nothing but listen as the divine power coursed through her body. Weak in presence, but there, very much there and very obviously there. She felt it like a stream, running through her body like a single vein in between many that were only for blood. Divine energy made her feel like a completely different person, even though little had changed.

"You and I, girl, we'll make great things happen," the goddess told her, for once using words and speaking louder. "The Pharaoh is wise, and some of his wisdom has been passed onto you. You'll make him proud, just like I'll make our pantheon proud."

Our.

She said our.

And Karin supposed she wasn't wrong. She was no longer just a member of House of Water and little else. She was now a member of the Egyptian pantheon. An agent, directly under the leader that was Davis. In the span of an hour, Karin had gone from a normal magician – if apprenticing under the best of the best – to being so much more. Few magicians could speak – or dream, even – of reaching such heights, let alone humans, and there she was, with the opportunity dropped on her lap.

Dropped on her lap by her teacher, who seemed to treat it all like he'd taught them a particularly neat spell, rather than presented them with divine blessings. She could see it in all her fellow apprentices', fellow Stars', faces. They were all trying to wrap their minds around what'd happened, to no avail.

"Everything alright?" Davis asked her, standing in front of her and looking her up and down as if looking for a visible sign of something going wrong. Karin just stared at him, wondering if saying she was hurting from excessive debt would help her case any. She had a feeling he'd think she was joking or something, however, and she wasn't in the mood to see that. "Huh, Renenutet was kinder to you than some of the others were. Particularly Sekhmet and Irer," he commented, glancing towards Meredith and Aika. "If you need anything, let me know, yeah?" he added, giving her a comforting squeeze on the shoulder and a warm smile before moving to check on George.

'I need a way to pay some of this back,' she thought, but didn't say. Because she knew he'd wave her away, brush it off. How was it that just when they'd managed to do something for him, an admittedly rather small thing compared to their debt, the man turned around and did this? How was that in any way fair?

"The Pharaoh's generosity knows no bounds," Renenutet whispered. It should have been a good thing, but they both knew it to be nothing of the sort. The words came out ominous and both of them were wary because of them. "But he's given you this opportunity for a reason. Help him with his mission, and that should be payment enough, don't you think? He helps you, so that you can help him."

That… made some amount of sense. Maybe it'd never be enough, but if she could at least do something other than continue to receive his favor for free, then Karin would be happy. It wasn't like they dreaded being in his debt per se, even if Ravel could be scary when invoking it, but they hated the idea that they couldn't return some of the favor. It made them feel undeserving, like Davis' efforts would have been better spent elsewhere.

However, maybe Renenutet was right. Maybe this was an opportunity to do more. If they could help spread word, raise the reputation of the Egyptian pantheon, then that'd be a favor to their Pharaoh, right?... Yes, she liked the sound of that.

"Together, we'll do great things, Daughter of Sven." What did that even mean? Her father wasn't called Sven. Why was she calling her-? "Your magic is overlooked, and so is my domain, but we'll show the world, won't we? We'll show them what we can do. And when we do, they'll see how strong both your Pharaoh and my pantheon are."

"Well," Davis said, snapping her away from Renenutet's sweet whispers with a clap of his hands. "I see you're all getting the hang of your blessings and the voices in your heads," he added flippantly with a grin while Ravel sighed behind him. Karin very much empathized with the devil, truly. "What do you all say we move this to a training ground and get some testing done? Better to know what you're capable of, yes?"

"Professor Davis, these are… rather busy hours for the training grounds," Meredith pointed out and Joshua just raised an eyebrow at her. Eventually, the girl blushed self-consciously.

"Don't worry about it. I'll clear one, maybe two, for us. Ravel-"

"I'll talk with Agnes, Mr. Davis. Give me a minute," the devil replied before the man could even finish, nodding at him and then leaving through the door. Karin sometimes forgot that Director Agnes was as deep in debt as they were. It was an insane notion, but it was true nonetheless. Nobody was safe from Davis, apparently.

"Right, while we wait. What do you guys say we discuss what we'll be trying out?" Davis asked with a half-smile and Karin resigned herself to her fate. She'd have to follow the path Renenutet had mentioned and hope that'd be enough, she supposed. They had been doing some progress just by doing well in jobs. If they did exceptionally well, then all the better, right?


[}-o-{]
​

[Joshua Davis]

"Thank you for the opportunity, Lord Balam," Joshua said, using his best acting to try and sell the idea that he knew what he was doing. In truth, he was just repeating the stuff that he'd been told by Ravel and Serafall, really. It helped that he did mean the words though, so that worked in his favor, at least. "I promise you that I won't give anyone else the ability to do what your family can."

His request for devil bloodlines was… going slowly, from what Sirzechs told him. Not that it was a surprise, admittedly, but Joshua couldn't help but feel a little frustrated. He really couldn't care less for the actual bloodlines themselves. He just wanted the data. It was all information that could give him ideas, approaches to doing stuff that he might not have thought of.

Studying the Phenex Tears by themselves – without doing so with the Phenex bloodline itself – had given him way more than just fast healing. He'd learned how to better keep the body in peak condition. He'd used what he'd learned about them in the arrays that he'd used to wait awake for Ophis. He'd used that for the arrays that he was, at that moment, using to patch up his soul when harmed by divinity.

There was so much that could lay hiding in those things, because devils were creatures of magic. Human bodies were approximately 50 to 60% water. Devils had a similar percentage of just pure magic making up their existence. He hadn't found anything similar anywhere else so far, except maybe nekoshous, and those were a tentative hypothesis, since the only ones he'd had access to were both reincarnated as devils. Not even valkyries reached that level, although they could be somewhat close in certain cases.

So, he really wanted to study them and their unique applications of magic.

"Think nothing of it, Lord Davis," the devil in front of him replied, looking mighty pleased with himself. Admittedly, it looked rather odd on his rock-like appearance, but such was the Balam family and Joshua wasn't there to judge the aesthetics of their bloodline. Although, he did wonder if that was somehow connected with their Power of Might. "After you brought my wife back to me? The least I can do is return the favor when asked," Lord Balam told him.

He was a great guy like that, he supposed. The man was the sole exception to the difficulties Joshua was having to get the agreement of devils in order to study their bloodlines. He had agreed almost straight away, after some minimal talks and reassurances. Thus, he marked himself as either a very nice guy, or a very reasonable one, or both. Or, as an extra option, the guy just loved his wife that much. If that was the case, then Joshua's respect for the guy would shoot up a great deal.

On the matter, Ravel had said that made him a smart man, but Joshua wasn't sure what being smart had to do with anything. It was all just a matter of trust, really. Because he knew he was asking for them to just take his word for it, for the most part, unless they sat down to talk about the aspects of an Oath that both parties would be happy with, which probably wasn't going to happen anymore than just making them agree normally because his terms were too vague. Or so he was told, at least.

One would have thought the Sitri and the Gremory would be accommodating too, but there were… issues in both regards. With the latter, involving a certain Bael and with the former… Well, his relationship with Serafall brought a number of issues in a number of ways and they were dealing with one of those. Joshua didn't hold it against her, at all. He had known what he was walking into… for the most part.

And dealing with that was a small price to pay to be with Serafall, really.

"Now, do you need us to do anything, Lord Davis? Or should we just leave you to it?" Balam asked, sounding genuinely curious, maybe even a little interested. Maybe he was trying to get something out of the agreement? If he did, then Joshua would be at least open to discuss things, considering the man hadn't tried to make a trade out of it in order to allow him to look into his bloodline.

"I'll set up the spells and look into things normally first. Then I might need to see your power in action, maybe test how much you can do, if that's okay with you, Lord Balam," he answered, happy to be more in his territory rather than the politics' one.

"Carry on then, neither of us want to waste any time, I'm sure," the devil told him and he nodded with a slight smile. He was liking Balam so far. Maybe he could talk with Ravel about doing something nice for them. His defenses were… interesting, for sure. They likely used some variation of their family's Power to make them work a certain way, but that was something he'd learn after looking into things more. Still, Joshua was reasonably certain that he could improve them after a more thorough inspection.

That was a talk for some other day though.

Joshua had other things to do at the moment and, as Balam said, he did not, in fact, want to waste any time. He might not have Ophis looming over his head like a Damocles' Sword, but the dragon was still a danger. Furthermore, Khaos was being worryingly silent once more and he didn't know how to feel about that. Because he knew they were trying to do something, he just didn't know what… exactly.

He had strong suspicions, however, from what he remembered and what he'd seen.

Joshua also didn't know if they were being silent because they were struggling with something – like the pieces of Valerie's Sacred Gear not working properly, for example – or if they were preparing something huge. He was very, very worried about that last possibility. Which was why he was trying to get as much done as possible and also why he needed as much information and ideas as possible.

"Everything's ready," he said, mostly because Balam and his wife seemed actually curious about his process and it didn't really bother him much to run commentary on what he was doing. Least he could do, for people that were willing to give him potentially very good tools for the future without making it annoying or slow.


[}-o-{]
​

Joshua was very wary of Ophis.

That was no surprise to literally anyone – anyone that knew about the dragon and what had gone down, which wasn't very many people – and didn't need to be said, really. However, that was still a fact, and as such, it stood to reason that he wanted to keep an eye on her. Or as much as he could keep an eye on a creature that could do whatever the fuck she wanted.

Hence, the fact that there was an entire array in place to watch over all three of the Project Silence spots at the moment dedicated to keeping the dragon calm. If she stepped out of the rooms and for some reason didn't immediately go into another or disappear, he wanted to know. Hell, he wanted to know even if she did do that, just to be informed. Because he was still rather on edge knowing she was right there but literally nothing else.

Although, admittedly, he was a lot calmer now that he'd moved the rooms far away from his home.

Still didn't change anything, but he felt better anyway.

So, on account of all that, Joshua felt like it was entirely fair and understandable that he knew the exact moment she came out of one of the rooms – the Sense Weakening Room – and didn't immediately go to another or elsewhere. Instead, she stood there, head tilted to one side. When he realized this, he moved as fast as he could to go visit her. He had several reasons for that, and he hoped she'd humor him for a bit.

"Joshua Davis," the literally infinitely strong dragon greeted when he teleported next to her.

"Ophis," he replied, gathering his wits as best he could. "I hope the rooms and the changes I've been making work well?" he started with, because he felt like it was a safe enough question. Surely she'd have voiced or otherwise shown her displeasure if that wasn't the case.

Sure enough, she nodded.

"They have," she answered simply, and that was all she said. Because of course it was. Joshua had started to expect such blunt, straightforward responses from her. It didn't make them any less nervewracking though, because they forced him to talk more with her in order to get what he wanted.

"If there's anything that stands out to you about them, I'd appreciate knowing. That way I can improve them faster," he explained. That time, he didn't even get a verbal response. Instead, Ophis just nodded and let the silence hang around them some more. Resigning himself, Joshua moved on to the next point he wanted to address. "... Was something the matter? You've never just… stood outside like this," he asked cautiously.

"I was looking at Khaos Brigade," she answered and he blinked at her with eyes as flat as hers. She'd just looked- 'Doesn't matter. Of course she can just look at them even if they're probably halfway across the world from here,' he thought to himself. Although, he made a mental note of the direction she'd been looking.

It might be useless, but it might also not be.

"They are… suspicious," she commented idly, with the same tone she said… well, most everything she said, really.

"Of you?" he asked, blinking. Did they not know what was going on in regards to his rooms and all? Were they unaware of his relationship with Ophis? That was… he wasn't sure how that'd happen, but he could kind of understand it. If they were as wary of talking to the dragon as he was, and if she was as vague and misleading as she was with him with them, then…

Yeah, it actually tracked.

"No… That too, but no," the dragon said, looking off to the side again. "They are doing… strange things," she added, as if that explained anything. Maybe it was just Joshua, but he felt like that cleared up precisely nothing. If anything, he probably had more questions than before. "I'll be going back into this room… Does it have a name?" she asked and this time she looked downright intent, which only served to set him even more on edge.

"... I call that one White Room," he answered hesitantly. Formerly Project Silence: Copy, he'd started calling it the White Room, after Ophis confirmed that, for her, it was basically a white noise room. "The others are the Quiet Room and the Soft Room," he added, waving his hand at Project Silence: Room and the Weakening version of the latter, respectively. Ophis had said that they were quieter and softer, after all.

"... I like them," she commented with a nod that he imagined was approving. Although, maybe he was trying too hard to get a read on her and imagining things. He couldn't really be sure. What he was sure about was that she didn't immediately move after that, which was also unusual. "Thank you," she said eventually, before walking into the White Room.

Joshua remained outside for a long moment, going over the interaction again and again. He'd make an illusion re-enaction for his partners so that they could help him see if he'd missed something. Although, they had about as much idea on how to deal with Ophis as he did, really. None of their social training and experience could really help them deal with the oddity that was the Ouroborous Dragon.

They could help him brainstorm though, that was for sure.

'I'm never going to get used to her,' he thought to himself, sighing and running his fingers through his hair in an attempt to calm his beating hard. 'At least she's not completely unreasonable, I guess,' he mused, although maybe he was getting complacent because things were going well. Nothing really said Ophis couldn't snap at the weirdest and/or most inconsequential thing.

All in all though, his life and/or world hadn't ended yet, so he was feeling cautiously optimistic.


[}-o-{]
​

"Thank you for coming, Joshua."

"Please, don't thank me for this," Joshua replied awkwardly with a smile that reflected that sentiment. "If I'm being brutally honest, I really, really want to just wash my hands off of this," he said then, drawing a giggle from Gabriel. Which was a lot better than the indignation that he expected from the angels when telling them that he wanted nothing to do with the System of Heaven Administrator role that he seemed to have been given for… reasons.

Granted, he already knew his partner didn't mind his attitude towards the whole situation, but he'd expected at least one of the Seraphs to be indignant or outright angry. Instead, Michael looked downright pleased, Raphael was looking at him the way he looked at the runes Göndul taught him and Uriel… Well, Uriel was the closest to what he expected, but if anything he seemed frustrated, as if he'd expected Joshua to say something else and was annoyed he'd been wrong.

"You seem confused," Raphael pointed out, as if that were a great mystery.

"I half expected you guys to be offended or something, I'll admit," he said wearily, because he'd been able to push away thoughts on the matter while away. But in Heaven? The entire System of Heaven issue wouldn't leave him alone, like a creature had climbed on his back and weighted him down.

"We'd be more offended if you tried to do whatever you wanted with that power," Uriel said, although his voice came out like he'd changed his mind right before growling the words rather than speaking them. "We don't know why you were given the designation you were, but you're a human, a magician, a representative of another faction and you're involved romantically with two-"

Gabriel interrupted the last part before it could be finished, clearing her throat.

"... You're not who we'd have picked," Uriel finished, although this time he almost sounded hesitant rather than annoyed.

"If it makes you feel better, I'm not who I'd have picked," Joshua replied, although that seemed to be the wrong thing to say. At least in regards to Gabriel, because it was his turn to get one of her stares of doom, which was something halfway between disappointment and sadness. Very painful, indeed. "But I was, so I'll do my best to use this for the sake of your faction, since it's… Well, yours. Just tell me what to do with this," he said, hoping that'd somehow make his partner stop.

Thankfully, it did, but when he turned around he was met with a beaming Raphael and a smiling Michael. Even Uriel looked almost pleased, which said a lot, at least from what Joshua knew of the Seraph so far. 'Not doing awful with the possible in-laws, I guess. I'll take that, even if I could do without… this thing,' he thought to himself, sighing and summoning the golden screen.

"So… Where do we start?" he asked and both Raphael and Michael traded a look before nodding and turning towards him.

What followed was a long, long process in which the Seraphs guided him through screens, asking him to translate as best he could. Not everything was in perfectly legible text. Sometimes, he'd go over a screen and instead of seeing text he'd get… impressions, ideas. Like someone was putting thoughts in his mind through text that he couldn't quite read so much as inherently understand.

It was a very strange thing to go through, but the angels didn't seem surprised. Michael looked downright vindicated when he tried to explain and Joshua got the distinct impression that those parts were the ones where his Moderator designation kind of fell short or something. It did slow them down, but none of them seemed to mind, discussing everything in depth, systemically dissecting every single thing Joshua read and explained.

It kind of reminded him of what he'd gone through when researching the Power of Might of the Balam family, actually.

That kind of study process was something he was familiar with, at least, so that helped ease him into things. Bit by bit, Joshua started getting more involved… in a sense. He didn't dare say much, but he listened to them speak, trying to learn as much as he could and asking questions when he didn't feel like Uriel would cut his head off for doing it.

"Do it," Michael urged at some point. "It's an isolated thing that Raphael and I set up just to see what you can do and how much you can do compared to me," he said as he presented a screen to Joshua. It was an inane rule of some sort that'd affect people reading a specific passage from… some text. Joshua didn't know the bible by heart and the rest of the texts and such he knew even less of. He was pretty sure there were others, at least, but maybe he should look into things before saying anything on the matter.

The point was that they wanted him to try and modify a specific part of the set up presented in the screen.

"Okay," he said, almost like a sigh as he stared at the screen. Eventually, he nodded, trying to interact with it the same way he'd interacted with his own system's screens – 'Are they connected?' – and… succeeding. "There… right?" he announced, leaning back a little.

"... Just like that, Michael," Raphael breathed out and the leader of Heaven seemed entranced by the screen.

"... I expected a difference, not… this…" the golden-winged Seraph said, before looking up from the screen and staring at Joshua rather intently with emotions he couldn't hope to understand. "We have much to test, Joshua. I hope you don't mind."

"Testing stuff is what I do every day. Far be it for me to stop someone else from doing it too," he replied and that might be a mistake because both Raphael and Michael got a slightly manic – and familiar, admittedly – look in their eyes. Off to the side, Uriel huffed, apparently getting comfortable in his own chair, while Gabriel giggled, amused.

Joshua got the distinct feeling that they were going to be there for a while.

As it turns out, he was right.

#1,434
I Can Feel Myself Coming Alive

[Joshua Davis]

Considering all that was going on in his life, Joshua thought it was kind of… sad how side-lined his study of runes had been.

When he'd started, it had been the biggest thing in a while, or at least so it had felt. Certainly the thing that made him the most excited to do, rather than just another project that he needed to get done. In a way, that remained the case… It was just that life had decided to punish him for having fun, he supposed. Because right afterwards, everything had turned upside down and then twisted into a pretzel.

Crazy how life can change in less than two months…

"That's… a lot of progress…" Göndul commented, although she sounded odd while doing so.

All the same, Joshua couldn't help but be a little disappointed as he looked at the circle he'd just finished casting. Not with Myrddin circles but with the Nordic ones this time and it was… It wasn't perfect, admittedly, but that wasn't why he wasn't happy with it. He just felt like it wasn't as meaningful as it would have been if he weren't dealing with infinite magic and somehow having control of Heaven.

Joshua was a little miffed about that, admittedly.

Which he realized was a little… maybe entitled? It didn't feel like the word, but it fit a little. It made him feel bad to complain about those things, more the former than the latter. The former was definitely a boon, even if he'd probably need quite a while to get the hang of just… living with the changes he had to go through. The latter was a little more understandable, he felt, because Joshua was genuinely feeling like that was a weight added to him rather than anything remotely helpful.

Sure, he could think of a lot of things that he could tweak here and there that'd be really nice for him… but he couldn't do any of that. He didn't understand the System of Heaven, for as much as he had a skill related to it. He didn't know what a minimal change could do to the entire thing, much like how changing a single rune of the circle he'd just cast would turn the simple sound-proof ward into a truly random bomb.

"This is huge," Göndul commented, bringing him back to the present. When Joshua turned to look at her, she even seemed a little annoyed herself, but at him. It only took his socially challenged ass a few seconds to piece together why. She probably was having one of those moments when people thought he was impressive and he was downplaying that by not being excited, right?

In all honesty, it'd taken him months. He was pretty sure he was casting his first spell with the Myrddin circles in a lot less time than that, and without any magic knowledge to speak of. If anything, he was laughably slow… He had a feeling that saying that wouldn't be a good idea though.

Maybe being friends with so many politically inclined people was giving him some social skills.

Now that would be worth celebrating.

"Sorry, I've just… I have a lot in my mind," he commented, taking a deep breath in and trying to get his thoughts on straight. That task was made a little difficult when the Egyptians seemed so amused by his struggles. "Lots of things going on and I'm a little annoyed I haven't been able to give this the attention or even the emotional bandwidth I want," he explained with a sigh. "But I am happy with this, this is progress. Soon, I'll be able to start adding this to my casting and I'm definitely looking forward to this. I already have so many ideas on how to apply it together with the Myrddin circles in a way that'll make both sides that much better than they'd be alone."

He really did. What he was learning about the Balam Power of Might would go great with Runes and spells to boost someone's capabilities. He didn't even need to directly try to copy the power, really. Just applying some of the concepts it did, together with the spells Joshua was already using would very much improve the efficacy of the enhancement.

He couldn't wait to test that, really, since it'd be his first application of the Balam data.

"I already knew this, but you're crazy. You know that, right?" Göndul asked, shaking her head, and Joshua just shrugged in response. Wouldn't be the first time he was called that, nor would it be the last. He'd gotten used to it, at some point, or maybe he'd given up trying to truly wrap his head around it. Because he could understand it, on some level… it was just so strange, after most of his life was spent being below average and a mess.

'Sometimes it doesn't feel like that's the most of my life,' he thought idly. Because his old life really did feel like the one that was shorter, even though that had been about 90% of it. 'Maybe the right way to word it is that this life has been a lot more eventful,' he mused to himself.

"So people keep telling me," he replied with a wry smile. "Now, what's next on the list?" he asked, leaning back and looking at the circle he'd cast. It wasn't even perfect. There were places he could adjust, improve upon. He'd cast the roughest version of the spell he could, an unmodified one, basically, and that was just… no. It felt wrong, somehow. "I'm behind my own expectations and I'm suddenly feeling motivated to catch up," he added, tapping his fingers on the table and already scribbling some of his ideas on how to modify that particular circle.

It was all kinds of different from Myrddin ones, but that was the idea, he supposed.

"Terrifying," Göndul said, but she seemed to be grinning. "Joshua, I heard you have romantic partners…"

"Three of them, yeah," he replied, the non sequitur making him suddenly wary.

"You wouldn't happen to have space for my granddaughter, right? I promise she's not as much of a mess as she appears to be," Göndul commented, beaming at him, and he could only smile wryly at her.

"I think my partners would have a problem with that," he answered flatly.


[}-o-{]
​

"Thanks for having us over," Sirzechs said and Joshua almost felt like giving the man an unimpressed look. Alas, he was growing a little more aware that some formalities were necessary… which meant he only half-sighed. "Millicas has been looking forward to this for a while now," the Satan added, more casually, and Joshua very much appreciated that shift compared to before.

"Dad!"

"Honestly, so has Kunou," Joshua replied just as calmly.

"Dad!"

It was only fair that both children were teased, far as he was concerned. That way nobody felt truly insulted… or both would? He wasn't too clear on that, but the rest of the adults seemed to agree with him that it was amusing. Maybe it was a parent thing, the need to embarrass one's kid. Joshua definitely felt like he understood his parents a lot better, admittedly.

"Come on, I'll set up the flight course and you guys can get started with your fun," Joshua continued, and that seemed to take the wind out of the children's sails a little bit. "That way I can get back to my tea," he added wearily. He was technically on a break, but that was because he needed one. Between working on improving all the Project Silence versions, and getting used to using his now infinite reserves, and visiting Heaven to experiment with Michael and Raphael and learning Runes and teaching classes in House of Water and spending time with his family and his partners, and…

Joshua's days were getting busier and busier with no sign of easing up. He was getting a little concerned, in all honesty. If things continued the way they were going, he really would be overwhelmed with stuff. The good thing though, was that his House of Water duty could, technically, be dropped on Levi at any point. He was just buying time for the guy to get a better grasp of things. Getting used to his new magic situation was a temporary thing too.

Then there was the Heaven thing… which he really hoped would be over at some point rather than him getting stuck with it. Ideally, he'd be able to give Michael Administrator privileges so that he could do his thing. He was kind of surprised none of the angels had brought that up with him, actually. Maybe they were getting used to things too. He could understand that.

Maybe he'd bring it up during his next visit.

"And here-"

"I'm not going to set up the course exactly as you want it, Kunou. You're the least impartial person here," Joshua commented, brought back to the present as his daughter – again – tried to convince him to put obstacles and goals for the flying course where she wanted them. As if he were dumb enough not to realize that she was trying to give herself an advantage. It was cute to see her reaction when he did the opposite of what she said though… although he did cave once or twice.

Admittedly, the other kids were almost as petty, and he tried to listen to them in equal amounts with their suggestions. Well, most of them. Millicas was new to the whole thing, so Joshua had to try and make things fair for him on his own without input. He just hoped he hadn't unknowingly gone overboard in that regard.

"Well, I think that's that," he commented, clapping his hands and cracking his neck with a weary groan.

"Dibs," Morag said instantly from where she clung to his back, taking advantage of their bond to know precisely when he was going to make his announcement. The chain of pettiness continued, evidently, but Joshua could only do so much to stop it. The rest of the kids made a valiant effort to be just as quick, falling a little short and cursing quietly under their breath. Joshua pretended not to listen to them.

"So, it's Morag, Koneko, Millicas, Kunou and Ravel," he announced, running his fingers through his hair. He was pretty sure Ravel hadn't really cared for going first, but he wasn't going to point that out. It'd just make Kunou sad if she realized she should have been last. "Have fun, kids."

"... Not a kid," Koneko mumbled from beside him, but he just rolled his eyes at her and planted his hand on top of her head to ruffle her hair.

"You know where to get us if you need anything," Joshua commented, stepping away and feeling Morag jump off of him. Cheshire, for her part, followed after him while Friday immediately jumped to rambling about things, like how Nagini and Raynare were sparring in the training grounds, or how Kuroka was spying on Koneko without the younger nekoshou knowing, or how Valerie was trying out painting rather than drawing because she said it'd be more accurate to her vision.

Joshua was morbidly curious about how the soul-scarred girl would translate her scrambled thoughts into painting, if he were honest.

"Kids will be busy for a while?" Serafall asked when he came back and he grinned wearily. "Bet one of them will come to complain about fairness in about five minutes."

"Margalo stayed to watch, right? She'll keep the peace for at least ten minutes, I'm sure," Gabriel said as she brought her cup of tea.

"Optimistic, huh? I'm with Serafall, I have to say."

"Guess I'll even things out and say ten," Joshua commented with a chuckle as he sat down in between his partners. "What do you say?" he asked Sirzechs and Grayfia, who looked incredibly amused for some reason.

"Ten." "Five." they said, respectively, at the same time, which made it their turn to be amused.

"Perfectly balanced, as all things should be," Joshua replied, knowing that nobody would get the reference. Although, Serafall seemed to like that. Maybe the next character added to her show would be Thanos-inspired… Fun stuff. "Now, tea?" he offered with a smile.

Some quiet time with some friends and his partners sounded like the break he was kind of needing, Joshua would admit.


[}-o-{]
​

"It's fine to take inspiration in stuff that you see," he encouraged, waving his hand to make the blackboard illusion behind him change. "I do that all the time. Maybe you'll see someone else's magic, or maybe you'll come across an odd Sacred Gear or magical creature or maybe even another race. I've found inspiration in all sorts of places, personally. I wouldn't be a quarter of the magician I am if I'd stuck strictly to the magic branches that I've focused on," he lectured and he found himself thoroughly unimpressed by the skepticism that he saw in his students.

Joshua wasn't sure why he was surprised. Magicians were a weirdly hyperfocused bunch. Although, in a way, he kind of got it. They didn't have as easy a time delving into new things as he did. Least of all because they all seemed to struggle with their one main branch as it was. His advice still applied though and they better listen… or not.

Didn't change much for him if they refused.

So long as the Stars continued shining, the rest of the students could do whatever they wanted. It wasn't his job to make them succeed. He taught them, gave them the tools and then sent them on their way. What they did with his classes and what they learned was up to them.

"Just to be clear, I'm not telling you to learn another branch or something like that," he clarified, although he thought they probably should. Maybe if they expanded their horizons, they'd find things a little easier. While he didn't think it all came down to that, he imagined the lack of confidence and ingrained idea that magic was a struggle the whole way through set many of them back. His Stars, for one, were doing progressively better the more they developed their confidence… Levi notwithstanding. "But still, many branches have a lot of overlap. Even when they don't, some ideas and concepts can still be applied to spells… or you can innovate. I know, crazy," he said, as a joke, even though he knew for many of them it was truly crazy, the idea of coming up with something new.

Admittedly, it made some sense, when you were already struggling with the known stuff, but still…

It just sounded so boring and not at all effective.

"Now, with that tangent done, let's move on to what you should- Yes?" he asked, seeing someone with their hand up. Even more shocking, it wasn't one of his Stars.

Not that the rest of the class didn't sometimes have questions, but it only happened once or twice a class, if that, so it still came as a surprise when they did. For as much as he tried to have them engage in the class, Joshua had slowly but surely lost his will to push them. He had the Stars by then, contrary to when he started. So, he couldn't just not teach, but he could tailor his classes for them if the other students proved too uninterested or unwilling to truly put in effort and show some determination.

They seemed to realize too, because they seemed to at least try to push for his classes to remain somewhat general oriented. Admittedly, Joshua had a feeling that him bringing up the topic with the Stars had something to do with that. Maybe they'd proceeded to tell the rest of the classes that fact so that they knew how things would go if they remained passive? Maybe he'd check, because he'd even count that as a favor to him, really.

Joshua liked teaching, but only when his students were engaged, showing interest. He'd rather stay home tinkering if all he was going to do was talk to the walls in a silent room.

"This is… unrelated to the class, sir. So… if you'd rather not answer…" The woman commented, shifting nervously where she sat. Joshua, for his part, raised a curious eyebrow before urging her to continue with a wave of his hand. "Did something happen with the… um, Stars?"

"Oh, that. You must be a good sensor," he commented with a half-smile that widened when she blushed. He saw one or two other students perk up, apparently having been able to sense that too. Maybe they'd bring up that talent during classes more often now that he'd acknowledged that as a point in their favor… of a sort. "And yes, something did happen. You might know that I've been a representative of the Egyptian pantheon for a while now. Well, the Stars are now officially my representatives, on top of my apprentices. The Egyptians are now giving them a fraction of the support they give me to show that," he explained freely.

Because if they were acknowledged in their roles, it'd make the whole "spread word and gain notoriety" thing easier, he imagined.

Joshua found it a little amusing though, how all of them straightened on their seats. He did feel like he was throwing them off the deep end a little, but there was no use just… waiting things out other than maybe letting them get used to their blessings… But fuck that. House of Water was spoiling them to no end, Ravel had reassured him. So, there shouldn't be too many issues in regards to danger or what not.

Besides, if people were already noticing in class, someone was bound to notice once they started going back on jobs outside the association anyway… So, there was really not that much of a point in keeping things quiet. Maybe he'd throw them a bone or two though, arrange for some specific jobs and other things with Agnes and Ravel.

Yeah, that sounded good.


[}-o-{]
​

[Navya Kumar]

Everything had been going fine.

One moment, they were preparing things for yet another project that was probably going to end in failure. To further add to that calm, they were better hidden than most of the previous bases, if only out of necessity. There were only so many members in their organization and the persistent hunting of the alliance of factions towards Khaos had driven them to… better secure their bases.

There were a number of drawbacks to what they had to do to stay under the radar, but Navya imagined all of them were worth it for the sake of… not dying. Way too many bases had fallen, raided and destroyed by the alliance, before they decided to start being smart about it. Personally, she'd have seriously considered making a run for it if not for that, damn whatever that Lucifer devil promised with his knock-off Sephiroth Graal.

No amount of improvements on their weak human bodies was worth facing the Ultimate Female Devil, the Strongest Woman of Heaven, the Violence of Heaven or, god forbid, the Domain Authority. Because one would just freeze you, the other would just burn you and the third would just punch you. Joshua Davis, however… Navya didn't know how information had gotten out about what he did with those he caught, but the fact was that it had and she wanted absolutely nothing to do with the man's mad magic experiments.

No wonder the lawful and "lawful" associations were falling over themselves to get on his good graces.

Just the things he came up with were crazy, but the fact that he could pull some of them off was crazier.

"Almost ready," Dominick said, his heavily accented voice – not that she was one to talk – carrying over from the other side of the circle on the floor. "Only two more pieces, two more circles and we can try this," the man added, standing up and cracking his back with a groan. "Will it work though?"

"Probably not," Navya said and the two shared a moment of commiseration, because… Really, what did that devil expect them to do, pull off a miracle? He'd destroyed a soul and a Sacred Gear and he expected them to just… find a way to fix that? Navya wasn't sure that kind of madness had been pulled off ever. How were they supposed to find a solution to something that had never happened?

Did he think they were The Professor?

"Still gotta-" Navya continued before being interrupted.

And she was interrupted very abruptly. In one moment, everything was business as usual. The next, Navya felt like someone had closed an iron maiden around her, like she couldn't move and barely could breath. In front of her, Dominick stiffened, probably feeling the same thing. She almost went to try and ask a question, she wasn't sure which of the hundred that had popped in her mind in an instant, but she didn't get to so much as open her mouth.

Why?

Because another spell fell around them, this time feeling like a school of piranhas had been dropped inside the iron maiden with her, ravenously eating away at her magic. That was far from it all, however, oh no. Another second and she felt more and more spells follow up after those two. She heard screams of different kinds from far away, but she could barely move, frozen in panic. Dominick stumbled trying to reach the door to the room they were in, but he struggled to even open it.

"Have to get away…" she heard him mumble and that seemed to give her enough strength to take some tentative steps forward too. It was all for nothing though, at least in Dominick's case. As soon as he opened the door, he let out a strangled sound followed by a desperate: "No, n-!"

And then he dropped like a sack of potatoes.

Navya had only a second to wonder what had happened there before she heard a heavy, ominous sound. It made her think of something being dragged on the floor… and then the hissing of a snake. 'Nagini,' her mind conjured up. It tracked. Overwhelming magical might the likes of which she couldn't fathom, fast and strong. And now, a gigantic serpent – she confirmed that when the creature peeked inside the room – that could just… kill like that?

It was him.

He'd found them.

How…?

They were supposed to be hidden!

"What do we have here?" a new voice said, receiving hissing – was that a laugh? – from the snake. Then a fallen angel floated in, four-winged and with purple flames. That had to be Raynare, the pet Fallen… the executioner. Because if Davis himself didn't destroy you in an experiment, and if his familiars didn't hunt you down, then there were three others you could encounter. The Maiden, the Trickster and the Executioner. Jeanne Davis, Kuroka the Nekoshou and Raynare the Fallen. "Oh… Joshua's definitely going to want to see this," the latter of those three commented, not looking at Navya but at the room behind her, at the circle, the ritual, they had been working on.

Then she seemed to notice Dominick on the ground.

"Shouldn't have killed that one. Joshua will want answers," the Fallen commented, sounding amused. The snake hissed some more, looking away from Navya, Dominick's corpse and, most importantly, Raynare. "Now you though… you will have answers for Joshua, I'm sure," the Executioner commented, floating up to Navya's face and staring intently into her eyes with her purple irises, matching the flames around her hands, the ones she used to threaten Navya. "Won't you?"

"Y-yes," she stammered, trying to lean away but finding herself frozen in place out of sheer fear… and too weak to fight that with her magic rapidly taken away. "Of c-course."

"Good girl," the fallen said mockingly. "Be helpful and maybe you'll go up in flames rather than one of Joshua's little tests. Believe me, you'll prefer that. Might even survive, if you know enough to need to be taken with us."

Navya dearly hoped that ritual was good enough to warrant that. She hoped that with all her being, more than when a blessing of Sephiroth Graal had been promised as payment. She needed that spell to be good for something and it wasn't even related to the effect it'd have when cast. No, she needed it to be good enough to be interesting for a mad magician.

"That's the look you should have," the Executioner commented. "It means you're smart."


[} Chapter End {]
