#1,477
Sincerely Me

[Joshua Davis]

"Sounds like you got plenty of information," Aika commented absently, seeing something he couldn't and making him wonder if he ever looked like that to other people when watching his system screens. He wasn't focusing too much on that though, admittedly. Mostly, he was checking on his own things, his own feedback, as they both checked on Valerie.

"I did," he replied, running his fingers through his hair. Because yeah, Elizabeth had pulled through and managed to get plenty of stuff from her shady association contacts. The problem was that he didn't know how to feel interacting with such a group of people… Alas, desperate times, desperate measures.

'No, you're not allowed to use Sacrifice Magic to power up our arrays, Friday,' he had to insist, again, as the living spell insisted on begging. To be honest, the way that one stray association had used the magic to power up their basic ass defensive array was crazy. The thing was as strong as some of his own arrays solely because of how much they'd juiced it all up with Sacrifice Magic.

Now, if only that branch didn't need as much… Well, sacrifice.

"Enemies?" Friday suggested, and she had no business sounding so innocently curious when talking about sacrificing their enemies to power up spells. Unfortunately, that wasn't quite as good for the branch of magic, since it worked similarly to Boons and Oaths in that it used the significance of the – in that case – sacrifice to the caster. "Still."

'God, give me patience…' he prayed silently, taking a deep breath in. '... Let's put a pin on that, Friday,' he decided to tell the spell, and she seemed happy that he hadn't straight out said no. Suddenly, Joshua was kind of understanding why his parents did that kind of thing so much. Unfortunately, it would only have so much use before it started working against him.

"So, things are good?" Valerie asked, all smiles and innocence that were painful to see. "When can we play again?" she added excitedly and Joshua smiled back at her as best he could. Then he reached like he would with Kunou, pushing a lock of her silvery hair out of her face and getting a giggle out of the girl.

'You're going to have a chance at a normal life, Valerie. I promise,' he thought to himself. That girl hadn't even gotten half a chance yet in her life, if his memories and what he knew were in any way accurate. He wanted to give her that, the same way the opportunity had been given to him. He felt like that was kind of something he should do, something he was responsible for.

Paying it forward, as it were.

"Joshua?" Aika called and he took a deep breath in before turning towards her. "Can we check notes?"

"Absolutely," he replied, straightening and giving Valerie one last sad smile. "We'll play in a bit, alright, Val?" he asked and he got a smile so big and that tugged at his heart so much. He almost felt like just putting things off. He probably would have, if he weren't about to work on something for her.

"Sure~ You look funny when you work," the girl told him. "Can't wait though."

"We'll be quick," he said with a nod.

When he turned, he saw what he imagined was a similar expression to his own on Aika. She was a weird, perverted girl, but she was like Issei and that she had a good heart. He guessed they were actually rather good a match, despite how canon things went for them. That was good, because if he was going to rely on her to help him with that whole situation, he kind of needed her to be good and give it her all.

Lucky him.

And lucky Valerie too, he supposed.

Was about time for her to get something going her way.

"So, I think I'm seeing something at some of the edges," Aika commented and he narrowed his eyes. "I'm not sure what, but Irer has some ideas of what we could do to get a better look at it. I'm gonna have to work with Levi on how to modify a few spells."

"If you need to, I can help too," he told her, glancing towards Valerie who had taken a spare notebook he gave her and was drawing doodles on it. "I think you might be getting more than I am," he added self-deprecatingly.

Although, that didn't mean he wasn't getting some results himself. With some more understanding and information… He would have to hit the books he got from his latest attempt at research with Elizabeth, but he thought he might be able to help Valerie achieve the "soul mending" effect that he'd seen happen a few times by then. He might even be able to use some of the strengthening effects he was studying from the Balam bloodline on that…

Grendel was a surprisingly good resource once Joshua remembered he was there. He might need to get Ravel to help him keep track of all the things he had around to work with, because forgetting that was a terrible mistake. All the same, the resilience of the dragon might give him something more to work with in regards to the dhampir.

"I have a feeling that you're lying through your teeth without knowing," Aika commented dryly and he chuckled. She could be right. Different opinions and all that. "So… time to play, right?"

"Really?" Valerie asked, perking up. "You didn't talk much."

"Sure thing," Aika answered with a wide smile. "Joshua and I can talk more while we play. So, what did you want to do, Valerie?"

"I wanna draw!"

"Maybe we can take turns drawing and see who guesses first," Joshua suggested and the dhampir seemed to get even more excited after that. Yeah, Aika was right. They could play and work. He'd picked his apprentice right, he supposed.

Never doubted.


[}-o-{]
​

[Ravel Phenex]

"Sorry for making more work for you, Ravel," Joshua said, an awkward smile on his face, but she couldn't feel anything but pride.

After all, how else was she supposed to feel when someone as strong and talented as Joshua depended on her so much for so many things. It made her feel like she might have a fraction of all the power that he had at his fingertips. Because she made some of the things he did possible. She helped prepare him when he had to negotiate or play politics. She organized the work needed for him to get his information and resources. She was the one that kept track of things for him, so that he could focus on what he did best.

And Ravel was so grateful for that.

"It's no problem at all, Mr. Davis," she replied, beaming at the man even as he sighed. He was worrying too much. Sure, it was a lot of work for her, but she was happy doing it. So, was it really an issue if that was the case?

"I know you like doing all this, for whatever reason," he commented, as if he couldn't understand how she could enjoy what she did, like a hypocrite. "But it's still a lot. I can probably get you a helper or thirty with a word or two to someone. You can even organize that yourself, if you don't think I could find someone good, because that's totally a valid concern for you to have."

That… was tempting, but no-

"Ravel, please," Joshua insisted almost immediately. Ravel had thought she had a better poker face, although maybe the man had gotten good at reading her. Which was kind of sad, considering she could get away with lying to her parents quite a bit. "If only for my own peace of mind. You're a child and-"

"Not a child," she cut in immediately, only realizing that she wasn't really helping her case with that at all after saying it. She felt her cheeks heat up afterwards, but she did her best to keep her face schooled and not look away from Joshua. No matter how amused the man looked or how embarrassing that had been.

"Do I have to make it an order? Because I will if it saves me from feeling like I'm working you to the bone, no matter how good you might be at what you do," he said and she tried and failed not to smile. Ravel thought he was being entirely too unfair though. "Just say the terms and I'll get it done, please?" he all but begged and that's what made her resolution crumble.

She couldn't make the man act like that; it was just wrong.

"Alright… I'll see what I do."

"If you don't get someone soon, you better have good excuses," he said then, reading right through her again as he narrowed his eyes. "Seriously, work on that, or I'll have to, and that's only going to be terrible for everyone involved and you know it."

She… couldn't exactly disagree, she supposed.

Still.

"With that said," Joshua said, his resolve to dealing with things he wasn't comfortable with crumbling bit by bit the more she resisted. He wasn't good at dealing with conflict with people that he liked, Ravel had learned. He wasn't much for discipline with Kunou, for example, and he let the Cat get away with a lot… And she guessed he let her do her own thing even when he didn't entirely agree when Ravel was working. "I'm going to go visit the Norse soon, so… I need some help with that, even if I'll have Serafall with me. I don't want to make her do all the work like I did with Elizabeth."

Ravel's expression immediately cleared now that it had something she was confident in to focus on. Maybe she was more like Joshua than she thought though, she considered after that thought crossed her mind. Because that was a very him thing to do…

She wasn't too bothered by that comparison.

Either way, that was a smart decision. Not only was going to visit a pantheon way different than visiting a stray association, but the Norse were the ones reaching out to him, not the other way around. The entire situation wasn't helped by the fact that the Norse weren't precisely a small pantheon at that. They were at the top of things, there with the Greek and the Hindu.

Ravel couldn't in good conscience just let Joshua go unprepared.

"Oh, right. Before that," Joshua started when she was going to get started speaking and her mouth clicked shut. Then she saw him giving her a soft look that always made her feel uncomfortable, but in a good way somehow. "Did things go well with whatever you had to do with your family?" he asked and she had to pause for a second to consider what to say.

Because she had a feeling that Joshua wouldn't like the fact that she was kind of going behind his back to negotiate her family into giving him more access to their bloodline. In her defense, he was already like halfway done with it, so they might as well try and benefit from giving him the rest of it and try to get some profit out of it. Riser wasn't too happy with her at the moment, but then again, he hadn't been for a while.

The rest of her family was at the very least considering it, Ravel knew for a fact, and there might be one or two that were actually somewhat on board.

She could work with that.

However…

"Some things happened and I'm trying to help them decide what to do in regards to that," she said vaguely, hoping against hope that Joshua wouldn't ask further. He seemed to stay away from topics around her family unless he thought he needed to ask, like at that moment, so maybe…

"Well, things should be fine then," he commented, easily letting her get off of that awkward situation. "You're good at doing that sort of thing, after all," he said and she gulped, taking in the proud look on his face.

Yes, she was definitely getting her family to agree with her idea.


[}-o-{]
​

[Gabriel]

She waited patiently, bringing a cup of tea to her lips and taking a sip.

She could see why Joshua enjoyed it so much. The right blend, prepared well, could be just what one needed to calm down, relax. Not that Gabriel needed that kind of thing at the moment, since things were going well. Ophis seemed to have been pacified and Joshua was likely to bring an entirely better era to her faction after the revelation they'd had. He was also making progress in regards to Valerie and other projects of his that were bound to help in many ways. Khaos was even facing setbacks that helped them plenty.

She was also rather relieved that Michael and Raphael didn't think Joshua was their father coming back to life. That'd have made things rather awkward. They weren't ruling out some kind of reincarnation business though, either with their father or their brother, but she'd cross that bridge when she came to it. Besides, they did have one theory that made things less of a mess, and she was clinging to that one with both metaphorical hands.

The point was that Gabriel was pretty sure things were going well and she was not complaining. That said, there was one minor thorn on their side and they might as well try to do something about it, they'd decided. Well, Serafall, Yasaka and her had decided that, just to keep the ball rolling, as it were. Joshua could use a little less stress in his life, so they'd decided to try and help out without involving him. He was juggling enough plates and they knew he'd rather not have to deal with any of that.

Silently, without a greeting or so much as a word, a woman moved to sit across the table from her.

"Good morning," Gabriel said with a slight smile. "Feel free to order whatever you want. They make great tea here though, so I'd recommend that," she commented idly. Maybe it was a little mean of her to feel vindicated when the woman squirmed the smallest bit on her chair.

"I'd rather get this conversation going. What do you want, Gabriel?" she asked and Gabriel nodded, setting down her cup. She regarded her appointment for a long moment all the same, however. Once, she'd envied them all the smallest bit. They had all the freedom in the world, after all. Now though, they might finally get to have a measure of that, once Michael and Raphael hammered out the plans to ease their restrictions.

The war was long over, after all.

There was no need to be trapped under those measures anymore.

"I want to help you, Penemue, what else?" she asked and if she smiled a little wider when the fallen angel shivered, it wasn't for any particular reason. "Don't you want things to get better? Don't you want your faction to regain some of the standing it has lost? Don't you want your fellow fallen to be stronger? Safer?"

"You've been spending too much time with the devils, Gabriel," Penemue told her, and it was supposed to be an insult… Instead, the fallen looked somewhere between wary and tempted. That was good enough for Gabriel.

"That's not a no," she pointed out with a smile. "I only want to help you, Penemue. I truly do. I give you my word," she emphasized and the fallen straightened where she sat. It might be a bit of a myth that angels couldn't lie, but it was definitely true that there was a limit to how much they could get away with, same as it happened with the Sins. Penemue knew the significance of what Gabriel had just said, so…

"What do you even want to do?" Penemue asked after a while and Gabriel supposed that was a small victory all on its own. They hadn't gotten to the hard part yet though, admittedly. "We're already working together."

"Are we though?" she asked, raising a skeptical eyebrow and staring at the fallen across from her. "We have meetings and we share bits of information. When was the last time our faction actually worked together?"

"It's not like we've tried. There hasn't been any need for that," Penemue pointed out, and it was kind of sad how hard she was trying. Gabriel didn't deign that with an explanation or a response of any kind. She just stayed silent, bringing her tea back to her lips. "Gabriel, please, I-"

"You're limited in what you can do," she interrupted, a slight smile on her face, even if it was a somewhat sad, pitying one. "Your hands are tied. That's what I can offer you. What we can offer you," she said and immediately, Penemue stiffened. She was a smart woman, after all, even if people tended to just think of her as Azazel's or Grigori's secretary. She had her fingers in almost every pie in her faction, after all. "We can offer you the freedom and the support you need to do more."

"You want me to rebel. You want me to start a coup in Grigori," Penemue asked, hissed more like. She pulled back, looking deeply offended and angry. That was about what Gabriel had expected though, so she kept her calm.

"Those are strong words," she commented, refraining from pointing out the obvious. It wouldn't be very different from what they'd done with Heaven, back in the day, really. But that had been so long in the past and Gabriel had things to deal with in the present. She could address that when they had time for it. "We don't care if you overthrow Azazel or continue to work for him, support him. We want to make you, to make Grigori, an actual ally, rather than a somewhat helpful neutral party. Azazel won't be a possibility for that anymore, not as things stand, and that's evident, so…"

She trailed off as she saw the fallen flinch, but she didn't point that out. It was truly sad to see her struggling so much, just as it was annoying to see Azazel continue to be as he'd always been. Too smart for his own good, and somehow still not smart enough when it counted. Too proud of his own genius to see past his own mind, his own ideas, and consider that there might be more to things than what he knew and what he considered.

Pride, for her brother, had come before, during and after his fall.

"So you want me to go against what my leader wants and help you."

"Against your leader, maybe, but in favor of your faction," Gabriel pointed out and there was the crux of the matter. Because Azazel was no longer just being annoying and a nuisance to them. He was hindering his own faction by that point. Would Penemue stand for that, like a faithful servant or…?

"What did you have in mind, exactly?" the woman across the table from her asked, eyes narrowed.

Apparently, Penemue was as smart as they'd assumed… and hoped.

Gabriel smiled.


[}-o-{]
​

[Serafall Leviathan]

"So, how awful is this going to be for me?" Joshua asked and Serafall smiled. For one, because he looked great in formal attire and she'd stand by that opinion forever. For another, because it was always nice to have the chance to go out with her partner. For a third…

"Absolutely," she replied, somewhat amused, but mostly pitying Joshua. He really was going to have a hard time, after all. The Norse were a warrior faction through and through, even if they'd calmed down quite a lot from how they'd once been. They were still the opposite of someone like Joshua, who liked his calm and peace. They were boisterous and noisy and he'd hate them for it all.

"Great," Joshua said sarcastically before sighing and running his fingers through his hair to calm himself down. It also had the opposite effect on Serafall herself, but she reigned that in. It wasn't the time. Maybe after the party. "I was hoping you'd have a different answer than Ravel."

"Unfortunately not," she told him, somewhat apologetic.

"It is what it is," he waved off wearily. "Speaking of Ravel, I was talking to her about getting her some help for her job. I'm really starting to feel bad about how much I'm piling on that child," he commented and Serafall beamed at him.

"Need me to get you another secretary?" she said and she'd have made a secretary joke of some kind, maybe, if not for Ravel being so young and how Joshua would take that. Maybe the next one would allow her to say that kind of thing. She imagined Joshua's reactions would be hilarious.

Food for thought.

"I mean, I asked her and she said she'd look for someone, but…"

"But she's a rather greedy little devil," Serafall finished with a giggle and Joshua smiled wryly at her.

"That's one way to put it."

"I'll make a list and talk it through with her if you think she's avoiding things and making excuses," Serafall offered, skipping around Joshua for one last check to make sure his outfit was fine. Which she knew it was, she just wanted an excuse herself to look at her partner very thoroughly.

"Thanks," he replied, stretching as if to get rid of the awkwardness that was no doubt building inside him. It probably hadn't worked, but Serafall would do her best to make the night bearable for him as best she could. And she did have a trick or three that she could pull to help with that, she knew. The Norse wouldn't even be able to mind them too much, since they so obviously wanted a piece of Joshua for… reasons that remained unknown.

There were a lot of reasons why someone could want her partner, after all.

"Don't mention it," she said, beaming at him. "So… you ready?"

"As I'll ever be," Joshua mumbled like he was resigning himself to his death or something like that. Serafall approved of the dramatics, even if it also made her a little sad. It was a shame that he had to deal with that kind of situation, and it was even more of one that Serafall – and Yasaka and Gabriel, to be fair – would all likely end up dragging him into similar situations in the future too, just because of who they were.

Joshua would never just let them keep him away from that, after all, because he'd feel like he wasn't putting his all into their relationships. It was a very endearing part of him, even if it made Serafall pity him a little bit because of how much it worked against him. All the same, she wasn't about to make it a problem. Instead, she'd just have to make sure it was all worth it for him and she had many ideas for that.

For the moment…

"Alright, we can go now then. No need to keep your adoring fans waiting," she commented and he groaned. All the same, he squared his shoulders and nodded, going along with her teleportation spell. Soon enough, they found themselves in a large and plenty gaudy hall where the party was going to be held. It was already almost filled up, except for those people that wanted to be "fashionably late", as it were.

Not like Serafall could talk, since they were also late, but some people really pushed for that.

Almost immediately, several of the people around turned towards them. Not only because they were the latest arrival, but also because of Joshua and his strange-feeling magic. Not every day someone got a sense of infinite magic reserves, Serafall would admit. She couldn't fault them, but she hated the way Joshua's expression closed off under the attention. It was like he became a completely different person just to deal with that.

"Joshua," a voice greeted and Serafall's feelings took another swift shift when her partner's expression softened. "Satan Leviathan. It seems I'll be the first to welcome you."

"Göndul," Joshua greeted, almost friendly despite everything. So, just for that, Serafall found herself thankful for the woman's arrival. She'd heard plenty about the retired valkyrie, but it was good to see her. If only because she helped Joshua ease into things with someone that he was familiar with and who he could talk about topics that he liked. "So good to see you."

All in all, off to a great start, Serafall would say.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,485
My Heart, It Never Gets Tired

[Serafall Leviathan]

So, things got out of hand very quickly.

"The poor man didn't know what he was getting into, did he?" the goddess that was sitting next to her commented, sounding very amused. "People often forget that we're a pantheon deeply connected to magic," Freyja added and Serafall could only nod. She hadn't forgotten, but she'd evidently underestimated the range of things. Not only that, but she'd underestimated Joshua's progress when it came to using Runes.

"Fortunate that he seems too focused on the magic to realize things, isn't it?" the god beside Freyja, Óðr, pointed out and that was true enough too. Talking magic was something Joshua could do for as long as anyone would listen and encourage him. And the Norse certainly could do both of those things, by the looks of it.

Serafall was more than a little taken aback, she'd admit.

She thought she'd have to carry the two of them through the entire gathering and she'd been more than willing to do so. It was always nice to be able to help someone she loved, for one. All in all though, she thought she could be excused for feeling a little confused and taken aback. She wasn't upset that Joshua didn't seem to need her, not really, but there was an awkward feeling in her, like a tiny part of her was disappointed or frustrated or something like that.

It was an odd feeling, that was for sure.

"I'm not complaining," Serafall said all the same, a slight smile on her face. "It's nice to see Joshua doing well," she added, feeling rather proud as she saw her man carry a conversation with several deities at the same time with ease and confidence. He seemed engaged, interested. He wasn't losing himself to his thoughts, or drawing away in nerves and hesitation.

Yasaka and Gabriel would be so relieved when they heard he did great.

Ravel might be a little put off by the fact that all her tutoring had mostly been for nothing though.

"It's always nice to see our loved ones do well," Freyja agreed, some mirth in her voice, but Serafall simply nodded with a smile. That seemed to please the goddess a great deal, but then again, she was a goddess of love. Married to Óðr who was a god of desire and passion to boot, so Serafall was counting her domains doubly so. "You seem to get along rather well," the goddess pointed out then and Serafall could almost hear a hidden tone there.

Almost like she wanted to add a "despite" follow up part at the end, although she couldn't fathom what would be said.

"We do," Serafall said all the same, and she tried not to let an edge bleed into her voice. She was even pretty sure she succeeded. Either way, Norse or not, big pantheon or not, she wasn't going to let anyone say anything about her relationship with Joshua. "He calms me down and I help him live a little," she oversimplified with a smile.

"It shows," Óðr replied, bringing her attention back to him. "Speaking of showing though," the god added and Serafall turned once more, this time towards Joshua, who seemed to have broken away from the conversation he'd been holding with several deities to approach them. "The man of the hour himself," Óðr greeted cheerfully and Serafall saw Joshua's shields come back up immediately, as if preparing himself for a conversation he didn't want to have.

That was more what Serafall had expected going in.

"Óðr, a pleasure to meet you," Joshua said, recognizing the god immediately. A lot could be said about her man, but Serafall knew that information was what he craved more than anything. True to the magician's ways, Joshua believed in being prepared for everything. The less confident he was, the more he prepared. And considering how badly he dealt with situations such as gatherings – political gatherings at that –, it was no surprise that he'd prepared a lot for that event.

He probably knew more about the Norse pantheon than Serafall did, truth be told, even if he couldn't use that information nearly as well as she could have.

"And you must be Freyja," Joshua added, turning towards the goddess and giving the same polite smile he gave everyone that night. Something that both deities noticed. Serafall was hardly surprised that they were surprised by that though. Freyja was a goddess of beauty too, so she was probably used to more… particular reactions from people meeting her, especially for a first meeting.

Little did she know, Joshua's mind was too worried about the social setting to bother processing how beautiful she was. Serafall would know, Yasaka, Gabriel and her had suffered because of that for quite a while. Frustrating as that had been, it was also a bit of a relief, really, to know that Joshua's eyes wouldn't stray no matter what, even with how much attention he attracted. Hell, the only reason he'd even looked at Gabriel was because Serafall and Yasaka had brought that up themselves.

Something that she tried to bring up as much as possible when around the angel.

Just because.

"You looked like you were having fun," Serafall commented after her partner and the two deities by her side exchanged greetings. Joshua's smile alone made her feel like she'd succeeded in life just with those words.

"I was. Everyone has very interesting takes on magic, how they cast, how they sense, how they think about it," Joshua replied with a wide grin, looking so exceedingly excited that Serafall herself almost wanted to hear about it… And she might even have asked him to actually tell her. However, she didn't get the chance. "But I wanted to come and spend some time with you. I'm supposed to be your plus one, aren't I?" he added, and the half-shy half-eager grin he directed at her made her want to kiss him.

And she did.

"Always nice to know when I manage to do well," Joshua said afterwards, looking very pleased with himself. He was so unfair. But alas, they were there to talk with the Norse, not flirt and kiss each other.

A shame, really.

At least Freyja and Óðr didn't seem to mind the attention they were throwing at each other too much.


[}-o-{]
​

[Yasaka]

"Well, I'm glad to see things went well," she commented, fairly amused, after getting a downright excited recount of what happened during the gathering that Serafall and Joshua had been invited to. By the man himself, no less. After the days she'd spent seeing and hearing about how worried or downright apprehensive he felt in regards to that, it was nice to see that things had gone about as opposite to how the man thought they would go as they could.

"So, you had fun?" Kunou asked, seeming almost shocked by that turn of events. Not that Yasaka blamed her, but it just made the entire situation even more entertaining. "How?" the girl added, a little wide-eyed as she regarded her father like she couldn't figure out how him and having fun at a party could mix together well.

"I mean, nobody seemed to mind talking magic with me," Joshua commented, like he was surprised by that fact himself. "No one even brought up politics or agendas or much of anything else, really," he added, almost childishly delighted by that. Gabriel giggled by Yasaka's side and she felt her lips twitch up.

"They totally did though," Serafall whispered to them behind her hand as Joshua continued talking with Kunou. "They were just very discreet about it. Mostly seemed to want to see how Joshua thinks, feeling him out," the Satan explained to them and both Gabriel and Yasaka focused intently on what she was saying. "Seems a little over the top that they did all that just to check, but there they are. And thankfully Loki wasn't there…"

Fortunate, but suspicious.

"The only one not there?" Gabriel asked, likely thinking along the same lines as Yasaka herself was. Did the Norse already suspect something was going on with Loki? That'd confirm Joshua's suspicions, which they were already inclined to believe, but considering how little solid proof he seemed to have for his theories…

There was more to Joshua than met the eye, but then again, they'd all already known that from the beginning.

"The only one, besides some rather minor and troublesome deities that they probably kept away so that they wouldn't cause trouble," Serafall explained and Yasaka could think of several ones that'd fit that criteria. There was a chance that Loki was also kept away for a similar reason, but as a major god of his pantheon… it stood out all the same. "I didn't notice anything suspicious about anyone, but then again, they were very subtle and mostly seemed to want to give Joshua a good impression. I'm pretty sure they want to join us."

"You guys know I can hear you, right?" a new voice asked, and all three of them turned to see Joshua still talking with Kunou, recounting some magic trick that a goddess had shown off to him and how they could apply that to the flying game Yasaka's daughter was tinkering in her free time… and when she should be doing her homework. All the same, they could hear his voice whispering to him as if he were by their side. "I'm a little disappointed to hear that they were actually still politicking, but I didn't have a horrible time, so it's whatever," the man communicated to them and Yasaka smiled fondly. "Anything I should know right now? I'm gonna take Kunou to the garden for a bit if not."

"Nothing we can't tell you afterwards, like I was already planning to," Serafall replied, and there was a bit of a pout on her voice… and on her expression even. Yasaka sometimes envied her the freedom of expression that she had. Although, on the other hand, it seemed as much an act as her own carefully maintained expression, so was it really freedom in that case?

"Great. If you need me, just call," he told them before both him and Kunou stood up and left the room with only a few words directed at them and a wave of their hands. Yasaka took a moment to look at the two of them walking side by side, like it was the most natural thing in the world. She watched how Joshua smiled down at Kunou and patted her head. She watched how her daughter beamed up at him, hopping excitedly as they moved.

It never failed to bring her mood up and make her love both of them all the more.

"So, that's more or less how things went on my side," Serafall commented, leaning back and looking at the two of them curiously. "How did things go with Penemue?" she added, focusing mainly on Gabriel. Yasaka had already received the "report" on that herself, so she picked up her cup of tea and simply decided to wait for Serafall to be up to speed.

"Went rather well, all things considered. She won't backstab Azazel, of course,-" Of course, she said, as if the three of them hadn't hoped for that. Yasaka guessed they had been asking for too much in that regard, but still. Such a shame. "-but she's open to work with us." That would have to be enough for them, Yasaka supposed. Not ideal, but still more than they'd feared. "Provided we can hold up on our end of the offer, she won't mind coordinating with us to some extent, even if it's behind Azazel's back."

Pretty good deal for something that Joshua wouldn't mind doing at all. He already kind of felt bad for the general populace of Grigori. So, giving them more wings to somewhat match what he was doing for Heaven would be no issue at all. He might have even done that himself, really. So, in a way, they were getting a much better ally out of Grigori for basically nothing.

That was a great deal, if Yasaka had ever seen one.

"On important matters, however," she started, getting the attention of both Serafall and Gabriel. "No one we need to worry about from the Norse, right?" she asked, and the angel immediately turned towards the devil.

"You mean, other than half the goddesses and Göndul trying to throw her daughter at Joshua?" Serafall answered dryly. Yasaka should have seen that coming. She had seen that coming, really. She'd just decided to be hopeful all the same. She should have known it was useless.

All three of them shared a suffering sigh between themselves.


[}-o-{]
​

[Kunou Davis]

"Fun, right?" her dad asked and she stared at him and then at the cloud of smoke/ashes that he was illusioning around them to demonstrate what this one goddess had inspired in the party Serafall and him went to. While she was already a little skeptical just because it had been a goddess that was talking to him and in a little too friendly a manner for Kunou's liking, there was also the fact that…

"Sounds miserable," she replied, looking at the display warily.

The idea was that there could be mist or smoke or something else obscuring sight in the obstacle course they'd fly through. Not only that, but to further complicate matters, there'd be fake environments showing up inside those clouds. So, they'd have to know by heart how the course looked without the cloud and not get fooled by any of that.

Which was likely going to be plenty fun once one of the others fell for one or three of the tricks. It'd be less fun when it was her smacking against a wall or something else. Still, the idea was interesting, so she had to at least consider it. Besides, her dad was so excited showing it off that she didn't want to just turn it away.

"Well, maybe you can leave it for a higher difficulty kind of thing," Joshua commented, reading her somewhat, his enthusiasm dimming a little bit. Kunou felt bad just seeing that, but he didn't seem too bothered by the unspoken rejection. Still- "Well, we can tinker with the idea or drop it entirely if we don't think it's good. No issues," he added, his grin coming back a little as he ruffled her hair.

She'd long since given up complaining about it, but it was still grating.

Doubly so because it was somehow really nice while being frustrating.

"... I guess," she mumbled, considering what he said. "Do we have to call Koneko and Ravel to talk about this?"

"Are they around?" her dad asked, raising an eyebrow.

"Koneko hasn't dropped by, I think she said her peerage was training today. And Ravel was checking on someone that might help her with her job." And if the Phenex was smart, she'd pick a boy or a man, because they really didn't need more women in Joshua's life… or more girls.

She liked having a big family and all, but even that had its limits.

"Then it's fine. It can be just the two of us. Morag is having fun with… Kuroka," Joshua told her, his eyes going a little off as he checked on his familiars with their bond. "So, like old times, eh?" he asked with a smile and she smiled right back, happy to hear that.

She understood that Joshua had more people in his life than when they'd met, and she understood that he was busy with a lot of things too, but that didn't mean she wasn't going to miss him when he couldn't be with her. However, that also meant it was all the more important whenever he took time to just be with her. Like at that very moment, Kunou was incredibly happy to spend some time just doing stuff with her dad.

"... So, an easier take on this would be to make the illusion surfaces solid, but shifting every so often. Make a part of the course that shifts constantly, basically. Or maybe it can shift at will when you do something, to mess with those racing behind you or something," Joshua brainstormed and Kunou couldn't help but stare at him. She heard him, but her mind wasn't really processing that. She was a little busy noticing the difference in her life from back before Joshua.

She did that at times, but it was usually when she was by herself, doing homework or tinkering or just in bed before sleeping.

Once, she'd been alone, surrounded only by servants and her mother, who couldn't be there much. And then, Joshua appeared, and now Kunou had a father, sisters, aunts, friends and so many more people. There wasn't a single day when she felt lonely anymore. Sure, she'd like her dad to be around more, but it wasn't like he was never there, and her mother was around more often than before too. Kunou even had other people to make things better for her when neither could be there.

And she couldn't quite believe it, sometimes.

"Something the matter?" Joshua asked, poking her forehead with his finger. He seemed amused by the fact that she'd gotten lost in thought, which she thought was hypocritical of him. "I'm the one that's supposed to get lost in his mind, aren't I?"

"I can do that too," she muttered, giving him a fake pout. "Learned from the best," she added with a shy, teasing smile that got a chuckle out of him.

"You didn't get that from me and I have a feeling that's not from your mother either," he commented. "Serafall is a terrible influence."

"I don't know what you're talking about," she denied, looking away and at her notes. "I like that idea though."

"Which one?" Joshua asked and she paused for a long moment. "You don't remember what the idea was, right?"

"... I don't, but I remember that I liked it," she answered and even she knew how silly that sounded, but she stood by what she said. No matter how amused Joshua looked.

Although, she could do without the teasing that followed.


[}-o-{]
​

[Joshua Davis]

"So, I was thinking, we have to work on your control of the mist," he commented, looking as Georg trained his Dimension Lost usage. "You should be able to have complete control over stuff inside it, but you don't. We'll get you there. First of all, let's have you move around all this stuff," he said, waving his hand vaguely towards the arrangement of swords made by Jeanne and other random objects like boxes, pieces of furniture and smaller trinkets. "I want you to arrange them in shapes. We can get more specific with it once you can consistently do the switching quickly."

"Understood," the hero descendant replied stiffly. He wasn't going to change that in a while, Joshua could already tell, but he wasn't too inclined to put effort into helping him do so either. Georg wasn't a friend, not really. He wasn't even approaching such a category, unlike Raynare or Kuroka. He might get there at some point, but by then Joshua would have gotten used to him and that'd be that.

It was what had happened with the aforementioned two, after all.

Joshua didn't see that as a bad thing. He didn't know if he wanted to be friends with such people. He could forgive them, he could even trust them, but he felt like friendship was… not the right word for it. Then again, he wasn't an expert in relationships of any kind, so maybe he was just wrong about something and that was that.

"What about us~?" Kuroka asked, peeking from behind him on his right like a little child. On his other side, Raynare stepped up to stand beside him. She seemed to be studying Georg's training herself, probably trying to figure out how to best fight the guy if it came to it, be it sparring or some other less pleasant situation.

He respected that, truly.

"Hmmm, I feel like I always pit you against my familiars or Kokabiel, but they are busy with each other now," Joshua commented, glancing to the side to watch those fighting. Although, maybe that was a generous way to put the smackdown that the fallen angel was getting from his familiars. In the guy's defense, Friday was kind of unfair, since she didn't have a body that the guy could even do anything to.

Joshua still said nothing though, because even if he wasn't actively testing stuff on the guy or keeping him in the dungeons, he was still not forgiven.

"You can practice against each other though," Joshua commented, turning his attention back towards Raynare and Kuroka. "Now that I think about it, I don't make you two spar all that often…" he added thoughtfully, narrowing his eyes. That was a bit of an oversight, he supposed.

It'd be good for both of them. Raynare was straightforward power while Kuroka was overwhelming tricks. In a way, they took the classification of power-based and technique-based combatants to the extremes. Technically, Kuroka should have the edge there, but Raynare might just have enough power – and be resourceful enough with Incinerate Anthem – to pull off a victory. The fallen was also way more determined than the nekoshou, so…

"Have fun," he added after a moment in which the two woman stared at each other, considering their options. They started immediately after he said that though, but he turned his attention back to Georg, watching him go through set configurations of the items one after the other. He wasn't being particularly fast, but the point of the exercise was for him to get better, so it was fine.

With all that done, he looked around and saw that everyone was working on something and he could just… go do something else.

So, he did.

'Give me a call if anyone needs me,' he told Friday, who replied by turning her full attention away from Kokabiel and towards him.

"Yes…" she said, her voice all sorts of distorted, but she was getting better at it all the same. "Daddy," she added, and he took that back. Maybe she was getting a lot better than he thought, because she managed to sound almost normal, definitely sweet, at that moment. He smiled, sending her pride and happiness in equal measure, which made some of the lights around the training area flare up a little bit.

She was an adorable little living spell like that.

'Have fun, Friday.'

"I will," she replied earnestly.

Adorable, way too adorable.

All the same, he had to put a damper on things by moving on to work on something rather unpleasant. Alas, the lengths he went to in order to get stronger and prepare for Khaos Brigade. There was little he wouldn't do for the sake of that battle, after all, even then, when things seemed to be going rather well. He wasn't going to rest on his laurels.

"Hey there," he greeted, walking in and looking at the two cells. They were a lot more… nice than they'd once been, but they were still definitely cells. He wasn't going to afford those two any more accommodations unless they showed him something to change his mind, which they hadn't, not really.

"Good day… or night, Mr. Davis."

Katerea's shift in attitude almost gave him whiplash, Joshua would admit. Although, it made sense. She was acting, after all, and he could see right through it. He wasn't complaining. He'd rather her lie through her teeth and make his job easier than be a general pain in the ass to deal with… like Shalba.

"Already back?" the devil grumbled, apparently trying to show off why Katerea was getting better meals than him.

It was funny though, the Beelzebub devil's bloodline was probably the one that Joshua thought would be the most useful to study. Not to say that the Leviathan was bad, but he already had plenty of ideas of how to apply the Power of Swarm, as opposed to the half-baked Power of Sea that Katerea had.

All the same, both of them would be helping him.

So, Joshua just smiled before getting started.


[} Chapter End {]

Eh, some parts of this are a little rough.

And I'll admit, I thought the Norse meeting would go way differently. But then I started taking a deeper look into it, and like, every deity I came across had some sort of connection to magic. So, I thought it sounded like an interesting thing to apply, that it's some kind of mix of pantheon and magician association, which is right up Joshua's alley.

Funny how that works.

Also, yes, that probably doesn't quite cover some of the things you guys might be unhappy with, like the lack of Odin, as an example. As I said in this chapter, this was just the Norse taking a chance to look at Joshua up close and see what he's about. This isn't some grand recruitment attempt or some summon for him to do something for them or anything like that.

Hope that's clear, and I apologize if you were expecting something bigger than we got.

#1,499
I Hope You Find What You're Looking For

[Joshua Davis]

He was not a fan of the new development in his search for data on devil bloodlines.

Or, more precisely, he wasn't a fan of having to work with Zekram Bael.

Normally, he'd have tried to stay far away from the man. Unfortunately, he didn't have that choice, because the man refused to let him study anyone else – like, say, the much more friendly Gremory siblings – other than the man himself. In his words "if the heir to his House was going to have a Power of Destruction, it'd be his" and Joshua… found himself slightly exasperated.

It was also odd, if anyone asked him. Because Sirzechs was known to be a monster of a Power of Destruction user. The Satan was openly regarded as a Super Devil, an anomaly of the race that put him in a league of his own almost as soon as he started applying himself and his strength. Why would Zekram not want to "steal" some of that for his heir?

The answer was Pride, or so Joshua guessed.

Because if there was one Sin that could be applied to Zekram Bael, that was pride. He didn't seem to resent the Gremory, but he did seem to have a certain disregard for them. Joshua couldn't pretend to understand how the devil's mind worked, but he found himself oddly fascinated by the thought process. Despite how odd it was, there was a certain… respectable nature to it.

The man was proud, of himself and of his family, his House, and Joshua knew a little about that kind of thing, he supposed.

"Do you have what you need?" the devil in question asked and he found himself surprised to notice a certain note of… deference, in a way. Or maybe it was just the fact that there was no impatience or edge to his words. He was genuinely asking, out of curiosity or something along those lines.

He'd been surprisingly nice and accommodating.

It was odd.

"If you could use it in different forms and shapes, that kind of thing, please," Joshua answered as professionally as he could and the devil started doing just that. He wasn't only analyzing the mass of destruction given presence and structure that the man was moving around though, no. He was also keeping a close eye on the devil himself, trying to find out what made things click in his own body, how it allowed him to manipulate the Power of Destruction.

Because Joshua was realizing that it was a blend of everything mixed together that made those do their thing. The bloodlines were intertwined in their essence, their magic and their soul, all that made them who they were. It was like the roots of a tree, spreading inside dirt, but also around rocks and into a water stream.

It was everywhere, and all of it did something to make the Power happen.

It was fascinating.

"Can you let it go and recast it a few times over and over? That part is one of the most complex," he asked eventually and the devil complied without so much as a word. It was really making him feel like something was wrong in the world, truly, but he was also having a great time analyzing the power.

It'd been something that he'd always been curious about, but also hadn't quite dared to look into. He knew it'd have been trouble, after all. Who'd have thought Zekram – his biggest fear on the matter – would be the one to offer and help him study the bloodline? Certainly not Joshua, but he wasn't complaining.

He was just very confused.

All the same though, he didn't quite have the time to go into that thought, he could do that once he went back home. He was much more interested in looking at what the devil was doing and how it was happening. The activation of the bloodline was something spectacular, truly, and he meant that in regards to every bloodline. All of them seemed to be unique too, which only made it all the more interesting to look at.

It rippled through the devils in a way that was almost worrying, like those roots that spread everywhere, came alive, twisting and turning to manifest a concept rather than an ability. It was no wonder the bloodlines were named as they were. Sure, they seemed to lean more or less towards certain things, but they were, at their cores, very conceptual when it came down to it.

And that was… Joshua didn't even think he had a proper word to explain it.

"Something the matter?" Zekram asked at some point, when Joshua was probably a little too awed in his appreciation of the power. It was something to behold though, truly, and maybe the Power of Destruction most of all. Not only in itself, but also in what Joshua could do with it. Because he had gotten a bunch of ideas for the Silence projects, which would be great, since he had started to make next to no progress there after a while.

"It's no wonder you're so proud of your bloodline," Joshua said, since he didn't expect the devil to have a problem with that. Expectedly, the Bael seemed rather pleased with himself instead. "It's a wonder, truly."

"I knew you were smart," Zekram replied with a very smug expression on his face. Joshua almost regretted his comment just looking at it, really. However… 'I mean, I know some of what he's done, but… he hasn't been too bad, right?' he realized at that moment, blinking to himself.

That was so odd to think about. Because Zekram had really just been neutral and even good to him, despite what he could – and had, admittedly – have expected. Joshua didn't know what to do with that realization, if he were honest.

Thus, he just pushed it aside.

"Alright, I'll cast a few new spells, we'll repeat some of what we've done and I think that can be that for the day. I'll need to go over what I learned," he said and the devil's expression cleared into something that could be called professional before he nodded. And that was that.

So incredibly odd.

But maybe not bad.


[}-o-{]
​

[George Pickingill]

For the most part, despite everything, he'd enjoyed some time of peace.

Sure, Davis had thrown him a few curve balls here and there, but at least he'd never been alone while it happened. George had at least suffered together with his fellow Stars. That was, he knew, much better than being singled out, like Levi or Meredith. Dion had been called the other day for something relating a similar branch of magic to her own. And Karin was friends with Morag, somehow, and she helped Davis with the garden at his house, which had ended up with her being friends with an Asia girl that George hadn't met yet but felt like he had just from all that he'd heard about her.

George was fine being the normal one though.

He'd been the special one before, back when his professor had needed help with that healing spell. With that no longer being the case though, he hadn't had much else to stand out for and he was grateful for that. He didn't want to know what'd happen if attention went back to him. His family still wouldn't let it go after the defense update Davis had given them.

He was kind of scared of what his mother would do if she met the man, truthfully.

Or what his father would let her do, for that matter.

So, yes, George was fine with some peace.

"George, can you stay behind?" Davis said at the end of a class and he felt his face paling immediately. He did not like the pitying looks the rest of the Stars were sending him. Nor did he appreciate the amusement Imhotep was feeding him through their connection.

Maybe he'd jinxed himself with just his thoughts.

"Did you need me for something, Professor Davis?" he asked, glancing at the door where the last of his fellow students left. He could feel their eyes on him, and he knew they envied him. He understood, really, he did. But he also knew that he kind of envied them too.

He didn't miss life before Davis appeared in it, not at all, but he did miss the times when he wasn't agonizing over how to repay his debts.

"I need your help," his teacher said and normally that'd have been great news. Something to do for him was great, since that meant doing something in regards to his debt, no matter how impossible it already was to settle. However, he knew by then – and the rest of the Stars did too – that there was no way Davis wouldn't do something to worsen their debt situation after they did whatever it was that he needed.

He was a cruel, cruel man like that.

"I need to discuss some concepts in regards to your spells," Davis said and George felt the gears shift in his head. That wasn't the time to be feeling sorry for himself. "Not the spells themselves, or what they do, but how they do it."

That was… an interesting topic.

Not what people usually wanted to talk about in regards to his magic branch – or any other, really –, but he wasn't really surprised. Professor Davis had a way to just ask or be interested in the weirdest things. Considering that, the mechanisms of George's Recovery Magic were rather normal, all things considered.

"Anything in particular you'd want to know, Professor?" George asked, nodding and whispering a thank you when the professor placed a chair for him to sit across his desk. Idly, he wondered what crazy thing he was working on, because he was very much aware that Joshua Davis never asked for help in regards to small stuff. No, if it were small, he wouldn't ask, he'd just work on it himself.

That was what George and the rest of the Stars had put together.

"Well, a few things, but I'm sure you can think of more yourself," Davis started with.

What followed was a rather long exchange in which George did his best to add some insights he had after years of using his branch that Davis didn't have from – rather intensive, admittedly – sensing and spell observation. How some of his spells encouraged natural or "natural" recovery, or how some of them helped mend what wouldn't otherwise do so, or how some others slowly ate away at curses and similar effects. There were a lot of details to share and a lot of "feelings" and "impressions" that he could add along the way, just to be as thorough as he could.

Imhotep even chimed in from time to time, helping George put into words things he'd never quite considered as he was then. Sometimes, the god even added some bits and pieces himself. Maybe it was presumptuous of him, but George thought the deity was rather eager to participate in the conversation. He even thought he might be right with that guess, judging by how the god went strangely silent after he had that thought.

Either way, the conversation went over all fairly well. Which was good, because his teacher seemed rather interested in those in particular, the small details. He couldn't figure out why, admittedly, but George supposed he didn't need to either.

They were, unsurprisingly, talking for a whole hour before he realized that no, they weren't going to be done anytime soon. He wasn't surprised by that fact, not really. However, he was a little nervous, because, after all…

"Um, Professor, I… I had a job scheduled soon," he commented, rubbing the back of his neck nervously. "Which is fine, by the way, I can stay. I just, I should at least call and-"

"No, no, it's fine," Davis interrupted, waving off his words as he leaned back and looked at the clock on the wall. "We've been here for a bit and I shouldn't expect your days to be free, I guess." He really shouldn't, considering they'd already had pretty full schedules without becoming his agents for the Egyptian Pantheon. George obviously didn't say that, but the point stood. "Ravel, can you make sure Agnes takes care of that. I think we're getting somewhere here," his professor said and the devil agreed rather easily before leaving through the door. "Now, let's continue for a bit longer, if you don't mind, George. I think this could help me out a lot," he was told.

And George for once entertained the notion that maybe he really was actually doing something in regards to his debt, no matter how small.

He'd still be skeptical about it though, because he could only be fooled so many times.

At least the conversation was fun.


[}-o-{]
​

[Aika Kiryuu]

"Hope the date went well," Joshua commented, leaning back on his chair with a smile. Beside him, Valerie was giggling at a small illusion that the man had no doubt cast. "You didn't give me many specifics, so I had to improvise a little."

"It was fun," she replied with a smile that she hoped did at least a passable job at telling the man that she was understating things so badly she wasn't sure how she could do worse. And yet, she didn't have other words, because everything felt like it'd fall short. "You said there'd be sea lions and penguins, but there were even whales and dolphins on the way. Did you know about those?"

"Nope. Guess you got lucky," he replied, casually. A little too casually. Well, there was also the fact that Aika had come prepared, with a spell in place to help her figure out the man more. So, he had set that up. She'd thought it was a little suspicious when even the guides were surprised by the animals they were seeing. "Funny how that works, right?"

"Yeah, very funny," she replied dryly, which didn't seem to phase the man at all. Not that she expected it to. So, with a sigh, Aika decided it was better to just let things be. Not like she was going to complain, but sometimes Joshua just complicated matters by being too blasé about things that certainly shouldn't be.

When he said he had a good spot for her to go on a date with Issei, she hadn't expected to be sent to the other side of the world. That was really goddamn far and the two of them had spent a good hour just coming to terms with that. Maybe they'd actually have to have a place in mind next time they asked Joshua for something.

Their extended date had gone spectacularly though.

"So, anything I should know before we start?" she added, glancing towards Valerie, who continued to be distracted by the illusion. She seemed particularly happy that day, which was saying something considering the state of the dhampir's mind. She really, really hoped they'd be able to help the girl, because it was so depressing to see her sometimes.

Aika had heard the phrase "husk of a person", but it was usually applied to people that were depressed, shut off, dead where they stood. She'd found in Valerie another way it could be applied, because she was all happiness and giggles and innocence, but there was just something about her that seemed off. Sure enough, she was incomplete, she was missing parts of herself, of her soul. A husk that had had taken away most of her, leaving only a child-like mind that couldn't even put together the issues of her own person.

It was, somehow, a worse thing to witness, in Aika's opinion.

"Not really, most new stuff I have is… Well, for my side of things, far as I know," Joshua answered, making her turn towards him. "We can start whenever you want. I've already started, actually," he added, but as he spoke, there was a pitying smile on his face directed not at Valerie but at Aika. She wanted to tell him she was fine, that she wasn't the one with a shredded soul.

She knew it wouldn't help.

"He worries for you, like a good pharaoh should worry for his people," Irer told her, sounding rather proud. Because apparently, the Egyptians were big on claiming the achievements of others. Not that Aika could talk, considering how huge a help having the god's blessing was for her magic and even some everyday things. Her regular sight had never been better. She could ditch the glasses any day if she so wanted. It just so happened that Issei liked them, so she was now using fake ones.

'I guess… it's just odd,' Aika thought to herself. She didn't remember the last time she'd had someone other than her parents worrying for her. It wasn't bad, not at all, and she knew it meant a lot to Issei, to have an adult that was a little more responsible than his parents were. She was just not used to it, she supposed.

"Ready whenever you are," Joshua said, snapping her out of her thoughts again and she nodded. Taking a deep breath in, she pulled out her notebook with circles and started casting. All the while, she felt her eyesight hone in even more than it already was those days, even time seemed to slow to a crawl so that she could take a better look at things. The spells almost talked to her too, telling her all that she wanted to know, and things she might not even have realized she needed, whispering not unlike Irer himself.

She looked, deeply as she could, into Valerie, reaching for her magic, which moved oddly, out of sorts, like a faucet that's broken or a fan that's shaky. The first glimpse at how torn the dhampir was, and that was before the soul. That was before she looked at the essence of the girl, frayed and burnt and rotten at the seams, like an eternally old ragdoll that kids had found any and all ways to use and break.

It made her sick, every single time she looked at Valerie's soul. Worse even was the fact that she was getting better, polishing and adapting her spells to see more. And the more she saw, the more twisted the pictures became. It was almost like she was torturing herself, but she owed Joshua and Valerie needed her, so Aika would endure.

She was going to save that girl, she swore.


[}-o-{]
​

[Meredith Ordinton]

"You seem… remarkably at ease," the woman beside her commented and she shrugged.

"Compared to a vampire war, this is fairly tame," she replied, her mind flashing back to that day. It'd been… a lot, but it'd also been oddly freeing. It wasn't often that Meredith got to feel so useful and also that she got to let loose like that. She'd never realized how much she craved a good fight.

She was no Jeanne, let alone Raynare, but Meredith had learned that day that she was a fighter through and through.

"I… see," the woman mumbled, clearly not seeing at all. "Joshua can never associate with normal people, can he?" she added and Meredith laughed. She had to, really. After all…

"I think I'm one of the normal ones," she told her, getting a confused blink in response before she continued. "And in my defense, it was Joshua that dragged me into that situation."

"That… makes sense, yes," the woman said. Griselda, Meredith was pretty sure her name was. She wasn't sure how likely it was that they'd work together again though. She didn't often bother learning people's names in jobs. Or, at least, she didn't try too hard to remember them once things were underway. Not much of a point.

Although, Joshua himself had set her up with that job with the Church, so maybe there was a chance for more encounters. 'Hm, yeah, I should try to remember her. Never know. She sounds like she knows Joshua,' Meredith mused to herself. She'd think about all that later though. As it was, they had a job to do.

"Either way," she continued, turning towards where someone was casting some sort of spell. Different from hers, and even the Norse runes she'd seen while around Joshua. The Church had its own system though, and she had no delusions about her chances of learning anything in regards to that, Alphecca Tyrant or not. "You sure you'll have the precise location today?" she asked.

They'd been set up to work together for a while already, with her offering a little extra force when hunting down Stray Exorcists and Devils. The Church was apparently a little short staffed, so they were… outsourcing some work. Griselda would be her handler for a while, until she proved "trustworthy" and then Meredith would be able to become a pseudo-exorcist, as it were. A mercenary doing exorcist work, basically.

Although, the woman had told her that it was all a formality.

Apparently, Joshua had the Church so far in his debt that they barely dared to set up that formality rather than just taking him up at his word. They were also all bending over backwards for her, not unlike how House of Water did. She'd caught one of the people that was more of a gofer actually tripping while trying to rush to get something to drink when she'd commented on it one of the other days she'd worked with them.

Meredith wasn't surprised, not really.

Because the answer to everything was rather simple: Joshua.

It was kind of funny how that explained everything.

"We should, yes," Griselda answered with a nod. She was a very no-nonsense person, Meredith had learned. She could respect that, truly. Although, maybe she'd gotten used to Joshua's more laidback approach or something, because it felt stifling at times, even though she knew she wouldn't have had a problem with that back in the day. "I was told that they were one or two scrying attempts away from finding that out," the woman added, with a tone and a look directed at the men casting the spell that said they better not have lied to her.

She almost felt bad for them.

Almost.

They would have been wasting her time too, after all. Time that she could have used practicing, or out on jobs that'd allow her to fight for real. Something that wasn't a great necessity for her, but it definitely was for the voice in her head.

Literally.

Sekhmet wasn't a great fan of just sitting at home doing nothing. She was a warrior goddess and it showed. She craved a battlefield, somewhere to prove herself, to show her might. Sometimes, Meredith would catch herself having dreams and daydreams about the fight during the vampire mess, except there'd be bits and pieces that had nothing to do with it, different fights, in a different time, with a different person fighting rather than her.

"We are the Pharaoh's weapon, the tool of his might brought to the world," the deity whispered and Meredith didn't disagree, but she did think the goddess was a little off her rocker. Which was rude, she knew, but still. She could do without the bloodthirsty whispers at the back of her head.

Maybe she'd ask Joshua to tune her down.

"The Pharaoh is a terrible influence on you, child."

'I'm the tool of his might, aren't I? I think being a little like him is fine,' she replied and she was fairly sure what followed was the emotional equivalent of a huff and turning away. That was amusing. Although, Sekhmet was likely not wrong. Joshua was a terrible influence if she could think and talk like that to a goddess.

"Yes, you should remember that you're not talking to some nobody like-"

Then again, it worked for him, and he was the Pharaoh, so it was probably fine.

"How did I get saddled with your absolute infuriating-?"

"They found the location," Griselda said and she was probably a little confused as to why Meredith was giggling.

She wasn't sure explaining that Sekhmet was throwing a tantrum in her head would help.


[} Chapter End {]
