#1,505
A Taste of Heaven

[Joshua Davis]

'Looks good,' he thought to himself with a nod as he laid out another set of spells around the room.

He'd already tested them – three times at that –, but Joshua could never quite shake the fear that he might cast something that'd ruin things and set Ophis off. It was a constant worry when trying to upgrade the Silence rooms, but nothing of the sort had happened yet. Closest he'd gotten was the dragon poking her head out of the room to tell him that she didn't like a new addition and then a few tense seconds of him trying to figure out why.

Joshua wasn't very sure what'd happened that time, but it'd been a fairly tame incident… Once he'd calm down and gone back home to get his thoughts in order. Because the whole time during the actual event had him feeling like he'd just disappear any second. The Dragon of Infinity was a nightmare for him that way.

'Now, the next set,' he decided, taking a deep breath in and steeling his nerves to keep going.

He'd gotten a bunch of ideas for those projects, after what felt like a long time of barely any progress. The Power of Destruction had given him plenty in regards to those, after all. It wasn't quite the same, but the devil bloodline and the Dimensional Gap had some similarities between them, and studying both had bridged the gap – 'That's a terrible pun.' – quite a bit and helped. He'd tried to apply the concept of destruction to create a space of nothingness, but that'd been…

Loud, according to Ophis.

That'd been what caused the aforementioned incident, after all.

There were still plenty to use all his notes from his research sessions with Zekram, but Joshua had had to approach the issue from a different angle. Not something new to him, but he'd have appreciated having a more straightforward time of it. No such luck, however. He was resigning himself to the fact that he'd never have an easy time with things.

"Good, right?" he asked Cheshire, who had been particularly clingy that day and had followed him there. He wasn't a fan, but he was growing a little less terrified of Ophis going off every day that passed. Which wasn't saying much, but it was enough that he was only freaking out a little bit while his familiar stuck to him.

He was going to have words with Friday for teleporting Cheshire with him though.

His feline familiar, however, rolled her eyes at him as if he were exaggerating… He didn't think he was, but… 'Cheshire will do as Cheshire wants,' he thought, taking a sip from the cup of tea he'd brought for himself. He had a history of caving to his familiars' whims, especially Cheshire's. So, Joshua guessed it was a bit of a stretch to think that'd change anytime soon.

Which lasted all of a few seconds after two things happened almost at the same time. The first was that there was a click sound coming from one of the room doors, the one where Ophis was in. The second was that Cheshire stiffened.

And then Cheshire was teleported away as fast as Joshua could manage.

The Infinity Dragons stepped out, face blank as always. Although, he caught her staring at the spot Cheshire had been in for a long second before her attention returned to him. Joshua, for his part, was already feeling cold sweat running down his back.

"Joshua Davis," the being said and he gulped.

"Ophis," he replied with a slight nod, unwilling to take his eyes off of her. "Was the last adjustment bad again?" he asked, and he was surprised that she didn't immediately answer. Instead, she stared at the cup in his hands for some reason. He was halfway through deciding to send it into a Storage Spell before the dragon opened her mouth and his attention was pulled fully onto her.

"No. The opposite," she told him and he blinked. "I like the new changes," she added and he had to take a moment to process that. Not only because it was incredibly good and relieving news, but also because that was the first time she went out of her way to tell him. That meant she either was getting more comfortable with him – which he didn't know how to feel about – or she was really happy with the change, which would be great.

Unfortunately, he wasn't sure how to ask, at least before the dragon spoke once more.

"I think I'll be staying here," Ophis said and he had to consider that for a long moment. Mostly because she was already spending most days there. Joshua was pretty sure he could count the times she'd left in one hand. And she didn't even leave for that long, really. "What is that?" she asked, eyes going back to his cup.

"Tea," he answered straightforwardly. "A drink, it's warm and soft and it helps me relax," he added… not entirely sure why. Sometimes he just felt like explaining a little more, just to avoid any potential misunderstandings… or just out of nerves, he supposed.

Maybe both.

"... Can I try?" she commented and he blinked at her again. He felt like he was doing that a lot. "I've seen you drink that a lot." 'Well, that's not worrying at all,' he thought to himself. Mainly because he'd only brought a cup with him to work on the rooms twice, so that meant she was checking on him often, from inside the rooms to boot. He really didn't know how to feel about that.

"Sure, I can-" he started, only to be interrupted as she took the cup from his hand before he could offer to bring one for her. So, he stood there as the Dragon of Infinity tried out tea for the first time. He stiffened when she frowned and passed the thing back to him.

"Bitter," she mumbled, eyes narrowed.

"Sweeteners can be added," he pointed out and he found himself on the receiving end of the intent stare of the dragon once again. "There's sugar, honey and other things. Maybe I can bring you some to try next time?" he offered and she seemed to consider that for a long moment before nodding and walking back into the same room he'd been modifying.

'What the fuck was that?' he wondered to himself.


[}-o-{]
​

"Only you, Joshua," Gabriel commented and he sighed wearily.

He also refrained from pointing out that Yasaka and Serafall had said the exact same thing when he told them what happened. He sorely wanted to bring it up, but he had a feeling that she'd find it even more amusing than she already did the situation he'd told her about. He didn't think he wanted to deal with that going into where they were… which was Heaven, again.

"I think my life just can never have a quiet moment," he commented, although he wasn't always complaining about that. There were times when the unpredictability of his life was a good thing. "By the way, that's new," he added, deciding to focus on something else, like the black iris that Gabriel had placed behind her ear.

It stood out against her generally bright and light color palette, maybe even looking bad. Joshua didn't know enough about fashion to know for sure, but he knew that it looked great to him. Mainly because that was the flower that he'd given her for their first date, the one from the tradition of sorts that he had started, or followed, if you looked at it a certain way.

"Felt like it," she replied with a smile that he was sure hid plenty that was going unsaid. He almost wanted to ask, but he was a little distracted by how pretty she looked, smiling a warm smile and reaching up to tuck a lock of her blond hair behind her ear around the flower. He was biased, of course, but what did that matter?

"You're beautiful," he said, and he felt silly for being that direct and simple about it. However, he'd learned that it was enough to do that sometimes. It didn't all need to be big and meaningful gestures. That was something that was proven when Gabriel beamed at him. "So, what's special about today?" he asked as they continued on their way to meet her brothers. She always liked to take the scenic route there when they visited, for whatever reason.

Joshua guessed she liked to show off her home-slash-realm, and it was entirely fair. Heaven was magnificent, truly, and it was no chore at all to admire the place. Besides, it was more time with his partner and less time dealing with people he didn't know well, so that helped too. And he'd never complain about being with Gabriel, or Yasaka or Serafall, for that matter.

"I think I'd rather not spoil the surprise," the angel answered and he side-eyed her suspiciously. There was definitely something going on, but he couldn't quite figure it out. His one guess was that they were finally going to do something serious rather than test things, which was… Bold.

Joshua had completely understood the angels' desire to be completely safe on their approach to his capabilities to alter Heaven's System. There was a lot that they could fuck up and they wanted to work on it in a way that wouldn't go against what their father had wished for it to be. They just wanted to deal with some inconveniences left over by the war that had been going on when God died.

Maybe there was something that they wanted to get out of the way quicker than other things? Or something they were more sure about how to deal with. Or both. Joshua wasn't too sure, but he guessed he'd get an answer soon enough. It was just that he couldn't stop his curiosity from being annoying and trying to find an answer.

"I can see the gears turning," Gabriel commented, poking the side of his head and he sighed. "You really can't deal with not knowing things, can you?" she asked, sounding both amused and fond.

"I guess I got used to having all the information. It's what I've needed to get this far," he replied with a slight shrug and a half-helpless smile. "I should learn to deal with it when it's not a necessity, like right now… I think." Even though he said that, however, there was a part of Joshua that rebelled against the idea. Knowing things meant he was safe, after all, and not knowing things meant he was in danger.

That's how his mind had started to work.

Sometimes, he'd manage to deal with unknowns to some extent, but others… Others he couldn't stop his mind from overthinking things, worrying about every single bad thing that could come from an unknown. 'I really should do something about that,' he told himself, closing his eyes and taking a deep breath in. Then he opened them rather abruptly when he felt Gabriel taking his hand.

"You've had a lot to worry about so far and still have plenty," she told him and he gave a smile that might as well have been a grimace back to her. "It's completely understandable that your mind is used to not liking unknowns. They tend to make you nervous because you see them as potential problems for yourself and those you care about," she explained, as if reading his mind. Maybe she knew a thing or two about that kind of situation. She had lived through at least one major war.

'Actually, I should brush up on supernatural history, at least from the bible factions and the youkai…' he mused to himself before deciding to focus on the present. He always ended up feeling bad when he drifted off too much on one of his partners, especially when it was a one-on-one situation rather than in a group one.

"So, other than the mystery thing, anything else I should know?" he asked, doing his best to put all his attention on Gabriel. He was pretty sure she noticed, just like he was pretty sure he saw the corner of her lips pull up into a wider smile than the one she was already wearing.

"Not really, but I'm sure you'll have plenty to talk with Raphael," she told him and he almost sighed.

"No offense to him, but he's exhausting and he gives me headaches," he replied and she giggled. He wasn't even joking. That one particular Seraph was probably the one he liked the least, and that was saying something when Uriel was right there, always on the verge of hating his guts. However, Raphael was like Ajuka in the sense that they were too much like Joshua. Being in the same room with one of those and any kind of business talk was bound to give him a headache just with how many ideas they ended up bringing up.

Most of which weren't even useful.

"He shares the sentiment," Gabriel told him and he wasn't really surprised. Although, the Seraph certainly did a better job at acting like he was fine than Joshua and Ajuka did when they were met with that situation. Maybe that was an angel niceness thing. "Do you think we could go somewhere after this? Or did you have something to do?"

He had been planning to go conduct some research with Grendel again, sure, but how could he say no to Gabriel?

"Nothing at all," he said, knowing full well that the angel would see right through him. He did it anyway though, because why not? "Did you want to go somewhere in particular?" he asked, instead of addressing that.

"Not really. I just feel like monopolizing your time for a bit. Is that greedy?" she asked and he could hear the joke in her tone. As if she even could be greedy. Although… 'No, no flicker of her wings,' he noted to himself with some relief.

That kind of thing was still happening from time to time, and it worried him greatly. He was really hoping that once they got to easing up on the System's restrictions on angels, things would get better in that regard. And if worse came to worst, then he'd just be a greedy fuck and just change the System himself. That'd be bad, but it wouldn't be worse than the alternatives, at least in his opinion.

"Stop worrying about it. I'm fine," Gabriel told him, poking his side softly with her fingers. "We're going to make this easier on us now, and that'll help a lot, not only for me but for everyone."

"I know, I just wish we didn't have to walk on eggshells every time we're together," he told her, being brutally honest. He could lie or underplay it, but she'd read right through him, and there were things that he didn't want to lie about. There were things he didn't want to do that with, no matter how much she could see through things.

Maybe he was just very particular about that kind of thing though, Joshua was aware of that much.

"And I appreciate that," she said, pulling on the hand she was holding and bringing him closer to her as she hugged his arm. "Now, some other topic, Joshua," she said and he knew she was making fun of him. She knew, after all, that he was terrible at carrying a conversation by himself. Especially one that he didn't have predetermined topics to address for some reason or another.

"You're very mean for an angel," he pointed out and she just smiled wider, the meanie. "Well, I think we can take a break in Asia's garden when we're done here. What do you say? It's been a bit since I've seen it all and she's been doing a lot of things. And got Karin's help to do a bunch of others."

"Sounds like a plan," Gabriel said, visibly pleased with herself for whatever reason. Maybe getting his socially awkward ass to do anything even remotely social was a victory of some sort for her. If that was the case, Joshua didn't like the fact that he'd be put on the spot more. He couldn't even complain either, because he kind of loved the look on her face at that moment. "She does beautiful work."

"I know, right?" he replied with a smile of his own. "I'm thinking about getting her a bigger area to work with, and maybe some help. Because she's great with that," he added, and he wasn't even thinking about all the materials he'd get from a bigger garden, although that was a plus. Asia just had a gift with gardening, for one reason or another. And he thought it was a shame that it'd never popped up in the actual series… or so he thought, at least. He could have forgotten. "I wonder what she could do with more to work with… Although, I might have to make sure she doesn't try to work the entire thing by herself, because she might actually try."

"Sounds like her," Gabriel agreed and he nodded, happy to have that confirmed. People weren't his forte, so it was nice to have some help from time to time. "And I'm sure she'd love that," she added.

She didn't say anything after that, simply walking beside him in silence.

"You're being very mean, Gabriel," he said and she giggled.

"I don't know what you're talking about," she replied and he could see the smile on her face getting wider. Even he could put two and two together. He wasn't that socially obtuse. "So…"

"Did I do something to make you angry?" he asked, almost whining, and he wasn't even ashamed of that fact. To that, she giggled again, but at least she didn't keep the silence going, so that was a plus, he supposed.

"I'm just in a good mood, I guess," she commented and he smiled despite his growing awkwardness. "I love you."

"I love you too."


[}-o-{]
​

Eventually, however, they did make their way towards where the rest of the Seraphs were waiting and Joshua had the feeling that they really had been waiting. As in, Joshua and Gabriel had kept them waiting. He'd have felt sorry or even worried, but that was all on his partner and he was not taking the blame for that. He'd gotten there at the time Gabriel told him to and he'd followed along with her, so it was all completely on her if they were late.

Not that he expected any of the three angels would take that as a good excuse, but still.

He was innocent.

"Finally," Uriel grumbled and Joshua kind of lamented the loss of some points with him. Then again, he rather doubted the Seraph would ever like him, so it wasn't a terrible loss, he supposed. And if Gabriel was happy delaying and such, then he'd do what she wanted.

Was he whipped? Certainly.

He didn't think anyone would blame him for that, all things considered.

"Sorry," he said, not quite shrugging, but he considered it. "Got a little sidetracked," he explained and he heard Gabriel stifle a giggle from beside him. And if he noticed, the other three definitely did, which was probably the reason why Uriel's expression twitched. "So, what are we working on today?"

That seemed to be enough to set off Raphael and a moment later Michael. Gabriel and Uriel, like usual, settled off to one side of the table to just listen and chime in here and there. For the most part, the two of them didn't usually have much to add to the conversations, but they still were there. Joshua wasn't complaining about having Gabriel there, at all, but he could have done without the grumpy one, admittedly.

All the same, he focused on work and that helped him calm down, at least. It was a little awkward at times, for sure, but he was good at turning his brain into research-mode and that was something that the discussions very much allowed. Raphael being kind of similar-minded to him helped too, even if it was also exhausting in an entirely different way.

Unfortunately, the topic of the day was one that made things extra hard for Joshua. Because apparently they were discussing the Lust restrictions on the System and it was very awkward to do that with Gabriel's brothers. And he couldn't decide if the fact that Gabriel herself was in the room helped or not. Uriel was just the cherry on top of the awkward cake, honestly.

At least his partner was benevolent enough to help him out, getting him a cup of tea.

He was still very much looking forward to being done with it all. The only reason he didn't try to cut things short was that… Well, they would have to get through that eventually, and he had a vested interest in it being sooner rather than later. Gabriel falling during one of their dates would suck, after all, and he didn't like the idea of possibly making an enemy out of Heaven when he inevitably pulled on his control of the System to fix that.

"I think we can actually get some things tweaked today," Raphael said and Joshua narrowed his eyes. Because he could understand him being in a hurry, or even Gabriel. But Michael? Raphael? Uriel? Those made less sense, because he had it on good authority that they were very much single, and he rather doubted they wanted to rush for some one-night stands.

Then again, it was the DxD world that they were talking about, so…

"If you're sure…" Joshua replied tentatively, looking between all of the Seraphs and trying to see if he was missing something. It was Michael that seemed to decide to just explain things to him, a weary smile on his face.

"I think it's no secret that our faction is the smallest of the three, Joshua," was all he said, and that was very much an explanation, he supposed. He just… hadn't really thought about that much, considering the faction seemed fine. Then again, he guessed it was difficult for them not to look like that, considering they were… Well, Heaven, and angels and all that. They were probably contractually obligated to look all kinds of nice… as it were. "Our people have been under harsh restrictions for way too long, which hasn't helped. So, we're all rather eager to ease things at least a little," the leader of the faction explained further and he nodded slowly.

Now that he was looking further away than his own situation, Joshua could see a little more. Like what Michael wasn't saying. Because he was pretty sure the Seraph was implying that Lust might be the Sin – or one of the Sins, at least – that got the most angels to fall. If they could cut down on that, and maybe increase the chances of the numbers of their faction going up, then it was all wins for them.

That was… interesting to think about.

Still awkward though.

"Well… what do you want me to do?" he asked, because ultimately, he'd do whatever they wanted. He might have the power, but he'd rather not have the responsibility. If he could have made Michael an Administrator, he would have, in all honesty. He didn't know their faction as well as they did, not even close, and he was a human like any other. Joshua was no saint and he was very aware of that fact, so he'd rather not make decisions for a faction such as Heaven.

All Seraphs smiled at that, Gabriel wider than most while Uriel was still somewhat scowling somehow.

They got to work though, making small adjustments here and there that Joshua could barely understand. Much as he could read and comprehend the system, there was a lot that kind of went over his head still, because he just lacked the context and adjacent knowledge necessary. Another reason why he'd decided to just trust Raphael and Michael, really.

Surprisingly, it didn't take much time at all, but that was probably because the two angels had probably gotten most of the prep-work necessary out of the way before he even dropped by.

"I think that's enough," Michael commented, a pleased smile on his face. "It probably doesn't seem like much, but it's a huge step for us," he added, turning to look at Joshua fully. "Thank you, Joshua."

"Don't mention it," he replied with a smile of his own. "Happy to help," he added… before a hand grabbed his arm and all but pulled him to his feet.

"Now, if you'll excuse us, we had plans to visit a garden," Gabriel said, all beaming smiles… But Joshua didn't miss the way her brothers' expressions turned awkward… and a little scared.

He didn't even have time to ponder on that though, because was suddenly standing in the middle of Asia's garden.

He didn't get to look at it either though, because Gabriel's lips stole his whole attention immediately.

Suddenly, several things were making a lot of sense, he had to admit, not that he had a lot of presence of mind to notice until later.

#1,512
Been Feeling This Shadow

[Joshua Davis]

"This is annoying, somehow," Serafall commented, eyes narrowed and lips pursed. Beside her, Yasaka rolled her eyes. "Why is it annoying?"

"I don't know," Gabriel answered, all smiles in a way that was making Joshua feel kind of awkward in a way that he thought he wasn't going to have to deal with again… much. "But I'm sure it's fine," the angel added, somehow smiling wider and more warmly, which was an achievement of its own, really.

"Are you sure you two didn't f-?"

"Serafall," Yakasa interrupted and she didn't even need to look at Kunou for them all to be aware of the kid's presence at the breakfast table. Jeanne was, as usual, looking on with immense amusement, while Asia didn't know what to do or where to look, apparently. Probably didn't help that the nun had been walking through the garden when Gabriel and him had gotten a little carried away. Joshua was starting to seriously consider sending them to have breakfast somewhere else rather than there, if only to make things less awkward.

Having the whole family share breakfast was great… but only when his sex life wasn't something that was all but on display.

"You guys know that I know what s-?"

"Finish that. I dare you," Joshua said, turning to level Kunou with a flat stare. "You're not going to be spell tinkering for a year," he added and the girl paled before nodding and looking down at her plate, very intently avoiding so much as looking at the rest of them. "Good," he muttered, sighing as he turned towards his partners. "Can we talk about literally anything else?" he asked.

Pleaded, more like, but still.

"What's everyone doing today?" he decided to add after a second, because he had a feeling that nobody was going to volunteer a topic and he was that desperate to stop so much as thinking about the previous one.

"The girls from the Kendo Club wanted to go shopping," Jeanne answered, almost making it sound like a question though. Joshua just nodded, because it wasn't like he had to give her money or anything. His sister could be a little shit at times, but she wasn't an idiot. So, he gave her an allowance, sometimes with a little extra if she helped at the cafe, and it was more than enough for her.

So far, she hadn't done anything stupid with it.

"Gonna get anything in particular?" he asked, grateful for the chance to focus on anything else. He hadn't expected that from Jeanne – she usually liked to see him suffer for entertainment –, but he wasn't complaining. Glancing at his partners, he knew things weren't over. He wasn't entirely sure what the issue was though. Serafall had some sort of competition thing going with Gabriel, but still. That was a little extreme a reaction.

And no, they had really not fucked.

The allowances he'd helped with didn't go that far. At least not safely. It wasn't like angels couldn't do that, even before, but it was a risky process and Gabriel and him had decided not to push their luck. Which made him want to work on his project in that regard all the more.

Sadly, it'd been pushed to the side as he continued to study Heaven's System with Raphael and Michael. What neither of those angels knew though was that the entire process was helping him learn more about how it all worked. It'd make the creation of a blindspot all the easier. Unfortunately, it was going to be far from easy, same as making something that would help Yasaka be able to leave Kyoto and explore the world safely.

Serafall really didn't have much to complain about, really.

Which was why he found himself alone with her, to ask her about it. Because if he'd noticed, then he really needed to do something about it. It had to be bad, evidently. Fortunately, Yasaka and Gabriel hadn't minded much when he pulled Serafall aside.

"It's nothing," the Satan answered when he questioned her about her attitude. She was also pouting, which didn't help her at all. So, he just raised his eyebrow at her. "Ok, it's not nothing. It's just stupid," she added with a sigh. "Can we not?"

"I mean, if you really don't want to," he answered, giving her a somewhat unsure smile. "If something is bothering you, I don't want to just ignore it though," he added and she gave him a helpless smile.

"You're unfair sometimes, Josh."

"Right back at you," he replied and both their smiles became that little bit more true, more fond. "So…"

"Did you know one of my strongest Sins is Envy?" she asked out of nowhere and he had to pause for a second to process that. As he did though, he only found himself more confused. Why would she envy Gabriel? It didn't really make sense to him, at all. "I envy Sirzechs and Ajuka's strength. I envy other people's freedom, when I'm stuck being a Satan. I envied Yasaka for a long time, because she had it so easy getting close to you. And now… I envy Gabriel for being so… so happy. I feel like she's enjoying something I didn't, somehow," she explained, a surprisingly vulnerable expression on her face as she did so.

"... I mean…" he started, thinking things through as best he could without taking too long, which was one of the reasons social settings weren't his thing. He had to do it anyway though, because Serafall looked genuinely upset. "It is different for her, but that's because she – and the rest of the angels, really – have had to live holding back a lot. She got to let loose a little and that's probably why she was so happy. In a way, I guess you'd be right, but-"

"But it wasn't because of you, not entirely," she finished for him, voice dropping as she stepped forward and dropped her head against his chest. "I… Why didn't I think of that?" she asked, more to herself than to him. So, he just settled for hugging her. "Now I feel silly."

"Would it help if I said is this much more what I expected when I somehow ended up in a relationship with three women?" Joshua asked with a slight smile.

"Unreasonable jealousy?"

"Nothing unreasonable about it," he replied, resting his chin on top of her head. "I can't imagine how jealous I'd be if the situation was reversed somehow. I don't think I could be in that position." It was terrible of him to think, he knew, but Joshua was sure he wouldn't have been able to deal with that if it had come to it. Maybe because he wasn't a local and he didn't have the DxD common sense ingrained in his brain or something, but he just… couldn't.

"I guess you're greedy where I'm envious, huh?" Serafall commented, because of course she could read his mind through his words somehow. He wasn't sure why he could hear a smile in her voice, even though it was muffled by his shirt.

"I guess so," he agreed, happy that she seemed to feel better. He wasn't sure if what he'd said was right at all, but it seemed to have worked somehow, so he wasn't going to question it much. Sometimes, social interactions just were like that. People hardly ever made sense, even when he knew them. Fortunately, he didn't seem terrible at dealing with them anyway.

Even if he had no idea what he was doing half the time.


[}-o-{]
​

"Must you act so…" Sona said, exasperation clear in her voice. "... undignified, sister?" she finished with, sighing and adjusting her glasses ever so slightly.

Not that Serafall was paying too much attention. The Satan was too busy giggling as she rested her back on his arm, sitting sideways. Joshua himself wasn't minding either of them too much besides enjoying the weight of his partner on his side. He had a notebook in hand and a project to work on, after all, so there was really no need to be bothered.

Serafall was also in a much better mood, so he didn't mind her sticking around. It didn't hurt that she wasn't distracting him as much as he'd feared. She seemed content to just be by his side and he was more than happy to let her.

"Can you switch back to mist again, Sona?" he asked, flipping a few pages on his notebook. Idly, he wondered if it was obvious that he was trying to divert the attention of the younger Sitri sister. Ultimately, the girl was too polite and serious to do anything other than listen to him. It helped that she felt pretty indebted to him after he'd started backing her school project.

"Of course, Joshua," she replied and she somehow made his name sound like she was actually saying "Mr. Davis". It was kind of impressive that she managed to do that, actually. "Any way in particular?"

"Just what comes naturally. We can push things some other time when I have a better idea of how your power works," he answered, closing his eyes to focus on his other senses as the girl did as he asked.

The Sitri, funnily enough, had a very similar power to the Leviathan. However, the latters had the Power of Sea, which allowed them to not only control water but also some strange kind of marine-based biokinesis. The incomplete nature of Katerea's power was making things difficult to understand on that front, but so far he'd narrowed it down as them being able to imitate sea creatures with their bodies… in a very extreme way and pushing it all the way past any sort of "natural" benchmarks.

Like Katerea's use of it during their battle, when she overpowered herself with Ophis's boost and then became an eldritch horror of tentacles.

The Sitri, on the other hand, had Power of Flow… which was the river to the Leviathan's sea. Where the Satan clan seemed to have their focus on everything regarding the sea rather than just the water, the Sitri's everything was dedicated to water. Mist, snow, ice – which kind of went against the naming of the Power, but he didn't ask about that –, water, all of it was what they could work with. Moreover, he had suspicions that they could use it on any liquid, rather than just water. He didn't have any proof, but he also hadn't asked yet.

If they did, then they were keeping it under wraps and he could offer them the courtesy of turning a blind eye to that.

They were going to be his in-laws eventually, most likely, so he had a good incentive to be on good terms with them.

"Thank you," he said absently as he started taking notes on what he was picking up from Sona's use of her Power. The main ideas he had in regards to how to use the data on Flow was for managing his magic reserves and the magic that resided in his spells and arrays. Maybe he could make it all more efficient or fast, or both.

Not much else he could do with that, he supposed. There was an idle idea of using that with stuff like his sand-form when he was using Set's blessing or channeling the god, but that was… Useful, yes, but also a little underwhelming. He'd rather have stuff that he could use to not have to fight at all, really. It was a good idea though, he supposed, so he might as well try and use that.

It wasn't what he was looking for though.

"Say, Sona," he called, taking a deep breath in. He'd have stretched a little, but Serafall was still pressing against his side, unfortunately. "Do you know anyone that'd be able to help Ravel with her duties? She has a little too much on her plate these days," he commented and the youngest Sitri blinked before the gears started turning in her head.

Was it hypocritical of him to say something like that? Extremely so, but there was quite literally nobody else that could help him except Friday. The spell was already helping him as much as she could too, so… There was nothing to do about it.

He could have made more living spells, he supposed, but that'd have… It didn't sit well with him. After seeing Friday quite literally come to life, he felt bad about just… creating more like her just to help him work. It was basically treating sapient beings like tools and that just sounded plain wrong to him.

He already felt bad about how Friday had come to be, if he were honest.

"I can think of a few," Sona commented and Joshua noticed how Serafall had stopped whatever it was that she'd been doing to turn to look at her sister too. "Should I coordinate with Ms. Phenex?" the girl asked and Joshua smiled.

"Please. And make sure she actually tries to find someone, will you?" he asked and the girl nodded. She looked entirely too serious doing that, but that wasn't really a bad trait to have, he supposed. A little amusing at times, but that was better than other approaches she could have to life.

A finger poked his cheek then.

"I thought I was going to help her with that?" Serafall asked and he could hear the pout on her face.

"I mean, you have been doing that, haven't you? I just figured you had better things to do with your time, and that Sona would appreciate helping me out as a way to repay her debt and what not," he reasoned with a half-smile.

"Finding little Ravel some help is much better than anything else I have to do though!" she whined and he grinned even wider.

"Better than going on a date with me tonight?" he asked and that seemed to snap the Satan out of her funk immediately.

"Where?"

"Well, there was that restaurant you mentioned the other day, the one an Agreas-"

"What are we waiting for?!" she exclaimed, already going to stand up.

"To finish here and get ready? You do know it's afternoon, not night, right?" he asked and she paused.

"Oh."

"You're having a day of all time, huh?"

"Shut up! It's your fault for being so nice and comfy!"


[}-o-{]
​

[Carmilla Karnstein]

She thought they might have escaped notice.

She thought that maybe, just maybe, they'd disappeared from everyone's radar. That would have been an ideal scenario and she'd quite enjoyed the delusion. It was time that she'd had to put together the remnants of her faction… and the dredges of the Tepes faction. It was a mess unlike anything that she'd had to deal with in her life, but at least the future was promising.

That is, until Joshua Davis decided that a surprise visit was warranted.

"I take it things are going well? We haven't heard from you in a while," the man commented, looking almost bored. If anything, he seemed more interested in the selection of snacks offered to him with his tea than the conversation. Yet, what he was saying…

'You didn't forget about us, right?' she heard in her head, her mind translating the words almost instantly. 'You haven't forgotten that all this is because of us, right?' her brain added as she watched him pick up a pastry and take a bite out of it while turning his attention back to her.

"I'm sorry," she said almost instantly, barely keeping her voice from cracking. "Things have been hectic while we try to get our feet under us," she tried… and then she saw the tiny girl beside Davis write down something in her notebook and she felt her unease grow.

The smile on the Phenex's face wasn't helping.

"I see," the magician commented, leaning back and taking a sip from his tea. "Well, if you need any help, let us know," he added and he offered her what could have been called a kind smile. That is, if it weren't for the context.

'Do I need to do more for you?' he seemed to ask. 'I don't mind, but can you afford that?'

"We'll manage, Lord Davis," she replied, bowing her head a little, even if it stung her pride to do so. "We appreciate the offer, however."

"Well, so long as you're not struggling," the man told her and she held herself back from reacting to the subtle insult. "As it is, we didn't come here to check on you, not really."

'You're not important enough for us to bother,' she heard in her head and she gnashed her teeth.

"We're here for you to pay us back," he said and the devil by his side cleared her throat. "At least a little," he added, for good measure, as if she weren't aware of that. If it were anyone else sitting across from her, she might have had to exercise more control to have so much patience and restraint…

But it was Joshua Davis.

She knew the man could end them all if he felt like it. And that was by himself too, improvising some spells on the fly. If he had time, he probably wouldn't even have to try. If he brought his people over, then they would be finished without him having to so much as cast a spell.

"What can I do for you, Lord Davis?" Carmilla asked and it galled her, to act so subservient, but this was the man that had annihilated the opposition for her faction. She better lower her head if she didn't want her faction to join those fallen in their last battle… if it could be called that.

"Do you have a particularly bad Tepes member that you really don't like?" he asked and she blinked. Not only because of the exceedingly strange request coming out of nowhere. But also because there was a shift in his eyes. Where before he seemed bored, disinterested even, there was a shine then, one that unnerved her to no end. Suddenly, the last thing she wanted was to be on the receiving end of that.

Carmilla wasn't sure why, but she felt like that was a spot she never wanted to be in and she found herself very grateful that it was directed at someone she'd been enemies with.

"I'm sure I can find someone," she answered, gulping as she started going over the prisoners from the Tepes faction. Some of them had been added to their numbers – because there were entirely too few vampires in her own faction to maintain any kind of power by themselves, mainly –, but there had been those that had been too troublesome to do that with. There was also the fact that Davis himself had spoken against just killing them all, which she had easily agreed to for the aforementioned reasons, and also in favor of taking them in and making a single faction.

She'd been a little reluctant about that part, but Phenex had been breathing down her neck ever since, so she'd had to do as she was told.

"Glad to hear that," Davis replied and the smile he gave her was borderline predatory. It made her want to run away. As it was, however, she had to settle for swiftly leaving to find the man's vampire for… for whatever it was that he wanted one, really.

The giggle of the Phenex girl was insulting, but Carmilla couldn't find it in herself to care.

Especially about half an hour later, as she watched Joshua Davis take a vampire and start analysing their soul. She watched as a member of her species wailed and thrashed helplessly under the "care" of a man with no mercy. She watched a vampire that had been proud and strong mere minutes before be undone, reduced to a crying, begging mess.

And she realized, with dread filling her chest, the kind of being that she'd all but sold her immortal soul to.


[}-o-{]
​

[Joshua Davis]

'Might be more tricky than I thought,' he mused to himself.

It had struck him while trying to apply what he was learning from the devils to Valerie's… situation. Calling it a project felt wrong even in his head, for some reason. More precisely, he'd been trying to see if he could apply Flow to better find whatever part of Valerie was missing… and after taking one too many looks into soul stuff, alternating between all the different beings that he'd gotten a look at…

He realized that maybe what he needed was a closer look at stuff similar to Valerie's soul, something that might help figure out what was missing. Unfortunately, the only other dhampir that he had access to was Gasper… or he could have access to him if he really needed to. However, poking the guy's soul like he needed in order to be effective was… harsh and he'd rather not.

If there were no other way, then maybe.

As it was, Joshua would start a little smaller. First, he'd take a good look at a regular vampire's soul. Then, he'd pull some strings to find a shitty dhampir somewhere in the world and deal with them. Preferably, one with a Sacred Gear would be even better, but he didn't know how picky he could be. Maybe he could shove a Sacred Gear into whoever he ended up getting his hands on?

'That's an idea,' he mused to himself, jotting down that plan just in case.

"Is this… a bad time?" a voice hesitantly said and he blinked, looking up. There stood Koneko, half hidden behind the partially open door and looking off to the side instead of at him. "I just… felt like visiting."

"Weren't you going to spend time with your sister today?" He was sure of that too, since Kuroka hadn't shut up about that for a good hour when they'd been training. "Did she do something?"

"No… not really," Koneko answered with a slight shrug. 'That's not an actual no,' he noted to himself, deciding that he'd have a chat with the older nekoshou. "It's just… a bad day."

"Want to talk about it?" Joshua asked, setting down his pencil and his notebook. He'd continue that later. He couldn't very well just turn away from Koneko when she looked that upset, after all. Admittedly, he'd rather not, because talking and comforting was stressful, but alas… Sometimes there was no avoiding it, he'd learned.

"Not really?" she answered, looking like she shuffled on her feet a little. He couldn't see well, since she was half hiding. Either way, he tried not to sigh in relief at that response, because that simplified things for him quite a bit.

"Want a cup of tea?" he offered then and that, the nekoshou seemed to consider for a long moment before giving a hesitant nod. He smiled then, sending a quick request to Friday, who happily got Fuyuko to help her out with that. She was still learning to make a decent tea, sadly.

"... What are you working on?" the girl asked, glancing at his now abandoned notebook.

"Just something while I wait for everyone else," he answered, not because he wanted to make Valerie's situation lesser, but because he imagined Koneko wouldn't feel better knowing he was putting that off for her. He wasn't that socially inept… most of the time… maybe? "Now that you're here, maybe we can tinker something together, yeah? Like something for the flying game, or maybe a card or two," he offered with a slight smile.

Joshua was very pleased to see some life come back to her golden eyes at that.

It made him feel like a complete winner in life, just like that.

So, the two of them started brainstorming card ideas like that, nothing was actually done, but they had fun nevertheless. Or Joshua thought they did, at least. He was pretty sure he'd caught Koneko almost smiling once or twice, which was huge, far as he was concerned.

Eventually though, two empty tea cups later, she seemed to have regained some of her confidence.

"I had a bad day," she admitted a bit out of nowhere, fidgeting with a card they'd been using as an example. "I was going to visit Kuroka and then… I just couldn't. I kept… remembering," she commented and Joshua did his best not to glance behind him, where he had long since noticed the presence of the other nekoshou.

Interestingly enough, she left at that moment and she hadn't even been there for that long.

Maybe she had decided not to eavesdrop for once.

"I miss them," Koneko mumbled, bringing his attention fully towards her once more. "Do you miss them?" she asked him. While she wasn't adding a lot of context to things, he was pretty sure he could put the pieces together all the same.

"Always," he answered with a sad smile. "I'll always miss my parents, I think. I have my bad days too, but… I guess I've learned to live with it. They are not coming back, but I take some comfort in the fact that… I think they'd be proud of me. I think they'd be happy for me," he explained as best he could and he could see the girl hanging onto his every word like they were a lifeline.

Very scary that, but somehow, he felt like he could manage.

"I think your mother would be proud of you, Koneko," he added, reaching to pat her head even as her eyes widened. "And I think she'd be happy for you," he told her. Because yes, her mother had made some questionable choices, but at least she'd tried and she'd cared in her own way.

As for her father… Well, Joshua almost wanted to see if he could get help from the gods related to death in order to give the guy a piece of his mind.

"You think so?" she asked, looking down.

"You're a good girl, Koneko. You study hard, you dedicate yourself, and you're well-behaved. Most importantly, you're nice and caring. You've also got people that care about you all around and you've managed to get a nice life for yourself," he listed, and he smiled a little wider when he saw her blush a little under the praise. "What could she be other than proud and happy for you?"

She remained silent after that, fidgeting with the card between her fingers. Joshua let her though, pulling his hand back and just giving her time. That is, until she leaned onto his side, resting her head on his arm.

"Thank you."


[} Chapter End {]

#1,524
None of Us Are Out Here on Our Own

Joshua was feeling his patience and his general calm tested.

The days were passing and little by little, he felt them more and more. Because every day that passed was a day in which Khaos Brigade could unleash their particular brand of madness upon the world. He was kind of surprised that there hadn't been some Evil Dragon attack somewhere in the world already by that point. Surprised, but not complaining, obviously.

However, the peace was unnerving on its own.

Because the terrorist group hadn't just randomly decided to retire, obviously. So, that meant they were out there, plotting, preparing. And nobody knew how dangerous that was better than Joshua himself. Granted, he was working on things on his end too… but he was more than anything working on Ophis' Silence and on finding Khaos. If he didn't find them before they came to find him in turn, then that was basically giving them the upper hand.

It was a shit position to be in, and he knew it. However, there was little he could do. It was either that or try to wait for them to make the first move. It was an option. He could just give up finding them and prepare defenses and countermeasures for anything he could think of, like Evil Dragons. However, what if they came at him from a direction he didn't expect, in a way that he wasn't ready for? Furthermore, even if he was prepared for whatever they did, who was to say that they wouldn't achieve whatever it was they wanted before he could stop them? Or even just cause a lot of damage before that happened?

No, letting Khaos do whatever they wanted was a terrible idea, at least far as he was concerned.

'I have to find them,' he told himself. Granted, that decision, that resolution, wasn't helping him achieve anything any faster, but it solidified his choice the smallest bit. It pushed the voices telling him to just focus on his protections and traps a little bit.

"Looks like you're thinking pretty hard there," Jeanne commented and he looked up to see her with a tub of ice cream in her hands. He hadn't even realized she had come back home. "And you're not actually working on anything, by the looks of it," she added, pointing at him with the spoon. She wasn't wrong about that, he supposed, since he'd spent the last few minutes going on a tangent, which wasn't particularly new.

Except this time it wasn't an idea tangent, so there were no notes being taken.

"Why the ice cream?" he asked, very obviously changing topics. Jeanne didn't seem to mind though, shrugging.

"Why not?" she asked back… and he didn't have a response to that. So, they sat there for a long moment. "Kiba's gonna go through a promotion to Middle Class," she commented and he raised an eyebrow. That sounded like a good thing to him. Although, High Class was when you got your peerage pieces. Was Jeanne worried the guy would pull an Issei?

Because if he did and Jeanne was upset, then Joshua would have to see about removing Kiba's ability to do much of anything.

"He has to prepare for that. Study more, train more," Jeanne commented and that reassured him a little bit. He made a mental note to talk with the guy though, just in case. "That's less time he'll spend with me."

"Is it? Don't you guys have training dates and stuff?" he asked, leaning back. "Besides, you could study with him, right?"

"It's not like school exams, Joshua," she huffed, rolling her eyes and all. He looked at her distinctly unimpressed as she did that. Sometimes, he missed the shy girl Jeanne had once been. Sometimes, he also forgot that she was, indeed, a teenager.

"I guess you're not very serious about the guy then," he commented, looking down at his notes and faking working on something. Jeanne might have changed a lot, but that didn't mean he didn't know her. And if he knew her half as well as he thought he did, then-

"What do you mean?" she asked and he could hear the frown on her face. Joshua had to make an effort not to smile.

"I mean, if you're gonna stick with the guy for the long run, then knowing about devil stuff just makes sense, doesn't it?" he asked, idly, casually, like it was any other topic and it wasn't all that important. There was a long, drawn out moment of silence that followed his words, although he could almost hear the gears turning in his sister's brain. "It's fine if you don't want to," he added, because he was having a little fun, he supposed.

As was his brotherly duty, after all.

He almost chuckled when he heard her take out her phone and the soft tapping of her writing what was probably a message.

"Nevermind that," Jeanne commented, but she sounded in a lot better spirits already which Joshua took as a win. She was probably feeling a little silly though, for not having thought about what he said herself. Which was probably why she decided to pivot into a different topic. "Working on something complicated?"

"When am I not?" he asked, a little helplessly.

What he wouldn't give to be able to work on something easy and irrelevant for once, but alas…

"What's this one about?"

"Valerie's thing. Finding where the rest of her Gear is. That's the only clue I have to find Khaos Brigade with," he explained, taking a deep breath in and holding back a sigh. "Soul stuff will never not be a mess though, evidently, and I have my doubts if even they knew what they were doing."

"Too bad you can't ask Agnes to run a few errands and call favors, huh?" she asked and he chuckled. House of Water was handy, for sure, and it was also growing very powerful. But a magician association could only do so much. "I'd offer to make a sword, but…" But she'd already tried, even if she didn't think he knew. Every other time he had a project, she'd try to make a sword that'd help. Sometimes, she had partial successes and sometimes they were even useful to push whatever research he was conducting.

More often than not though, she ran into the issue of not having enough power to fuel whatever sword she wanted. And, unfortunately, Sacred Gears were more complicated in how they were fueled than simple magic energy, even if it also used that. So, Joshua couldn't just set up an array that'd push Jeanne to make better swords. Or, he could, but it only reached so far.

"It's fine. I'm cursed not to have free time, evidently. I can't wait for it all to be over and be able to sit back and let Ravel do her thing," he commented with a grin, drawing a smile from his sister. That is, before the pieces of the conversation shifted ever so slightly in his head and he blinked, face falling flat.

"Joshua?"

"Say, remember that you wanted to go visit places connected to the original Jeanne?" he asked and it was her turn to blink, that time with confusion. "You're going."

"There's a reason I didn't go, Josh. I wanted to go with Kib and he can't-"

"You're going," he insisted, his mind already getting away from him a little. "Gabriel will make it happen, don't worry. I have something to do," he said, standing up and leaving a very confused sister in his wake.

God, he loved her, even if she was a handful at times.

The idea she had just given him certainly helped too.


[}-o-{]
​

"Hey, Ravel, sorry for calling you when you're taking time off, but-" Joshua greeted before pausing and blinking at the gathering of girls that had apparently teleported with the Phenex. One of which was Sona too, which was also a surprise. The other two, he didn't know, although the older one looked to be about the same age as Sona and Rias, and struck him as slightly familiar, even if he couldn't place where he'd seen her.

The younger girl, however, he definitely didn't know. She seemed to be at least close to Ravel's age, so that could explain things a little. She was also giving him strong flashbacks of how the Phenex used to be, and still was, half the time, what with the flat and serious expression she wore. As if someone had taken a lawyer or an accountant and placed them in the body of a kid.

""Mr. Davis,"" both girls said immediately as they straightened and then bowed. Joshua, for his part, stared at them for a long second before turning his head towards Ravel and Sona. Predictably, it was the former that gave an answer to his unasked question.

"Mr. Davis," she greeted, beaming at him. Although, he did notice a tinge of nerves in her expression and she seemed to have trouble looking at him. "These are Iryuka Glasya-Labolas and Seekvaira Agares."

"Huh, I knew I remembered you from somewhere," he said and the older girl stiffened. "You were at the Devil Youth event thing."

"The Young Devil Gathering," Ravel corrected, but that wasn't really the point. He was more interested in the way Agares reacted to the words, like she wanted to make herself small or even disappear. Which was hilariously impossible, seeing as she was the tallest of the four girls.

"Hm, your recruits, I'm guessing?" Joshua asked and Ravel beamed while Sona pushed her glasses up, as if preparing herself. "Neat, how soon can you start?" he added, and the Sitri girl's brain seemed to stumble at his words. She did a double-take immediately before visibly leaning back, as if trying to deal with a sudden shock.

"I can start immediately, Mr. Davis," the younger girl, Iryka – 'That was her name, right?' – replied without even missing a beat. Seekvaira seemed to take a few more seconds to pull herself together and give much the same answer. He didn't blame her for that. She seemed to be processing something when he dropped the question already, after all.

"Great. Ravel, how quickly can you have them take over most of your duties?" he asked then and by then the Phenex girl was realizing that something was going on, because her pride and excitement disappeared, replaced by her usual reliable professionalism. He still found it very odd and somewhat off putting, to see a girl that young do that, but he'd learned that it was just part of Ravel.

He was even guessing that… Iruka?... the other girl was going to be more of the same.

What was it with Devil little girls growing up like that? Was Rias just a huge exception or what? Evidently, that was probably the case, because otherwise he didn't know what was even going on in those households.

"I can get them started right away myself," Ravel answered, visibly switching to secretary mode. He was surprised she hadn't- 'Nevermind,' he thought, somewhat amused as the Phenex took out a notepad from a Storage Space. "They should be able to start taking over some of my duties relatively soon if you don't mind putting them to the test quicker. I could divide things between them. If you need me to do something immediately, I can see about helping them do their side of things while I do mine, Mr. Davis."

"... One of you gotta remind me to do something extra nice for Serafall," he commented and he raised an eyebrow when Ravel nodded and made a note of that. Then she paused, turned towards the other two girls, who had nodded along with her. Ravel frowned for a long moment before waving her hand and making two notebooks appear in front of them, together with pens.

It was a little amusing, to see the three of them standing there, taking notes. It reminded him of his classes at House of Water, in a way, except he was very aware of the huge differences between both things. All the same, he didn't dwell on that too much, because he had an idea and he needed to get that out of the way quickly.

"Great, so, you can start with that then, Ravel," he said, taking a deep breath in. "I need everyone here to explain an idea I just had, especially Serafall and Gabriel," he added and Seekvaira straightened once more while the younger girl's eyes widened. The Phenex, for her part, narrowed her eyes and he could almost see the sparks flying in her brain as she tried to figure out what was going through his head. "Focus on your thing," he told her, tapping her forehead with his finger so that she'd snap out of it. "And you, Sona," he continued, pausing when he saw the girl stand at attention as if she were working for him too. "I'm guessing you brought Seekvaira to Ravel?"

"Yes…" she answered immediately and he was pretty sure she'd been about to say something else before stopping herself. Then she said something different instead. "Are you sure you want to have them start so soon? You haven't talked to them at all, you don't know if they are capable of doing the job."

"Ravel is the one that's been doing the job so far and she's done a magnificent job at that," he replied with a smile that only widened when he saw how pleased the Phenex looked at his words. "She knows better than me what someone else needs to be capable of doing. If she thinks they're good, then they're good."

"I… see," Sona said slowly, as if she couldn't quite wrap her head around that.

"Also, thanks for helping her out," he added, patting the Phenex's head.

"Mr. Davis!" the girl whined, but he paid her no mind. "How am I supposed to get them to listen to me if you do this kind of thing?!" she protested but he paid her no mind. Instead, he was keeping his eyes – or the corner of them, at least – on the two new additions to his life.

Seekvaira and Irykya didn't seem to know quite what to do at that moment, but that was fine. And if a little informality was enough to make them disrespect Ravel, then he'd deal with that… and them. They seemed to be smart girls, and they had to be to pass both Sona's and Ravel's standards. So, Joshua was optimistic about them.

Besides, it wasn't like they'd be doing anything too important.

That'd still be on Ravel.


[}-o-{]
​

"Dad?"

"Yeah?" he asked, leaning back and watching as his familiars and Kunou played some strange game of tag. They were all going pretty strongly about it though, using their abilities and such. Joshua was pretty sure Kunou hadn't used the barrier Artificial Sacred Gear she'd gotten from Penemue nearly as much when training.

The power of games, he supposed.

"Why is Kuroka upset?" his daughter asked, having moved to stand in front of him and using her barriers to keep the rest of the familiars away from her while they chatted so that she wouldn't lose. And if Friday was helping her power the things a little and using the spell arrays of the house for good measure, Joshua wasn't going to snitch.

"Because eavesdropping is bad, and eavesdropping half a conversation is worse," he explained and his daughter paused, considering that. "If you only hear half a conversation, don't assume that's all there is to it, yeah? Because the part you missed might change anything you heard into something completely different," he added and she nodded slowly.

"I see… Are you gonna help her?" Kunou asked and he thought that over. He had meant to talk to Kuroka, but… Well, he'd gotten distracted and then he'd forgotten. In his defense, it wasn't his fault that she'd eavesdropped in the first place.

At the end of the day though…

"Yeah, I guess," he replied, glancing to the side, where Kuroka was training together with Raynare, Georg and Kokabiel.

"Good," Kunou said with a nod. "I can feel how upset she is from here," she added before beaming at him. "Good luck!" And then she turned and skipped back to where she'd been playing.

Sometimes, he thought Serafall was a terrible influence on his kid.

Or maybe Jeanne was.

Or both.

"Oh well," he muttered to himself before deflating and looking up. It'd be a bit before Gabriel was finished with whatever it was that she'd said she needed time to deal with. Serafall and Yasaka were already there, but since he didn't want to have to explain things twice – nor did he want to leave someone out for even a little bit –, he'd decided he might as well kill a bit of time and spend it with his daughters. Besides, he could use a bit of extra time to organize his idea and just go over it in his head.

As it turned out, he was going to spend half that time doing that and the other half dealing with a mess related to one of his kind-of daughters. He wasn't sure if Koneko counted as one, admittedly, but that mostly because of her and what she might want out of her relationship with him. Far as he was concerned, it wasn't that much of a difference.

Although, he was a little concerned by how many children he had somehow ended up caring for.

"Kuroka," he called and all four individuals engaged in the spar stopped what they were doing. "Can we talk?" he asked, tilting his head to a corner that was less populated than the rest of the training area. Raynare, for her part, took advantage of the distraction and punched Kokabiel right in the face.

She was probably feeling great about that, he supposed, because she had most definitely not forgotten about what the man had done. Joshua sorely wanted to give her another pair of wings or two just so that she'd be even closer to the Cadre's level. As it was, she'd have to settle for being helped by his "equalizing" training arrays for the time being.

"Josh~ Did you need something from little ol' me?" Kuroka asked, skipping towards him and he just raised an eyebrow at her. She kept the act up like a champ though, wide smile and all.

"Even Kunou is worried about how upset you are," he commented and her expression turned brittle almost instantly. "And you're a dumb, dumb cat, you know? You can't just hear the worst half of a conversation and bail," he told her with a roll of his eyes.

"I think I heard quite enough," Kuroka replied, lowering her tone and her head.

"Evidently, you did not," Joshua said with a sigh. "She was feeling sad because she was thinking about her parents, not you and what you did." That seemed to immediately take some of the wind out of her sails, if the way her shoulders dropped was anything to go by.

"It was still me that reminded her," the nekoshou argued weakly.

"There's a part of me that feels sad when Kunou calls me dad, because I remember that my dad is forever lost to me," he confessed with a sad smile. "That doesn't mean I blame her for that, or that I want her to stop. I love her, and I love to hear her call me that," he explained and he could tell that Kuroka was paying close attention, even if she was trying to play it off, getting her act back up and even glancing around a bit. "Koneko loves you. Just let her, alright? If she has a problem with you, she'll leave, but don't push her and try not to misunderstand, yeah?"

"... I… Yeah, I'll… try," she replied, hesitantly, slowly. Neither was something that he was used to seeing in Kuroka, but such was life, full of surprises. "... Thank you."

"Thank Kunou. She pointed out that you were in a funk," he replied with a grin that she responded to with a smile.

"You're doing well with her… and with Koneko and Ravel."

"I try," he said with a nod, feeling somewhat proud. "That's all you need to do, most of the time."

Kuroka didn't say anything to that, but she did nod before taking a deep breath in and turning to go back to the spar, looking much more subdued.

Joshua hoped he'd helped, but he was feeling cautiously optimistic… Or maybe it was the fact that he thought he had a great idea and that'd cheered him up.

Either or, really.

'Speaking off…'


[}-o-{]
​

"So…" Yasaka started slowly, bringing her cup of tea to her lips for a sip, and Joshua prepared himself. Now that they were all there, he was suddenly decidedly less sure of how good his idea was. "What's this new idea and how crazy am I gonna think it is?" she asked. Although, contrary to what her words might have one think, she looked downright excited.

"Alright, so I was talking with Jeanne-"

"A Jeanne-inspired idea? Oh, this will be good," Serafall commented and while he was a little annoyed at the interruption… he couldn't really blame her. When he thought about it, he'd be just as skeptical. Nothing against Jeanne, but a decision maker, she was not. She had run away from home and ended up in the streets with nothing going in her favor… and would have ended in Khaos Brigade if not for Cheshire.

"I know," he replied wryly. "But the gist of it is that I'm not making that much progress trying to locate Khaos Brigade. And even tangential bases are getting more and more difficult to spot even with all of us working together… and with Grigori," he said, adding those last ones almost like an afterthought. Although, that was mostly because of how much Azazel annoyed him. Useless as Vali was as a spy, the rest of Grigori was doing a decent job as allies… for the most part.

Especially those days, for whatever reason.

He wasn't complaining.

"So, I thought we could add some extra help to our cause," he suggested, leaving it vague just to gauge how the three of them took things as he slowly presented the idea. He wanted to see if he was really going somewhere with his thoughts or if he'd just made a dumb idea sound good to himself.

"We have offered others to join this alliance, Joshua. It's just… everyone's dealing with it on their own and alliances are complicated. It's already a minor miracle that this one took form and half of it is held together because of you," Gabriel explained and he almost wanted to ask how she meant that. Was it held together because of Joshua himself or because of his relationships with the three of them.

Ultimately, that was a discussion for another time.

"Yes, but that's where we can change things up," he acknowledged before continuing. "We could make it less complicated. Make it simpler and convenient," he explained and then he was starting to see some interest in their eyes. Good, maybe he was actually on to something. "We can make it less of an alliance and more of a… transaction," Joshua said and they were definitely intrigued, he could tell.

Now came the part that had him the most nervous though and he glanced around the room, at Yasaka, at Serafall, at Gabriel, even at Ravel. That was far from comforting, the opposite in fact, but it did remind him somewhat that that was precisely why he was there. To run the idea past them so that they could shut it down if they thought it was stupid.

"What if we offer them something for their help," he stated. "What if I offer them something? Just like I cured the Devil's Sleep Disease and just like I'm giving angels extra wings… what if I offered other factions a deal just as good for their help?"


[} Chapter End {]

On the other hand, I'm sure Khaos Brigade won't suffer because of this.

Well, provided that Joshua's idea isn't shut down, but that'd be mean.
