#1,534
The Lunatics Have Taken over the Asylum

Surprisingly – or maybe not –, none of his three partners laughed nor did they scoff or otherwise show any negative opinions on his idea.

They did frown though, most of all Yasaka. Gabriel pulled back as she did, looking away from him and towards a random corner of the room. Serafall, instead, stared right at him, but her eyes seemed to have unfocused the smallest bit. All three of them remained silent then and there, and as the seconds passed, Joshua realized that they were considering his idea, rather than disapproving of it.

Somehow, that was worse.

All the same, he waited, taking a sip from his almost forgotten cup of tea.

He almost wanted to use that time to consider ideas for his… Well, idea. However, there was a real chance that it'd get rejected. So, instead, Joshua tried to focus on other projects and get some work done as the three women went over things. Tried being the operative word there, because his mind was barely on it. At least he did manage to get some things done, if only halfheartedly.

"I mean, it could work…?" Gabriel said hesitantly, not looking at him but at the other two. That seemed to snap them out of their thoughts too and Joshua saw them start trading looks between themselves. "It'd certainly get them moving…"

"Probably too much," Yasaka pointed out.

"Certainly," the angel replied. "But is that bad, considering everything?"

"Who would we even approach?" Serafall asked, frown deepening. "Would have to be careful who we empower if we do," she added and the other two nodded, acknowledging the point.

Joshua followed the conversation like one would a three-way tennis match – if such a thing existed –, but it wasn't long before things started flying over his head. The fact of the matter was that the three were very obviously seriously considering his idea. That made him feel ever so slightly validated… but also scared. Because if they went through with the idea and it didn't work, or it blew up on their faces…

Well, they'd cross that bridge when they got to it, he supposed.

He had to trust them not to let him go through with a bad idea. That was why he'd brought it up in the first place, really. 'If I can't trust these three, then who can I?' he asked himself before nodding and turning his attention away again. That time though, he did so with a lot more confidence and calm.

They kept trading words for a while though, discussing pros and cons of factions and favors that they could offer. Apparently, Mexico, Central and South America had a lot to offer… if they could manage to unify the small factions all over the place. They'd been weakened a lot, but they were very much still around, like slightly lesser versions of the Egyptian pantheon. That had a lot of potential, if they could balance things with the bigger factions, which were the Inca, the Aztec and the Maya factions.

North America was trickier, but there were ideas being bounced around for that too.

Joshua had, admittedly, gotten lost at some point there, and that was before they started going on tangents and backtracking and going on tangents again. It was like hearing his thought process, except that he could only understand a fraction of what was going on. It was… interesting. Confusing, to be sure, and a little overwhelming but also interesting.

He decided to leave them to that though, because really… He had no business really getting involved at that point. He did keep an ear out for anything that he could actually make sense of, but that was mostly just so that he wasn't completely unaware of what they were talking about. Ravel was taking notes off to the side and he was sure she could dumb it down for him to understand at some point after the meeting.

"The short version is that this is a good idea," Serafall told him, finally turning to actually address Joshua. She was beaming too, which went a long way to reassuring whatever part of him was still nervous and unsure.

"However," Yasaka picked up then, grabbing a cup of tea that would have long since gotten colder if not for some convenient use of magic. "It'll have much bigger implications than just getting us help to deal with Khaos Brigade. The factions that we don't help will have a problem with it, even if they reject offers too… provided we make them."

And Joshua supposed she meant that already problematic factions they might already not want to deal with would get worse. Not a terrible problem, especially once they made some more allies and friends, but it was definitely worth noting. Maybe he should keep that in mind for the next defensive update to his arrays.

"Those that we do deal with will owe more than just the help they'll offer, most probably," Gabriel added and he leaned back and considered that. It wasn't necessarily a bad thing, of course. However, it was something that could be problematic in its own way. He'd know. How many times had someone's supposed debt made them do something that turned out to be awkward, unnecessary or downright troublesome?

Although, it was never too bad, so it was probably fine, right?

"Something to consider," Gabriel told him and he nodded slowly.

"So…" he said, glancing between the three of them, which seemed to prompt another round of shared looks.

"So," Yasaka started, straightening the smallest bit. "We think it's better if we take our time deciding what to do, but it's definitely a good idea," she said and Joshua it was very obvious to the three of them that he wasn't sure about the idea himself, because that was at least the second time he heard them say it was a good one. "It just needs to be very carefully handled… but it will almost definitely improve our chances of dealing with Khaos."

"Well, take your time. It was just an idea," he replied slowly.

Somehow, the excited look Serafall was wearing and the fact that Yasaka and Gabriel didn't look that much more composed wasn't as reassuring as he thought they should have been.


[}-o-{]
​

With his idea out there and being reviewed and prepared by people way smarter and more knowledgeable than him, Joshua was free to do his own thing until they were ready to go ahead. Or, worse come to worst, he was free to prepare stuff in case they scrapped the idea altogether. That was still something that could happen, after all.

Ravel had stayed behind to talk with his partners and organize things too… which left him with Iryuka – he was pretty sure he got her name right that time – as his shadow instead of the Phenex girl. Apparently, she wasn't to actually do anything other than follow him and take notes. If he asked or if she got his permission, then she could try and do things, but only after checking with Ravel. The Phenex herself would go over any decisions and any notes with the girl later so that she could properly teach her how to do her new job.

Joshua wasn't going to comment on her methods one way or another. Far as he was concerned, Ravel knew what she was doing. And if she didn't, then he was likely to pick up on it at some point. Or someone else would, he was sure.

As it was, he just had to decide if he was going to work on Silence or-

"Um, Mr. Davis?" the girl by his side asked and he blinked, turning to see her fidgeting with her notepad. She'd gotten a different one from the one Ravel had given her. That one didn't have the Phenex seal, for one. He was guessing it had her family's instead… 'Glasya-Labolas, was it?' he thought to himself. "You have an appointment in fifteen minutes. Valkyrie class at House of Water," she informed him and he blinked.

'I do?' he wondered, tilting his head as he processed that and rumaged his mind for that bit of knowledge and… 'Ah, so I do,' he confirmed with a slight nod. Apparently, he'd gotten too distracted by his new idea.

"Do you need me to communicate to them that you won't be able to attend? Maybe reschedule?" the girl said then, going over her notes and probably looking for a free spot or something that she could juggle to make time. She was already off to a great start, apparently. The flashbacks from when Ravel started – and for the current Ravel, really – were getting stronger with every passing second.

"That won't be necessary," he said, running his hand through his hair. "Thanks for the reminder, Iryuka," he added and the girl looked down with a small smile, as if trying to hide her expression behind the notepad. 'Huh, that's different, I guess,' he mused. Ravel had been a lot more proud and had kept trying to put on a tough exterior at all times. 'Got her name right too, thank God,' he thought, relieved. "Alright, so… did Ravel go over House of Water with you?" he asked as he turned to walk towards where they had the teleporting array.

"She gave us a summary, sir. And she gave us a dossier to study," Iryuka said and he raised his eyebrows at that. Certainly a thorough approach, the one Ravel had taken, but he was hardly surprised. Impressed might have been a better word for it, he supposed. "If you want to go over it yourself in case she missed something…"

"I doubt she did," he replied with a slow nod. "But I'll tell you my side. It might be different from hers," he explained and the girl flipped a few pages on her notepad and readied herself.

It was kind of adorable, looking at her.

"Alright, so the first thing you need to know is that House of Water can and will accommodate pretty much anything for us, but the valkyries' class is a little more complicated than that," he started with, since that was what they were going to deal with in the immediate future. "They can still give us a little wiggle room, but it'd be difficult for them to pull off since the Norse are… Well, the Norse. So, if it comes to it, we don't want to mess with that too much unless we really need to."

Either she was humoring him, or he was dropping some actual new stuff on her. Or maybe she was noting it down to compare to what Ravel had told her and see if there were any differences. The fact of the matter was that Iryuka was writing down seemingly everything he was saying. It was kind of… odd, but maybe it was just him.

Joshua kept telling her basically all that he could think of regarding his dealings with House of Water all the way to the teleportation array and even afterwards, through the halls of the association. Granted, he might have let his thoughts go on tangents as he spoke, which meant a whole lot of useless stuff being thrown at Iryuka, but she'd have to deal with it if she was going to work with him. Was he throwing her off the deep end a little? Probably, but it wasn't like he expected her to just keep up with everything.

He was just letting her know how things went when working with him.

It was definitely not because he was too lazy to control himself and go easy on her.

Honest.

"You don't need to note every random thing I say, Iryuka," he told her after a particularly off-topic tangent. Mainly because he felt bad seeing her furiously taking note of everything after a bit. "You realize that half of what I've been saying isn't pertinent nor important, right?"

"I do," she answered, surprising him a little. "It might be important later on though, so I want to keep track of that. I'll probably go over it in my off time to properly filter it all and catalogue it."

Joshua blinked at her for a moment, which seemed to make her feel a little self-conscious if the way she shifted on her feet was any indication.

"Huh, well… Let me know if that helps," he commented, suddenly feeling curious if there was a method to her madness. If nothing else, he respected the dedication and the inventiveness.


[}-o-{]
​

"Did you adjust the magic allotment?" he asked, looking at a failed spell's circle and the rune rings that formed it. The thing had failed rather spectacularly, taking up more magic than intended by a lot and filling the entire room and part of the adjacent ones with magic presence, for a second, that is, before the spell went into critical failure. Kind of the point for a magic flare that was being modified into a magic sense flashbang, but not quite.

He made a mental note of it though, because what had happened was basically a magic sense smokebomb instead, which had its own uses.

"I did," the valkyrie said and she sounded way more distressed than she should have for a simple failure.

"Alright, no problem, let's go over the problem together, yeah?" he asked with a smile. He tried to look extra calm about it, because the woman looked like she was a slight push away from pulling her hair out. "It was a problem with the magic itself, I could feel it spiralling before the failure. It's not the effect, it's the energy. If the allotment wasn't the issue, what else could it be?"

"Amount?" she offered as an answer and he could almost see the gears in her head shifting into spellcrafting mode. It was kind of neat, actually. "I was sure the amount was fine though."

"Alright then, assuming the allotment and amount is fine…" Joshua said, trailing off and giving her a moment to see if she could think of the reason. Granted, they were assuming she hadn't made a mistake she couldn't see in the parts they were talking about and he couldn't quite tell himself, since he wasn't that advanced in the runic system yet, but still.

"If the input is fine and the output is fine, then there's a problem in the middle," the valkyrie replied and he smiled more widely. "Right?"

"Sounds right to me," he answered and the woman beamed rather endearingly, if he did say so himself. "I would still make sure the rest of things are actually well done as you think, just in case," he commented and he heard a giggle behind him. He made a mental note of who it was a moment later, checking on his classroom array. "Maybe it'll be ready next class; good job so far though," he told the valkyrie he was helping and she gave him a shy smile, which seemed particularly affected by that laugh.

Which was why Joshua approached that particular valkyrie a moment later.

"Well, that's not an energy issue," he commented with a raised eyebrow, looking at the ball of light floating over the circle. "That's a very nice light spell though, I have to say," he pointed out, making the valkyrie turn red and a bunch of the others giggle, much like she had before. Maybe Karma was an actual thing. Wouldn't surprise him, considering… Well, DxD. "Probably an issue with the manifesting part, I'd say," he pointed out, after getting his fun out of the way and going back to actually teaching. "Considering the concentrated magic presence you're trying to go for, you probably missed something in the shape part," he added and the valkyrie nodded rather stiffly.

Maybe she shouldn't make fun of others if she was that sensitive.

"Don't laugh at others, by the way," he commented and she turned even more red. Maybe valkyries weren't as smart as he thought they were, considering there were three more giggles that followed that. He'd let them have their fun before, but considering what he'd just said… "That goes for all of you," Joshua added, glancing towards those that had laughed just then.

It was going to be a long class, he could already tell.

He made a mental note to tell Iryuka – and the others later – to take note of anyone that behaved like that so that he could take points off their scores at some point. Because the entire thing about spellcrafting was that one would fail a whole lot before getting things right. Just a few days prior, he'd been testing a Power of Destruction Silence application…

And Joshua was pretty sure he'd deleted from existence a sphere about the size of a beach ball. Like, air, the ground and the circle he'd used, magic included. He'd basically deleted all that and replaced it with a void that got filled with air a moment later.

It was interesting, for sure, but also kind of worrisome.

He was still working out the kinks on that one, and he would for a while before testing it again.

"I think that class went well," he commented once things were over. Göndul seemed pleased with his assessment, which was funny because he always said something along those lines and she always looked the same. "They are getting a little too comfortable though, I think."

"The laughing, I'm guessing?" she asked and she seemed to be a little nervous all of a sudden.

"Yeah. I mean, a little teasing is fine, but spellcrafting is hard enough without adding pressure to it," he said and the old valkyrie nodded. "I'll deal with it on my side though, no need to get involved if you don't want to," he added for good measure, leaning back against his chair.

"If you say so, then I'll leave you to it," Göndul replied, hesitating but ultimately standing by that decision. That was fine by him, really.

"Well, with all that said," he started then, running his fingers through his hair. "On with my lesson, then?" he asked, and he was fairly pleased with his own progress. He was actually getting the hang of the runic system and starting to cast spells. He wasn't good enough to start spellcrafting, but he probably would get there soon. He was starting to get confident and seeing some of the mistakes in the valkyrie's works, even if he didn't feel confident enough to apply that to his lessons.

"Of course," Göndul told him and Joshua took a deep breath in to prepare himself.

It was a long day, like most days.

He couldn't wait to get some free time already, but Khaos Brigade wasn't really helping him in that regard, sadly.


[}-o-{]
​

For once, Joshua found himself strangely relaxed in the presence of Ophis.

It surprised even himself, but he really, truly was. He sat there, with a cup of tea in his hand and a smile on his face. There was an underlying worry, sure, deep under his amusement and curiosity, but compared to how he'd gotten used to feeling when around the Dragon of Infinity? It might as well be nothing.

"It's… better," Ophis said with a sage nod that Joshua couldn't help but find funny. "I think I like it with honey the best," she added with another such gesture and he nodded along.

"Tea with honey is nice. I like it when I have a sore throat and such," he replied, to which the dragon looked at him like she didn't understand what the words he'd just said meant. That made sense, he supposed. One of the two – maybe three? – strongest beings in existence probably didn't have any idea what a sore throat even was.

Or a sore anything, for that matter.

"I like it when I'm not feeling well," he tried and that seemed to get the point across better, getting an agreeing nod from Ophis. "So, honey is the best one for you, huh?" he noted to himself, leaning back a little and sipping from his own tea. Ophis seemed to follow suit. It was kind of amusing to have such a conversation.

However, that didn't mean he wasn't taking it seriously.

"Well, I can bring different kinds of tea next time, maybe you can try different sweeteners with those too. There's a lot of options," he explained and Ophis suddenly looked strangely intense about the topic. That was… interesting, to put it in a certain way. "I'm guessing you want to try that?" he asked.

"Yes," she replied, straightforwardly and very seriously.

He was kind of loving that conversation. For once, the eldritch omnipotent being didn't feel like an eldritch omnipotent being… So long as he didn't look straight into the void that were her eyes. Massive improvement, all things considered, really.

"Alright, some of them might not be for you, I don't like a bunch of them, but trying new things isn't always bad," he commented, taking another sip from his tea. "And if it doesn't work out, well, there's always the safe options," he added and Ophis nodded again.

"Like the rooms," she replied and Joshua considered that.

"Like the rooms," he agreed. He guessed he could see how that made sense to her. In a way, the different options of rooms he'd made could be considered like different flavors of tea… possibly… maybe. 'Or different genres of music, or different styles of painting… The point gets across, I guess,' he thought to himself.

"Thank you," the Dragon of Infinity said while his mind went on a slight tangent and… He wasn't sure, but he was pretty sure there'd been actual emotion in her voice there. It was actually kind of… neat. Although, he wasn't sure if that was just for the tea. Surely it wasn't that important to her, right?

Then again, the inner machinations of her mind were an enigma.

"Happy to help," Joshua replied with a smile. "I'll be working on the rooms now, feel free to just step in them if you want, or keep drinking. There's plenty of tea where that came from," he told her and the dragon simply nodded and remained silent afterwards.

Or, at least, she did for a solid minute while he worked.

"You've been looking at the cup for a while," Ophis said and he frowned. He had left his cup behind after finishing it, after all. "The cups are reaching for each other," she commented, turning towards him and tilting her head. "You know that, right?"

"The cups reach for each… other," he repeated, slowly realizing that she wasn't talking about cups of tea. 'Sephiroth Graal?' he hazarded a guess in his mind, his back straightening.

"Their patience is running out though," Ophis commented, her attention going back to her drink. Or, at least, her eyes.

"The cups'?"

"Khaos," she answered and he felt a cold shiver run down his spine. Were they about to make a move already? "They are considering something reckless," she added and he almost wanted to ask. Would that be appropriate? Was she already giving him all that she was willing to or…? "Less stable, they think it might not be too bad," she said with a shrug before finishing her cup of tea. "It'll be noisy, especially if the creature is let out of its cage. I thought Red and the creature might take each other out… but it might just make it all worse," Ophis commented and Joshua was getting more and more unnerved the more she talked.

He wanted to ask so many things, yet he couldn't seem to find his voice. He almost wondered if Ophis had done something to silence him. Or, maybe, she had just surprised and scared him enough with what she was saying.

"I like the quiet here. I don't want more noise," she told him as she stood up. "You might just give me Silence, if of a different kind. I want to try that. More noise sounds unpleasant and I don't want that," she declared before going inside one of the rooms.

And Joshua, he was left to analyse what he'd just been told.


[} Chapter End {]

Hey guys! How's it going?

Ophis…

Ophis is a character…

Ophis is a character of all time, yes.

I'm kind of afraid of writing her now. She always pulls the weirdest shit, apparently. I just wanted to write a goddamn fluff scene with some tea! So… What the fuck was that?!

I swear to God. She must have seen that I had a half-formed path forward and decided no, fuck that. The Muse has an ally, apparently, because of course she does.

Now I'm gonna have to see if I can negotiate with Red to help me out, because this is just unfair.

And if not, Trihexa. Because fuck this.

Now, You Can Trust Me

Ophis's words kept replaying in his mind, over and over again.

It'd been a few days already and Joshua could hardly think of anything else other than those. He'd barely slept and he almost couldn't get any work done, even on things related to what he'd been told. It'd set him on edge in a way that didn't even let him focus. Any second, he waited for someone to bring him bad news, for one of his arrays to pick up something.

After so long with only a vague, distant threat in his mind, he couldn't cope with the much more on-his-face one that Ophis had presented. Because according to the dragon, Khaos was growing impatient and they could make a move at any point. Nothing they could try to pull off would be good, he just knew it. And the worst part was that he didn't even know what they were trying to do.

"Joshua," Yasaka said and he blinked blearily as he turned towards her. "You need to relax," she told him. Although, to be completely honest, the hand she placed on his arm helped more than the words. He focused on the softness of her fingertips on his skin. He focused on the subtle warmth, likely aided by her senjutsu mastery. His attention honed in on that and, for a second, his entire world was focused on his forearm.

"I know," he mumbled, taking a deep breath in as if that would help. It didn't. "I just… I don't know what to do, or if I can do anything," he admitted, and he was surprised at how easy it was to do that. Once upon a time, he'd have struggled, maybe even hidden such a thing. Because saying something like that, it'd have felt like a confirmation that he wasn't good enough, that he failed, like he did so many other things.

And even after he'd gotten good at what he did, after he'd found his calling of sorts in magic, he still would have felt like that.

Yet there, with Yasaka, it didn't feel like defeat. It simply felt like what it was, asking for help. Because Yasaka – and the others, for that matter –, they had seen him in lower lows and still remained supportive, caring. So, maybe he'd learned, at some point, that he could trust them, that they'd have his back no matter what, not even if he failed.

Or, maybe, he'd just learned that it was okay to fail, that it didn't make him a failure.

"There's much you can do, Joshua," Yasaka reassured, her hand squeezing his arm ever so slightly. "But not if you are so deep in your head that not even your own thoughts reach you," she said, and it sounded funny. It sounded like a contradiction of sorts, to say that he was thinking so much he couldn't think.

Except that it was accurate.

"You're not wrong," he replied, deflating where he sat and staring at the notebook in front of him, which he hadn't written anything on for quite a bit already. "I just… don't know where to begin, and I'm suddenly not sure if I even have time to do much."

"Well, if you don't do anything, then probably not," Yasaka said and she somehow managed to make that sound funny and reassuring rather than worrying and harsh. "But if you feel that way, then what's left for the rest of us?" she added and it sounded like a joking comment, but he could tell it wasn't.

"I'm sorry," he said then, an apologetic grimace on his face. "I know it's… I know it's kind of rude for me to say this stuff, but-"

"I'm not chastising you," Yasaka told him, reaching to grab his hand and giving it a reassuring squeeze. "You're capable and that makes you feel like you need to do more. It's admirable that you take that pressure on yourself, but don't let that overwhelm you, Joshua," she added and he knew she was right. He absolutely knew she was.

The problem was that knowing that didn't help him deal with the emotions nearly as much as he needed it to.

"Now, first things first," Yasaka said and he focused on her voice, hoping against hope that she'd have a solution for him, maybe some kind of senjutsu technique. She'd helped him so many times already, that he expected her to have something that could help him, he supposed. "What do you need to work on?"

"That… hasn't changed, really. Find Khaos, deal with Khaos," he answered almost immediately, yet… Had it been that simple when he'd been trying to think? Although-

"What do you need to do to achieve that?" Yasaka asked and that was the complicated part… Or so he felt, yet…

"Biggest clue I have right now is what Ophis said, about the Sephiroth Graal cups reaching for each other," he answered and where were the other hundred thoughts that would come to mind then? Well, some of them were in regards to how to do that, but-

"What do you need to do to use that?" Yasaka asked and he blinked.

"Spells that can sense that. I think Aika and I have been getting glimpses of it, but Ophis made it sound very obvious. Speaking of, maybe Aika can help," he summarized and he was surprised to find his thoughts… smoothing over, streamlining themselves. "Yes, I think… I have a few ideas," he mumbled, reaching for a pencil with his free hand and starting to write down a few ideas. Not all of them new, but certainly stuff that he could use with a bit of work in certain directions…

"And what else could you do?" Yasaka asked and he paused…

"I can prepare my defense arrays a little more. If they are trying to use Sephiroth Graal, broken or not, then I have a few ideas," he muttered to himself, noting down other ideas on another page. He had already worked on defenses against Sephiroth Graal and what Khaos could do in that regard, but he'd need to put more work on that, especially in regards to the likely broken and thus unstable nature of the use that the terrorist organization was likely to try and pull on them.

Going silent, Yasaka rested her head on his shoulder as he started working and he could have kissed her for the help.

And he did, after a bit once he got all his ideas out and in order.


[}-o-{]
​

"You're getting better," he commented idly, looking at Georg work on his Sacred Gear mastery some more.

He was still training to teleport things around inside his mist and he was, for the most part, succeeding. He was getting faster even, which was the important part. Soon, he'd be able to have complete control of the position of things – and people – inside his Gear's influence. Although, with each slight improvement in speed, his control kept having chances of slipping and sending something to the wrong spot or… half complete, as it were.

Concerning, but Joshua was sure that the man could work well enough if he slowed down, which was also kind of important. Pushing the limits of what he could do was the point of training though. The "guaranteed success" teleportation range in terms of speed was… not ideal, but it was acceptable. And it was getting better too, but…

Well, Joshua was a little concerned about how fast they could get to a good spot in terms of the man's skill.

"Thank you, sir," George replied, pushing his glasses up.

The ex-Hero Faction member was doing a lot better those days in terms of how he felt too, Joshua had noticed. The man was less terrified and more dutiful with each passing day. Maybe because he'd realized that he really would be fine so long as he behaved and that behaving wasn't some impossible standard placed on him. It helped that Joshua was slowly relaxing around the guy too, he supposed.

Maybe it was soft of him, but Georg was proving to have changed, so he wanted to forgive the guy a little more with each day that passed. That was not to say that he wouldn't just bring the man's worst nightmares to pass if he did something stupid, but he didn't seem to be heading in that direction, thankfully. Joshua didn't think it was unreasonable of him to expect decent behavior in exchange for forgiveness.

"Keep at it, Georg. Things will get hectic soon," he said and was very careful and thorough with the full scan that he made of the guy after saying that. Because, just because he had started to forgive the guy, it didn't mean that he had let his guard down or that he wouldn't keep an eye on him, especially in certain moments such as that. However, the man didn't react in any way other than nodding and getting started.

'Well, it seems that he's smarter than I thought,' Joshua thought to himself. A moment later, he decided that the Dimension Lost holder would be fine on his own and he could turn his attention elsewhere. Like towards his familiars, who were in some sort of messy battle royale amongst themselves.

Or Kokabiel, Raynare and Kuroka, who were fighting amongst themselves too. 'Speaking of…' he mused, looking at Raynare in particular. She was approaching the point in which he could give her another pair of wings. Between that and Incinerate Anthem, she might be able to finally beat Kokabiel with her own power. And that was without training to start pushing for the next step.

He took a deep breath in as he looked at them, his muscles suddenly felt stiff, his fingers itched for something and he found the sight of the battle somewhat… enticing. Before he knew it, he was already walking up to the trio and he noticed his familiars slowing down until they stopped, watching him. With a twist of his wrist and a wave of his fingers, he had Carnwennan and Setan Kober in his hands, the daggers eager for a fight in a way that True Longinus never was, familiar and alive in a way that the spear never quite reached.

"Hey," he called softly, his voice not even remotely loud. The two fallen and the reincarnated devil all stopped all the same, all but freezing mid-motion. They turned and stared and then paled as they noticed the weapons in his hands. "New exercise," he announced with a slight smile that he was pleased to see scared the fuck out of the trio. "You're all sparring with me," he told them and they stiffened.

That is, before Kokabiel shot the first light spear his way, because of course he did. The man was always ready for a fight, for one. For another, he hesitated very little, which he guessed was related to the first thing. Or maybe both of those were related to the fact that much of his life had been dedicated, consumed, by wars and battles. It was… sad, in a way, or so Joshua thought, at least.

All the same, the three of them fought him with all they had and he, in turn, fought them with… almost all he had. The arrays around the training room had several settings, but he didn't use any of them at that moment. Instead, he fought with everything else, his body, his skill, his senjutsu and his active spells… And then he started setting down a new array, simulating a fight outside of his designated areas.

Unlikely to happen, sure, but it paid to be prepared.

Maybe he'd been focusing too much on his spellcrafting – not that he thought that was bad –, but it felt incredible to let loose a little physically. His weapons certainly appreciated it, especially after True Longinus had arrived to cast a shadow over them. Better, the spear might be, but those daggers had more personality to them, quite literally, and they had helped him through battles in the past.

So, maybe he was a little attached to them, but he did feel like that and their personalities gave them a little more… edge, as it were. True Longinus didn't have that, even if the spear was quite literally able to pierce anything. There were still likely to be situations when Joshua would want something else, and that's when Setan Kober and Carnwennan would be able to shine.

And aside from all that, with how nervous he felt those days, it was nice to just… focus on something else and vent.


[}-o-{]
​

[Seekvaira Agares]

"So, yeah, I'm taking the day off," Davis said in what was supposed to be her second day working with him alone rather than with Ravel or Iryuka or both. Seekvaira supposed she should be grateful that hadn't happened on the first day, but still.

Something to get used to, she supposed.

It was still odd, to work for someone, for a human even, when she was the heiress of a Pillar House. House of Agares was even an important one, what with Agreas and all the resources the city held. It wasn't like they were a half extinct house or one of those that had always been small.

Yet there she was.

Because Joshua Davis was that ridiculous of an existence. Her father had taken one look at Ravel Phenex and the power the little girl held at her finger tips after Seekvaira told him about Sona's offer and almost the next moment there she was, offering. There was so much to gain and so little to lose by bowing their heads a little to the man, that it was just a no brainer, really.

That didn't mean that it was less odd for Seekvaira to be in that position, however. She wasn't displeased per se, but she did find it all very… awkward, as it were. It was strange, not at all what she'd known all her life. She found herself out of her depth, especially whenever she had to deal or even witness one of Davis' many eccentricities.

Such as the one she had encountered immediately after teleporting to the man's house.

"Sorry for wasting your time, but I'll be training here for the rest of the day, I think. If I'm not, I'll send a message," Davis said, all smiles and filled with an energy that she found new in him. Although, she hadn't known him for very long, admittedly. He was still usually very calm and borderline cold and calculative, not unlike Seekvaira herself, or Sona to put another example.

At that moment though, he reminded her more of Sairaorg.

She did wonder what was up with the dog-like eyes and the fangs that had replaced his teeth. She could ask Ravel about that, however. She didn't want to ask too many questions, especially ones unrelated to her job. Seekvaira might not be an expert in what it took to be a secretary, but she was pretty sure it didn't involve interrogating your employer.

"Did I have anything to do today?" he asked and she immediately stood straighter, pulling her own notepad – because she was not using the one with the Phenex seal, no way – and checked the schedule for the day. For whatever reason, Davis always seemed amused when they did that and she wasn't quite sure what that was about. At first, she'd thought it was just her doing something wrong without realizing, but even Ravel got that look.

The best the Phenex had been able to guess was that "he tends to think some things are a lot less important than they are", which was… crazy. How does one reach a point in which dealing with the Norse valkyries is unimportant? How does one reach a point in which they can laugh about forgetting they have an appointment with Heaven's Seraphs? Because yes, she'd seen both of those happening and she was still wrapping her head around both.

Admittedly, he was dating one of those Seraphs, but still.

"Just your Spell Modification class, sir," Seekvaira answered and the man nodded.

"Alright, I'm gonna give you some notes for Levi. He'll take over for me. Ravel will know the rest. You can take over that for today along with anything else you three might be doing," he told her as he absently moved to one side, summoning a notebook and starting to jot down things quickly. Seekvaira, for her part, just stared, processing what was happening.

Never in a million years would she have considered just… dropping responsibilities, duties, like that. Yet, there was Davis, ignoring his class and throwing an apprentice off the deep end because he felt like training some more. What a strange being she had started to work for, she couldn't help but think to herself all the while.

"There, sorry again for the inconvenience," Davis told her, passing her a few torn out pages of his notebook with class plans and ideas for Levi to work with. Good thing there were at least a few hours left until class, because Seekvaira could only imagine how difficult that'd be to pull off for the poor apprentice. "See you around," the magician told her then before walking off towards the training field.

Seekvaira took another moment to wrap her head around what'd just happened before teleporting.

"I think the carefree way he tends to deal with some things actually helps," Ravel pointed out about an hour later after Seekvaira was done setting things up for the class later that day.

Levi had not been a fan of the sudden change, but he'd taken that on the chin and rolled with the punches. Seekvaira could respect that. Maybe she should consider the man for a position as a contracted magician…

"It makes him seem all the more grand, since he can treat such things as minor," the Phenex continued and Seekvaira found herself agreeing with that opinion. "It can be infuriating, yes, but I don't think it's worth trying to correct. It's also a hopeless endeavor, as I understand it, so it's better to just use it to our advantage, or try to," she added dryly, with the tone of someone that was looking at a silver lining rather than at an actual positive. "Now, about tomorrow's schedule, I'll be the one directly involved and I'll need most of the day to instruct Mr. Davis, but you will have jobs of your own to carry out too. First, you, Seekvaira…"


[}-o-{]
​

[Göndul]

"Thanks for organizing this in such a short notice," Davis said and she couldn't help but stare at the man.

He'd just teleported in, to be fair, but it'd only taken those few seconds for Göndul to notice that something was different in him. He held himself with his back straight and his expression closed off. Gone was that eager and curious expression he had during their classes, or the open if often distracted features she'd gotten used to seeing when he was teaching others.

Instead, those deep lakes that he called eyes were now frozen and his expression belied nothing. Beside him, the little Phenex walked with none of that quiet, forced professionalism that she used to make up for her employer's lack of care. For once, Davis actually looked the part of the individual that he was, the faction leader that he was, the force of nature that he was.

And Göndul found that incredibly unnerving.

"It was no problem," she said and she meant it.

Getting a call from Davis to set up a meeting with Odin wasn't what she'd expected, but it was certainly welcome. Her faction very much wanted to get involved with the man, and the alliance behind him if possible. It was regrettable that things had been… less than ideal before, but with the rise of Davis' reputation, let alone how he'd helped the other factions grow stronger too, that was no longer a problem.

So, considering their dealings with the man, they had hoped to get another invite to the alliance.

The time seemed to have come, but...

"Odin, thank you for making time for us," Davis said after following her to meet her faction leader. However, she was looking at him closely, and she could tell his smile was barely a mockery of one. His eyes remained cold, empty, the man walked forward to shake hands with Odin like one would an enemy faction in a neutral setting.

Had they done something to anger Davis? Göndul had to wonder, because things weren't making any sense. Maybe it'd been her valkyries, or maybe someone in their faction had done something without the rest of them knowing. She really, really hoped it hadn't been Loki, or that at least it hadn't been too bad.

"Joshua Davis," Odin greeted, apparently not at all bothered by the disposition of the human magician. "How could I not, after the impression you left on my people?" the old god asked and Göndul acknowledged the truth of it, even as she remained standing by the door.

The Gods of Asgard hadn't shut up about the man that seemed to just… understand magic the same way a good husband understands his beloved wife.

"Well, you didn't seem to have it some before, so I had to wonder," Davis answered, his smile growing even less like a real one, which was kind of impressive… At least, it would have been, if it weren't for what he'd said, what that meant.

"Alliances are complicated at the best of times, I'm sure you're aware," Odin replied, unbothered, or maybe trying to keep the peace. It could even be both. "It was nothing against you or your allies."

"I'm sure," Davis replied dryly. "I'm not here to talk about the past though, but I am here to talk about our factions collaborating," the human started. "Certain new developments have forced my hand, alas."

"Well, I thought you were never going to ask again, boy," Odin said and Göndul held back a grimace. That was not something that needed to be pointed out like that, she felt. It was bad enough that they had forced Davis to come and ask them again after his allies and him had been ignored before. She understood the why, of course, but still.

Any moves on the board were risky, yes, let alone when they involved several powers at once. It was why faction alliances were rare. The more that were involved in such moves, the more attention, the more enemies, the more tension. Things were already difficult enough around the world those days without adding more risks.

"Now, tell me about this alliance," Odin said and Göndul watched a new development on Davis' face at that moment. Instead of the cold mask that he'd been wearing, his lips pulled up and his eyes softened into something… amused.

"Who said anything about an alliance?" Davis asked and both Odin and Göndul paused. "No, I'm here to make a deal with you, Odin. Nothing more, nothing less. You do something for me and I do something for you, end of the story."

"That… is unexpected," her faction leader replied slowly, carefully.

"Is it?" Davis asked, turning to look at the Phenex girl beside him. His expression was still colored by amusement all the while as they communicated something between themselves without words. "You weren't interested in an alliance with us and we respect that. So, we came up with a new arrangement that will hopefully fit your wishes better," the man said as he turned back to Odin.

And Göndul felt herself grow nervous, as she understood the message implied.

"You rejected us, so we're not going to ask again. If you want an alliance, ask yourself."

"I see…" Odin replied, very clearly considering the new development. So much so that his usual borderline clownish behavior was nowhere to be seen even when it'd been very slight to begin with as he tested the waters. He hadn't even had time to get started before that'd had to be pushed aside, evidently. "And this deal you wanted to make… what does it entail?"

"We're trying to stop Armageddon," Joshua started with, tilting his head with a smile. "So, we were hoping you would help us with that, and in turn, well," he added, his lips pulling back even more into something that probably was meant to be friendly but ended up coming across as… dangerous. "It'd only be fair if we helped you with Ragnarök, wouldn't it?"


[} Chapter End {]

#1,552
Slow to Rise in Here

[Joshua Davis]

"That was exhausting," he said, dropping on the table like all his energy had left him. It certainly felt like that to him, at least, so… Either way, they'd just come back from the meeting with Odin, which had been an entire ordeal and had reinforced the already deep-rooted dislike for politics that he had. He still didn't understand why so much song and dance was necessary, but…

'If it gets things done, I guess,' he thought to himself, pulling his body up with a groan.

He did understand the insult that every faction had delivered to them when they rejected their offers for an alliance against Khaos, even though he hadn't when it happened. It annoyed him plenty, really, after taking a bit to consider it. He understood the reticence to try again less, but that might be because he wasn't a very prideful guy and politics kind of were built upon pride, your own as a leader as much as your factions'.

And from there, it got more and more complicated as he was explained why he had to act like he did through the meeting. 'Thank God for the acting gig we have with Serafall, certainly helps in situations like this,' he thought, running his fingers through his hair. He'd have given anything to not be the one to go have that conversation, yes, but his partners seemed to think the good impression he'd delivered during that one gathering was enough to make him a better candidate.

At least they'd be the ones talking with other factions, thankfully.

"You did great, Mr. Davis," Ravel praised and he wondered if that was supposed to make him feel better. It was always awkward to be complimented by a child. Admittedly, he'd never underestimate the Phenex girl's competence… but she was still a girl, so it made things a lil' weird. There was no changing that though, so he'd just have to deal with it.

"Thank you, Ravel," he replied with a smile on his face, even if he couldn't get rid of the exhaustion. He knew some people would call him dramatic, but dealing with people normally already drained him like crazy. Stuff like what he'd just gone through? He'd need a few days of being a proper hermit to feel like he could tackle someone other than family again. "Couldn't have done it without you," he added, and his smile became the slightest bit more full just seeing how pleased and proud the girl looked after he said that.

Admittedly, Yasaka, Serafall and Gabriel had also helped him a lot to figure out what he needed to do and say and the general approach of the meeting. However, Ravel tended to have an easier time dumbing things down for him and she had more free time to just coach him through everything. On top of that, just the fact that she could accompany him everywhere was a boon, because Joshua would keep an eye on her through Magic Sense and Life Sense so that he could realize if he messed up at any point.

"Just doing my job, Mr. Davis," the girl mumbled through her smile and he shot her an amused smile. She was great at a lot of things, but she seemed unusually weak to compliments…

Which had some worrying implications, but Joshua wasn't going to delve into those. Instead, he'd just endeavor to praise her as much as possible. Not something complicated, considering she was so skilled in things that he was terrible at, so he had a lot to praise her about. Nevermind the fact that she was always helping him with things even outside her job description, as it were.

Joshua did make a mental note to check with his partners if he might need to pay the Phenex a visit.

Because Ravel was a lot more than just his assistant of sorts.

In the meantime…

"Please, tell me that we have nothing else to do," he all but begged… and the pitying look he got was not what he wished to see. "Please?" he tried anyway, visibly making the girl gather the will to speak, which only made him feel worse. It wasn't Ravel's fault that his schedule was shit.

One day, he'd be able to just not deal with people more than once a week.

He couldn't wait.

"Carmilla said she'd have results to show in her searches by today," Ravel told him and he was already going to say they could make the vampire wait. Apparently, the Phenex girl had seen that coming though. "And yes, you could make her wait, but it'll set a precedent where she doesn't need to stick to deadlines… and you did say that Valerie related things took precedence over anything that wasn't pressing and directly Khaos Brigade related."

"I hate myself," he grumbled, running his fingers through his hair. "When do we need to be there?" he asked wearily. "Because if you say right now, I might cry."

"... We can go in an hour if that works for you, Mr. Davis."

She'd been about to say they go right that moment. He knew it. She knew it. She knew he knew it, even. Joshua really did not know how to feel about that. Neither the fact that he'd been expected to jump from one meeting to the other nor the fact that he was being pitied by a child.

"Why are you so cruel with me, Ravel?" he asked with a grimace. Because it was definitely her fault that things were that packed together. He wouldn't scold her – he was too soft for that, especially after the thoughts regarding the girl he'd just had –, but he definitely considered it. That counted for something, right?

"Just doing my job, Mr. Davis," she answered, more amused than anything, which was good. "You're too capable, which means there's a lot to do."

"I hate myself," he repeated, slumping on the table. "Did Koneko say anything about dropping by?"

"Not that I know of. Do you want me to ask?" Ravel said and he was fairly sure she'd slipped out of her professional attitude a little there… Although, maybe he was just imagining it.

"If you would. I'm gonna need to recharge batteries after this day, so I was thinking we could get the three of you together and play some games," he commented, not even needing to clarify who the third was. It wouldn't help his exhaustion, but spending time with his daughters would be fun and make him feel better.

Maybe he'd even drag his familiars into it too… except maybe Nagini. She was getting more aloof by the day.

Teenagers, honestly.


[}-o-{]
​

[Penemue]

"Josh is working on how to give more wings, a third pair, to be exact," Serafall commented, humming happily as she drank from her milkshake. Penemue, for her part, could only stare while her coffee got colder by the second, because… that was not what she expected to hear when she got called by the three women that were in the process of turning her life upside down.

And she still didn't know if it was for the better or the exact opposite to let them.

She just knew that she had to do something.

"Raynare is doing a lot of work to motivate him. You should thank her if you see her," the devil woman added, smiling at her in a way that seemed half mocking and half amused. Thanking a traitor, she was suggesting that Penemue thank a traitor. For that's what Raynare was, Raynare, Kokabiel and the other two, who were now being worked barely better than slaves.

Because their faction was falling behind, and they couldn't afford to lose anything, and those two might not have gotten extra wings, but they were at the peak of their wing class. So, they had their uses, but Penemue wouldn't be thanking them and she wouldn't thank Raynare either. Although… Serafall wasn't wrong. The woman was likely the cause for many of the boons they enjoyed those days.

And Davis' capacity for forgiveness worked both ways, she supposed. He had patience with Azazel's blunders just as much as he did with Raynare and the rest. It was just that the Stray had gotten the better deal just by virtue of behaving better and grasping the opportunity she was offered with both hands.

How ironic, in many ways.

"Now," Serafall started then and Penemue wondered if she was going to have to swallow her pride even more or not. The answer was most likely yes, but she could hope, she supposed. Not much else she could do. "How's your end of things?" the devil asked, a friendly smile that failed miserably at hiding the fact that they – all three of them, and maybe Davis but she had her doubts – had her firmly under their thumbs. "Any progress?"

She said that so easily, asked so casually, as if they hadn't asked her to basically turn her fellow Fallen against Azazel. Azazel, who had led them through the wars. Azazel, who was the strongest of them all, who had been the leader they all needed, who had rallied their scattered, messy selves into a faction strong enough to oppose Heaven and Hell. The man might be a mess, even more so those days, but he was still their leader, what Michael and Lucifer were for the other two factions.

She couldn't just talk to a few people and suddenly have the support they asked of her.

"Slow progress," she admitted all the same, keeping all her bitter complaints to herself.

Because, in the end, she'd been the one who agreed. Because much as she hated her situation, seeing Azazel slowly but surely burning every single bridge around them had pushed her to her limit. She couldn't just sit there and let him keep doing that until they were surrounded by enemies. She had to do something.

So, she was doing something.

She hated it, but she was doing something.

"If Davis can really do as you say-" And Penemue had no reason to believe otherwise, honestly. "-, then we can work something out. I'm sure I can use that in my favor." Especially because Azazel would leave everything in her hands, meaning she could twist things a little to benefit her goals. And if he was there, he was most likely going to keep dragging his own reputation through the mud in front of other Fallen.

A win-win situation, if there ever was one.

Except both still felt like losses to her.

"What you've been doing is a start, but that's only provided we can keep it up for long enough that everyone has time to consider things, change their minds," she added and Serafall hummed. The three of them hadn't just come and started threatening her, after all. They'd pulled her into a pseudo alliance.

They'd empower her position so that she could be more useful to their actual alliance. In exchange, she… gained an empowered position. On top of that though, they were helping her faction, not in huge ways, but they were and she appreciated that.

Serafall was, apparently, allowing reincarnated fallen to have an easier time all around, allowing easier promotions and enforcing what few rights they had more thoroughly. Yasaka, on the other hand, was using her connections to ease a lot of business that they were doing in her territory and even the East's. And she gave them access to senjutsu arts services from her people, which was huge in a number of ways.

Both of those paled when compared to Gabriel though, her fellow angel allowing the fallen to be closer to Heaven than they ever had been after falling. They couldn't step into Heaven again, she doubted that'd ever happen, but they could be close to it again. Penemue herself had already gone way more times than she'd like to admit. Furthermore, connections that had been severed when they fell, they were being allowed to be mended, those that could be. Close brothers and sisters that had been separated were being allowed to reunite, to interact, to bond once more.

And that may sound like nothing, but to her people?

It was already causing waves, and it would only get better.

"Keep working diligently, Penny,-" Serafall said, beaming at her even as her eye twitched. "-and things will only get better from here." For a terrifying moment, Penemue feared that the Satan had actually read her mind. Then she realized that couldn't be… and that was worse, because that meant she was being read like a book.


[}-o-{]

[Issei Hyoudou]

"Thank you for this," he said, and it was a testament to how much he'd been through that same moment that he didn't even feel awkward. After all, the man was basically a stranger, and that was without including the rest of the situation, which was also a little offputting.

"It was our pleasure," the man across from him said. "Seriously. Not everyone can say they trained with the Red Dragon Emperor," he added and that was certainly awkward for Issei, but he was getting better.

[They should be proud, yes,] Ddraig growled in his mind. [Everyone that can relate themselves to us is someone that history will write about, even if it's just a footnote sometimes.] That was weird too, but Issei guessed that was his life and he'd have to get used to it.

"Same time next week, then?" he asked, forcing the words out the same way he was trying to do with the conversation.

Sure enough, everyone was up for that. Not that he expected differently. Aika had talked him into asking Joshua for help training, and he'd ended up with an invitation to House of Water himself. Instead of learning magic though, the association had contacted a bunch of mercenaries and such to train him and with him. A poor replacement for training with Joshua, even with the training arrays the man set up, but it was what it was.

Ultimately, it fixed one of the problems they had, he supposed. They still weren't having nearly as many sessions as they had once, but there was little to be done about that. For one, because Joshua was super busy, and seemed to get busier every day, really. For another, because Issei felt bad for taking up his time when he was so busy.

He knew Joshua would make time if he actually asked, but he didn't want to get in the way. So, he'd have to make do with their conversations when they happened to both be at the man's cafe. And other odd times, like when he went to pick up Jeanne at school for whatever reason or such occasions. All in all, Issei wasn't seeing the man much, but he tried not to be too sad about it.

[Stop being so pitiful, would you? This is pathetic.]

He wasn't always successful, evidently, and Ddraig loved to remind him.

All the same, the man wasn't any less important to him than he'd been back when they trained together and met up more often. Because Joshua was still the guy that had changed Issei's life, in so many ways too. He felt like a better person, instead of just acting like one. He had a girlfriend and his studies were going well, what with all the study dates and making other friends to have study sessions and such rather than… Well, what he used to do with his old friends.

He'd also turned Issei into someone important.

[You were always going to be.]

Issei wondered about that though. Because he'd been a mess, so even being the Red Dragon Emperor didn't feel like it'd be enough to make him less of an idiot and a pervert and a disgrace. And he wondered how that would have looked, if he'd never met that crazy man.

"Issei!" Aika said once he took a shower after training and then made his way through the halls of the magician association – feeling thoroughly like an outsider, but he was getting better at dealing with that too – towards where she was having her lesson/study session with the other Stars, as people seemed to call Joshua's magic apprentices.

Idly, Issei wondered if they had a nickname for him too, or if they would if they knew more about him.

"Had fun fisting and getting fisted?" she asked then and he grimaced. She didn't need to say it like that. She really, really didn't. "Or were those men using their long, hard swords today?" she added, and she made it sound ten times worse than the words already would have by themselves. He'd have found it impressive if it weren't so thoroughly embarrassing and uncomfortable.

The fact that they weren't by themselves only made it that much worse.

He could see the guys in her study group grimacing behind her, one of them even shot him a sympathetic look. Issei wondered if they suffered his girlfriend's antics too. Because he loved Aika, he really did, but she was a character and a half. Not that he was one to talk though, admittedly, but still.

"Do you have to do that?" he asked her, and he knew she knew what he meant. She stood up from where she'd been sitting at the round table with the rest of the other apprentices and approached him.

"Yes," she told him, beaming. And damn him, if she wasn't pretty like that. It almost made it worth the awkwardness. Almost…

Oh, who was he kidding?

"Do you still need more time here?" he asked and his answer came in the form of Aika taking his arm and dragging him to the chair she'd been sitting at before. Then he made him sit there and then she sat on his lap. "I'll take that as a yes," he commented and a part of him felt a little self-conscious with everyone in the room looking at them… but there was a much bigger part of him that was just happy to be with his girlfriend.

So he just wrapped his arms around her and read over her shoulder even though the text made no sense to him.

"Just a little longer, then we can go to the cafe and get that cake you like," Aika told him and he had a funny feeling that he was the one supposed to say stuff like that. In his defense though, the cake was really good. And spending more time with his girlfriend sounded even better.


[}-o-{]

[Joshua Davis]

Carmilla was surprisingly effective.

Or she'd gotten lucky.

Either way, she'd procured a bunch of vampires for him to study. Normal vampires of different kinds, women, men, younger, older. None of them children, thankfully, although some vampires a little younger than offered would have helped more, it'd also have been… a little too much. Besides, he rather doubted there'd be many – if any – of those that were heinous enough to warrant his… research approaches.

Beyond that, Carmilla had even found a few dhampirs, some even had Sacred Gears, and then there were vampires with other special abilities even.

There were all sorts of vampire flavors for Joshua to try things out and find out things about. That was what it all boiled down to, really. He needed it to see what might be different in Valerie's soul compared to everyone else. Because sure, every soul was different, but it didn't mean there were no similarities, the same way that two humans were more similar to each other than to, say, a devil… Generally speaking. Because the DxD supernatural world was crazy and had miracles and "miracles" all over the place.

"You've done good work," he commented and he heard Ravel take note of either that or something else almost immediately afterwards. As for Carmilla herself, the vampire queen preened, a smug smile tugging at her lips in a way that made him want to take back the compliment. Alas, she was an ally. A helpful one even, which was rather depressing that it was such a plus in her favor, but such was Joshua's life. "Ravel," was all he said.

"Got it," the little Phenex replied, stepping forward and starting conversation with Carmilla.

Making deals for money felt off, he'd admit. He hadn't made a supernatural deal for money in forever, really. Because one or two payments had been enough for him to live comfortably for the foreseeable future. Everything else afterwards was just overkill, really. Furthermore, he had a lot more use for favors or knowledge and other such payments.

Joshua wasn't even the only one thought like that.

However, Carmilla was leading the vampire factions – or was it just a faction by then? –, factions that had suffered a great many losses and were recovering still. To them, ridiculous amounts of money were useful. Especially if it didn't come with more strings attached, which he reassured her there wouldn't be. She'd seemed disbelieving in the moment, but had ultimately agreed anyway.

So, there they were. He'd even thrown in a few minor magic artifacts and such that Ravel had reassured him would be helpful and wouldn't go too much against the spirit of "no more strings attached" promise he'd given. Which was great, because he was starting to like Carmilla in the same way he liked Elizabeth. They were capable, reliable women that he could call upon if he needed something and know that they wouldn't screw him over, willingly or not.

Joshua had come to appreciate such people a lot.

It was very nice to just be able to give someone a call when he needed resources or knowledge regarding something for a project.

"Now then…" he mumbled to himself, going back to studying the subjects Carmilla had provided.

All things considered, he was rather optimistic in his progress. He didn't know if he was going fast enough, but he wasn't going slow per se, so he'd take it. Carmilla had really made things much easier for him. Beyond her, however, Penemue had also helped a lot… and he wasn't sure why.

His partners had asked him to trust them on that though, so he tried not to think about it too much.

The fact of the matter was that the fallen angel's ultimate secretary had given him access to a lot of Sacred Gears and holders to study, both original ones and artificial ones. So, between that and all that Carmilla had gotten her… He had a lot of data. A lot of data that felt kind of… not as connected as he'd have wished, admittedly.

'What am I missing?' he wondered idly in between research sessions.

Glancing to the side, he saw Ravel dutifully keeping her eyes on her notes and away from what he was doing, as instructed. He wasn't going to let her see what he was doing to those vampires, even if they were pieces of shit. On top of that, there was a small array just generally keeping her from picking up on anything on his side of things anyway.

Carmilla, by her side, wasn't given that and she looked like she might have needed it. Joshua made a mental note to offer it to her the next time. As it was, he had other things to focus on, because he was struggling with something, even with the many resources he was given.

'Sacred Gears are all different, that side of things is messing with everything,' he thought to himself, taking a deep breath in and considering that. Furthermore, all Longinus were wildly different from each other, so the ones he had access to weren't doing him many favors… if any. The vampire side of things helped, as did the dhampir and human side, admittedly. However, it was the Sacred Gear that was key at that moment.

After all, tracking the pieces of Sephiroth Graal and giving those back to Valerie should at least be a start.

'How do I approach this if not with just Sacred Gear and species information?' Joshua wondered, taking a deep breath in and thinking. 'Effect? I don't know anything that quite does what Sephiroth Graal does, do I?' he asked himself, going over everything he knew. 'Twilight Healing, sort of… Maybe Jeanne can make some swords with similar effects…'

The problem was that he'd already tried those and they weren't quite right. He needed something more than just healing, something more than just slight changes. Sephiroth Graal could modify the essence of a creature, their life and their soul, able to create monsters out of nothing and bring back to life monsters long dead. So, Joshua needed to find something… like… that.

'Fucking…'

"Ravel, we're leaving."

#1,568
I See a Tunnel Full of Light Again

So, his newest epiphany wasn't useless.

It wasn't as good as he'd have liked either, admittedly, but Joshua was happy with any increase in progress. Especially those days, when it felt like anything he wanted to do was a huge undertaking that would take him years and he needed to cut down to weeks or months. He hated the rush, the pressure, but it wasn't like he could do anything other than grit his teeth and do it anyway.

What alternatives did he have? Let Khaos win?

Yeah…

No.

'It's similar… ish,' he thought to himself, watching a rather tense Katerea.

Because her incomplete Power of Sea was actually rather similar to what he knew of Sephiroth Graal. It only worked on herself, and only in regards to maritime creatures, but it did. It changed her essence, shaped her existence into something else, gave her new properties and shedded others. A change to behold and exactly the kind of effect that the Longinus was supposed to have on people it was used on.

He'd even been able to check that too, analyzing the vampires from the Tepes faction that were affected by the Sacred Gear and comparing them to the Carmilla faction ones. It was almost like they were completely different species, actually. Their everything was changed, not unlike when he gave angels and fallen new wings, but more drastic. There was only a remnant of who – what – they were supposed to be, just like there was always at least a remnant of Katerea deep down no matter how much she changed herself.

"Change," he instructed and the devil did exactly that, applying her Power to shift into some unholy – never more accurately put, he supposed – sea creature. And the process of changing was fascinating on its own, to see the way her soul and existence twisted and morphed into something else entirely. Beyond that though, he caught glimpses of similarities between that and the Grail, which was what he was looking for.

Because the Power of Sea was, essentially, the most similar thing he had access to – and could even think of, really – to the Sacred Gear in terms of effect. Between that and every other little piece of data he had managed to find in regards to other things – vampires, humans, dhampirs, Sacred Gears, Longinus, holy artifacts, holy Sacred Gears, etc. –, Joshua thought he could get somewhere if he arranged them in a good enough puzzle. Although, he could only hope that it'd be that easy, admittedly. He was honestly expecting it to be a nightmare to get through, but he had a goal and an approach and that was more than he'd had before.

At least, at that moment, it felt like he had all the pieces, so that was something.

"Keep changing," he said and the creature shifted from some kind of shark existence to an eldritch coral structure of some kind and then onto… algae? And so on, none of them the same, even when she started cycling through different kinds of fish-based forms. Joshua had to hand it to her, she knew how to use her power and she knew her sea creatures. Or, maybe her Power came with some innate ability to just… pull something like that off, but he doubted.

Maybe she'd decided to do the best she could with her faulty Power, which… he could respect, honestly.

"Strange," Friday communicated to him, and he agreed with the living spell wholeheartedly. Although, it was rather amusing to "see" her trying to put together the puzzle pieces herself. It gave him the mental image of a child trying to fit forms through holes and getting stumped when shapes that should fit didn't. Not that he was doing much better himself, but that was the picture that her emotions and stray thoughts painted in his head.

"Thank you," he said out loud, making Katerea stop, going back to her base form. "You can stay around here, if you want," he decided, much to the devil's surprise. Mainly, it was because Joshua wanted her close by in case he needed to test or check something regarding her Power. However, it wouldn't hurt to make her think that- "I think you've earned that much. Don't leave the property though," he told her.

Not that she could leave the property if she wanted, but maybe it was worth checking if she'd try.

Although, admittedly, he felt like a politician handling things like that. Ravel seemed rather proud from where she was standing off to the side, which kind of confirmed it. Joshua had very conflicting feelings regarding that possibility, but if it worked in his favor… He just hoped he wouldn't turn into an idiot like most politicians tended to.

His partners would probably give him a good smack and set him straight though, so he wasn't too scared.

"Thank you," the devil said, rather stiffly and unsure, but he didn't much care for that.

His attention was already on what he'd learned and trying to apply it though. And also on checking if there were any puzzle pieces he could be missing. There were probably some, but none that he could think of. He'd keep an eye out though, and maybe ask some of his contacts. Because Power of Sea might be the closest thing that he could think of in regards to Sephiroth Graal's effects, but there had to be some more, surely.

Maybe he could even find them… but that might be tricky.

As it was, he also needed to find ways to piece together the puzzle with what he had, which was not going to be easy in itself. After all, things were rarely that easy in general, let alone when they involved Sacred Gears. The fact that it was a Longinus just added insult to injury.

Penemue's recent cooperative streak might help in that regard though…

'I'll tell the others to deal with that,' Joshua decided, because it devolved into having to talk with Azazel… Well, he wasn't keen on doing that anytime soon. Not if he could help it, and he definitely could. So, instead, he focused on his side of things.

He'd make it up to his partners somehow.


[}-o-{]
