[Dion Fortune]

"Sounds… complicated," she replied hesitantly, slowly.

"Tell me about it," Professor Davis said with a wry smile that made her at least feel somewhat like she wasn't a dumb idiot for thinking what he said was absolute madness. Not that she'd tell him that either way. He had come to her for advice on the subject, so she would do her best and keep her opinions to herself, but…

Mixing all the properties that he mentioned? In a way that worked?... That was insane. It was no wonder the process ended with a Longinus, really. And he wanted her help to put that together? She was a good magician, if she did say so herself, but Dion knew she was nowhere near qualified for such an undertaking.

And yet, Davis had come to her.

"Professor Davis, can I ask… why is it necessary to put it together?" she asked and the man paused, considering her question with all the seriousness she'd expect from a colleague rather than a teacher. Dion found a little bitter amusement in the fact that not nearly half her actual colleagues had treated her with that much respect, at least not before she'd made a name for herself due to Davis himself. If anyone had the right to treat her – them, really – like less than, then it was him, but he never had.

"Because I need to know what the full picture looks like if I want to know what's missing and how to find it," the man said slowly, which… made some sense. As much sense as anything could when considering the circumstances, at least. "I know I'm missing something. The piece of Sephiroth Graal is supposed to be trying to reach for the rest of it, but I don't know how to figure out the way to follow that. So, maybe if I know what's missing, or how it's supposed to look whole, that'll give me an idea."

"And using the piece you have to scry out the rest…" she started, trailing off because she knew he had to have considered that already. Aika was a Divination magician, after all, so there was no way he'd considered Dion for the absolute madness he'd brought to her and not Aika when finding out about stuff was the whole point of her branch. Right?

"Aika and I are already regularly meeting to try and figure out a way to do that. But we're lacking some information, hence…" the man himself said, finishing off his sentence with a vague wave of his hand towards the notes and everything else that he'd brought to her.

"Alright…" she mumbled, looking at the notes with something akin to dread. However, she wouldn't – couldn't – say no. She'd just have to try and hope it'd be enough instead. "So, what I do is combine effects and energy for spells, so it's a little out of my area… but I'll see what I can do," she said, considering where to even start with the entire thing.

"That's all I ask," Davis replied with a smile that seemed both relieved and proud at the same time, somehow. That wasn't really helping Dion feel any better about the entire thing. Because she knew it was unlikely that she'd be able to help.

She had to try anyway though.

Part of trying would be to ask some of his other fellow Stars and pull some of the strings she'd managed to spread around since things had taken a turn in her life. She didn't have the pull that Davis had, nor the one that House of Water had, but she might just have the one person they'd need that those two didn't. And besides, their contacts would be different. One never knew if that might just be enough.

It'd be by sheer luck, but sometimes that was all that you needed.

Dion made a mental note to bring that up with the rest of the Stars. A miracle between all of them was marginally more likely than it'd be by herself. Those were the odds she was working with, but it wasn't like the alternative was much better, right?

"Do we know the difference between effects?" she asked as she skimmed through one of the notebooks full of information. Davis, already working on his own stuff, looked up and blinked at her as he processed her request.

"Yes, it's somewhere on the third quarter of this one," he commented idly, pulling another notebook from under a pile and giving it to her. "Pre-separation and post-separation effect. From both Valerie's side and Khaos' side," he explained and sure enough, she found what she was looking for after some more skimming. "Looking for something in particular?"

"I just thought that might be easier for me to understand," she answered somewhat self-consciously. Although, that was silly of her. It wasn't like Davis expected her to succeed. He was just doing what she was thinking about doing, throwing everything at the wall and checking if something stuck, by some miracle. At least it made her feel better to know that she'd reached the same conclusion as her teacher, in a way.

Although, it stung a little too, but the man was probably feeling just as bad, really.

Alas, as it turned out, that part of Davis' information wasn't easier to understand for her. 'Worth a shot,' she thought, lamenting herself. So, it was back to square one for her once more, but it'd been too much to hope for anyway.

Thus, time passed her by and a few minutes turned into an hour, then into two.

Although, as she continued reading through that particular notebook, with all the dedicated information regarding Sephiroth Graal's activation and usage… She found that there was one thing that wasn't anywhere on it. Still, not wanting to interrupt again, she continued reading. She'd already pulled the man out of his thoughts once already and she felt like it'd be lazy of her to ask before she at least put some effort into looking for what she'd thought of.

But when their time was nearing its end, she decided to go for it rather than wait for whenever Professor Davis decided to have another session like that one.

"I was checking the activation effects," she commented and the man raised an eyebrow at her. "It doesn't say anything about effects it might have on the pull you say the pieces have towards each other."

"Because nothing seems to happen. If the pull's noticeable, the activation doesn't seem to be…" Professor Davis started explaining before he slowed down and trailed off a bit. "... any more obvious than in dormant state…"

"Professor?" Dion asked, because that looked like a breakthrough if she'd ever seen one.

"Sorry, I have to go check on something," the man told her, suddenly eager to get somewhere and do something. And she had no idea where or what. "Remember to tell Ravel that you helped me a lot next time you see her, alright? Don't be shy," he said.

And then he teleported away.

And Dion was left wondering what she'd clued him in on.

The curiosity alone would kill her, she was sure.


[}-o-{]
​

[Joshua Davis]

Not to toot his own horn, but Joshua was very proud that his idea had borne fruit.

He made a mental note to seek out outside perspectives whenever possible, especially if he was struggling. Maybe the people he talked to wouldn't have much of an idea of what was going on, but they could always say something outside of what he considered. 'It's also happened a lot, hasn't it?' he thought, pausing as he remembered at least two instances when that kind of situation played out.

All the same, he focused back to what he was doing almost instantly.

Because Dion had given him an idea. Maybe the activation of Sephiroth Graal didn't show any obvious effects… but that was on their side. What if Valerie using it had an effect on the other side? What if Valerie using her side of the Sacred Gear made the other side pull towards hers? If so, maybe the times when they thought they'd picked up on something were Khaos Brigade using their piece or pieces for something, maybe testing things out considering they were now trying to fix something.

'If so… Maybe we can find them,' he thought.

Immediately afterwards though, it was like someone threw a bucket of cold water at him. Because how was he supposed to do that? He didn't know where to look, after all. So, how was he going to know if somewhere out there, the Sephiroth Graal piece reacted when Valerie used hers? He could spread out a net of arrays to look for something, maybe. But that'd leave holes everywhere.

If the terrorists were somewhere in his area of influence, then he'd have found them already.

He could try to spread his reach more through the agreements he was making with other factions, for sure, but… Would that be enough? 'It might need to be enough,' he thought to himself, pursing his lips. That didn't sound good, at all. However, it was either that or thinking about something else. And considering he had come up with the idea by being inspired by his student when he had run out of good options and started looking for alternative approaches…

Well, it might really need to be enough.

"That's a worrisome face to see," Yasaka commented and he almost sighed. Instead, he offered her a helpless smile as a response and a shrug. "Well, that's reassuring," she added sarcastically. "Want to talk about it?" she asked and he had a denial at the tip of his tongue.

Joshua didn't like to worry his loved ones, in general. He wanted to worry them even less so when it came to his own failures and struggles. They all had plenty on their plates already too, considering his partners were all faction leaders, for example. Nevermind all the other extra things they were doing as part of the Anti-Khaos alliance.

Alas, it wasn't like he could make them let it go if they really wanted an answer.

"I just got an idea… but it feels like I'm running at a wall, again," he admitted, leaning away from his notes and sighing. "I keep getting hints and ideas and all these things… and Khaos is still out of my reach. It's frustrating," he explained and he felt horrible for doing that. Because Yasaka was in the same situation, wasn't she? They were all hunting the terrorists down and yet… nothing they did seemed to bring them any closer to the end of things.

"You're making progress, are you not?" she asked him with a patient smile and a soft tone. The same one she'd used more times than he cared to count with him. It was, just like most of those times, accompanied by her life energy wrapping around him like a soothing blanket. And that was accompanied, that time, by a few of her tails around body too. "That's not nothing, Joshua."

"Then why does it feel like it is?" he asked, even though he could almost feel his worries bleeding off of him by the second just with her and her life energy by his side. "They are out there, making plans and progressing and I'm… I feel stuck. They are gonna be ready eventually. If I can't find them, then they'll have the advantage," he said and he knew she knew all that. But… she had asked, hadn't she?

"We're all in the same situation as you," she said, moving to sit closer, leaning on his side and all. "You're not alone. We're working on this too and we're getting help. Eventually, we'll manage."

"And if we don't?" he asked, one of his hands absently running his fingers through the soft fur of one of her tails.

"Then we'll have to be strong enough to answer Khaos Brigade's plans when they strike," she answered bluntly. "It's not ideal, not at all. But there's nothing else for us to do, so that's what we have to do."

That was… not reassuring, or it wasn't supposed to be.

Yet, Joshua did find it somewhat comforting.

Because they'd do it, or they wouldn't. It wasn't their fault if they failed and that… that did take a bit of the weight off. Not a lot, not even enough, but it made things ever so slightly easier.

"Now, I believe that brilliant brain of yours will work better if you manage to relax. What do you say we go somewhere for something to eat, just you and I," Yasaka suggested and he smiled. "You did manage to make my range reach some new places, after all, and I'd like to enjoy that."

"That sounds perfect."


[}-o-{]
​

[The Rising Power to Live]

The world was forgetting that he existed.

Again.

Contrary to before, he was not going to allow it. It was not okay for it to happen. Because now… now he'd found a mission, a goal. He wasn't going to just let them all forget that he was there, that he was a threat. No, he had spent way too many years being nothing but a spectator of the world.

He had decided to step out into the world, so the world wasn't allowed to just think he was done. No matter how much the new little devils and the rest of the shining birds worked together, no matter how many pets and strangers they brought into the game, he wasn't going to let the indifference build again. He had a lot more to show the world and all his power, all his skill, they weren't going to just be ignored.

Unfortunately, just like they were underestimating him, he had underestimated them. He had thought the little strays from all over the world would be enough. Fools could only get so far, evidently, even if one gave them all the power in the world. They had ruined everything, but maybe it was on him, for thinking they'd be enough, even when given a sliver of Infinity to help them.

Now he'd lost the Ouroboros Dragon somehow and he just knew it had to do with the alliance of pests that had gotten in his way. He would even go as far as pointing at the one human amongst beasts, because he had repeatedly, stubbornly gotten in his way again and again. Joshua Davis was a human in name only, far as he was concerned, because no normal human would do half of what that one man was doing all over the world.

He had to be dealt with.

Everyone had to be dealt with.

So, that's why he moved, hating that he had to skulk around like a rat, but alas… Annoying times required annoying measures. One such measure was what he was doing at that very moment, walking through the ruins of an ancient city with stories almost forgotten and overshadowed, but nevertheless full of potential. Potential that he could very much use.

So, once he reached his destination, he ignored the way the magicians and other little pests he'd gathered around him inspected the area. He ignored his servant, always so idiotically determined to do his duty to the House. Instead, he put all his attention in his one prize, the one thing he'd gotten out of the entire mess that had befallen his organization, his project.

He pulled out the cup of the Holy Grail and inspected it.

It was cracked, the golden metal stained with dull grey and even sickly purple-black spots spread over its surface. It shone weakly even in bright light and in darker areas it even seemed to dim the light around it more than anything. Liquid poured inside went bad faster or outright disappeared. It was a mockery of what it was supposed to be, what it once was…

But maybe it could still be used.

Because he could no longer expect the little strays to help him fix the broken artifact. It'd been a stretch of the imagination to think they could before, but after they had continued to be raided and hindered… It was a fool's errand if he'd ever seen one. He was also having more and more trouble recruiting, what with how many losses they'd had to take.

No promises of power, riches and more could turn people towards a cause that they saw as lost already.

Fools, the lot of them.

However, he would show them, he would show them all and he had just the things he needed. Because he couldn't quite go with what he'd planned at first. Not then, not with how the Holy Grail had been wrecked. He couldn't risk ruining everything by his own hand. So, instead, he would need to do something different, run some tests… and maybe spread some chaos while he was at it.

The idea made him smile, but that would have to come later.

For the moment, they needed to get started right there in Thebes. He might have all the time in the world, but that didn't mean he could waste it. Not when his enemies were getting better and better with every passing day. So, he focused and channeled his magic into the Grail. He let it process the energy, and then…

Then he used it, spreading its power over the burial grounds that had taken him so long to find and access. He channeled its power… and found the presences there, never truly gone. He found them and he shifted them… except they started to twist themselves. The corrupting power went out of control almost immediately, but he could only watch, fascinated.

He watched what once had been mighty warriors turn into the kind of creature that Grandfather would have balked at. He watched beings the likes of which his enemies would cower at and grinned. Because this… this was much better than what he'd thought he would get. Not what he wanted, but better.

Oh yes.

'The world is not ready for these Spartoi,' Rizevim Livan Lucifer thought as he watched his creations rise. 'Not ready at all.'


[} Chapter End {]

#1,576
I Didn't Know I Was Blind

[Joshua Davis]

'You're sure you're fine?' he asked in his mind.

"Fine fine," Friday replied almost cheerfully. Some of that was lost in her determination and focus, however, but that didn't make her less adorable. If anything, it just gave Joshua the mental picture of a child very intently working on a drawing, tongue poking out and eyes narrowed. "I do this," she insisted, as if taking his amusement as doubt, which prompted him to reassure her of his confidence.

He did so while walking, feeling the weight of Morag's body clinging to his back.

Idly though, as he did so, he noted that Friday was getting places with her speech. She didn't even seem to be slipping all that much even when she tried more complex "sentences". Her "voice" came clear and more defined. She didn't sound like anyone in particular, but sometimes he thought he caught hints of both Serafall and Gabriel, interestingly.

He'd ask about it, but he felt like that'd be rude, sort of. He had tried to subtly get an answer anyway, but she'd seemed to divert from that topic when he approached it, not suspiciously, but obviously. Maybe because she didn't want to talk about it, which meant that he felt even more reluctant to push for it. Maybe she just wanted to keep that to herself, making it into an exclusively "her" thing.

Joshua could respect that.

"What are we doing today, daddy?" Morag asked, peeking over his shoulder curving half of her body over it. Giving her a piggyback ride was always a little awkward like that. After all, she could cling to his back with her spider legs, leaving most of her human body free to do whatever. It was sort of – but not really – like having her sitting on his shoulders, rather than a piggyback ride, he supposed.

"I thought we could just spend some time in Asia's garden," he commented, his left hand falling on top of Cheshire's head. She was in tiger form. She tended to be when he was free to pet her and walking, since that was at about the right height for it. Otherwise she was more likely to be in cat form unless they were fighting, in which case she'd just use the byakko form. "Nagini's already waiting for us there," he added.

Because the snake had a somewhat difficult time slithering around the place, what with her size. So, she'd either take her time slowly getting wherever she was going or she'd just have him teleport her. That latter one was the case that very day, for example. It was a shame that she didn't have a size changing skill like Cheshire, but maybe that was because she didn't care for it.

She never seemed particularly bothered by the limitations of her size, at least.

"But are we doing something there?" Morag asked, switching from peeking over one shoulder to the other. "Or are we just walking around?"

"Did you want to do something in particular?" Joshua asked, because it felt like maybe she was trying to get to something. "Because I'm down for pretty much anything," he said. He needed some time to get things done, after all.

And he also needed to wait before trying something he had in mind.

It was odd, to have to just… let a project sit there because he couldn't do much about it until something outside of his control happened. However, that was just the way the world worked, for the most part. It just hadn't happened to Joshua in particular for quite a while. Those days, however, he had to deal with his stalled project and with Khaos just remaining hidden.

They weren't even getting very many raids on random bases anymore.

They had either hunted down most of the organization or their targets had gotten that much better at hiding. The latter was a worrying possibility, but his partners did seem to think the former could be the case, or that it was at least a mix of the two things. The world was full of idiots and bad people, but it didn't have that many. Especially in the sense that those that were still around would be more wary of joining Khaos. Not all their raids and battles were public knowledge, but enough of them were that they'd give people pause.

So-

"I thought maybe I could make some web art about all of us. It's been a while," Morag answered, pulling him out of his thoughts and by then they were already halfway through the garden, with Nagini in sight. Joshua tried not to grimace at the little jorōgumo's words. That was basically her saying that he hadn't spent time with them for long enough for her to make one in quite a while. "Can we?" she pressed and he smiled a little.

"Sure, Nagini will love to just sit there curled up, for sure," he answered, his smile widening when he heard and saw her cheer. Then he glanced at the aforementioned snake and he saw her having a hissed conversation with a chirping Margalo. "Good luck convincing Margalo of that though," he added and that seemed to take some of the wind out of her sails. "Do you need Friday here?" Joshua added, because he'd feel bad if they left out the living spell, admittedly.

"She can join later if she's busy," Morag reassured him and he nodded.

He felt a little bad, but the living spell seemed fine with the arrangement before and also after he checked again just then. She had even seemed excited about working on her own, actually. At that very moment, she was studying Katerea on her own, having the devil using her Power over and over and trying to pick up stuff. She had also been the one to suggest it and on her own and Joshua hadn't wanted to shut her down or anything.

He also hadn't had any reason to do so, so there was that.

"Be there," Friday commented when he communicated the new development. "Just call. Busy now."

Why did all his children inherit his worst traits?

Was he cursed somehow?


[}-o-{]
​

"Very thorough and very quick," Joshua commented, looking over the files that Serafall had brought for him.

As planned, his partners had dealt with Grigori in order to get him some information on Sacred Gears similar to Sephiroth Graal. Granted, there wasn't much that came even close, but there were some tangentially similar ones here and there. For the most part, nothing quite got as close as Katerea's Power of Sea, but some of them could somewhat – maybe – fill in the blanks left by it. He'd have to study the information and then maybe run some tests.

"Penemue is very efficient," Serafall replied, smiling happily, content to leave him to his reading while she dug into an ice cream bowl that had enough of the stuff for a school bus full of children. He wasn't sure how she managed to ingest so much of it without dealing with any issues, but he chucked that to Devil physiology or some kind of magic use or inherent Devil power. Maybe it boiled down to her ice variant of her family's Power?

Maybe that would be worth studying once he had time.

"You've all been working with Penemue a lot," Joshua commented absently, although he was anything but. He didn't care for politics, he really didn't. He also didn't care for Grigori much those days. Neither of those things stopped him from noticing that his partners almost never seemed to mention Azazel. It was always Penemue.

At first, he'd thought it was just because they didn't want to bring the fallen Governor up around him because of all the problems that surrounded that particular individual.

He wasn't so sure anymore.

"Yup," was all Serafall said and she seemed preoccupied, so he kept his theories and thoughts to himself. It wasn't that important anyway. Maybe he could ask them at some other point. As it was, he had reading to do.

That is, until he flipped to a different folder expecting to see more Sacred Gear stuff.

Instead, Joshua saw a file on a devil pillar's Power. Before he opened it though, there was a note stuck to the front of it, keeping it closed. 'Conditions,' the title on the note read. Blinking, he glanced at Serafall and saw her still very much focusing on her snack.

Silently, he started reading the notes conditions and he found himself more and more surprised. It boiled down to him being allowed to learn about that particular Power if he, at a later date, helped devilkind with a particular issue. The issue of their birth rate, to be specific.

His eyebrows shot up.

"Found the Power file?" Serafall asked, finally tearing her eyes away from her ice cream to look at him. "Zekram's the one that brought that one up, actually," she added, as if everything else weren't surprising enough. "That Power's house is extinct, they didn't survive the Great War. Zechs was working on getting its Power information for you, but… Well, the old man beat him to it."

"Huh… Well, this is awkward," Joshua commented with a wry smile.

"How so?" Serafall asked, eyebrows up.

"I was already planning on doing something about this," he commented, waving vaguely at the file. Or, more precisely, at the conditions' notes. "Unless I read things wrong and you were really joking when you said you wanted children too," he added, looking through the writing to see if he'd missed something. "How much of a priority would this need to be though?" he asked, because he knew Zekram…

Or, at least, Joshua thought he knew him.

The man was being entirely too nice and accommodating those days. Surely there was something wrong. Surely he was missing something, or the devil was up to something. It couldn't all be going without issues, right? The man had to be up to something. He was a schemer. Much as Joshua would like to think that he was an ally because their goals were somewhat aligned for the moment, he had to consider the idea that he might want to screw him over.

Although, if Serafall had brought the file, then that probably meant that Sirzechs and her had already checked it and it seemed fine?

Speaking of…

"Serafall?" he asked when he received no answer, looking up and seeing the devil staring at him, spoon frozen midway between her mouth and the bowl. "Something the matter?" he added, blinking. Then he went over what he'd said before and considered… "Did I say something weird?" He grimaced. "I did, didn't I?" Joshua added with a groan, setting the files on the table and rubbing a hand over his face. "Sorry."

"Sometimes you say some things so casually, Josh," Serafall said and he all but flinched.

"I know, I just don't realize-," he started before cutting himself off. Right, it didn't matter. "I'm sorry," he told her, eyes down on the files. Better to get it over with and go back to talking about something else before he cringed to death. "So, if you think this is a good deal, then-"

"I do," Serafall interrupted and he nodded.

"Right, so-"

"I do want them," Serafall interrupted again and he paused, blinking again as he tried to figure out where her words fit. "I do want children," she clarified and he looked up to see her giving him a look that she didn't wear often. There was a hesitation in her smile and she seemed to make herself look small, which she was even if she didn't appear to be most of the time. All the same, there was a glint in her eyes that took his breath away.

"Oh," was the most eloquent response Joshua could manage and her smile widened the slightest bit.

They didn't talk about the files – or much of anything – for quite a bit after that.


[}-o-{]
​

"Dad?" the question made Joshua jump a little and it took him a solid second to remember that he was in bed. Then another second to recognize that it'd been Kunou that called him and he blinked. "Sorry," he heard his daughter say and he brought a hand up to his face to rub the sleep off.

"What's up?" he asked, his voice kind of growly, even more than it usually was when he was just waking up. Then he paused and held back a flinch, or any other reaction. "Did you need something?" Joshua added, and he hoped his voice didn't come off strange with the lingering exhaustion. "It's early to be up, isn't it?"

"It's ten in the morning though."

'Ah, that's why the spells didn't work,' he thought, making a mental note to change how they kept track of things. Evidently, time wasn't a good enough measure.

"I said what I said," Joshua mumbled, getting a giggle out of Kunou. 'Alright, so we're safe for now,' he told himself, taking a deep breath in and shifting to push himself up a little. Very, very carefully, however. "So, what do you need?" he asked and he saw the girl shifting a little.

"Koneko and Ravel dropped by and I wanted to know if we could set up the flying game again," she asked and he took a moment to think that over. All he wanted was to go back to sleep. He was still exhausted. And besides that, there was also the fact that… Well…

All the same, Joshua crumbled at her hesitantly hopeful look.

"Sure, give me a bit, yeah?" he asked with a weak smile. "Can you get me a cup of tea while I get up?" he added but she was already cheering and shouting something to the other two girls while leaving the room. With a thought, he closed the door behind her and groaned.

Then he huffed and turned to sit on the edge of the bed.

"That was close," a voice said and then he felt soft arms wrap around him and a head resting on his shoulder. And then there was the rest of Serafall pressing against his back. "Good thing she was too eager to even turn the lights on, huh?"

"No kidding," Joshua mumbled, bringing a hand up to his neck and rubbing it wearily. "Well, I guess I have to go now," he added with a half-smile. "You coming?" he asked, not even aware enough to realize that was a poor choice of words with Serafall. Although, mercifully, she didn't go for it.

"I mean, I really want to stay here for a little longer," she whispered in his ear and it was so unfair that he had to leave. "You sure you can't stay a little longer?" she added breathily and then she gave his ear a slight nibble.

And so unfair turned into too unfair.

Which…

"You took forever!" Kunou whined some time later before pouting at him and Joshua just stared at her. Then he brought his cup to his lips and took a sip. "Dad!"

"Hm, I'll remember this attitude next time you wanna sleep in," he commented and that just made her pout harder. Joshua didn't have the energy then and there to deal with any of that. So, instead, he moved past Kunou and the other two girls – he dutifully ignored Koneko's narrowed eyes – and waved his hand to start setting up a flight range for them to play in. "Morag's going to be joining, by the way," he added, feeling his familiar crawling their way.

"But she cheats!" Kunou protested.

"You're going to play with her too, or there'll be no spellcrafting for you for a week," Joshua said, giving her an unimpressed look. That seemed to snap her out of it for a long second in which she paled and stared at him wide-eyed.

"Why?"

"Because she's your sister too, so I don't want you to leave her out of things. You also woke me up to do something for you and you're still whining," he pointed out and then he raised an eyebrow. "And I haven't heard a single please in all this time, have I?" he added. Kunou looked like she wanted to protest that for a moment before she deflated as she realized that he was right. "That's what I thought. So, Morag is playing, and you're not going to make her feel bad for doing well. Is that clear?"

"... Yes," Kunou mumbled.

"Louder, like you mean it."

"Yes, dad," she said, more clearly. "I'm sorry."

"So long as you know what you did wrong and try not to do it in the future," Joshua commented, ruffling her hair. "How're you two doing?" he asked then, turning his attention towards the other two girls. "I don't remember either of you saying you'd come in the morning," he added.

"Felt like it," Koneko replied, taking a cookie from the tray he'd brought.

"Riser was being an idiot," Ravel offered with a shrug.

Joshua just nodded at them.

Sounded about right.

"Well, are you staying for lunch?" he asked and the two shared a look between themselves. "I'm cooking."

"Yes."

"If you insist."

He stared at them.

They stared back.

He raised an eyebrow.

"What do we say?" Joshua asked when it became obvious that they weren't getting the hint. Seriously, he'd just brought up the issue with Kunou and she was right there. What kind of example was that?

"Please?" Koneko asked, catching up first.

"Please," Ravel said, more earnestly, realizing that the reincarnated nekoshou's guess was right.

"Look alive, girls," Joshua told them with a roll of his eyes. "You're older sisters now. You gotta be good role models or Kunou will end up more spoiled than she already is." Granted, that was almost entirely his fault, but he could be excused for that. He had a weakness and everyone and their mothers knew it. Said weakness was like, most of the reason why the two had ended up all but adopted too.

"Wait, what?" Kunou asked, suddenly catching up with his words a second later.

"I said what I said."


[}-o-{]
​

"Your chosen is doing well," Isis commented at the back of his mind as he watched Levi take over his class for a moment to explain one of the points they were learning that day. It was a matter of about fifteen minutes in a course that was an hour long, but it was something. Better than when he had to throw the guy off the deep end, but also not completely taking back over the class himself.

'I know. He's great,' Joshua thought back to the goddess.

He noticed Thoth's pride reaching his mind too. Interestingly, the god's messages and emotions felt like they were far away, like he was in another room compared to the rest of the pantheon that was freeloading in his mind most of the time. He guessed it was because Thoth was more with Levi than he was with him, in a sense. That'd make sense, even though it sounded odd to him.

He wasn't about to start questioning that kind of thing though.

He had other things to focus on.

That's why Joshua turned his attention back to his stuff and continued working on it. Between the Stars and Ravel, Levi had all the back up he could possibly need. And if that wasn't enough, then someone – probably the Phenex girl sitting beside him – would poke him and then he'd send whoever gave Levi trouble away for the day… or the month… or forever.

As it was, he wanted some free time to go over some new data that he'd gotten. It wouldn't be enough to do much of anything, but at least he could get started getting the gist of it. Then he could read it properly when class was over. As it was…

'It seems… possible,' Joshua thought, somewhat surprised as he went over some of the data that Friday had forwarded to him. He'd had her running some tests as a way for her to learn and… she'd gotten him some very interesting information. 'That's… good,' he added, although even in his own mind he couldn't quite make it sound certain nor happy. For once, he had wanted one of his ideas to be completely impossible, after all. 'It's gonna be a nightmare to implement.'

A political nightmare at that, which made it about ten times worse.

His partners and him would be having a lot of trouble convincing people to go along with that. At least Joshua had somewhat gotten things started with his deals. The Norse were going to be on board, especially once he got started on fulfilling his side of the deal. Serafall and Gabriel were still discussing some things with a few South American factions and Yasaka was positive she could have the Koreans on board. Not even needing a big favor like he'd suggested with those latter ones, at that, but maybe that'd be necessary if he brought up his newest idea…

"Mr. Davis," Ravel called him and he nodded.

"Right," Joshua said, looking up. It was time to continue the class, which he did. Good thing it was all stuff that he had very clear in his own head. He could almost turn his brain off while talking at that point. He didn't though, because he didn't want to ruin the class by doing so. He knew what a teacher droning off could be like and he didn't want to do that.

Besides, thinking too much about things wouldn't help him.

He needed the opinion of more knowledgeable people.

"That's that," Joshua announced once he was done about twenty or so minutes later. "If you have any doubts, feel free to approach the Stars. If they can't help you, they can get your messages to me and I'll see what I can do," he said, like he'd taken to not too long before.

It helped the Stars build up some connections and a reputation, and it took work off his back.

Two birds with one stone, which was great.

"Mr. Davis?" Ravel asked, clearly noticing that something was up. "You asked to have a visit to the dungeons scheduled now."

"We're putting that off. Are Yasaka, Gabriel or Serafall free around this time?" Joshua asked and she startled a little before flipping pages on her notepad.

"I'm… not sure. Yasaka should be occupied. Serafall had a meeting with one of the Pillars, but I'm not sure if she'd still be there now," the girl answered, clearly upset that she couldn't give a better answer. He reassured her with a pat on the head.

"It's fine. You manage my schedule, not theirs," he reassured before taking a deep breath in. "Guess I'll call Gabriel and hope she's free," he commented.

"Yes?" was the response he got when he did and it was quick, so he imagined things were fine. "Class went well?"

"Well enough," Joshua answered, running his fingers through his hair. "Are things going well over there? I hope I'm not interrupting."

"Not at all," Gabriel answered and she sounded like she meant that, at least. "I was just reviewing some things. I was actually going to drop by the house in a bit, maybe we can both work together," she added he smiled. That sounded like a great idea.

"Sounds like a plan to me," he replied with a nod that the angel couldn't see. "Anything I can help with?" he asked, before he might as well offer. There was often not much he could do to actually help, but he felt better at least offering. And sometimes they did take him up on the offer… and sometimes Ravel would have to point out that he could help, when they refused to let him.

She was a life saver like that.

"I don't think so, but we can see," she said and he took that to mean yes. "What about you?" she asked.

"That's kind of why I called you immediately, actually," he answered honestly. "I found out some stuff, so I want to run a few things past you three and I wanted to check if anyone was free."

"Well, I am. We can meet and- Wait. Give me a minute," Gabriel said.

"Sure," he said, but he could tell that she'd already turned towards whatever new thing had popped up. So, while he waited, he turned towards Ravel. "What do you say we go get something to eat?"

"... Fries and a soda?" she asked after a moment, almost shyly. It was adorable.

"Sure, that sounds-"

"How fast can you get to Greece, Joshua?" Gabriel said, and her tone alone made him straighten.

"Tell me where and why and I'm there," he replied, already feeling bad for having to call an immediate raincheck on Ravel.

"Thebes and… Khaos used their Grail."

'... Fuck'

​

Hey guys! How's it going?

The four sections of the chapter were written in harmony. Then everything changed when the Khaos Brigade attacked. Although, let's be real, everyone saw that one coming.

Or did you?

#1,579
Tainting My Blood with Toxins

"You!" a voice shouted immediately after he teleported in and Joshua blinked at the very angry woman. "You will solve this!" she demanded, not quite sounding hysterical, but close enough. It kind of reminded him of his mother when things got the better of her.

And his mother had not been a calm woman when she spiraled, at all.

"Excuse her," another, deeper voice said with a somewhat apologetic, somewhat exasperated expression. "She can be rather emotional despite everything, especially about her things," he added, shrugging in a clear "what kind you do?" gesture.

"... I was told the situation was handled," he commented, unsure of what to do or even say, especially faced with such a… situation right off the bat. Gabriel had said it was better if he got there as soon as possible, even if Khaos's mess had already been dealt with by the locals. Which was new, admittedly, but maybe that was just from his side. Maybe factions had been dealing with Khaos on their own, even if they hadn't joined the alliance Joshua was part of. "Lord Zeus," he added, almost having forgotten the fact that he was, well, dealing with a Faction leader.

In his defense, most faction leaders he dealt with were… friendly, to say the least, and accommodating too. It'd been a while since he'd had to interact with one that he didn't know, even, and forever since he had to without any prior preparation. Because yes, the Norse had been rather recent, really, but he'd had plenty of information going in and a game plan. To add insult to injury, Joshua also didn't remember much of anything in regards to the Greek pantheon from canon, admittedly.

"This is not handled at all, Davis!" the woman hissed, waving her hand behind her and Joshua blinked at the sight of the… man?... 'Creature, more like,' he decided. And he was reminded of Katerea, but much worse. The thing had a bundle of tentacles for a head and an amalgamation of fur and scales for skin. A chittering sound like a cicada's came out of… somewhere and a tail covered in wet – slimy? – feathers swished around erratically. The arms and legs were thrashing around under a net that covered the whole thing and he noticed that they twisted and turned in impossible angles, at least if the thing had anywhere close to a normal bone structure.

"What am I looking at?" he asked, blinking, and that seemed to infuriate the woman even more. Idly, he noticed how his question could be applied to her too, even if he hadn't said it with that intention. Fortunately, he imagined nobody would take it that way… hopefully.

He would rather not cause an interfaction incident.

"That," the woman said, visibly trying to keep a semblance of composure and not being very successful. "Is one my Spartoi," she said and he blinked.

"Oh, I think I know that story," he commented, turning to look at the chaotic creation. Well, he wasn't sure how they were supposed to look like in DxD, but he doubted they were supposed to look like eldritch abominations. "The warriors that rose from sown dragon teeth, right?"

"Yes," the woman answered and she seemed to calm down considerably for whatever reason. "I gave those to Cadmus," she added and he nodded, although that still didn't clear out who she was. His question had covered about as much as he knew of that particular myth, Joshua would admit. "You offered a miracle for us, I want you to fix him," she added, eyes narrowed, before Zeus coughed into his fist.

Which earned him a glare from the woman.

"Athena, be reasonable," the god said and Joshua silently thanked him for letting him know who the woman – the goddess – was. "I know you're attached to them, but-"

"Are you going to deny me this, father?" Athena interrupted and the Greek leader paused, considering his daughter for a long moment. "Because you don't want to do that," she added, with an edge in her voice.

Joshua was getting the feeling that he was missing some context in that exchange and he wasn't sure if he should even be paying attention to it at all. They were right in front of him though, so… It wasn't like he could do much else. Was he supposed to turn away and do something else? He was pretty sure that'd be insulting.

So, as discreetly as he could, he checked on Ravel, who was slightly behind him and to the side. She seemed to be of the same awkward opinion as him, unfortunately. Thus, in the spirit of doing something productive with his time while the deities argued, he checked on the captured Spartoi…

And it was most certainly… something.

He could make no heads or tails of it. Vaguely, if he looked really, really deep, he thought he could get hints of a man… but that was about it. No surprise there, he supposed, since Spartoi weren't supposed to be men, not really. Last he'd checked, men didn't just spawn from sowing teeth on the ground.

And that was without whatever the fuck the broken Grail had done to it… him?

The worst part was that, upon further inspection, Joshua noticed that it was still changing. Slowly, ever so slowly, but the energies were shifting and he could almost see it in the color of the fur, or the shape and number of tentacles or how the feathers seemed to be turning into some kind of weird filaments. 'Fascinating,' he thought to himself. 'Horrific, but fascinating.'

"Very well," Zeus said, with a tone of finality to the words that dragged Joshua's attention back to him and Athena. Which was good, because the god had straightened and turned to look at him. "Davis, Seraphin Gabriel spoke to us of your offer. If you could help us with this matter, we'll consider it. However, we can't promise that this will be all there is to it on our side," he explained and Joshua considered that for as long a moment as he could afford to.

"I'll have to check with the rest of the alliance," he replied as diplomatically as he could, using a phrase that he'd been taught long ago for such circumstances. "But if you don't mind, I can take a look at him now, so that I can start faster if we can reach an agreement."

"Please, do," Athena told him with a nod that he returned, glancing between the two of them before turning his attention to the Spartoi. 'Actually, are they called that when it's just one? Or is Spartoi a plural? It sounds like a plural,' he wondered idly. Something to look into.

Ultimately, it wasn't that important.

"Mr. Davis," Ravel said and he looked at her with a raised eyebrow. Had he messed up without knowing? That was a real possibility and he knew it. He hadn't gotten cursed, at least, so he was a little reassured by that. He noticed, with some amusement, the Egyptian gods at the back of his mind scoffing.

Good to know they had his back.

"That was well handled," Ravel told him and it was odd to be praised by someone that not only was but also looked and behaved so much younger. He knew she knew what she was talking about though, so he took it as the compliment it was. "Not quite how I'd have said any of that, but for a surprise interaction, you did well."

"Thank you," he commented with a grin. "Maybe you all are rubbing off on me," he added and that seemed to please the girl. He wasn't sure he was as happy about that, but he didn't comment on it either way. "Now… this," he mused, looking at the twisted creature that had once been part of Greek myth and was now… part of unspeakable horrors somehow.

"Do you want me to ask for permission to cast spells, Mr. Davis?" Ravel asked and he considered that for a long moment before running his fingers through his hair. He shouldn't agree to that, he knew. Ravel was great, indeed, but she wasn't a proper representative when talking to a faction that didn't know him or her. Maybe if they grew close, but as it was…

"I'll handle it, just tell me what to say," he decided, resigning himself to more talking and dealing with people. He could feel the energy leaving his body just thinking about it. Alas, it was a small price to pay in order not to put Ravel in a bad spot.

"Seeking advice from those better qualified," a voice said and he saw Ravel stiffen. Joshua, for his part, found himself fairly calm, mainly because the words had been spoken calmly, even positively. "It takes wisdom to realize that's necessary," Athena said, a barely there smile tugging at her lips and a calm warmth in her eyes that hadn't been there before.

Maybe she'd calmed down already.

Idly though, Joshua wondered if it was just him thinking it was incredibly cliche for the Goddess of Wisdom to say such a thing.

"And you can cast your magic, goēs," the goddess said and he blinked, wondering what that word was supposed to mean. He was almost sure that it wasn't meant to be English there, but it did sound like goes... He didn't ask though, simply nodding and waving his hand to make a bunch of pieces of paper appear in a perfect arrangement. Then came the foci, wardstones and plants and creature pieces and trinkets. All of them were part of his usual analysis set-up.

He could do something more specific to the situation once he got more information.

"You had that ready?" Athena asked, narrowing her eyes at the circles. He wondered if the Greek had their own system, like the Norse and their runes. They very well could, he supposed. He almost wanted to ask about it, but it was probably not the time.

It was very tempting though.

"I've found myself analysing a lot of things for data," he explained, his attention almost fully on the spell array as it slowly came alive. He could have had it appear faster, for sure, but there was no harm in taking his time. The Spartoi wasn't going anywhere. "I've learned to have something ready for a rainy day," he added and the woman nodded beside him.

She remained silent afterwards and that was just fine for Joshua.

He preferred it, really. Sure, it would've been better if he was left to his own devices, but silence was the next best thing. Better than having to talk to her, that was for sure. He didn't know her and while she looked calmer, her previous mood hadn't done anything to make him want to talk to her.

"I'm sorry for how I acted before," she said after a good few minutes, when the last spell in the array came alive and he was about to start checking things for real. He almost sighed, disappointed at the broken peace. He didn't, thankfully, but he sorely wanted to. "That was unbecoming of me."

"No harm done," he replied with a nod, hoping against hope that he didn't sound like an idiot or too curt. "This must have been an unpleasant surprise," he added and he was pretty sure that was a neutral enough comment not to trigger much of anything.

"That's one way to put it," the goddess told him and he could tell the beginnings of an edge in her tone again. "This is an insult the likes of which I haven't received in quite a while, to twist my creations like so… You're sure Khaos is behind this? Gabriel seemed to be."

"This is the broken Grail, I'm very sure," he confirmed almost immediately. He knew what to look for and while it was different from what Valerie could do, there were enough similarities. "And for what it's worth, I'm sorry this happened."

"Nothing for you to apologize," Athena told him, suddenly a little amused. Although, there was no hiding the storm brewing in her eyes. One that her father would be proud of, he was sure. "Do you think you can fix this?"

"I might," he said, maybe a little too calmly, a little too casually. "If I can't, then the Grail's rightful holder should be able to. If that fails, then there'll be a better chance if we can manage to fix it," he added, which was where his calm came from. If those options failed though… How difficult could it really be? With time, Joshua wasn't sure if there was something magic couldn't do.

It was that amazing, really.

"Thank you," the goddess told him before nodding and walking away.

And Joshua relaxed, getting back to work.


[}-o-{]
​

"I had the most interesting conversation with Athena today," Gabriel commented and there was something in her flat tone that set Joshua on edge. He stiffened the smallest bit as he looked up from his notes on the Spartos – apparently, that was the singular for the sown man – and what had happened to him.

"I knew I was too informal," he groaned with a grimace. "I shouldn't be left alone with political figures. Ravel can't speak for me if they don't know us," he muttered, massaging his forehead.

He was met with silence though, and he noticed after a few seconds. Holding back a second grimace, he looked up again, preparing himself for another politics lecture that would wither his poor soul away. He could feel the Egyptians' amusement at the situation too, which wasn't really helping.

That is, until he saw the looks that his partners were giving him and he wondered if he'd missed something.

"What?"

"Never change, Josh. Never change," Serafall said, patting his arm comfortingly. Which only confused him further, really. "Although, I think changing a little would be easier on us," she added wryly.

"What did I miss?" he asked, because he was getting a little nervous, admittedly, if for different reasons from before.

"Nothing you need to worry about," Yasaka answered, visibly turning towards her cup of tea and taking a sip. That was extremely suspicious, but Joshua decided that he might be better off not knowing. "Although, you make a good point. Someone should be there with you if you're meeting other factions, especially unprepared."

"I agree. I was busy, but maybe I could have asked the Greek to wait a little. They had the situation handled, after all," Gabriel replied consideringly and Joshua wondered if he should say what came to his mind. In the end, he decided to do it anyway, even if his insight was probably all sorts of wrong.

"They seemed to really want some more answers," he said and all three of them turned towards him. "Even Zeus, but especially Athena. They really wanted some answers. I couldn't tell them much, but they seemed happy enough to know something and even happier to know I was looking into it," he commented, a slight smile pulling at his lips as he glanced at his notebook. "It was kind of flattering," he added with a slight shrug.

It made him feel silly, to be happy about something like that. He was praised for what he did all the time, but most people tended to be more shocked than happy about his skills. They tended to look at him like he was a freak of nature rather than someone helpful.

And besides all that, it was just generally nice to get some validation, admittedly.

"Girls!" Serafall exclaimed and he glanced her way with the resignation of someone that knew some Serafall nonsense was coming his way. "That witch is trying to steal our man!" she cried out dramatically and Joshua sighed, bringing a hand up to drag it over his face wearily.

What he wasn't expecting was the follow up though.

"She'll find that it's not that easy," Yasaka said, somewhat reassuring, but also somewhat serious.

"Joshua is ours," Gabriel offered with a smile that he couldn't help but find odd.

"Why are you humoring her?" he asked. He'd expected the two to be voices of reason, like usual. He hadn't expected them to join in. Not that it was unheard of, but this was another pantheon they were joking about. He was pretty sure that was new for them.

"I'm not joking, Josh!" Serafall protested and he rolled his eyes.

"Well, then don't worry. I wouldn't know interest unless it hit me in the face," he said flatly, which they knew first hand. That was what had happened with all of them, after all. "And I wouldn't be with anyone else if you're not okay with it," he added, which they also knew first hand too, since that was what happened with Gabriel.

"Oh," Serafall mumbled thoughtfully.

"Right," Yasaka added with another sip from her tea.

"That's true," Gabriel agreed with a nod.

"I feel like I should be offended by those reactions."

"Still!" Serafall continued, picking up the energy she'd lost for a moment there. Joshua held back a sigh. He would only be so lucky to be done with such a conversation quickly. Life just didn't like him much, especially those days. "It's the principle of the matter, Josh!"

"Can the principle of the matter be less awkward for me?" he asked dryly.

"No!"

"Figured…"

"That aside," Gabriel commented and Joshua could have kissed her. He also would, but later. "Khaos is moving again. Athena confirmed that all five of the Spartoi that rested there were targeted. That means there's four of them somewhere out there." And wasn't that concerning. Because sure, the Greeks had handled that one Spartos, but Joshua had taken a look at the thing.

It was problematic.

It was like a lesser version of dealing with Annihilation Maker, at least for him. Its existence was constantly shifting, which made it very hard to have any kind of defense ready to deal with it. Friday might be able to help him with that, but she could only do so much. Especially if they didn't know when or where they would have to face the aberrant creatures.

'More work,' Joshua thought to himself wryly. 'What's new?'


[}-o-{]
​

[Athena, Goddess of Wisdom]

What they had done was…

She had too many words to describe it and none of them, not even put together, came even close.

She was far away from the mockery that her creation had become, but she could still feel it like she had when she was in front of it. What had once been a perfect warrior was now a monstrosity the likes of which not even her pantheon had seen many of. Echidna herself would have been surprised at the sight of what her Spartoi had seemingly become, she was sure.

And all of that with her divinity in the middle, twisted, perverted. Khaos had taken her energy, her blessing and her legacy and it had spit on all of them equally. Athena couldn't push it away, couldn't stop it from poking at her, at the back of her mind, deep in her domains and reaching to her from her ruined Spartoi. Her dad tried, but it was a feeling unlike any she had ever experienced.

She wondered if that was how her aunts and uncles had felt, back when their own father had devoured them, deprived them of everything they were supposed to be.

Lesser it might be, what happened to her, but Athena found it incredibly vexing all the same.

'They must die,' she thought, eyes narrowed. It'd been a while, admittedly, and her brother tended to be the one in charge of such things, preferred it even and she often let him have that… But she was a goddess of war too. 'They will die, before they defile more than they already have,' she thought, no, promised to herself.

And there was a simple, easily accessible key to make that happen.

Joshua Davis.

The Heracles to Khaos' Hydra. The Perseus to their Medusa. The Theseus to their Minotaur. The Bellerophon to their Chimera. The goēs had made a name for himself in many ways, and one of those ways was the abandon with which he fought Khaos Brigade. He hunted them down like it was his life's mission, his own, personal, self-appointed labor.

'He will be a nice asset,' she thought, her lips pulling into a smile.

Working with the Egyptian pantheon would be… It'd be tricky, but she could make it happen. Gabriel had seemed wary of her, but Athena had no interest in her chosen partner. Not that way, at least. Honestly, she was about the last the angel should be worried about, really. If she knew half the things Athena had heard Aphrodite and Hecate say regarding the man…

Either way, she was more interested in how the man could help her settle the scores. Because Khaos had made the wrong enemy in her, and she would be teaching them exactly that. The goēs would help her do that. She just needed to find the way to make that happen.

And Athena happened to have some ideas already.

So, with a smile, she would approach an old friend. Happily, she would lay the foundations for an alliance. Eagerly, she'd urge her own brother. Because, for that sliver of her that Khaos had decided to taint with their madness, she'd burn them all.

She'd cursed people for lesser insults.

No, they deserved worse, but she knew Davis would have that covered.

"It's been a while since you visited on your own and without plans," was the greeting she got, but she smiled nonetheless. "What brings you here, Athena?"

"Plenty," she answered, and she could tell her fellow goddess was neither amused nor impressed by her non-answer. "But as of right now, I have scales to balance," he added and the goddess raised her eyebrow.

"That sounds more like a Nemesis thing, maybe Themis, depending," was the response she got and she only nodded, acknowledging the point. She moved past that determinedly though.

"Yes, but this fits you so much more and I'm sure you'll agree," Athena replied with barely maintained calm. "After all, magic is your territory, isn't it?" she asked and that earned her narrowed eyes in response. "How would you like to meet that goēs you won't shut up about, Hecate?"

"Davis?" the goddess said, instantly, hurriedly even, almost tripping over the single word. "I heard what happened, but-" Hecate started then before cutting herself off and looking at Athena as if reevaluating her presence there. She was always a smart one. "What is it you want, Athena?"

"Retribution," she answered firmly. "Khaos has done something unforgivable. So, how about you? Don't you want to meet the Domain Authority in the flesh? Don't you want to see the man loved by magic?" she asked and the tone with which she spoke that last word was not missed.

"Athena…"

"I care not for whatever your feelings for the man are, Hecate," she said, and that was the whole truth. Magic goddesses all over the world couldn't shut up about him. They wanted to be either Nepthys, with him firmly in their grasp, or they wanted to be his partners and see what a man for which their very domains bent could be like. Athena sort of understood, because that was a man that knew the importance of knowledge and wisdom and strategy, but alas… She had other things in her mind. "I care for if you're in or out."

"... I'm in," she replied and Athena grinned. "I don't like that face you're making."

"Now, first things first, that was a good idea you presented to me," she mused, because her father tended to be the go to God of Justice, but… "Nemesis and Themis…" she mumbled to herself, considering that. Although, admittedly-

"You're the one dealing with Nemesis, let me tell you," Hecate said and that was really such a shame. However, that wasn't all bad, not entirely. Because-

"Then you're talking to Themis," she replied, because yes, Nemesis could hold a grudge like few others, but Themis could be just as hard to deal with. It showed in the grimace on Hecate's face.

"This is your-"

"I guess I can bring them and not you then," Athena commented.

"I hate you."
