#1,588
Demons I Can't Fight

'How very interesting.'

Joshua had thought that helping the Norse combat Ragnarök would involve limiting Loki somehow. He'd actually kind of bet on it, since he knew the god of mischief was either part of Khaos or just a regular unconnected villain. He didn't remember too well, but ultimately it didn't matter. Either way, stopping him would have been a plus, even if he couldn't outright kill him and be done with itt.

Any amount of power he could take from Khaos and/or evil that he could spare the world from would help.

Alas…

"So… cages," he commented, sitting across from Odin.

And that was a surprise in and off itself. Or, more accurately, the god was. Because he was nothing like Joshua had imagined and prepared himself to deal with. Hell, he'd talked to everyone that could give him some information on the matter, and everyone had painted pictures that matched his knowledge of the guy fairly well. A bit of an oddball with a perverted streak, more or less, in a way not dissimilar to Serafall's own magical girl act, everyone – and himself – guessed.

Except, the god had been fairly tame. If anything, he was reminding him of… Actually, he didn't have a good example. Because he wasn't completely professional, but he also was nowhere near as bad as Joshua had feared. If anything, he was kind of like Joshua himself, but more whimsical than reluctant in his approach to politics.

"Indeed," the old god said, smiling and waving towards wooden cabins arranged in a circle of sorts. "If it helps, I'd make them good enough to contain a god, or an evil dragon, or something to that effect," Odin explained and Joshua nodded slowly. He wasn't sure which version of Ragnarök they were dealing with, but he didn't really need to know if he had the pantheon on board, right.

The event itself was known by everyone, at least, but nobody knew the specifics. The myths, like back home, weren't very… official, as it were. There were a lot of versions on record and none of them was any more legitimate than the others, as far as the general public was concerned.

If anyone knew though, then it had to be Odin.

'Wonder if that's a subtle way of saying Loki is involved, and Miðgarðsormr too, for that matter,' Joshua thought to himself, running his fingers through his hair as he considered that. 'The first struggle will be that Odin doesn't seem inclined to confirm anything to me,' he mused, taking a deep breath and looking at the old man to see if any new information could be found or offered…

Alas, it was not to be.

"I can do that," he replied with a slow nod. With any luck, letting the god keep his secrecy wouldn't backfire on either of them. And if it did, Joshua hoped it was on the Norse. "Well, if you can give me any specifics, it'd be appreciated. If not, I guess I'll make them as good as can be in a general way. The more I have to do, the longer it'll take to have something ready," he explained, which was truly his only concern on the matter.

Sure, knowing names and stuff would be nice and he was curious… But ultimately, it didn't matter. He had enough on his plate with just Khaos Brigade and Trihexa. That was his main mission at the moment. Far as he knew, DxD never tackled the Norse's Ragnarök, so he should be somewhat safe in that regard. 'Please, let that not be an immediate issue. I might cry if I have to add that to my list,' he thought to himself, taking another deep breath in.

"If time's not an issue, then that's that," he finished with and Odin stared at him with his one eye. For someone that was supposed to be somewhat of a silly old man, the piercing stare of that somewhat faded sky blue eye was fairly intimidating and serious. Joshua stood his ground though, partly because he was saying nothing but the truth, so he wasn't about to apologize for that.

Another part of it was that the Egyptians were all but pressing against the back of his consciousness and he could feel them so very clearly. He wasn't sure what was up with that, but they were very interested in his meetings with Odin. They had before and they were then and there. However, that particular moment seemed to be of special interest, because they were communicating rather than just sitting where they were.

The message he was getting at that very moment was that he shouldn't cave.

"Pettiness shouldn't be encouraged, don't you think?" Odin asked then and Joshua raised an eyebrow at him. He had to be talking about the Egyptians there. It made him wonder what could possibly have happened for the pantheon to be reacting like they were. Especially since they seemed very chill with everyone else and even with the Norse up to that point.

"That's a very odd change of topic," he commented and it was Odin's time to pause and stare. "So, about this job…" he pressed, because if he had to choose between the Egyptians and Odin, then he knew who he would go for. Only one of those options had been helping him with pretty much everything for quite some time.

The other hadn't even bothered to join his alliance against Khaos because of fucking politics.

He was not bitter about that, truly.

"Crow seeks crow, huh?" Odin said, sounding thoroughly unimpressed. Joshua was fine with that. He wasn't there to impress the old man. He was there to carry out his part of the deal so that the Norse would actually work with them. And if he wanted to make things difficult, then he'd just leave. It wouldn't change much.

And with an in with the Greek, who were fairly strong too, Joshua didn't have to worry quite as much.

He didn't need Odin.

"Can we talk about the cages?" Joshua replied, using a tone very similar to the god's.

It was going to be a long afternoon.


[}-o-{]
​

"That was…"

"Terrible?" he finished for Ravel. They had just teleported back home and he'd already sent a message to Fuyuko to get him some tea. Which, of course, made Friday shift her attention from where she'd been checking on Grendel apparently. The living spell was going on an analysis spree ever since she'd taken up helping him figure out Valerie's Sacred Gear.

'Speaking of, I should go visit Valerie,' he thought to himself. Sometimes, it was difficult to keep track of everything he needed to do and all the people in his life that he should be interacting with. It was especially bad with Valerie, since she was… more or less incapable of coming to him herself. Not in the sense that she literally couldn't, but more in the sense that she didn't have the mental capabilities to do so. She probably thought about it sometimes, but her mind was so fractured that she wasn't likely to hold onto the thought long enough to leave the room she was in, let alone reaching him.

"Not the word I'd use," Ravel replied hesitantly, slowly. "But it was odd. From both sides. I imagine the Egyptians' had something to do with it? There were some clues…" she commented afterwards, her notepad in hand like she expected to be given key information again.

"Yeah, apparently, there's some beef between them and Odin. Not bad enough for it to be an issue before today though, for some reason," he said and that seemed to give the Phenex pause. "I'm not too worried, we can work together. We can check with the others later to see what we need to do," he pointed out, running his fingers through his hair and trying to recover some of his social battery. "Take a break, Ravel," he added, when the girl started jotting down stuff in her notes.

"But I have to-"

"Iryuka and Seekvaira are there to help you, are they not?" he pointed out and the girl deflated.

Neither of those could have accompanied him to a meeting with Odin of all people, especially when he might need help and such. However, smaller matters like stuff that could be done in the safety of his home, they very much could help with. And if he had any say in the matter, then they would, because Ravel wasn't about to overwork herself on his watch.

No way.

And fortunately, he did have a say in the matter.

"But, Mr. Davis-"

"Ravel," he pressed and the girl deflated. She was also pouting, but she'd deny that like her life depended on it, so it was better to ignore that. Even if it was adorable… "You'll take a break and you'll like it," he added and the girl huffed, turning away.

"I guess I could call Koneko and wait for Kunou to be free," she mumbled and Joshua nodded. It was always nice to see that all three of the girls got along. However…

"You don't always have to spend time with them, you know that, right?" he said and the girl seemed taken aback by that, like she couldn't believe she'd heard that come out of his mouth. It was fair, but also kind of telling. Especially when she seemed unsure of what to do when her mind caught up. "You're allowed to want to spend time with one of them, or neither of them. I'm not saying you have to, but it's an option like any other."

"... I don't feel like going home yet. Rosar is visiting and he's been a bit insufferable, so I just…" she half-mumbled as a response, shrugging and looking away as she trailed off.

"What I said applies if you want to just stay here too," Joshua pointed out and, if anything, that seemed to surprise her even more. "My house is your house and all that," he offered as softly as he could, ruffling her hair. "You're all but part of the family already, Ravel, in case you didn't notice," he added, smiling as the girl blushed.

"I have a family though," she said, but even someone as oblivious as Joshua could notice the tinge of wistfulness, of regret.

"I have a family too, but beyond a few of them… I barely could stand any of them, so I think you're better off than me in that regard," he explained, leaning down so that he wasn't looking down at her… as much, at least. 'At least, I hope you are,' Joshua added in his own mind before continuing to speak. "The family I have here, none of them share my blood, but I love them just as much as I did my parents and my cousins."

"Just like that?" Ravel asked, her voice tiny yet carrying so much emotion all the same. "You can just say it is like that and… it is?" she asked and there was something in her blue eyes that spoke more than her mouth did. There were unsaid questions there, even Joshua could tell.

"Yes," he answered all the same. "It's not easy, not at all, but it is simple," he assured her with a smile. "So, think it over, yeah? Maybe a cup of tea would help?" Joshua suggested and then offered. Visibly, Ravel took a long moment to think that over, her usual composure thoroughly broken. She wasn't always that open about her feelings and her thoughts.

Joshua made sure nobody would stumble upon them and he even kept his familiars away for the moment.

"... I think I'd like that," the girl mumbled, shifting on her feet.

"Great, let's go then," he said and then he started walking. "How're Iryuka and Seekvaira doing anyway? I don't need to talk to them, right? They're supposed to be helping you work less," he said, going back to a previous topic and away from the one they'd just been talking about.

He had a feeling Ravel had had enough deep, personal topics for the moment.

Her visible relief confirmed that his guess was right, at least.


[}-o-{]
​

"By any chance…" Joshua started, taking a sip of the literally divine tea that had been offered to him. "Are you ever going to stop glaring at me?" he asked blandly.

"Unlikely," Uriel answered flatly.

"That's not a no, I guess," Joshua replied with a nod and holding back a sigh. "I'll take that," he added with a shrug. Then he remained in the awkward, silent moment that they were sharing. After all, Gabriel, Raphael and Michael had to leave to check on some things. He was pretty sure Uriel had only remained behind to keep an eye on him because he was likely the least useful for whatever they'd had to check in a hurry.

In the spirit of not making the entire situation worse though, Joshua turned his attention to his notes.

It was another day of helping Heaven ease the restrictions on them, although not quite as focused as they had been before. He was almost certain that Gabriel had been the reason for that particular instance, especially since that was the only one where they had focused their efforts like that. Their excuse that Lust was a particularly bad area… It could be true, but Joshua had to wonder all the same.

Not that he had a problem with any of it.

If anything, he preferred the lie in that case. The lie was a lot less uncomfortable for him, that was for sure. He couldn't imagine sitting alone in a room with Uriel if that wasn't how things were. 'And maybe I should stop thinking about it,' Joshua told himself, shaking off those thoughts and focusing on something more productive.

Like his ideas for how to approach the Spartos.

Or preparing for Khaos Brigade to make a move.

Because they were going to. Of that, Joshua had absolutely no doubts. It was a matter of when and where. Because he rather doubted they'd turned the Spartoi and just… leave that one behind because they felt like it. There had to be a purpose for that, which was why he hadn't argued with the Greek's to move the guy to a place of his own.

No, he'd rather they kept that ticking bomb themselves.

It was cowardly, he supposed, and maybe even selfish. However, Joshua had never denied being either. He would much rather live. And he would much rather his loved ones lived too. So, yes, the further away he could keep threats like that one, the better. It was why he'd wanted to move Ophis away…

Even if it wasn't like it did much, in the dragon's case.

"You always have one of those, don't you?" Uriel asked, making him blink and look up from his notebook. He was looking at said notebook, apparently. "It's always a different one too."

"My notes. I have a lot of projects and several notebooks per project, usually. Circle designs, information, ideas, all sorts of little things are written here and I just… I like to go over them as much as possible, and add new stuff too, of course," he answered and he felt awkward after talking so much all at once. Sometimes, he knew his mouth could just get away from him. Which was fine, because it mostly happened with family and friends…

But Uriel wasn't really either, even if there was a chance that the former could be forced on them eventually.

"I see, very… Raphael," Uriel noted and he seemed somewhere between unimpressed and amused. It was a weird combination, and Joshua hadn't even known that was possible to pull off, but yet there the Seraph was. "You seem more focused than he is," the angel continued and it was then that Joshua wondered if he was missing some kind of interrogation tactic. After all, Uriel was just about the last person that he expected small talk from. "He gets… flighty."

"Thank you," he said, although he wasn't even sure if that'd been a compliment. The tone the angel was using didn't really help him clear out the doubts.

"I've heard that you improved the Youkai's defenses," the Seraph commented out of nowhere and Joshua stiffened. "And that you've breached a bunch of other people's defenses," the man continued and he could only turn to stare at him warily. "I wonder, what do you think of our defenses?"

"Very solid," he answered, because he didn't need to think about it, really. "I wouldn't even know where to begin improving them," he added. Then he turned his gaze to his notes again, if only to help him calm down a little.

Although, he could probably find a way or two if he really wanted to. Gabriel had advised not to for the moment, precisely because of the brother he was talking to. So, he hadn't. Although, he would admit to being curious.

"Have you tried?" Uriel asked and he smiled wryly.

"No," he answered truthfully. "Gabriel asked me not to look into it," he added, wondering if maybe that was too much honesty. Ultimately, he decided that if he couldn't be honest with his possible angel in-laws, then there were bigger problems to deal with than Uriel, probably.

"I see," was all the Seraph said in response to his words.

From there, the room remained silent until the other three came back. The rest of the day's work progressed as usual and neither of them really shared many words, certainly not in regards to that… strange conversation. Joshua would admit to sharing the details of it with Gabriel to make sure he hadn't somehow ruined everything. His hyperactive mind hadn't shut up about that being a possibility, after all, and… Well, he'd grown worried.

She had assured him he didn't though, which was a relief.

She didn't explain much after that, which was less so.


[}-o-{]
​

He'd wanted to wait, but Khaos Brigade had really forced his hand.

Joshua had been waiting, hoping, for one simple thing. He needed Ophis to come out and hopefully be in the mood to entertain a conversation. Something that once would have terrified him. He thought he was getting better in that regard though. After he'd shared tea with her and learned that she liked it, he thought it was somewhat safe to assume that maybe he wasn't in as much danger as he initially thought.

Ophis was still a terrifying force beyond nature and he couldn't risk anything with her… But maybe everything he'd seen and experienced up to that point was safe to be interpreted as good things. She seemed… relatively at ease with things and happy with his progress in regards to her Silence. So, Joshua assumed she wouldn't just snap him Thanos-style just because he had a thing or two to ask of her.

A risk still, to be sure, but that was why he'd been waiting for a good moment.

Waiting was less of an option after Khaos made a move that he couldn't understand or really prepare much for.

"Ophis?" he called once he had thoroughly steeled his resolve. He was sitting at a table outside the Silence rooms and he had tea ready to try and "bribe" the dragon… sort of. He waited after that, because he knew the dragon could hear him. So, he just waited, taking a sip of his own tea that tasted like nothing at all, his mind too preoccupied with other things to bother actually picking up on a taste.

"Joshua Davis," the voice said as soon as the dragon in a girl's body stepped out of the room she'd been in. "You have need of me?" she asked and the flat delivery wasn't helping him decide if that question was something good or bad. So, instead, he decided to focus on his own side of things.

"Of a sort. Tea?" he asked, waving his hand towards the arranged drink and the dragon's only answer was to walk up to the table and take the seat across from him. "I also brought some snacks, if you wanted to try them out," he added, signaling the tray beside the teapot.

From there, and with words burning at his throat, he settled for waiting until after she'd tried some things, at least.

"... It's good," she commented at the third snack.

"That one or all of them?" he asked and the dragon paused and tilted her head. He didn't think she would need that long to decide, but she took a handful of seconds all the same and took her sweet, sweet time going over things in her mind. Her mind would always be a mystery to him, however, so… Joshua wasn't too surprised.

"All of them. Second was better," she answered when she reached her conclusion, nodding for emphasis as if she were particularly proud of her verdict. Or maybe like she was affirming the decision in her own head. "I hope the rest are good too," she added, reaching for another snack. The words added more fear to Joshua, but he did his best to hide that.

"... Say," he started when she reached her seventh snack and started her second cup of tea. "I had something I wanted to ask you about," he prefaced carefully. The blank stare with those windows into the void wasn't helping his nerves, but Joshua soldiered on. "You see this?" he asked, pulling out a wardstone and holding it with the tip of his fingers. "Do you think you could… make better ones?" he asked.

Because Wardstones were ambient magic manifesting and coalescing physically through time and a bunch of other circumstances. That was why their appearance was more or less random and unable to be replicated. That is, unless you were the Dragon of Infinity and the rules of anything were optional for you. Or, at least, that was the theory Joshua was working with. There was a real chance not even she could make that happen, but… he had to ask.

Especially after the new developments.

Ophis stared at the little rock in his hand though, much the same way she'd stared at the snacks before. He was starting to associate that state with "thoughtful" in his own head. Joshua had to wait once more, but at least he hadn't been vaporized. That was a win if he'd ever seen one. A good outcome to that conversation was not dying, after all.

Anything he could get out of Ophis beyond that was a bonus, but a bonus that was why he was risking everything for that.

"I can," she answered eventually, nodding firmly and then continuing to eat and drink.

Joshua, for his part, wanted to jump on that and ask more questions. Maybe he could outright say what he wanted to say right away. Maybe she'd do it and that'd be that. However… He couldn't, shouldn't. Ophis was a creature that seemed stable enough, safe enough. However, seemed was the operative word there. She could, like anyone and anything in the world, just react randomly or unexpectedly or both at any point.

And then poof, no more Joshua.

"You want one?" Ophis asked eventually and he almost sighed in relief. He'd been preparing himself mentally to have to ask anyway, despite the dangers. Alas, the dragon had beat him to it, and he was very grateful for that.

"A few of these and these other kinds," he started answering, pulling other types of wardstones to place on the table. "They would be incredibly helpful to me. Both for the Silence attempts and other personal things. I was hoping you'd help me with this, yes," he explained as best he could without talking too much and risking Ophis deciding she didn't feel like bothering.

Or worse.

The dragon stared for another long series of seconds, munching on the last snack – a brownie – and holding her cup of tea on the other hand. She stared and stared and then stared some more. It was only after she was finished with both that she so much as twitched, and it was only tilting her head a little to one side.

Then she waved her hand, and the table – other than the tray, the teacup plates and the teapot, was covered in black stones.

Black wardstones.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,595
I Want Everything and Nothing

"So… Can you make better rooms now?" Ophis asked, staring at him… Not intently, but the flat expression and stiff posture gave him that impression all the same. Joshua didn't appreciate that, at all. However, he could at least understand where the dragon was coming from, which was more than he could say about most of their interactions. It was nice to have some idea of what was going through her head, no matter how small.

"Not right now, but once I've had a bit of time to work something out using this? Absolutely," Joshua answered, carefully but almost enthusiastically. Because it wasn't often that he was sure of something, especially when it came to Ophis' Silence. However, considering she seemed happy with his progress? This new addition to his available resources was going to make it all so much easier and overall better.

Because the Wardstones she'd just… willed into existence?

They were crazy.

For one, they seemed to be able to hold infinite magic within them, which was… not surprising, not really, but it was still bafflingly strong all the same. For another, they were just overall much better as wardstones than any he'd gotten his hands on. The best wardstones he'd ever found seemed like absolute trash next to those.

Which was great, but he'd have to work in order to be able to use them.

Much like his infinite magic reserves, it was great to have that available, but the Infinity Wardstones were going to be severely limited by his circles. They were designed to accommodate normal wardstones. He'd have to rework the entirety of his spells if he wanted them to work with those wardstones. Fortunately, they didn't feel too different from normal wardstones in terms of functionality, even if they were so much more incredibly better. It wasn't like putting a bow next to a gun, at least. They did, in fact, work the same way, one was just much better at it.

'I have the magic to fuel them and the hardware to hold them. Now I just need to work out the actual spells,' Joshua thought to himself, looking at the thumb-sized stones. Spellcrafting something that'd use the new resource would take time, he'd have to trudge into new territory again and in a completely different way… But once he did? There'd be no limit.

So many things had been so complicated because he could only work with so much energy before foci started blowing up or something else. These wardstones… 'Actually, could I use them for hexes and boons too, maybe?' he considered, his interest intensifying.

"Thank you," he said, because he couldn't not say it again.

"If it'll get me my Silence," Ophis replied flatly and he almost laughed. How was it that Ophis seemed to be the easiest person to deal with? It was offset by the fact that he had to be extra careful or risk disappearing from existence, but Joshua would have been so happy if other people were that straightforward.

He really couldn't have nice things.

"I like this," the dragon added and Joshua had to hold back a chuckle again. Because she was pointing at the brownies. She'd just casually created the solution to a bunch of his problems, artifacts so powerful that only one of them would have been a faction treasure. She'd made so many of them and he was almost positive that she'd just make more if he asked.

And yet, Ophis seemed fascinated by brownies.

'Is this how people feel about me?' Joshua wondered.

"I'll bring more anytime you want," he told the dragon and she turned to stare at him. Joshua smiled. "I'll even bring ice cream. It goes well with warm brownies," he commented. His mother had loved that combination, he remembered. He wasn't as much of a fan of it, but people in general seemed to like it. And if all else failed, he was sure that Ophis at least wouldn't hate it.

"Ice cream," the dragon repeated, as if testing the words. She probably had never tried ice cream, he supposed. That was not surprising, considering every snack and drink he'd brought for her had been new to her. Hell, he had to wonder if she'd ever eaten anything before. 'That's kind of… sad, actually.'

"Yep," he replied, giving the dragon a slight smile. And it was only then that he realized he might be… getting a little comfortable there. That was dangerous. "I can bring other things too. There's a lot you can try, maybe you'll find new things that you might like," he offered, not hesitantly, but certainly carefully.

"You think?" she asked, blinking at him. 'Does she actually need to blink?' he wondered. Thinking about it, he hadn't really checked if she blinked, had he? That could be part of the reason why he found her so incredibly uncanny, he supposed, if he'd subconsciously noticed.

"We can try, so long as you don't mind the occasional bad experience. Everyone's taste in food is different," he explained, hoping that saying as much would prevent the disappearance of everything when they inevitably stumbled upon food that Ophis couldn't stand. Maybe he should have expected the slightly frown/pout expression that the dragon adopted after that.

Ophis remained silent then, her expression clearing as she turned her attention back to the food and the tea. Joshua, for his part, focused on the wardstones. The dragon was clearly thinking things over, after all. Or, at least, that was his best guess on the matter. Regardless, he'd made his offer and that was that. If Ophis didn't say anything else, he'd take that as a negative and keep bringing things he knew were safe.

He had already risked plenty enough as it was, really, and that was with only a vague guarantee that it'd be fine. Canon knowledge wasn't something he wanted to bet everything on, but he supposed it couldn't hurt when he had nothing else to use. Uncertain knowledge was better than no knowledge… for the most part.

"I want to try," Ophis said after all the food and drink he'd brought was finished and she was already halfway to one of the rooms.

Joshua just smiled as the door closed behind the dragon.


[}-o-{]
​

"So, it worked," Yasaka commented, sipping at her tea while looking at the wardstone that Joshua had presented for her after coming back home. "It feels incredible, and I have no idea on the matter. I'm guessing I can't comprehend how much of a big deal these are?"

"No, you can't," Joshua answered, grinning widely as he looked at the little artifact himself. "They will change everything. No more limits in terms of focus takes away a big part of what was holding me back. The things I can do with these…" he mumbled, feeling a chuckle clinging to his mouth even though it wasn't voiced.

He found himself surprisingly happy with this development.

Sure, he'd been terrified to try and ask Ophis, and he'd also had to hold back his reaction in front of the dragon. But those Wardstones were game changers. They were going to help him so much that he almost could forget about Khaos Brigade and the fear they brought to his life.

Friday seemed to be of a similar mind, her mind all but dancing around him as she spewed ideas. There was so much both of them could do with those. All of them immediately useful. They could make their defenses even more secure against Annihilation Maker and the Spartoi. They could more decisively shut down any enemy. Giving wings to angels could be so much easier and a more smooth process. Curing devils of the Sleep Disease. Working with Devil Powers. Helping Valerie, maybe fixing Sephiroth Graal if it came to it.

So many things were now within reach, or more easily done.

So many doors were opening for them.

"Someone's excited," Yasaka commented, an amused and fond smile on her lips. "I'll take your word for it. Is there anything we can do to help you achieve these things?" she added and he considered that for a long moment.

"Keep me away from politics?" he asked and she smiled wryly at him. "Yeah, I figured," he muttered, running his fingers through his hair. Alas, his time would continue to be divided in way too many things. The fact that he'd just delved deeper into politics didn't really help, but he stood by that decision still. They needed extra help if they wanted to find and deal with Khaos Brigade. They needed coordination and allies and more reach…

And if all else failed, then he could pull all those strings if he had to use Project WWW.

"I'm sorry."

"Not your fault," he said, waving her off and leaning away from the table. Then he blinked and looked around. "Where's Kunou?"

"Just noticed?" Yasaka commented and apparently she'd finished her tea, because she left the cup on the table and stood up to walk around the table towards him. "She was invited to play with Millicas. I thought it'd be nice for her to get out of the house for a bit and they seem to be good friends."

"Huh," was Joshua's eloquent response as he processed that. He'd been a bit too distracted with other things, apparently. "Yeah, now that I think about it…" he mumbled, frowning. "We should look for ways for her to do that, shouldn't we?" he wondered, mostly to himself.

Maybe because he was a bit – a lot – of a shut-in, but Joshua hadn't even considered that she kind of needed to do that. Or, he hadn't done so all that much, at least. Not to say that Kunou always stayed inside and at home, but… she probably didn't get out as much as she should. That was on him, sure, but he was kind of surprised that Yasaka hadn't considered that either until that day. Although, he had a fairly good guess…

"It'll take some getting used to, knowing that she can be safe in other places," Yasaka commented, confirming one of said guesses. "I'm actually wondering if we can take her to make friends, normal friends. Children that don't know who she is. It'll probably be good for her."

"Sounds like a plan to me," Joshua replied with a slight smile. It would, certainly, give Kunou more perspective, if nothing else. That could never hurt. "So, did you want to…" he trailed off then when Yasaka's arms wrapped around him and he felt her rest her chin on his shoulder. "... do anything?"

"Well, it's just the two of us today. Not even your mistresses around-"

"I don't think they'd like you calling them that," he pointed out, but there was no stopping the youkai woman, apparently. And his words came out absentminded, because it was kind of difficult to focus with her whispering in his ear. Let alone the tone she was using.

"-, so I thought we could enjoy the night between the two of us," she added and he could hear the smile on her voice.

"I have a feeling you have ideas already," he commented, tilting his head a little and giving her a half-smile of his own. "Do you plan to have dinner somewhere in there, at least, or are we skipping that part too?"

"Hm, we might need a break at some point," she told him and her smile became something else entirely.

His brain was halfway shut down already by then, but the kiss Yasaka delivered to his lips finished the job very quickly.


[}-o-{]
​

"Thanks for taking over, Levi," Joshua commented, yawning before rubbing his weary eyelids. "I know it was a little last minute, again, but something came up."

"It's no problem, Professor Davis," his student replied, and even his sleep-deprived self could pick up on the tone. When he glanced at him, Joshua noticed that Levi was glancing at his neck and not being very subtle about it. 'I knew I should have healed that, but nooo. I had to listen to her,' he thought, eye twitching.

"I also might need to pick your brain later. I came across something pretty good and we might be able to make use of it, all of us. Might make it into a Star group project even," Joshua commented, snapping his student out of useless thoughts and focusing him on something else. Granted, he didn't think he'd let very many people even look at the Ophis Wardstones, but his Stars were trustworthy.

And even if they weren't, they knew enough about him to know how much of a terrible idea it'd be to cross him.

"I look forward to it, Professor Davis," Levi replied, actually sounding rather excited. He knew he liked the guy for a reason. "Do you need me for anything right now though? I'd like to go over the class plan," he added and Joshua waved him off.

"Not at all. Knock yourself out," he reassured, running his fingers through his hair as Levi walked away towards the classroom. Joshua watched him go for a moment, before sighing wearily and glancing to the side. There, he found Iryuka. "Make a note to be extra nice to Levi. Guy's covering for me a lot more than I thought. Might need to talk with Agnes about actually making a schedule of classes that are outright his, at this point," he told her and the girl nodded quickly, scribbling away on her notepad.

"Yes, sir," she replied, completely seriously. It made him grimace. She used "sir" a lot more than Ravel did. At least she didn't use it when she was pulling away though, so Joshua guessed that was good. It was just incredibly awkward every single time. Something to get used to, he guessed.

He thought a little informality might stick if he insisted enough, but the world was determined to ignore him in that regard.

With that out of the way though, Joshua could focus on what he actually wanted to do. He was a little… distracted the previous night, but he wasn't about to put off working on those wardstones more than that. He couldn't really afford to, not really. There might not be an identifiable immediate threat to deal with, but Khaos was right there and they were obviously making moves.

Joshua needed to be ready when they inevitably decided to ruin his day.

He already had emergency plans and such, but updating those with Ophis Wardstones would be so much better. And that was without mentioning how much faster some of his projects could develop then, without the constraint of having to account for several spells of the same kind and different foci and a bunch of other factors that complicated matters more.

Although, admittedly, there was a chance that the wardstones would bring a whole bunch of new problems to the equations. Because infinity was likely to break a lot of his spell calculations. Fortunately, Joshua didn't think it'd be to the point of making them impossible to be worked with.

That would be very, very sad if it turned out to be the case.

"Mr. Davis?" Iryuka asked and he blinked, his mind returning to the present. "Did you change your mind?" the girl asked him and he considered that. She likely meant in regards to leaving House of Water. He could work in the classroom to back up Levi, but… It was distracting to do that.

He might get some work done, but that'd be negligible, really.

"We're going back home," he answered, stretching his back a little. He had a lot more to work with. He wasn't pushing to find something else, searching for new info, testing for new ideas. The Ophis Wardstones were a whole new toy to play with, added to everything else. Joshua would be damned if he didn't immediately try and make the most of them.

Especially considering how things were at that moment.

"Say," he commented as they walked to the teleportation circle. He could have disappeared away anywhere in House of Water, but it was only polite not to ignore the place's defenses like that, even if he'd been the one to place half of them. "Ravel will be there, most likely, and Koneko said she'd drop by. You can spend time with them if you have nothing to do," he suggested and he was rather surprised by the wide-eyed look Iryuka sent his way.

Of all times to mess up, he hadn't thought that would be one of them.

What kind of weird ass landmine had he stepped on?

"I… I happen to get along well with my family, sir," the girl stammered and he stared at her for a moment, no longer walking.

"What's that got to do with anything?" he asked, genuinely confused and Iryuka turned bright red. She wouldn't look at him either. 'Where in the fuck could I have possibly caused this?' he wondered, positively baffled. "Look, it's just an offer. You don't have to take me up on that. I just thought it'd be better. It'd also make me feel better, because you're rather young. So, it makes me feel less like I'm exploiting minors," he explained wryly.

Maybe he should just fire her and hire someone else. He hadn't wanted to reject her purely based on her age though. Especially after Ravel. Admittedly though, things had escalated a lot, which was the reason why the Phenex could no longer just take care of everything. Hell, it had been way too much for Ravel in general for a while. She was the only one in the know about a lot of things though.

She'd become essential.

Besides, she'd be sad if he fired her, and Joshua couldn't really bring himself to make that happen. What could he say? He had a particular weakness to sad girls, he supposed. Which… might apply to Iryuka, now that he thought about it.

'Fuck,' he cursed in his own mind. 'I'm such a pushover sometimes…'


[}-o-{]
​

"You know it's kind of scary that you progress this fast, right?" Göndul asked him and Joshua just offered her a half-hearted shrug.

He was a little busy at the time, mainly looking over the circle he'd just finished working on. It was a rune circle, of course, since he was in his Nordic Circles class with the old valkyrie. He'd made some very slight modifications to it and they had actually worked. To be honest, even Joshua was deeply shocked that they had. He had half expected it to go poorly.

Although, there were a lot of things he'd have to do to it for it to work "properly", but the spell worked, and that was what was important.

He was also just the smallest bit closer to being able to use runes like he wanted.

[Nordic Circles - Lvl 30/100

Determines the user's ability to understand and apply Nordic Circles.]

'Maybe at level 40?' he mused to himself, leaning back and cracking his neck. 'Level 50 would be the ideal, but… I don't know if I have that much time. I'll have to make that work… and hope I can.' Not the best of situations to be put in, but then again, that was his life. He'd never have an easy time like that, evidently.

With a pause in his thought process, he blinked and turned towards Göndul.

"Sorry," he mumbled, straightening a little and rubbing the side of his neck. "What did you say?" he asked then, because he'd gotten so distracted he forgot. In his defense, runes were fascinating and he'd been clear about it since forever ago. He already had so many ideas on what he could do once he got the hang of them. And every class he took, all those ideas would rework themselves or be replaced by new ones.

"Nothing," Göndul answered and he knew it hadn't been nothing, but if she was willing to just forget about it, then so was he. "Now, onto the next part, I think it'll make it clear why it was a little weaker than you expected if you look at this other circle here…" the old valkyrie started and he focused on what she was saying, teaching.

A new spell, which meant more context on how circles were supposed to work. At that point, he was pretty sure he could get by with just learning new spells. However, the same could be said about the tomes Göndul brought with her and he always tried to devour them like his life depended on it. After all, he couldn't take those home and that was very limiting.

It was kind of sad, that it'd been easier to get Boon magic from the Church than it was to get Rune Circles from the Norse. Maybe the formers had been that desperate for help. Or maybe the latters were that closed off to outsiders. It'd explain why they were so reluctant to join the alliance without their political games.

Or, maybe he was just missing a bunch of other context things.

Ultimately, he was getting what he wanted, even if the process was a little more annoying and slow than he'd have liked. Joshua had a lot to work on, so the limitation wasn't the worst thing in the world. It allowed him to focus on other things instead of trying to manage the time himself. Not even with three assistants could he perfectly manage his time. Especially his magic studies, because those could jump from one thing to the other or completely neglect a few things in favor of another.

It all depended on the most arbitrary things, really.

"I think I get it," he mumbled, giving the new circle another passing glance and then checking his experimental one from before. There, he could see at least one spot that he thought he knew how to improve. He'd do that after the class though. "Alright, yeah, definitely something to work on later. What's next?" he asked, turning to stare at Göndul. The woman seemed to pause for a second there, which made him wonder if he was maybe a little too intense.

"It really is a shame that you won't give my granddaughter a chance," she said then and it was a good thing he hadn't been drinking tea then or he'd have choked on it. What her obsession with Rossweisse and him being together was, he didn't know, but he also didn't want to know. His partners were plenty enough for him as it was. And besides, they didn't like the idea of him getting more partners, from what he'd gathered. Hell, even Gabriel's addition seemed to have been… special circumstances of a sort.

He still didn't get that, but he wasn't complaining.

Obviously.

"I'm sure she'll find someone else," he replied blandly, and then he got an idea. "The valkyries seemed to like Levi," he tried, only for the woman to scoff, which… ouch.

"No offense to the little genius," Göndul said, looking off to the side as if she were considering it. "His mind is a gift, truly, but Rossweisse doesn't need someone to challenge her mind. It'd be nice, but that's not all there is to it," she explained and Joshua wondered if he should just end that topic of conversation before it got awkward. Although, admittedly, it was a little late for that… For both things, he supposed. "That boy's too mild, in my opinion."

Mild was… not inaccurate when describing Levi, he supposed.

If that was her deal breaker though…

"What about George?" he asked and the old valkyrie narrowed her eyes at him. At least she hadn't dismissed the idea immediately, he supposed. Although, that might have been because she didn't know George.

"Tell me more," she all but demanded.

'Why am I having this conversation?' Joshua wondered as he started telling the woman about his other male Star. 'Oh, right, to get her off my case,' he remembered. Was that basically throwing George under the bus to save his own skin? Yes, yes it was.

He regretted nothing.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,607
Don't Need More Motivation

"Mr. Davis," Ravel commented before he ran his fingers through his hair.

With a wave of his hand, the notes and books he'd been working with disappeared inside storage spells. It almost felt like a shame to do that, but the fact was that he had things to do. 'One day, I'll be able to just work on magic and relax,' he thought, although it felt more like a hopeful wish rather than an actual expectation.

He was pretty sure he was cursed to live in interesting times, after all.

"If you're not ready…" Ravel offered, because of course she did. If he was a pushover when it came to her, she was a pushover when it came to him. It was a funny balance like that, he supposed. Although, the humor was ruined by the fact that he knew she was, deep down, a little afraid that he'd turn his back on her.

Joshua dearly hoped he could one day reassure her that wouldn't happen. Alas, it wasn't as easy as telling her and there was no simple way to show her either. The best he could do was just let time pass and hope that would do the trick eventually. Far from an ideal plan, he was sure, but it was what he had.

"It's fine," he reassured her, cracking his neck as he got ready to get on with things. It was early, which was the only reason Ravel had been about to offer him to push things off, but arriving early would be a point in their favor and he knew it. He could definitely afford to do that. "This is better, isn't it?" he asked and, even though he knew it, it was still kind of disappointing to get a nod. "Better to take advantage of the fact that you're around for now too," he added with a slight smile.

Her own expression dimmed a little, which worried him.

"What was it you had to do?" he asked then, because he knew it was a family thing that'd take her away shortly. He didn't remember the specifics of said family thing though. "Nothing Serafall or I can do, right?" he asked, which was probably the case. Had he asked when she'd first brought it up? Surely, right? But still-

"Sadly, no," Ravel answered and he hated that she had to add that first part. "And it's a small gathering of Pillar families." The explanation had him nodding. He knew Serafall sometimes had to go to those. The Leviathan title-slash-name change had spared her from most of the Sitri duties, but it had also brought others, if less in number.

And that was without the Satan duties added.

"Hm," was his very eloquent response. In his defense, he wasn't sure what he could say to that. It sucked that she had to participate in that, but… At least Ravel seemed to enjoy that kind of thing more than he did. "Well, hope you have fun."

"Iryuka should be there, so it won't be too bad," the girl commented with a slight smile. "And Koneko too, I guess," she added, as an afterthought and he raised an eyebrow at her but didn't comment. It was amusing to watch the girls try and play off their affection to one another like that. Although, they did sometimes border on rude.

"I'm glad to hear that," he told her with a smile of his own. Hers turned the slightest bit softer, more real at that moment. "I'll have to deal with the Greeks on my own then, I guess. The worst part should be over by then though," he added then, stretching a little as he prepared to teleport away. "I promise I won't set fire to that bridge."

"You better. Speaking of not burning bridges though, we should be on our way," Ravel told him, visibly amused as they started making their way to the teleportation circle. Although, that seemed to be impeded by something as her expression dimmed. "Seekvaira should be able to take up these kinds of duties once she's up to speed and we've verified that she's trustworthy," the girl continued and he tilted his head to look at her.

"Hm, good to know," he replied, trying to get a read on the little Phenex. It wasn't as easy as he'd have liked, unfortunately. So, it was time to poke her and see if that told him anything. "That eager to ditch me, huh?"

"Not at all!" she exclaimed, exaggerated and dramatic as she could be on occasion. No wonder she'd done well in Serafall's show with her few appearances. "I just don't want to limit what you can do!" she added, all but shouting and he almost expected her to add a "sir" at the end. He could hear it in her voice.

That was more of an extreme reaction than he'd expected, admittedly.

"Ravel, you're not limiting me at all," he told her, but that didn't seem to do anything.

"I am though," she mumbled, looking down and away, fidgeting a little as they walked. "I'm- Seekvaira is a heiress, a proper one. She's been trained in political maneuvers a lot more than I have. I've studied to eventually have to manage my husband's business and those sorts of duties, so I can more or less make do in other situations, but… it's not the same," she explained.

Joshua stopped and stared at her.

"Do you want it?" he asked and she paused, her expression twisting in confusion, uncomprehension. "To study that sort of thing, to know how to do it," he clarified and she blinked at him. She'd sounded wistful to his ears, at least, so… "Because if so, I'm sure we can find someone to teach you. Kunou has classes on that sort of thing. Failing that, Serafall surely can help us find a tutor for you that can do the devil equivalent," he added.

There was a moment of silence then as they moved, but when they reached the circles…

"... I'd like that," Ravel whispered, her voice so low it was almost a whisper. He barely caught it and he wondered if he hadn't been meant to actually hear her. He wondered if she'd said it not quite daring to mean it, to hope for it.

And Joshua thought about why that could be, because he'd been spoiling her together with everyone else, yet…

Sometimes, he really wanted to test the immortality of the Phenex family.

"I'll look into it then," he said instead of the myriad of ideas he had in mind regarding what to do. The smile he got in response felt like a victory, but he had plenty going on at the back of his mind. Because that wouldn't be the end of things.


[}-o-{]
​

"Lady Athena," Joshua greeted and he noticed that the woman in front of him looked way too happy to see him. It was a little worrying, actually, although he wasn't sure why. "Didn't know we'd have company today," he added and he looked at the other three goddesses. He knew that much because the Egyptians were helping him pick up on it. Apparently, they could do that.

They'd just had fun watching him flail a little during his last visit to Thebes.

Joshua was seriously considering just turning away from their collective unfunny asses.

Alas, the buffs were too good for that. And if they didn't want to feel offended by his thoughts, then they should stop giving him excuses to think badly of them, really. 'Glad we can entertain you though, Set,' he thought to himself wryly and the god gave him the equivalent of a laugh in response.

Asshole.

"Mr. Davis," Athena greeted and her smile got even wider. That wasn't doing much to reassure him, at all. "These are Hecate, Nemesis and Themis," she said and… He knew two of those goddesses. Well, he wasn't sure if he could count Nemesis, on second thought. Hecate was a lot more well known, that's for sure. Nemesis kind of seemed self-explanatory enough, but he didn't want to assume too much. "They are here to watch and, potentially, help us in our quest," Athena explained…

Which told him precisely nothing.

He stared at her for a long moment, then glanced at the other goddesses, who seemed remarkably at ease with just… not saying anything. Was that normal? Letting someone else do all the talking? Was it because Athena was higher ranked or something?

Admittedly, they seemed a little distracted, like their focus was half on some other thing.

God stuff, he supposed.

"I see," was all he could think to reply with, but his brain kept working on something. "Feel free to tell me if there's anything I can do then," he added with a slight smile that he hoped didn't come out half-assed. He appreciated all the help offered, really he did. He just didn't feel like dealing with more people. Especially deities and especially deities of a pantheon that he barely knew in DxD context.

In a way, it was better that the goddesses weren't feeling very chatty, apparently.

"Perfect," Athena said, beaming. "Now, I'm sure you're busy and would rather get on with things," she added, showing why she was the Goddess of Wisdom. So, without further ado, she led him to the Spartos. There wasn't much fanfare there either and he was growing increasingly grateful for that.

He'd dreaded the worst when he'd been faced with a bunch of goddesses.

'Wonder if I'll get used to… this at some point,' he thought, looking at the strange creature that the Spartos had turned into. Beside him, he knew Athena was making a face like she was smelling something foul at the same time that someone was poking at her with a knife. She reacted like that when in the presence of the Spartos, he'd noticed.

He'd also noticed that the Egyptians were strangely sympathetic towards that.

All the same, the bizarre sight of the Spartos aside, Joshua had a job to do. So, he didn't delay his casting much, if at all. After a cursory glance at it, noticing all the changes from the last time he'd seen it – it had scales and spikes and gills and antlers and… –, he placed his first spell down. Then the next and so on until he had an array set up and then another.

He didn't use the Ophis Wardstones that time. He was still working on the spells that'd use those, first of all. Second of all, he wasn't sure he wanted to reveal those to the world at large quite yet. Not without a good reason, and he didn't have one at that moment. His partners had also agreed with that assessment, which was a large part of the reason why he carried on with that in mind.

"Fascinating," a voice said to his side and he almost jumped when he turned and saw Hecate almost touching shoulders with him. Her eyes were fixed on his circles though, his arrays. "So many spells, all of them unique, all of them working in perfect harmony… How long have you been working on this?" she asked and he blinked.

"A few days," he answered and it was the goddess' turn to pause. "I mean, most of the foundation is the same I use for analyzing things and gathering data," he explained, turning his attention back to the information he was getting for the most part. Maybe he'd been a teacher for a little too long, because he kept on going even while he did that. "I've just modified it with what I gathered last time to try and pick up new things, that's all," he said with a shrug.

When he turned towards her, Hecate was looking at him like she had previously at the circles. Keenly aware of her as he was, Joshua sensed Ravel shaking her head behind him. Had he done something wrong? He'd just answered the question. What was wrong with that?

And why were the Egyptians laughing at him? Especially Nephthys.

Deciding to ignore all that, Joshua turned towards the Spartos and took a deep breath in.

'It's… reaching, shifting as if trying to expand but not… not doing it,' he noticed. It was like it moved through shifting. Or, at least, it tried to. It was in a cage then, not under a net anymore, but it wasn't moving much. It barely could reach through the bars, as if there were an invisible barrier besides the physical one.

Yet, Joshua noticed how the shifting almost seemed to push against that.

"Very interesting," he mumbled, summoning a notebook to write some things down.

"Disgusting, that's what it is," a new voice said and he turned to see Nemesis to his other side. Immediately after she spoke, Athena bristled. "Don't deny it, Athena. I know they are yours, but they are… It's so off balance. Pieces are missing and they've been replaced with something… more. It's an aberration in general and to my senses."

"Laws that had been left alone for eons were broken for this," Themis said as she joined too, somehow sounding both sad and angry.

And as they spoke, Joshua tilted his head. He wasn't sure if any of that was useful to him, but… He watched the Spartos hit the barrier, its cage. He noticed the shifting it did, trying to escape. And he pondered the goddesses' perspectives…

"Tell me more about that," he said, turning and glancing between Nemesis and Themis. Both goddesses faced him a second later, and the former seemed taken aback while the latter paused. "Tell me what you see when you look at it," he pressed, glancing towards Athena too.

And maybe he was a little intense, because Ravel brought a hand to her face.

The goddesses didn't seem to mind, at least.


[}-o-{]
​

"So, yeah, things were… I wanna say good, but I have to start testing this information," Joshua explained, leaning back and bringing his cup of tea to his lips. "At least I have a lot to work with, which is always nice."

"And I'm glad to hear that," Yasaka said, smiling widely as she had for a bit. She was always happy when they were on a date, but she was especially so when they went somewhere outside of her range. Like they had at that moment, sitting in a store that she'd never been to before. He didn't blame her for that, at all, but it was still very interesting and amusing to see. "So, how was it to meet so many goddesses?" she asked and he sighed.

"Worrying?" he answered as he ran his fingers through his hair. "I mean, I thought it'd be a disaster, so I guess in that sense it was fine. I'm just not made to meet new people in general, let alone in groups, and even less when they are important like that, you know?" he tried his best to explain. Sometimes he wondered if he did a good job though, because he was more or less the only person that had issues like that… that he knew, at least.

'Why are all my acquaintances extroverts?' he lamented with a sigh.

Then again, he guessed meeting another introvert would just end up with both of them avoiding each other. 'Suddenly the non-relationship with Ajuka makes a lot of sense, maybe,' Joshua thought idly. It would explain quite a bit if that was the case, at least.

"Couldn't have been that bad. Ravel seemed to think you made a good impression," Yasaka pointed out. Strangely, he felt as if there was something odd in her voice. Like she meant something other than what she was saying or maybe like she was leaving something out, that was the impression he got. Before he could ask though, she continued. "That aside, this place is rather nice," she commented and that was a remarkably bad topic change for someone like Yasaka.

Yet, when he looked at that mock-innocent face, Joshua knew he'd go along with it anyway.

"Glad you like it," he replied with a slight smile. "It's always a little nerve wracking when I have to find a place. Especially because I don't really have time to actually try the spots before bringing you," he admitted to himself, bringing a hand up to rub the back of his neck.

"Well, somehow, you've managed to get more hits than misses. Congratulations," Yasaka told him, sounding way too amused. Joshua didn't appreciate that, he really didn't. Alas, that was one of the women that he loved. "Do you think Kunou would like it here?" Yasaka asked and to that, Joshua grinned.

"Sure she would, I saw a bunch of snacks that she'd like in the menu," he answered immediately and the answer seemed to please the youkai woman. Or maybe it was the fact that he'd answered so quickly, already having thought about that himself. "There was this one, let me look for it," he mumbled, pulling the menu and looking for the one that'd specifically caught his eye. "This one… here," he mumbled, pausing when he looked up and he was met with Yasaka's fond expression. "Sorry, I just-"

"Don't apologize," she told him, her smile widening. A second later, he felt her tails under the table wrapping around his legs and his body. It was a good thing that he'd already thoroughly covered the entire area with spells, he supposed. For one, that'd keep them somewhat safe. For another, it prevented people from mundane backgrounds from noticing… Well, anything supernatural. "What about your other daughters though? Won't they feel neglected if you focus so much on Kunou?"

"Cheshire and the rest get to come with me to most places if they feel like it. And they are more than happy just staying home or exploring random forests and such," he replied with a roll of his eyes.

"And what about the other two?" Yasaka asked with a raised eyebrow and he paused.

"They are more complicated," he answered with a shrug. "But I try," he said as he brought his tea to his lips. "I'm always open to suggestions," he added with a slight grin that became more certain when Yasaka giggled.

"Well, first of all…"


[}-o-{]
​

"We have a new participant in today's training," Joshua announced unnecessarily. Everyone in the training facilities could see the devil standing to his side. "This is Shalba Beelzebub, you will call him Shalba," he said and he made sure that there was some emphasis there, because he said "will" not "may" and that was important.

The guy was nowhere near being in good standing and he wanted that to be obvious.

"Well, two, really, since Katerea hasn't actively trained with us," he added and the devil woman shuffled where she stood. "Shalba, Katerea, you'll be joining Raynare, Kokabiel and George," he told the two and the group gathered and looked at Joshua's familiars. "Kuroka, you'll be with my familiars." She had somewhat of a chance of working better with those, since she had senjutsu to help her a little. That was what he was banking on, at least.

It was the next best thing to his Bond for communication with most of them.

"You got it~"

"Nagini, if you absolutely have to kill someone, make sure it's Shalba," Joshua told the gigantic snake, which hissed something half-hearted. That was the best he'd get, he supposed. "You're the least useful here and the one I like the least. Don't look so surprised," he added, turning towards an indignant Beelzebub descendant. Granted, he was useful enough, but he was the least useful of the bunch, for a number of reasons.

"Can we kill him?" Kokabiel asked, making the devil pale.

"No," Joshua answered and the fallen angel clicked his tongue… together with Kuroka and George. 'Shalba has no friends,' he noted to himself, more amused than anything else. It was even more funny because two of those were on Shalba's team, but… Oh well. Good to know that even Khaos Brigade could hate Khaos Brigade… in a way. "Anyway," he said, deciding to just continue with his life. Being a little silly was fine, but they were there for something other than that. "I'd appreciate it if you tried not to kill him," he told Nagini, who hissed something halfheartedly.

Cheshire purred something, the communication through the bond telling him that she'd make sure the snake wouldn't. He believed that a lot more, Joshua would admit. Nagini didn't even seem offended, which was very telling.

"Have fun, yeah?" he added for Margalo, who chirped something and flew off his shoulder. "And you…"

"Yes, daddy?" Morag asked, blinking at him, and he would swear Kunou had taught her how to be that cute. He almost wanted to pull her into a hug and bring her with him away from the training ground. Then she smiled a little wider, a little more excited. "We'll win," she added, as if reassuring him.

"I'm sure you will," he replied, tucking a lock of hair behind her ear. "Don't be too mean, yeah?"

"It's not cute," Morag said, as if that was the only thing to worry about. Joshua stared at her for a long moment, wondering if he should say something to that. Ultimately, he smiled and patted her head. Morag had good reasons to be an odd one, after all. But he still loved her.

"Then," he said, turning away and walking off to the side. "Begin," he called without turning and the battle started immediately. His mind was already moving on to the next thing though. "Sorry to make you wait."

"Wait?" Valerie asked, as if he hadn't brought her there and made her wait on a bench for about five minutes on her own. Although, admittedly, he figured her fragmented soul and mind could barely track that much time. For her, it might as well have been a few seconds, the way her thoughts got all tangled and jumbled.

That didn't make things any better though, not at all.

"Yeah, wait," he answered with a nod as he sat beside her. "It wasn't nice to just have you sit here until I was done," he admitted, running his fingers through his hair. "Sorry about that."

"You are nice," she replied, beaming and he smiled sadly at her. "I like you," she added, her expression brightening even more. She was way too much like that, but he loved it. He loved it, but he also was incredibly sad about it, because at least half of that was because of her condition and he knew it.

"I like you too," he replied and that seemed to make her happy too. "So, do you have anything in mind for what to do now?" he asked her. Because that was just about the only things one could ask her, things about the present, things regarding the very moment the question was asked. Because things in the past, she could barely remember and using that to formulate thoughts was hard. She also couldn't think about the future, because she got lost in her imagination whenever she tried.

"They are funny," she commented instead of answering, looking off to where the others were waiting. "So excited."

"They are like that," he replied with a nod.

"Could I join them?" Valerie asked and Joshua stopped midway through opening a notebook.

"When we've managed to make you feel better," he answered and the girl let out a light cheer.

"Thank you," she told him and he nodded absently, looking for the page where he had her notes to look through them again. 'Go help your sisters, Friday. Stop looking over my shoulder,' he thought out loud and the living spell pouted and her presence shifted away. That was when a magic beam shot at Raynare, who burnt it away with Incinerate Anthem. "I mean it," Valerie insisted and Joshua blinked before turning to look at the vampire. She was staring straight at him with bright red eyes, intently and aware. "I appreciate that you're trying so hard," she explained.

She was having one of her lucid moments, apparently.

"You'll be fine some day, Valerie," he promised and the girl smiled. Not the half-vacant one she usually wore. No, this one was smaller, but no less meaningful. It was full of so much more emotion and thought that it was more meaningful, actually.

"Thank you."


[} Chapter End {]

Hey guys! How's it going?

Writing new characters is a pain. And writing many characters in one scene is also a pain. Both of those issues presented themselves in this chapter and I hate it. Alas, that's what always ends up happening in my stories. Because I can't really limit things to a small cast for whatever reason. Maybe because… Well, a world should be full of people. There's more than a handful of people to it and if you're actually making waves like Joshua…

Yeah, he's kind of shooting himself in the foot in that regard.

He does seem to be cursed that way, doesn't he?

Still, I hope you guys enjoyed the chapter.
