#1,621
How Do We Grab Hold of It?

There was something interesting about the time after the Spartos appeared in his life.

It brought Khaos Brigade back to the forefront of his life, yes, and that was a terrible thing for his nerves. However, the terrorist organization seemed to have disappeared off the face of Earth again and that was… worrying, yes, but left everyone in a spot where nothing was happening again. Stuck back where they'd been, but not really. It was jarring, whenever he stopped to think about it.

For Joshua in particular though, it had brought a lot of new things to do, let alone that it'd given him the push to ask Ophis for the wardstones. So, all in all, he'd gone from having nothing to do to having a lot of stuff to work with. Sure, none of it really made his work any easier and it piled onto his already exceedingly busy schedule, but… Joshua was feeling kind of better than before.

Because before he'd been working a lot just to get scraps. With new things added to the mix, he was back to feeling like he was getting somewhere with his work. It made his time feel like he was actually being productive with it, rather than working a lot and being busy for nothing or almost nothing. So, in that sense, Joshua was doing better than before, and he appreciated that.

"What are you thinking about?" Kunou asked, throwing a ball at him and he caught it with his left hand before throwing it back much more gently than she had.

She'd seen a scene in a cartoon they'd been watching, of a father and son duo playing catch and she'd asked if that was actually fun to do. Admittedly, it didn't look like much and it wasn't the most thrilling thing to do, but… There was something nice about it. So, she'd liked it when they tried and there they were, still doing it.

She was fine just playing and letting his mind wander, so that helped.

"Just going over the current situation," he answered, catching the ball again and throwing it back. "Sometimes it helps to step back and look at the full picture for a bit," he commented, which wasn't a lie, but also felt like a lie.

So, he decided to turn it into reality.

The reality was that he was working on a bunch of things regarding Khaos Brigade. The main points were the Spartos and Sephiroth Graal though. Yasaka, Serafall and Gabriel would take care of the rest of the mess in that regard, with raids and such. They'd let him know if they found anything new that he might need to be informed of.

"So," Kunou started throwing the ball and catching it again when he threw it back. "Is it helping?" she asked and he shrugged. There wasn't much to think about. He'd thought about maybe having Valerie trying to do something with the Spartos, but he was pretty nervous about letting her use her Sacred Gear much in general. The fact that the Spartos had turned out like it did only made it all worse. Furthermore, using a broken Sephiroth Graal on the abomination created by another broken Sephiroth Graal just sounded like a recipe for disaster.

His partners had agreed with that assessment too.

"Not really, I don't think," he answered, but his mind was latching onto that. Was there something else he could do? Maybe there were some other pieces on the board that he wasn't seeing. Or maybe there was another way to use the two that he had for something.

Grendel was a product of Sephiroth Graal, he supposed, so he could try to take a look at him. He already had though, but it couldn't hurt to take another look and go over his notes. The vampires that had been augmented fell into that category too, he supposed. 'What else is there?' he mused to himself.

Spartoi. Grendel. Vampires. Valerie herself.

'Two of those are related to dragons,' he noted to himself, but that could just be DxD bullshit. The entire verse seemed to be obsessed with Dragons. One only needed to look at the strongest beings in existence, Ophis and Great Red. Both were dragons, so…

'Wait, Spartoi were born from dragon teeth,' he thought to himself, pausing as he caught the ball again. He didn't throw it back though, his mind fully committing to the thought. 'How close are Spartoi to dragons, if at all?' he wondered. It didn't sound very relevant, but Khaos had four more of those, so…

'Something to ask Athena,' he decided, throwing the ball back to a slightly confused Kunou.

"You thought of something," the girl pointed out and he nodded. Fortunately, she dropped matters then. It wasn't that he didn't want to tell her, but he preferred not to talk too much business with her if he could help it. What he did wasn't always child friendly, for one, and for another… he'd rather let Kunou be a normal child rather than talk about business with her.

She had enough seriousness in her classes and whenever Yasaka needed her to be the "princess" of her faction. Yasaka agreed with him that they should let her have time not needing to worry about any of that. Some things were inevitable, but not all of them were, so they'd try their best to offer her more instances of the latter case when they could.

"Fine," Kunou pouted even as he considered his latest idea some more. Maybe he could test how the Spartos reacted to Ascalon and how Ascalon reacted to it. The sword didn't seem to care for much other than dragons, barely having any personality, so… Maybe he could get something, maybe he wouldn't. It couldn't hurt to test. "This is surprisingly nice," she commented, throwing the ball back at him.

"I know, right?" he asked with a smile that his daughter returned. "We should do this again," he commented.

Kunou readily agreed.

A little amused, he wondered if Koneko and Ravel would be down. He rather doubted it, but he'd also doubted Kunou would like it so… Who knew? Especially if the two saw Kunou having a good time.

Joshua entertained himself with that thought for a bit.


[}-o-{]
​

"That was… a lot more thorough than I thought it'd be," Joshua commented, blinking repeatedly.

It hadn't taken him long after thinking about it to contact Athena and organize another meeting. It helped that the goddess was more than eager to get things done in regards to her Spartoi. Apparently, it was very disturbing for her, since the Spartoi all had traces of divinity that she could feel.

It was unfortunate that she couldn't use said traces to track them though, but he guessed that would have been too easy. His life could never be easy and he knew it by then. Furthermore, it didn't really help that whatever Khaos had done had seriously screwed with the sown warriors, he supposed.

"You do remember who you're talking to, don't you?" Athena asked with a raised eyebrow and he snorted. "I'd be very ashamed of myself if I weren't able to tell you this much about my own creations."

This much being pretty much anything he'd been able to think about asking in regards to the Spartoi, and plenty that he hadn't thought about. She'd been speaking for quite a long time, and he'd made sure to write it all down. Joshua knew that he'd spend a few days just going over everything she'd told him, to make sure he was properly processing and using it all.

"One question though," he commented and Athena seemed taken aback. Had she expected to have answered any question he might have? That was… valid, yeah. "How do they react to Dragon Slayer energy?" he asked.

"They are not dragons, Dragon Slayer energy doesn't affect them like it does dragons, even though they were born from dragon teeth," Athena answered calmly and he stared at her for a long moment. "Does that not sufficiently answer your question?" she asked and he considered that.

"I asked how they react to Dragon Slayer energy, not if Dragon Slayer energy affects them the same as dragons," he clarified and she narrowed her eyes for a moment. The previously half-dismissive attitude sharpening. "Is there no other effect it could have on them? If so, do Dragon Slayer artifacts react in any way to the Spartoi?" he asked.

Silence was his answer for a long few seconds and he could see the goddess's mind working. It was… very interesting, to think that he might have stumbled over something that the Goddess of Wisdom didn't know. Although, that struck him as… odd too. Then again, none of the gods that he'd interacted with or "interacted with" such as most of the Egyptian pantheon struck him as absolute, even in their main domains.

Fairly great, yes, but not absolute.

The only thing even remotely absolute that he had met was Ophis and it wasn't even close for anyone else.

"I can't rightfully say that I know the answer to that," she admitted and she almost looked like it physically hurt her to say as much. "I only checked that Dragon Slayer energy wouldn't be harmful to them and… nothing else through their life provided further knowledge on the matter," she commented and that explained things, he supposed. Still kind of interesting to find something a goddess of wisdom didn't know though.

"Well, we can find out then," Joshua replied, turning his head towards the captured Spartos and summoning Ascalon to his hand. It didn't react like it had to dragons, that was for sure. However, it seemed to stir from its almost permanent slumber all the same. Not in the eager-hunt mode that reminded him of Cheshire chasing prey in the forest, however. Instead, it reminded him more of Friday or Morag looking at something new, curiosity for the most part. Maybe some confusion, like the sword thought it should go into slaying mode but wouldn't. "That's an interesting reaction," he mumbled to himself, looking between the Spartos and Ascalon.

"What is it?" Athena asked, a hunger in her eyes that was very Cheshire like. Maybe it was the fact that she'd just found herself lacking in something related to knowledge. Or maybe she was like that every time new knowledge was offered to her. All the same, Joshua found himself briefly amused.

So, he explained what he got from the sword as best he could.

After that, he continued, testing things. He tried to pick up any information he could from the Spartos, but that was harder to do. Far as he could tell though, there was nothing of note there, but it was difficult to tell anything when it came to the abomination, really. Interestingly, the creature was affected by Dragon Slaying energy though, they found out when he nicked with the tip of the blade.

Even Ascalon seemed surprised by that.

"That's…" Athena mumbled, looking deeply disturbed. "That's impossible. I tested for that," she said, looking like she desperately wanted Joshua to believe her. Although, she also sounded like she might be trying to reassure herself.

"The change," he commented, tilting his head. "It makes them… a little bit of everything. So, just like it always has a handful of different features at all times, there might be bits of dragon thrown into the mix. So, the shifting isn't only physical…" he noted to himself, taking a deep breath in and considering the implications of that. "Just like it reacts now, it might not react at another time, if it loses the dragon property it probably has now… I should test that though. If it always has a weakness like that, then that's worth noting. It might be very slight, but…"

"Every advantage is worth exploiting, if freely given," Athena finished for him and he nodded. Then the goddess took a deep breath in. "Now I find myself curious what else is there to learn about them," she mused out loud, mostly to herself.

She didn't look interested though.

She looked curious the same way someone might be curious about how a car crash will turn out.


[}-o-{]
​

"Am I boring you, Joshua?"

He took a deep breath, his eyes remaining closed. He was sitting on a bench, leaning back and facing the sky. Around them, there was the whisper of people talking some distance away and the faint ambient music that was set up. There was a gentle breeze washing over them, like a careful caress. The smell of old stone and wood permeated the entire place, but there was also the hint of his date's perfume that almost made him smile.

"Not at all," he answered, not opening his eyes even then. "I just… I was struck by how peaceful this place is," he added. That is, before he snorted. "Although, there's a chance that I'm more tired than I thought," he admitted and it seemed to take effort to push his head up and forward as he opened eyes to look at Gabriel. "Sorry about that though, the last thing I want is to make you think you're boring," he told her and he meant every word. Hopefully, she'd realized that.

There was no reason for her not to, since she was just as good at reading people as either of his other two partners. Not for the first time, he wondered why he'd ended up in a relationship with people so scarily good at reading others. Idly, he also wondered if that said something about him, or them, or both.

"It is rather calm here, isn't it?" the angel commented, looking around and taking in the place around them. It was an old building, a house or something of the sort, that had been turned into something similar to a park. Or, at least, the garden-like spot in the middle of the building had. The actual building, a square surrounding the spot they were at, was more of a museum sort of deal… ish. "I hadn't quite noticed that," Gabriel added, as if seeing the place in a completely different light.

"You don't have to humor me," he told her with a half-smile, especially when she took a seat next to him. "We can check out the east side," he suggested, but she shook her head.

"No, I think I want to sit here and enjoy this," she replied and his incredulity and doubt might have shown on his face rather clearly, because she was rather quick to add: "I mean it. I'm usually too eager to look at the place, take in the architecture, the crafts that went into the buildings and statues and gardens, but… The atmosphere isn't something I tend to appreciate much, I think," she explained and he nodded slowly, still not quite sure he believed her. "I'm not lying."

"I'm gonna trust you about that," he said, as if he weren't. He knew Gabriel could lie to him no problem, sure, but he also knew she wasn't likely to, especially if she insisted like that. Especially over something so inane. So, he just sat there next to her for a long moment as they took in their surroundings. Although, it was kind of ruined a little when he noticed people around them looking their way, because of course they did. Gabriel was ridiculously beautiful, after all.

It was always a little amusing to see people's reactions to her.

He'd even get his own looks more often than not, probably wondering how he'd managed to get with a woman that gorgeous. Sometimes Joshua wondered what looks he'd get if he ever went out with all three of his partners. Not that he would, since they didn't seem interested in that, but the hypothetical was funny in his mind.

"You can close your eyes and lean back again, if you want," Gabriel told him but he shook his head and waved the idea away.

"I'm afraid I might fall asleep if I do," he admitted with a chuckle. Although, he was only half joking, really. "I'd rather not have to deal with light attacks today," he added, which was definitely a joke. He knew Gabriel wouldn't attack him… Instead, she might look sad, or disappointed, or something, and that'd hurt so much more, he knew.

"It's fine if you do," Gabriel told and if he'd been skeptical before, he was downright suspicious of a trap then and there. "I mean it," she added with a warm smile. "You've been working tirelessly for quite a while. You deserve some rest, so I'm not going to begrudge you for it," she reassured him. "I'm not going to feel bad at all, really. It's kind of flattering that you've come here with me even though you could be resting at home instead."

Often, Joshua would find himself disbelievingly wondering how he'd gotten so lucky with his partners. Not only because they were completely out of his league, but also because they had somehow decided that they'd be happy sharing him even. It was the kind of bullshit that he wouldn't have even dreamed off back in his old life. The kind of thing that belonged in nonsensical fantasies.

Yet, there he was.

"One day," Gabriel started again then, running her fingers softly through his hair as if pushing a lock behind his ear, even though his hair wasn't long enough to really do so. "We might convince you that you're worth plenty. I really hope we do," she told him and her smile seemed a little sad.

And he hated that he was the reason for that.

"You're succeeding," he replied, but even he knew there was more to it than just that. "Just… not completely, I guess," he added with a shrug. It was how he was, he supposed. It sucked, but his mind worked that way and it wouldn't be easy to dispel that notion.

"One day," Gabriel repeated before gently moving her hand around his head and pulling him in for a kiss. "We'll just have to keep trying, I suppose," she said with a slightly wider smile before she pushed him down, resting his head on her lap. "Now, enjoy the atmosphere, alright? I think I rather like this spot," she told him.

"I love you," he said with a smile on his face that wasn't likely to disappear anytime soon.

"I love you too," Gabriel replied, a hand moving up to touch the iris flower resting behind her ear.


[}-o-{]
​

"You don't trust me."

Joshua raised an eyebrow at that, looking at Zekram Bael with an otherwise flat expression. Because, really, what kind of statement was that? The devil knew that he… Well, that he knew a bunch of things, many of those things he didn't have any business knowing. Furthermore, the man had to know that Serafall had told him a thing or two about him herself.

"Are you surprised?" he asked instead of deigning that statement with any other response.

"Not at all," the Great King answered with a slight smile that took him aback some. "I mean that in the sense that you don't even try to pretend to trust me," he explained and that made sense. However, Joshua didn't think that made much sense, both the statement and doing as he said.

"I don't see the point," he replied, taking a deep breath in and running his fingers through his hair. "You've been playing this game for way too long for me to think I can fool you, and that's without me being terrible at the game to begin with," he said and that seemed to deeply amuse the Bael. He wasn't sure how he felt about that. "Besides, I don't see any reason to even try."

"That makes you smarter than most people I have to deal with on a regular basis," Zekram commented and somehow Joshua wasn't sure if that was a compliment for him or an insult for the others. It was probably both, maybe, but if he had to bet, it was more the latter than the former. "It's a real shame that you're not a devil," the man added.

Joshua felt like there was a lot to unpack there and he did not have the emotional bandwidth to deal with that at the moment. So, he just pushed that to the back of his mind and picked up his notebook. Better to go back to working on the Power of Destruction project for Sairaorg. The sooner he was done with that, the sooner he could stop having to interact with Zekram.

He felt like that'd be the best for his continued sanity.

Or whatever was left of it, at least.

"Giving up already?" the devil asked, an amused grin on his face. It always looked off to Joshua whenever the Bael looked happy and just generally nice and positive. It made him feel like he was missing a trap somewhere. "Maybe you underestimate yourself rather than overestimate yourself like everyone else does. I wonder if that's better or worse."

"Moving on," he said and that only seemed to amuse Zekram more. "Can you do anything other than projecting, manifesting or controlling Power of Destruction away from your body?" he asked and that seemed confuse the Bael for a bit. Or maybe it took him a moment to process the question. Either way… "What I mean, basically, is… can you do anything you haven't shown me? Like applying Power of Destruction to your body or doing something else that'd be different from what I've seen so far."

"Oh, you mean how Lucifer can turn his body to Power of Destruction," Zekram noted, a hint of disdain in his tone. It was no surprise for Joshua to find that the man didn't like Sirzechs much. It was a little surprising that the Bael called him Lucifer though, but not much. "I'm afraid you'll have to ask him for that if you need it. I've pretty much demonstrated the extent of what I can do," he commented, but he didn't seem to be a fan of that. "If possible though, I'd rather you don't. I want Sairaorg to have as pure a Power of Destruction as possible rather than whatever it is the Gremorys have."

'Ah, Pride, that's a lot easier to understand,' Joshua noted to himself, reassured that Zekram had stopped acting completely different from what he expected him to. He'd been a little worried for a minute there. They were in much more understandable territory once again and he was relieved by that.

"Alright, I'll try not to use that unless I really have to," he replied and that seemed to please Zekram. Honestly, the project was interesting and he would carry it out, but he had zero issues with the Bael hindering the entire thing with his Pride. It wasn't like Joshua needed to finish it to get "paid" for the work. And Sairaorg seemed kind of ambivalent on the entire thing at best so…

It was fine if things didn't go particularly fast.

"With that said," he commented, rubbing the back of his neck and looking to the side thoughtfully. "Let's go over things one more time. Then I think we can stop with the regular testing. I have more or less what I want. I'll give you a call if I have new stuff to work on and if you want a progress report, just let me know," he told the Bael.

Mostly because he just didn't want to interact with the man all that much. So, if he could cut back on such instances, all the better, as far as Joshua was concerned. Besides, he did more or less mean what he was saying and he wasn't cheating the guy out of what he'd asked. He was just tweaking the situation so that it'd be less awkward for him.

Joshua didn't think it was crazy for him to do that.

And if it was, then it was whatever.

He didn't like Zekram anyway.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,629
The World Owes Me a Debt-

"And Levia-tan saves the day again!" Serafall exclaimed, looking very proud of herself and twirling around to celebrate her victory. Off to the side, Joshua golf clapped with his expression deliberately the mildest flavor of impressed. "Domino, you're ruining my moment here," Serafall mock-whispered and he faked surprise and offense.

"Me? I'd never," he denied, not even trying to put proper scandal into his voice nor his expression. "That was properly impressive, Levi. The stuff of legend. They'll put that in the history books, for sure," he reassured her with barely any enthusiasm.

Serafall groaned.

"You suck."

"What'd I do?" he asked, a half-smile on his face that said he knew exactly what he'd done. "I'm congratulating you."

"You could congratulate me less," Serafall hissed and then sighed. "Ok, that just ruined everything."

"Would a smoothie make you feel better?" he offered with an easy smile. One that only widened when Serafall deflated. "I'll take that as a yes. Let's go."

"Can't you let me celebrate the victory for a bit?"

"No."

Serafall sighed again… and that was the end of that scene.

"That needs more work," she said immediately and Joshua nodded. "You think so too?" she asked, turning towards him, curious. "I think I could do better on my part."

"I'm not selling myself with my own dialogues either. I think we should change some of it," he admitted, running his fingers through his hair. "We can go over that for a bit, I guess," he commented thoughtfully. "Maybe over an actual smoothie?"

"I like the way you think," Serafall commented with a smile. Then she turned towards her show's crew and started talking to people. There were a bunch of things to go over, so he settled for watching her work. He didn't have much to do in between scenes and he wasn't really that close to most of the other actors, really.

He was feeling particularly antisocial those days too, so that didn't help either.

Admittedly, some would say he shouldn't even be bothering. There were more important things going on in his life than acting in a magical girl show. However, he'd tell those people that he didn't care for their opinions. Any time spent with a loved one was worth it. Just like playing with Kunou would never not be important, or visiting some place with Gabriel, or sharing a meal with Yasaka, or helping Jeanne study, or walking around Asia's garden.

Working in the show was something Serafall loved and he was all too happy to share that with her.

Besides, he knew what working on something all the time could do to him, and that was neither healthy nor productive. Things would be worse if Khaos pulled something on them and he was too burnt out to face them. So, he needed to take it easy, take breaks when he could in between all the work.

"You're thinking about something," Serafall commented, making her way back to him, and he smiled at the sight of her. "What are you thinking about?"

"The fact that I love you and I like spending time here with you," he said and there was a slight pause and he was pretty sure he saw a very slight dusting of pink on her cheeks. He could be imagining it though, but he decided to think it was actually there. "And that I appreciate the chance to take a break on top of that," he admitted with a shrug.

"I love you too," Serafall replied, walking up to him until her breasts were almost pressing against him. She beamed up at him and it pulled a smile right out of him just to see that. "The writer and the director agree with us, they say they are going to go over things for a bit and get back to us, unless we have a clear idea ourselves," she said and Joshua knew that her "us" and "ourselves" meant her, but he appreciated being included. "So about that smoothie…"

"Sounds like a date," he commented, leaning down to kiss her. "Did you have anywhere in mind?" he asked and she blinked for a moment. "I'm sure there's somewhere around here we can go if not," he added with a second kiss.

"Stop kissing me," she muttered. "It's distracting," she added with a breath. "Especially in that suit." He almost laughed at that. Instead, he kissed her again. "We're not going to get those smoothies like this, you know?"

"Hm, that'd be a shame," he commented as casually as he could. "We could leave the rest of the date for later tonight, I guess," he said, very aware that he was leaving a "but" hanging to the end of his words. It was even more obvious for Serafall, obviously, and it showed in the way her eyes bore into his with renewed intensity.

"I'm a terrible influence on you," she said, but she was grinning, so she probably didn't regret it. Joshua grinned back at her. "What happened to that shy man I dragged to Kyoto?"

"He got a little less shy," he answered with a chuckle. "Especially when this gorgeous woman kept pulling him out of his shell, whether he liked it or not."

"I regret nothing," she replied, both amused and proud. "Well, maybe a little. You're bound to attract more women like this."

"I only have eyes for you three and you know it," he reassured, but that only got a laugh out of Serafall.

"It's cute that you think that matters," she told him and he was suddenly getting a little worried. "That doesn't matter right now though."

"Oh, and what matters right now?" he asked and her smile was answer enough. However, he waited for an actual answer. Which he got when she reached forward to grab his shirt and pull him closer to her.

"How fast you can get us somewhere private, that's what," she told him, grinning wider when she pulled away. "And that the costumes stay on."

"Got it," he replied as a circle flashed under their feet.


[}-o-{]
​

"Think of a spell like a full glass, whenever you try to make a change, it's like adding water and making it overflow. From there, you have to adjust things all around so that the glass is the right shape for the new water volume," he explained, because it never hurt to go over the basics of spellcrafting again. "Following the water analogy in a different direction, imagine you have a river and you drop a giant rock on it. The water will flow around it. That's what a single adjustment does. You need to drop enough rocks that the overflow is stopped. A spell design should be almost completely different, even if the actual change you've made is minimal."

"Does that mean that a big change and a small change are just as difficult?" someone asked and he was pleased about it. Because nobody had asked that the first time he explained things. The valkyries were feeling more at ease, evidently, and that was great. An engaged audience was much better than one that just sat dutifully and listened.

"Is it just as difficult to stop the flow of a river as wide as this city and one as wide as this classroom?" he asked and that seemed to get through. "Big changes and small changes both affect the entire design, but there's still a very clear difference between both cases. It just means that the misconception that a small change is easy is wrong, no matter how small it might be," he explained, taking a deep breath in. "Let's go through an example, I imagine most of you know at least some basic storage spells?" he asked and there were enough nods for him to run with that. "Let's say I'm trying to cast a storage spell and the base is…"

And on he went.

As he spoke, he saw Iryuka taking notes of everything he said, like usual. Idly, when he finished his lecture and told the valkyries to work on a quick exercise, he wondered if the devil was learning too. Devil magic had clear differences from most other magic approaches, but they still could benefit from parts of it. They used circles too, for one, even though they didn't strictly need them.

'I should look into that, actually,' he thought, tilting his head as he considered that. 'Myrddin circles are already based on their magic, but maybe there's more that could be done…' Food for thought, maybe. If he found the time, that was definitely something he could check. It wasn't like he didn't have any devil friends to demonstrate a little. Hell, failing all of those for any political reason, Kuroka was right there and they could "illegally" get shit done while Serafall looked the other way.

Fool proof plan, really.

Surely.

"Alright," he said when a spell notified him that the time for the valkyries to do the exercise was up. Half the class groaned and protested while the other half remained in silent despair. Some might call him sadistic, but it was always fun to pull that on his students. Kept them on their toes and all that. He mostly did it for fun though, admittedly. "Let's see what you all have managed."

As it turned out, there were even some successes.

Impressive stuff.

"What do you think?" Göndul asked, like she did after almost every class. She was very curious about how the valkyries did, evidently. Either that or she wanted to know his opinion on them very clearly. Maybe both, even.

"They are all very good and they are getting better at engaging with the class," he said and he kept to himself the fact that they were all around much better than his regular magician classes. He didn't want any of them to get a big head. "They are getting better all around really fast, honestly," he added and the old valkyrie seemed very pleased to hear that. No surprises there though. "Some of them are a little too proud, but at least they aren't problematic about it," he pointed out, just to take the wind out of Göndul's sails a little.

It wasn't a lie though. His regular magician classes were full of assholes, yes, usually ones that had learned how to control themselves just enough that he couldn't reasonably lash out anymore. It was more trouble for him than they were worth at that point. Besides, Ravel and co. would take that up with Agnes and let her use such instances to drain the offending magician's association little by little.

Sadly, they couldn't quite do the same with the valkyries, but they weren't quite that bad anyway. They were just a little annoying, but never intentionally offensive about it. They just had a lot of confidence and it wasn't always warranted. He could understand where it came from though, since they were pretty good. Just not always as good as they thought they were.

He hadn't had to make a true example of any of them, thankfully.

"If you would tell me who, that'd help a lot," Göndul commented curtly and he grinned, opened his mouth and- Joshua blinked, tilting his head as he raised a hand with a finger up. "What?"

"I need a moment," he answered, stepping away and waving off Iryuka. "Yes?" he answered the incoming call. "Did something happen, Yasaka?"

"Perun gave us a call," was the answer he got and he blinked.

"Who?"

"Leader of the Slavic Pantheon," she answered and he straightened his back. "They got a visit of their own, apparently. Khaos made a mess, the remaining Spartoi were there and they apparently disappeared with Aždaja, a previously dead Evil Dragon."

"How did they get away?" he said and he barely kept his voice from turning into a full growl. "Why didn't they-?"

"Because Pantheons don't like calling for help, Joshua," Yasaka told him, sounding tired and it drained his own energy to hear her like that. "It's been a full day, actually and they are just reaching out about it, apparently. Serafall will be going to talk to them but… I thought you should know."

"Thanks for telling me. I'll talk with Agnes after I'm done here and then we can have a meeting about this," he muttered, getting an agreement and then pinching the bridge of his nose.

Khaos Brigade couldn't disappear fast enough, truly.


[}-o-{]
​

"The Slavic, got it," Agnes replied and he nodded.

She was efficient like that. Joshua felt like he didn't appreciate just how much, actually. Because the woman had been very helpful almost from the get go. Hell, even when their working relationship had just gotten started, she had already more than accommodated him.

Granted, things were a little different by then, but Joshua still considered her somewhat of a… friendly ally. Sometimes a very useful asset, but that felt a lot colder than he'd like. Not untrue though, he supposed, but that might just be him getting a different view of things as time passed. The him from before would probably never have done that.

The him from before had been a completely different person though, he felt.

"Thank you," he replied with a slight smile. "If you could also keep an ear to the ground and tell me if there's any news. I'm pretty sure we should hear from anything, but one never knows," he added, taking a deep breath in… and then turning towards Elizabeth. "Both of you."

"You got it," the slightly more shady magician accepted easily. Which was good, because she was the one that might get information they wouldn't by themselves. Admittedly… "You know that I'm burning a lot of my resources for your assignments, right?" she asked him and that had been something that came to mind from time to time.

"I considered that might be the case, yes," he answered with a frustrated grimace that seemed to set them on edge. Thus, Joshua was quick to continue before they could get in their heads too much… Which he knew was kind of funny. "If you can think of anything I could do that wouldn't be too bad and would help you keep your contacts, do let me know," he told her.

He knew that'd further damn him and his soul – maybe even literally –, but it was a small prize to pay for what he might need to keep everything he loved safe. He could worry about the repercussions of his actions once there was a future for him to do so. That was not a guarantee so long as Khaos Brigade was around. So… he'd have to make do with what he had.

"When you say not too bad…" Elizabeth started and he gave her a flat look.

"You know what I meant, but if you somehow don't, then just ask and I'll see," he told her and she nodded quickly. He really hoped she knew what his limits would be, because if she came to him with something exceedingly stupid, he might have to consider teaching her a lesson somehow. She seemed too smart for that though, so he decided to trust her on that. "That was all I had to say, so unless you need to tell me something…" he said then, offering them a chance to let him know if something was going on.

They were allies, after all, so, if they did need something…

"Nothing on my side," Agnes waved him off, Elizabeth quickly following with a "Not at all". They seemed a little nervous all of a sudden though. And he wasn't sure what the exchanged look was for, but he waved it off. "We don't want to hold you up," Agnes added and he nodded, standing up.

"Then, I'll take my leave," he said before making his way outside. Once the door closed behind him, he took a deep breath in. "Iryuka," he started, making the girl beside him straighten. "I need you to get a message to Ravel and Seekvaira."

"Anything you need, sir," the girl replied and he nodded.


[}-o-{]
​

"Sorry for the delay," Joshua said as he walked through the door, seeing the alliance already gathered. It gave him pause though, because there were extra faces around the table. On one side, there was Odin and on the other, Athena. Immediately, he wondered if there was any tension for the absence of Zeus himself, but that didn't seem to be the case, thankfully. "I missed some things, apparently."

"That's what happens when you take your time on the way," Azazel commented, making his eye twitch. At least he did so casually, rather than more overtly aiming it like an insult towards him. Not that Joshua was in the mood for that shit, but there were new faces around and he'd rather not have to go down that path in front of them. "We were just agreeing to look out for any new appearances. Some agents will be spread around allied factions so that we can cover more ground and let each other know if anything happens."

That was actually kind of helpful of him to say.

Almost made Joshua not be annoyed looking at him.

"It'll ruffle some feathers if it comes to it," Athena commented analytically. "But it's a risk worth taking and it should be relatively easy to keep the… consequences to a minimum."

"Alright," he mumbled as he took his seat. "Anything else or was that the gist of it?"

"That's the summary," Serafall answered, leaning against his side rather casually and intimately, which he thought was odd. He didn't point it out though. She knew more about what she was doing than he did, after all.

"Well, I took my time because I was telling House of Water to keep an eye out for news too," he informed everyone, running his fingers through his hair. "And also a contact I have in the less nice magic society circles."

"Everyone knows House of Water has a few bad eggs, child," Odin commented and Joshua refrained from replying to that. "That's not a terrible idea, but do forgive me if I doubt how useful they'll be."

"Everyone underestimates magicians and their associations. I'm counting on that, actually," Joshua replied, not quite curtly but it could be understood like that, he supposed. He wasn't opposed to that interpretation. Although, Odin seemed to take it very easily. The god even seemed amused.

"There's that, I suppose."

"So, what else do we have?" he asked, looking around. He really, really hoped that wasn't all, because it was going to turn out to be a very frustrating meeting if that was all. Even with the evident progress in terms of allies and such. He wasn't sure what had happened there, but he knew his partners would fill him in eventually. It wasn't that difficult to put together that his partners had probably managed to talk the other two factions into officially joining.

Which was great, because as much as the agreements he'd gotten for the "miracles" he sold those two were worth, actual participation and direct help was better.

"The Slavic aren't telling us much, they are…" Yasaka started, hesitantly. "They don't get along with most of this alliance," she admitted and he'd have to be blind not to notice the way she looked at Athena, Gabriel and Azazel. He wondered what the story there was… but most of all, he found himself internally grumbling about the issue.

Because of course there had to be an issue.

There was always an issue.

"We do know one thing though," Gabriel commented and he turned to give her his full attention. "They are using Annihilation Maker to get through our defenses," she said, taking a deep breath in. "We need to find ways to deal with that," she added, looking around.

The atmosphere around the room seemed to grow tense at that.

"Hm, that makes sense," he replied, leaning back and considering the point. "Annihilation Maker is such a cheat," he added, aware that it was a little hypocritical of him to think so. He did have his own cheat in the shape of the system, after all. Speaking of systems, he so dearly wished he could use Heaven's System to help out, but… Not only was that a mess that not even his Administrator access helped navigate, but he also continued to be very reluctant to do much of anything with it.

The last thing he wanted was to cause more problems just by trying to fix one.

No, that was something better left to the angels to slowly figure out while he helped them get things done.

"Fortunately, I think I've more or less countered it," he commented, summoning one of his notebooks and mentally calling for Friday. "It's a little tricky, admittedly. But I think I can set up something in a bunch of locations. I'm kind of limited in that regard for now though and I have to keep working on it to smooth things over… But I should be able to cover one location for every faction here," he explained, nodding to himself after going over everything and confirming what he'd just said to himself.

The addition of the Norse and the Greek pushed things a little in regards to that particular project, but he was confident.

One or two more locations would have him start properly doubting things though. Friday was only one entity, no matter how versatile she was. And Joshua refused to make more of her for convenience's sake, like she was some kind of tool. So, he'd have to make do. With some improvement on his arrays, she should be able to keep an eye on things all over the place without issue and he'd be able to add more arrays to that count.

He just needed to make the process smoother and, furthermore, maybe less reliant on her for everything.

Funnily enough, adding more arrays would help too, if they were placed more spread out around the globe. It'd have Friday's moving between arrays with less distance between one another, if there was a "relay" in between, for example, Japan and Greece. He did tell the alliance that.

"So, while I work on that," Joshua continued, looking up and seeing every face fixed on him. "Well, not sure about you guys, but I trust you'll come up with something," he added with a shrug. He blinked, however, when none of them looked away from him after a long moment. "What?"

"Nothing," Serafall answered with a giggle in her voice. "Nothing at all. So, next order of business…" And off she went, bringing up a bunch of politics in regards to non-alliance pantheons and what they could and couldn't ask from them. Joshua kind of wasn't well equipped for that conversation, so he left them to it. He did keep an ear out even while he worked on his own things though.

Unfortunately, he couldn't really help them come up with ways to better negotiate with the Inca pantheon or smooth over some of the issues inside the Norse faction or any of that. It was kind of interesting to hear though, he'd admit. That is, when it wasn't confusing and sounding like a different language altogether to his ears.

Idly, as that went on, he wondered if Ravel, Iryuka and Seekvaira were having any luck looking through his library. He had sent them to do that for him, to check information on the Slavic pantheon… and also any mention of dragons and dragon-related things. It seemed Khaos was targeting though, after all. Granted, it didn't narrow things out at all for them, since every Pantheon seemed to have some flavor of dragons and such. However, it might come in handy to have some extra information on those.

He'd already studied up on those that he remembered from canon… but clearly things weren't going the canon way in that regard, between the Spartoi and Aždaja.

And he was really not liking any of it, he'd admit.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,640
-And Now I've Come to Collect-

Joshua was starting to take measures that he'd put off before.

For one, he'd already approached Ophis in regards to the infinity wardstones he now possessed. That had been the biggest "idea" that he'd been reluctant to tackle. Although, that had been more a matter of not wanting to go up to the dragon and just straight out ask her for it. He'd been planning to at least wait for her to come out of the Silence Rooms on her own accord.

Alas, that hadn't been possible, but things had worked out well anyway.

"So, you've been very vague about this," Katerea commented, and he could – or Cheshire could, at least – tell that she was nervous, even if she acted like she wasn't. The sharp sense of his feline familiar wouldn't be deceived though, and she shared everything with him through the bond. For once, however, that wasn't brought about by Nagini's gaze locked onto the devil.

No, it came from Joshua… which wasn't that rare either, admittedly.

"This is going to be very painful, isn't it?" Katerea asked and he considered lying to her. Ultimately though, he decided that it wasn't worth the effort. It wasn't like he hadn't put her through hell already. That was the reason why she was so wary, really.

"Chances are that it'll be," he answered and the devil gulped and grimaced. She seemed taken aback too, for some reason. Maybe she'd expected him to say something else, regardless of if that was true or not. "If it makes you feel better, I'll give you a little extra freedom if things go well. I might even talk to Serafall about allowing you in the Underworld and all," he commented and she perked up.

Admittedly, it was a little funny to say that, considering the whole Leviathan issue between both women.

"Why are you offering that?" she asked, eyes narrowed in suspicion. "You can get whatever you want without that. I'm a prisoner."

"You've been behaving yourself," Joshua replied with a shrug and he was a little confused by the half embarrassed and half angry grimace she pulled. "And I might need your cooperation with this. I don't honestly know what to expect going into it," he added and that seemed to make her relax a little bit. Maybe because she could understand where he was coming from.

"I see," she mumbled, sounding and looking like she hated the entire idea. She didn't curse him, nor did she say anything else for that matter. Instead, she stared at him and he could almost see her going over things. Ultimately, there was only one option for her to take, really. Especially after her pride had been thoroughly destroyed already. There were remnants of it left, yes, but nowhere near enough for her to actively do anything even remotely against him. "Very well," she said in the end, and he took it as the agreement that it was.

"Great," Joshua replied with a slight smile.

Not that he was looking forward to possibly inflicting pain on the devil, but he was looking forward to getting good results – hopefully – out of that particular project. It wouldn't be immediately useful, he didn't think, but it could come in handy later down the line. Possibly. There was still a chance that he might be going through all that for nothing, admittedly.

Joshua was at a point where he was doing everything he could and hoping something would stick, however.

"Alright, stand in the middle of the circle, please," he said, more as a formality than anything else as they entered a particular room. It was covered in spells, giving Katerea pause, but the devil moved where he'd gestured towards after a moment. She was a little nervous, understandably, and even Joshua noticed, what with how she shuffled on her feet and clenched and unclenched her hands.

He didn't pay her too much mind though.

Instead, he went over the arrays he'd already put together. Then he activated a bunch of them, making Katerea flinch. He hadn't started yet though. Most of them were background things, support set ups for the actual thing. Everything read fine up to that point and Katerea herself looked as he expected under the sensing spells.

In hindsight though, he should have told her what he was doing. Which was why he started talking as he went over the process himself. He explained to her what they were going to be doing, and what every spell he had set up was supposed to do. He had doubts the devil was even understanding most of it, but she seemed ever so slightly reassured all the same, which he guessed was good.

"Whenever you're ready," he told Katerea and she stared at him for a long moment. After that, however, she relaxed her still tense shoulders. Then she gulped and visibly took a deep breath in before letting it out slowly. She was trying to calm herself, but she was only marginally succeeding.

"... Thanks for saying that," she told him and he was a little surprised by that. He hadn't thought much of it, but… Maybe he should have expected it. In the position she was in, maybe it was to be expected to appreciate such small courtesies.

Or maybe she expected things to go really badly.

Joshua couldn't say that was unwarranted if it was the case.

"I'm ready," Katerea said and he wasted no time, nodding and activating everything that was left. Immediately, the many arrays reached for Katerea like hungry creatures, clawing through her. They ignored her magic, her life and her body, however. They reached for the Ophis Snake, after all, and they caught it.

Unfortunately for the devil, the thing had metaphorically curled and half-fused with her soul to boost her as it did. It was like a parasite already way back when he'd first caught her, when she'd first taken it even, he'd bet, and it had only gotten worse with time. He had barely managed to make zones where she wasn't going to be destroyed by the tithing, after all. That meant that the process of extracting that wasn't going to be nice for her. He had expected that. It was almost guaranteed, even if he'd told her he wasn't sure.

Joshua hadn't been one hundred percent sure, but he had been very sure, he'd admit.

Sure enough, Katerea's body stiffened where she stood, her mouth opening to scream so loudly that Joshua grimaced even as he focused on what he was doing. He suspected she'd have collapsed if it weren't for the spells holding her in place. Her very soul seemed to writhe under the effects of his magic, trying to recoil away from his spells. Alas, it was kind of trapped inside her body, fortunately.

Or unfortunately, for her.

With a deep breath in, Joshua ignored all that, focusing on what he was trying to do. Extracting the thing was difficult, after all. Not only did he have to carefully separate what was Katerea's soul from the Ophis Snake, but he also had to filter the parts that were both and neither at the same time. It wasn't, after all, a case of water and oil. There were plenty of areas where they mixed together way too much and he had to make a distinction there or he risked leaving one or both Katerea and the Ophis Snake completely butchered.

It was a good thing that he'd spent so much time studying her soul, he supposed. Furthermore, it was a good thing that he'd spent so much time studying soul magic in general. He'd had to put together pieces from plenty of projects to try and pull off what he was doing, from the Sleep Disease to his attempts at Valerie's situation, passing through Friday's creation.

All of it had helped him pull off that one attempt, together with plenty of experimentation and studying in regards to Katerea herself when she'd been a prisoner and even after she got out.

At one point though, roughly halfway through the process – he wasn't sure how much time had passed; he wasn't keeping track –, Joshua noticed a shift on the Ophis Snake side. The parts that were still attached got even worse, not stronger, but more desperate, reckless even. It was worrying to notice, but the part that struck him as more interesting was the other side of the Ophis Snake.

That one seemed to start writhing not unlike Katerea's soul. Distinctly though, it snapped around like trying to latch back onto the devil, even though he wasn't letting it. He watched that a little – wondering why it looked so familiar – before he decided to try something. That was when he paused the extraction process, letting things calm down for a bit.

And then he poked the detached side with a gathering of magic, like offering a piece of meat to a dog. He even did his best to improvise a way for that magic to feel soul-like as best he could. It was a crude attempt, but that was supposed to be more a random experiment rather than a serious attempt at something.

Joshua was surprised when the thing latched on and the parts that were still attached to Katerea even seemed to relax a bit.

Quickly, before anything could happen, he went back to trying to extract the thing from the devil. He was honestly very surprised – baffled even – that things continued sort of calmly even then. Every bit of Ophis Snake that he separated from Katerea snapped off and latched onto the magic offering he'd made. Little by little… every bit of it came off.

And then the devil dropped to the ground like a sack of potatoes. She was alive though, and didn't even seem that hurt, soul-wise. Slightly traumatized, maybe, and "bruised" all over, yes, but alive and with an all but guaranteed recovery.

Joshua, meanwhile, looked at the pitch black snake-like gathering of pseudo-infinity that reminded him of his new wardstones slithering around inside a sphere of magic.

'That went both exactly as expected and nothing like I thought, somehow,' he mused to himself. 'How very interesting,' he thought, taking a deep breath in as he gave the Ophis Snake to Friday. She'd be able to keep the thing entertained with magic and she'd be able to contain it if it came to it. Not that it was difficult, really. Once on its own, the thing was surprisingly easy to handle, just like it had before.

And Khaos Brigade had kept the things inside barely enchanted vials.

'Let me know if anything happens, girl,' he told her in his mind, and he added Cheshire onto that for good measure. Both readily agreed, the former even seeming excited. She did like being helpful though, he supposed, so that wasn't surprising.

With that done, Joshua turned his attention to a gasping, twitching Katerea. The devil laid on the floor on the spot she'd previously been standing on. Her dark skin had paled and her eyes were unfocused. Her hands reached out, as if trying to grasp at something that wasn't there and her feet would kick out, as if starting to run from something but achieving nothing.

She didn't even seem aware of what was going on around her or the fact that Joshua was walking towards her.

So, in the spirit of not being an asshole and acknowledging the fact that she'd been fairly cooperative ever since she… Well, agreed to cooperate with him, he cast a few more spells. All of them reached for her, soothing the bruises on her soul. Considering he'd worked most of them to help Valerie with a torn existence, using them on Katerea might as well be the equivalent of spending a fortune on treatment for a scrapped knee.

Although, that comparison was kind of laughable considering how much damage the process had done to Katerea.

It did put into perspective how bad Valerie's situation was though, not that Joshua needed that.

"... Thank you," the devil mumbled after a bit of that, her spasming lessening and her breathing evening. She still seemed half out of it though, but he didn't blame her for that, at all.

"Don't mention it," he replied thoughtfully. Maybe he could be nicer to her, he supposed. Raynare had turned out pretty alright, all things considered. Katerae had also been fairly agreeable, so… Maybe that was worth considering, at the very least. 'I'll ask the others what they think,' he decided.

That seemed like a good spot to start with.


[}-o-{]
​

"She seems trustworthy enough," Yasaka commented as they walked through passages that didn't see many people. They were also very different from what he usually saw around her places, but that was to be expected. There were no warm colors nor wood walls and doors. There were only cold grey stone blocks and even colder metal bars. "But I don't know about giving her more. Might need to watch her more closely if you want to give her proper freedom and welcome her."

"That's fair," Joshua replied with a nod, running his fingers through his hair. "I'll have Cheshire follow her around," he commented. The cat would love that. She was no sadist like Nagini, but she would still be very happy to mess with someone. Two sides of the same coin, those two.

"Do that," Yasaka agreed easily, looking a little relieved. Did she think he'd let a former Khaos Brigade member do whatever she wanted with Kunou around? If that was the case, that would be a little insulting. Although, he guessed she might be a little wary that he might relax too much, what with Raynare and Kuroka. And to a lesser extent Georg and Kokabiel, he thought a moment later. "Please, do try not to seduce her."

He sighed.

"Are you surprised?" she asked then, seeming amused.

"I haven't seduced Raynare or Kuroka, have I?"

"Debatable," she answered and he sighed again. "I guess that's my fault for choosing so well," she added and he wasn't sure if that was the compliment that seemed to be. She didn't have to sound so genuinely sort fo annoyed about it, for one. "I guess I have to tell the others about this, mainly Serafall. She'll have an opinion on this."

"You think she'll be angry?" he asked, not all that worried. Having another opinion never hurt though and Joshua kind of liked to have as much information as he could before tackling a problem. That was something that he liked to apply to as many aspects of his life as possible.

"No, I don't think so. If anything, she'll be pleased. She might get Katerea to help her with some things," Yasaka answered and that was more or less what he figured. It made him feel like maybe he wasn't as much of a failure as a boyfriend as he feared sometimes. "You worry too much."

"Is how I am," he replied with a somewhat helpless smile and shrug.

"I have to wonder if you'll someday see what we see," she said and he tried not to express how doubtful he was. Because he couldn't ever see things like they did. He would have never been okay with any of them being with anyone else. Maybe that made him greedy, but if so, then he was greedy and he accepted it. "You think it's a bad thing, that you're greedy," Yasaka continued, as if she were reading his mind.

Joshua was kind of used to that kind of thing, he'd admit.

"We don't agree with that," Yasaka told him and he wondered if she was going to throw one of those DxD logicless logic moments at him again. As it turned out… "We like it, because it shows that you care. We do the opposite for the same reason, ironically enough." … Yes, yes she was.

"Sometimes, I wonder if I did die and I ended up in some weird version of the afterlife," he commented and he saw Yasaka twitch. Right, that was… not a great thing to say, taking into account the original Joshua and his choices. "Sorry, that was insensitive."

"I guess that's a sign that you're doing better in that regard, if you can forget and even make jokes like that," Yasaka replied, although it sounded like she was justifying things to herself. She did seem to feel a little better though, so he relaxed the smallest bit. "Now… here we are. And Kunou gets off her classes soon, so…"

"Go, or she'll be sad," Joshua told her with a half smile. "I'll try not to take too long. I promised her I'd set up the flying game for her and the girls," he added and Yasaka smiled warmly at him before kissing him and leaving.

"We'll be waiting," she called over her shoulder and he watched her go for a bit. Joshua was sure it wasn't his imagination that told him she was swaying her tails a bit too much and a big too… 'I hate being this busy,' he complained to himself before resigning himself to doing what he'd gone there to do. No rest for him, unfortunately. Nor any distractions, for that matter.

Cracking his neck, he walked some more and eventually stood in front of a familiar cell.

"Hey there," he greeted, running his fingers through his hair. "Been a bit, hasn't it?"

"Not nearly long enough," Grendel growled, although he sounded more annoyed than properly angry. "What do you want now, magician?" the dragon asked, shuffling where he laid inside the cell to a standing position. "Are you here for a rematch, finally?" he asked, although he sounded doubtful.

'He actually wants that rematch, huh?'

"Not yet, but I wouldn't be opposed to a fight if it makes you more cooperative," he answered and the dragon narrowed his eyes.

"Without trickery? A proper match?" Grendel asked and Joshua almost sighed. They had very clearly different views of what a proper match was.

"I'm a magician," he said, and that'd have to be a good enough answer. If it wasn't, then… Too bad. Grendel stared at him for a long moment before huffing.

"That'll have to do, I suppose," the dragon replied. "Do whatever you have to do, magician."

"So kind of you to allow me to," Joshua said, smiling.

As he started testing some things in regards to dragons – which was becoming an increasingly important matter –, he did ponder on that conversation. Because some fights against a dragon might be very useful. That could be good preparation for facing other dragons that Khaos might decide to drop on them.


[}-o-{]
​

"Hm… I don't like them," Kunou commented, sitting with her legs crossed beside him and Joshua gave her an amused look. "What? I don't," she added with more vehemence. She could be entirely too adorable sometimes.

"You don't have to like them," Joshua replied with a roll of his eyes. Then he picked up one of the infinity wardstones. "They are not even something you're supposed to see a lot of. They do their job and usually they do it out of sight. How many wardstones have you even seen without me casting momentary spells for a game?" he asked with a raised eyebrow.

"But I see those," Kunou pointed out like a smartass.

"I guess I'll use the normal wardstones if you don't like these ones that much," he replied with a shrug.

"I didn't say that," Kunou protested immediately. Joshua paused and turned to look at her. Then he raised an eyebrow. "I just… what difference would they make?"

"I mean… I think I could work out an array that uses a single wardstone," he answered. That was one of his more interesting ideas. Not something he was going to dedicate too much focus to, but he liked it all the same. "That'd be interesting and I wouldn't need as much space for arrays."

"That sounds neat," Kunou replied before her expression turned thoughtful. "How'd that work with the circles though?" she asked and he considered that for a long moment before picking up a notebook.

"Like this, or so the theory goes. This is the ground," he started, drawing a straight line at the bottom. "Then this is the wardstone," he added, drawing a circle over the line. "And these are the circles," he finished with, drawing a bunch of lines parallel to the "ground" from right beside that first line and then up, over the "wardstone" and then even on top of it.

"Ah… I think I get it," Kunou replied with a nod, looking rather interested in the drawing. "Do you think you could teach me that if you figure it out?" she asked, turning towards him with those big golden eyes that she used when she definitely wanted to get whatever it was she was asking.

"Of course," he answered, like he wasn't offering his daughter to use literal unique wardstones with the element of infinity imbued in them. And he fully knew that she'd use them for some game or maybe just for some illusion project of hers. "It'll be nice to have proper classes for ourselves again," he added and the smile his daughter gave him told him that she fully agreed. "For now…"

"Alright… I still have to finish my homework anyway," she muttered, deflating a little. He felt bad for that, but he was planning to spend more time with her later. He just had to do some tests with the infinity wardstones.

He was still working on just… being able to use those, really. It'd take a bit, but they were definitely going to change things once he fully figured them out. As it was, he had to approach it all like everything else, slowly and with lots of research and tests.

That very moment, he was taking a rather small but important step, making a draining ward with one of those as a base. Draining wards were more or less the foundation of all his arrays, they were the ones that powered everything else, after all, and it allowed him to not need to spend all his magic at once. Not that it was a problem those days, with his infinite reserves, but it was still useful. He could only handle so much output, even with his infinite reserves, after all, but he could push past that point with Draining Wards.

Basically the same he'd always done, but the starting point had gone way up.

The infinity wardstones promised to push the end point even more so, with potential… Well, infinity in the cards.

'First though, I have to make the spell work to the full potential of the wardstone,' he mused, taking a deep breath in and setting the focus on the ground. Then, with a snap of his fingers, the spell was cast. It was simple, anticlimactic even, but that was all that he needed to do. From there, it was a matter of watching. If the attempt was a failure, it'd be something that'd come up later, the more the spell drained energy. He'd spend more time preparing the measures in case that happened than actually preparing the circle for that experiment, really.

In the meantime, Joshua sat with Kunou, watching her work on her stuff while he kept an eye on his spell attempt. To the girl's credit, she didn't try to use his idle time to put her off own work. He had definitely expected that to happen, but he was pleasantly surprised that she hadn't.

"Did it work?"

"So far," he answered, tilting his head. "I don't think that one's right," he commented then, pointing at one of her answers. "Wasn't it the other guy that did that? What was his name?" he asked, snapping his fingers as he tried to remember the actual answer. He remembered helping her go through that text. It was a history bit about a deal between her mom – funny how that worked, that she was part of Kunou's history classes – and a minor pantheon. He was pretty sure she'd gotten the name of the leader of that time wrong though, which was-

"Oh, right," she mumbled, erasing the name and writing another.

"That's the one, yeah," he replied, leaning back. "Good thing you remember it, because I definitely wasn't going to," he added and Kunou let out a giggle that put a smile on his face. "Say, if you finish that before this test is over, we can go get ice cream," he offered and he could almost see her eyes turn into stars – or maybe ice cream – and he knew she'd succeed.

Although, difficult for her to fail, considering the test was going to be running for a few days.

She didn't need to know that though.


[} Chapter End {]
