#1,648
-So, Don't Get in My Way

"Fascinating, I have to say," he mumbled, laying on a couch at home. Everyone was busy, so he was having a bit of a lazy morning, he'd admit. However, he was also using that time for something, and that was checking on the Ophis Snake that he'd taken from Katerea.

It had taken a bit to stabilize after the process… Or so he'd assumed, but that seemed to not be the case, on account of it staying pretty much the same after a few days had passed. The reason why he'd assumed as much was because he still had the unused one he'd taken from the Satan descendants and… It was very different from the one he'd taken from Katerea.

For one, that one was more of a very strange, unconventional potion, by the looks of it. However, the one he'd taken from the female devil? It looked like a caged animal, sort of. It slithered around inside the vial like he'd trapped an actual snake inside… one that could fly, but still. It was quite interesting, that was for sure. Made Joshua wonder what'd changed between the before and after use. Or if there were differences between the Snakes to begin with.

He doubted that though, considering Ophis had made them and at least he hadn't seen that kind of wild differentiation between the Infinity stones. Hell, he couldn't tell two of those apart if he tried. So, surely the Snake's would be the same… right?

Sadly, he only had the one unused one, so he couldn't quite find out what the answer to that was. He did have Shalba, who he could take another used Snake from and check. However, he wasn't quite confident he could try to do the same there. The guy was a lot more reluctant to agree to things than Katerea was, and intent mattered a lot in magic. Somewhere deep down, even if her soul was too busy struggling and wailing, Katerea had agreed to things, she had been willing even, far as he could tell.

He wasn't sure if things would go quite as well with an unwilling participant and he was a lot less willing to fuck around and find out when it was something that Ophis made that was involved. Joshua was – understandably, in his opinion – wary of that kind of thing. There was a non-zero chance that the Snake would just blow up and destroy literally everything. He'd rather that didn't happen.

Joshua was weird like that, he supposed.

There was Kokabiel too, he supposed. That one was a lot more of a viable choice and he'd probably go through with that. He was a fallen and the woman was a devil though. Joshua had to wonder if there'd be a difference because of that.

Either way, it'd be interesting to see what happened there.

'Should keep one willing and one unwilling subject of study though, maybe,' he thought idly. That was a valid point, yes, just like how he had one use and one unused Snake.

"What's the difference from now though?" he wondered to himself as he looked at the Snake moving around inside the vial. "If I use you or the other one… What would happen?" he asked himself idly.

Then Margalo peeked at him from the backrest of the couch he was lying on and chirped something.

"Talking to myself, girl," he replied, getting a few more chirps in response. "I think that's like, the least concerning part of my mind," he added and the bird considered that for a long moment.

"Daddy is crazy?" Morag asked, crawling on the back of the couch herself and resting on the backrest beside Margalo. "Does that mean we have to be crazy too?"

"No, Morag. It just means I'm crazy and that's that. You can continue to be sane," he answered idly. Although, he refrained from pointing out that many people would call her – and her siblings, with the possible exception of the non-familiar ones – crazy too. That was a rude opinion, after all, and he wasn't about to voice it at any of them.

And if anyone did say that to them, then Joshua reserved the right to experiment on them to improve his magic knowledge.

They'd deserve it and it'd be useful, probably.

"Oh, alright then," Morag replied, like she was disappointed she couldn't share madness with him. Joshua wasn't sure how to feel about that. "So, what are you going to do with that, Daddy?" the girl-spider asked afterwards, peering at the vial in his hand with eight very curious eyes. She looked quite adorable, if anyone asked him, but that was beside the point. "Reminds me of Friday when she tries to make a body," she added and he paused to look at the vial again. He guessed he could see the similarities between the two… sort of. Friday did sometimes make little wisps of color to "show herself", although it wasn't quite that often.

She did then and there though, making one that circled around the vial. The living spell had gotten curious when she heard her name being spoken, evidently, and had decided to drop by. She was easily influenced like that sometimes. It was a little adorable. She'd often jump into conversations like a puppy running into a room and barking and bouncing around to get attention.

"You're not wrong," Joshua conceded with a smile. "What do you think, Friday? Similar enough?" he asked and the living spell "examined" the little black snake closely as if trying to find what they were talking about in the little slice of infinity.

Which reminded him of how mindboggling that was as a concept, but it was still the best description he could use for them. The same went for the infinity wardstones, for that matter. It wasn't infinity, not really, but it was also not… finity. It didn't make any sense how it could be both and neither at the same time, but there it was.

'Makes about as much sense as anything related to Ophis can, I guess,' Joshau thought to himself. Then he was distracted when Friday gave him what he assumed was some flavor of "I don't see it". He even thought there was a bit of a metaphorical pout there, which was kind of interesting.

"Anyway, where are Cheshire and Nagini? You girls want to go and play a game or something? I'm having a lazy day in, I think, so…" he commented, and all three of them perked up. Friday more metaphorically speaking, but still.


[}-o-{]
​

"You've all gotten quite strong," Joshua commented, tilting his head as he looked at Sona's and Rias' peerages sparring against each other. He'd lost sight of them for the most part after the entire Young Devil Gathering thing was over. Hell, he hadn't even watched most of it, to be honest. He was way too busy for it, but he had watched Sona for the most part, since that made for good time spent with Serafall.

"You're exaggerating, but we appreciate it," Rias replied wryly, but he really wasn't. They weren't quite as strong as he remembered them getting in canon, but that had been with them being in life and death situations every month or so. Although, there was an argument to be made about them being just as strong, just differently developed.

At least in the little training sessions at his place, their development was more spread out rather than just focusing on their strongest points.

"And even if you're not, we do owe most of this to you," Sona pointed out and he didn't try to argue that. It was the truth and there was really no point. "We appreciate you taking the time to help us even though you're busy, by the way," the girl added and maybe he showed something on his face because she continued almost immediately after with: "My sister is always talking about how you barely have time for anything."

"Well, if it makes you feel any better, you're also helping me," he commented, running his fingers through his hair and with a sigh hidden somewhere in his voice. He smiled wryly when both girls raised an eyebrow at him. "These days, I have so much stuff to do that I feel bad if I take a break. So, you're giving me an excuse to do nothing for a bit."

Sure, most of the time he had good excuses in the form of his partners and Kunou, but… He could only do that so much. Especially because his partners felt bad if he spent all his free time on them. They'd told him as much. It also didn't help that he didn't have that many friends. Speaking of… Sairaorg was very busy himself those days, what with Zekram apparently preparing him to take the heir spot "flawlessly", whatever that might mean.

That sucked, since the guy was like, his closest friend.

Some would even say his only one.

"Well, you won't see me complaining," Rias replied, although she looked kind of amused. That is, before her expression softened. "By the way, I'm very grateful for how you've been taking care of Koneko."

"You don't have to. She earned her spot here," he told her, waving off her thanks with ease.

"How? By being cute?"

"Yes," he answered straightforwardly, drawing giggles from Rias and a snort from Sona. "She's also easy to like and she's good with Kunou… for the most part," he added with a smile, not even having to exaggerate. The girls didn't always get along, or appreciate each other, but Joshua saw them interacting almost every time they met and he knew they helped each other, pushed each other in the right directions.

"Still…" Rias pressed and Joshua almost wanted to sigh. He was getting used to people having that kind of attitude.

"If you want to help, just keep an eye on her. We love her, even if Kunou would be reluctant to admit it," he said. It was more that his daughter would never admit it. He knew it to be true though. None of them had quite said it out loud, least of all to each other, but Koneko was already part of the family. Same with Ravel, for that matter.

"We already do," she replied and he didn't have any doubts about that either. "But maybe we can be extra nice to her."

"Good," he told her with a smile that hopefully would stop her from going overboard. Because Koneko was too good to turn into a spoiled brat. That'd be a shame and a tragedy. "By the way, Jeanne is turning into a true teenager and barely tells me anything about school so-"

"She's doing well in her classes, far as I know," Sona said, and she was too quick about it. It made Joshua think that she was actually keeping tabs on his sister just in case. That was… good. Maybe a little extra, but that was the Sitri heiress, an overachiever if there ever was one. "She also seems to be doing well with her friend group. Especially since they have an easier time without the… questionable members of the student body that were around before."

"Issei and his friends?" he asked with a raised eyebrow, slightly amused. Did she feel like she had to beat around the bush because he'd taken the guy under his wing? He was mostly independent by then, especially since Joshua hardly ever made time for the cafe in Kuoh. If anything, Aika was closer to him than Issei. Although, the boy seemed to still look up to him a fair bit.

Joshua wasn't complaining.

It might sound… bad, but having the Red Dragon Emperor willing to answer calls and help out was fairly useful.

"Yes," Rias answered straightforwardly and he chuckled to let them know it was fine. "They seem to be much better behaved as of late," she added and he was glad to hear that. It'd been a while since he saw the other two, after all. Maybe Sona had really listened to him. Or maybe Jeanne had beat some sense into their thick skulls. Either way, that was reassuring, because it meant his sister was having a better time in school and that was always welcome.

"Well, with that said, are you two not going to join your peerages?" he asked with a raised eyebrow. "Maybe we can spice things up a little extra. Nagini's always eager for a fight, especially an interesting one. So are the rest of my familiars for that matter."

"No," Sona replied, maybe too quickly. "There's no need. We wouldn't want to take up their time when-"

"Don't worry about it," he interrupted, acting like he didn't see their slight panic. Maybe he was getting better at reading people too. Was that how his partners felt around him all the time? Because it was kind of amusing. "You'd be doing me a favor after all. They can get bored sometimes," he added.

And he knew he had them when he used the word "favor". Joshua was learning, after all, that it was a wonderful word in the world of DxD. Such a convenient piece of culture… Troublesome at times, for sure, but very useful at others, he'd admit.


[}-o-{]
​

It was a strange feeling, to have Set eagerly trying to channel himself through him.

Joshua stood there, feeling like there was another him inside his skin and pressing forward. His teeth itched as if trying to stretch into fangs and not managing. He felt like the hair on his body stood on end, a hint of fur that tried to poke out of his skin. There was also an intrusive urge coming not from himself that told him to just go.

Which was all sorts of annoying.

'Calm down, Set. Or I'm channeling literally anyone else,' he pressed back at the deity. Finally, he got some reprieve as Set pulled back the smallest bit. He was thankful for that, because it'd been getting a little much. Although… 'You might get your chance,' he added and he could almost see the canine grin on the god's face, which he was pretty sure was an image sent by the deity. After all, he had never actually seen Set, like he hadn't seen… any of the Egyptians other than Nephthys.

Funny how that worked.

Anyway, he did think Set might get a chance to do what he wanted. As for what he wanted, well… It was to fight Grendel. As it was though, that wasn't quite what Joshua was doing. He was doing nothing at all, really. The Evil Dragon was, in fact, fighting his familiars rather than him. It'd fit Grendel's wishes for a "fair fight" better anyway, and it'd give his familiars something to do.

And he had time to study the dragon in action, which was something he kind of needed.

If things went south, then Joshua would teleport everyone out of the way and let Set go in to kick the Evil Dragon's ass again. Both Grendel and the deity were eager for a rematch, as it turned out, which was kind of funny. Joshua himself wasn't opposed to that, but he was better off learning more on how to face the dragons spell-wise than just regularly fighting against them.

He'd won one fight of those already, but Khaos seemed to be going around collecting creatures. Joshua would need to face several of those when the time came, or so was the assumption he was going with. In theory, it was unlikely that he'd face them alone, but it was better to plan for the worst just in case. He had to use the information he had to see what the worst setting could be and assume that's what was going to happen.

If it turned out that things went better than expected, then good, and if not, then it'd be good to be prepared.

Which was another reason for why he was pitting his familiars against Grendel. Joshua also had plans to pit the rest of the oddball group of misfit ex-enemies he'd put together and throw them at the dragon too. Because they might find themselves facing something similar to Grendel too and without him to save their asses.

'I hate not knowing things,' he thought, not for the first time, even as he watched Cheshire claw at the back of one of Grendel's knees. 'What are you doing, Khaos?' he wondered, even as the dragon tried to bite Margalo out of the air. 'Where are you?' he hissed, even as his mind processed the information his spells were picking up.

He had no answers to a lot of the questions he had in his mind those days. And that was scaring and concerning him more and more with every passing day. Because with every second that passed, Khaos was preparing a hit that would potentially destroy everything he loved. He could do nothing but prepare for it and he hated it. They had hit two more factions after the Greek and the Slavic, all of them to raid some old site with the remains of a long dead dragon.

They were putting together an army, one tougher than random devils and fallen and other strays. They were putting together a force that would do a lot of damage wherever it was pointed. Furthermore, Joshua had nothing to work with, even with the added support such actions brought to the alliance he was part of. Every attack brought someone else to the table, even if nobody had joined the actual table after the Greek and the Norse.

They were getting more information, and factions were offering support.

Things were good…

But they still had no idea where they were or how to deal with them other than waiting for the next attack. Joshua hated that. Defense was his thing, yes, but he didn't know how to defend against whatever Khaos was planning. That was making everything worse and he'd freely admit it.

'They could have anything,' he thought to himself, feeling his face twitch in annoyance. 'Between Annihilation Maker and Sephiroth Graal, how the fuck do I cover for that? Friday and I can only do so much,' he thought, trying to find a hole in what Khaos was doing, some kind of weakness or clue that he might not have seen. Just like he was studying Grendel – not really getting much new information even, which didn't help –, he studied the situation and…

Came up with nothing.

'It was bad enough when it was just Annihilation Maker I had to deal with, but now…' he mused, pausing and blinking.

"Seekvaira," he called, startling the girl. "Look alive," he commented flatly and the girl looked at him with wide eyes. He raised an eyebrow at her and she blushed, but her eyes were still wide, darting between him and the spar of the dragon against his familiars. "Remind me to check my notes on Valerie later, alright?" he asked and she seemed confused, like he'd spoken in a language she couldn't understand. Which was impossible, since she was a devil. "Alright?" he repeated and she nodded quickly, pulling up a notepad and writing it down.

Maybe she'd been thinking about something else.

She was new.


[}-o-{]
​

"You're funny," Valerie commented with a giggle and he smiled at her. "It's just a funny cup though," she added. To that, he had to wonder how the rest of the world would react to hearing her call Sephiroth Graal a "just a funny cup", especially Heaven. It'd probably be a very funny moment, that was for sure.

At least, if they didn't know Valerie and her situation.

"I know, but it's a useful funny cup," he replied and the dhampir seemed to find that exceedingly amusing. As it was though, Joshua turned his attention momentarily towards the aforementioned Sacred Gear, which he was holding in his hand. As it turned out, he could grab a hold of it… even if he could do literally nothing by holding it. He could carry it around and whatever though.

The moment Valerie wanted it though, the thing would fly back at her or just outright disappear and appear by her side. The girl had plenty of fun when they found that out and Joshua would admit to humoring her in a game of pseudo-catch for a bit. Sadly, he didn't have as much free time as he'd have liked, but he made a note to play with her some other time. Maybe they could play actual catch whenever he did find some though.

"What can it do?" Valerie asked and he fought not to grimace. She should know. That was her Sacred Gear, after all. One that she'd used a whole lot. Yet there she was, with no idea what Sephiroth Graal supposedly did. "What can it do?" she repeated, with the same voice, as if she hadn't asked before and he felt his face twitch.

"Plenty of things, but most of them are really complicated," he answered, feeling old anger rise in him. Not that he needed an excuse to hate Khaos Brigade, but what they'd done to Valerie always hit harder, maybe because he had to face it so often and it was so jarring every single time. "Maybe we can find out together when you get better."

"When I get the other funny cup?" Valerie asked and he paused, blinking. "I can still feel that one. Do you think the bad man will return it?" she said then and he felt the blood in his veins freeze. 'She can feel it? What does that mean?' he wondered. Then he remembered something he'd heard once, from Ophis he was pretty sure.

Something about the cups calling each other? Was he remembering that right? He had tried to find some kind of connection to follow, but that had led nowhere. He had half given up on that route, really. 'Did she ever mention it? I did ask about it, right?' he wondered with a frown, trying to remember.

He'd have to check his notes, but…

"Can you feel anything in particular?" he asked, trying to keep his voice calm, casual. Valerie wouldn't understand urgency or anything. It'd probably just confuse her more, or worse, worry her.

"Sometimes it feels like someone pulls the cup away from me even though I don't have it. That's funny," she commented and he stared at her for a long moment. "What?" she asked then, noticing his look. Joshua, for his part, gulped. 'Calm down. Just… just ask questions.'

"Sorry, it's just… really interesting." Way to understate things, but that'd have to do. "Does it feel like they pull you in a particular direction?" he asked, holding back a reaction as best he could. Maybe because they were always watching, or maybe because of his emotions, but Joshua felt the Egyptians pressing against his mind, like a hundred people trying to peek through a window.

"Yeah, like… pulling," she answered, as if she didn't understand his question.

'This… why is this the first time I'm hearing this?' he wondered, going over every session he had with the girl, trying to find out a moment in which she might have said something like that. Or if he'd even asked something that'd lead to it. Surely he had, right? Surely he hadn't just been a massive fucking idiot or-

"Focus, Pharaoh," Isis told him, the voice of reason that she was.

"We hunt?" a bunch of voices asked almost at the same time, his familiars even mixing in through their own bond. Joshua tried to keep his thoughts straight as best he could… and he barely managed. Their eagerness was mixing with his own.

'Maybe,' he thought, a grin pulling at his lips.

"I'll need you to stick with me, Valerie," he said, placing his hands gently but excitedly on her shoulders. "We'll be playing and talking and just doing a lot of things," he all but promised and he saw her start beaming. "I just need you to tell me when you feel this pull, alright? Then I'll get you the cup from the bad man," he told her and he saw it more than sensed it, her soul pulling itself together right before his eyes.

Her half-vacant expression honed in on him.

"You promise?"

He stared right into her eyes firmly.

"I promise."

And right in front of him, Valerie Tepes appeared, maybe for the first time since he'd first seen her. Fully there, without her tattered soul affecting her at all. Joshua saw the girl she'd once been return for a single second… and he promised himself that he'd return her permanently.

"Good."

That single word, spoken softly and through a tiny, but no less real smile, punctuated the start of things.

He had a lead, finally.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,653
Laying Out the Wire, Light the Fire-

"I'm making things very difficult for you, aren't I?" he asked, and he could see Agnes going to deny it. Unfortunately for her, he'd asked Ravel already before dropping by House of Water. Thus, he knew he was right. The devil – who was keeping an eye on Valerie a little off to the side – had told him, reluctantly, that yes, it was very inconvenient to have to adjust to his changes in schedule. "Don't deny it."

It wasn't like him to borderline order someone like that, Joshua would admit, but alas… He knew Agnes would try to argue if he let her. She was stubborn and felt indebted enough to him. Funny how that kind of thing worked against him sometimes. Not only with her, which was both frustrating and funny at the same time.

Joshua really did feel bad, but unfortunately… Well, his responsibilities to House of Water were kind of low in his list of priorities. He liked teaching and what not, but all that was kind of secondary in the face of everything else that was going on. Some plates he just couldn't juggle properly, so…

"If there's anything I can do to smooth things over, let me know," he told her and her expression twitched. He knew she owed him a lot, but still. He didn't feel like that was quite the case himself, so it was difficult to feel good just dropping unexpected problems on her lap. "Or if I can do anything to make up for the issues," he added.

"It's fine. Your Stars will surely be able to give your classes in your stead in the meantime," Agnes waved off easily and he wondered how to approach things if she denied him more. "You want to do something for me, Joshua?" she asked and he felt his eyebrows shoot up. That was certainly something that he hadn't expected from her. "Focus on whatever is pulling you away now. Deal with Khaos Brigade. Then you won't have an excuse and I'll be able to take full advantage of your link with my association, right?"

'Huh… maybe she's smarter than I thought,' Joshua thought, which was very much a compliment. He already thought she was plenty intelligent, after all. However, maybe she'd found a way to work with him without the cultural difference impacting their interactions. Which was impressive, considering Joshua himself often struggled with that himself.

"... I can do that," he replied and the woman smiled at him like she'd won some kind of battle. Maybe she really thought so. Did she think that he was always out there trying to find ways to screw with her? Joshua guessed he could kind of see why she'd feel like that, but it was still a little awkward… and amusing, admittedly.

"Then do it," she told him with a nod. "I'll organize with your Stars. Tell you what, I'll even talk to the valkyries, if you want, but no promises on that front," Agnes added and he grinned. That was one thing he didn't need from her.

"Don't bother. I'll talk with the Norse myself," he replied. Although, it was more that his partners would talk with the Norse, but details. Considering those were already allies and he was working on his part of the deal with them… He was sure they'd give him the time to work on something to deal with Khaos Brigade.

Besides, the terrorist group was a lot easier to use to smooth things over with how they were causing trouble all over the world. It was funny, but them being so active was helping Joshua have more time to work against them. Not that he felt like it was a good thing, but there were certainly some convenient parts to the whole mess.

"If you say so…" Agnes said hesitantly, very much looking like she wanted to press the issue. Alas, maybe she decided to quit while she was ahead – at least in her opinion – or something, because she straightened and let the matter go. "Then, I guess I have a few calls to make. If there's nothing else…" she commented, trailing off and he smiled at her.

"Again, sorry. But no, nothing else. I'll let you deal with things. If you need me…" he said, giving her a silent offer in much the same way she'd used for her question.

"I'll call," she said with a nod. There wasn't much said after that, just a few quick words and then Joshua moved back to Ravel and Valerie. His mind stayed in that conversation for a bit though. He was giving up a lot of things to dedicate himself to preparing himself and trying to hunt Khaos Brigade.

It was frustrating, and worrying, but all the same, that was how things were. Joshua just had to deal with it. One day, he'd be free of them, he knew. He just had to keep solving problems, one after the other. Eventually, he'd get where he wanted to be.

Or, that was the hope, because otherwise…

"Did I miss anything?" he asked Ravel, pushing unnecessary thoughts aside. It was easier said than done, but like with a lot of things those days, Joshua would just have to keep going anyway. "You having fun?" he asked, making an effort not to laugh as the dhampir poked the Ravel's cheek with a smile on her face.

The devil, in turn, visibly tried to contain a reaction, but Joshua saw her eyebrow twitching.

"Lots," Valerie replied cheerfully.

"Did your talk go well, sir?" Ravel asked in turn.

'Huh, that's new. She calls me sir when she's annoyed too, huh?' he noted to himself. That was a little amusing and a little cute. Alas, he had a feeling he couldn't point that out without getting a fireball to the face. Well, he could, but that'd have been mean. Maybe he'd use that at some other point.

"Yeah," he answered, taking a deep breath in. Entertaining as the sight before him was… he did have things to do. That was the whole point of the meeting, really. "Let's go back home, yeah?" he asked and then he smiled when Valerie let out a fairly adorable cheer.


[}-o-{]
​

With time in his hands and nobody at home, he'd gone to his study.

Ravel had been all for that, which wasn't strange or anything. There was a part that was amusing though and that was that she'd argued in favor of her having a small desk for herself, much like she did in his classes at House of Water. He hadn't seen the point in going over that, but Joshua definitely found it curious, if nothing else. He had offered her to just share a desk, since his was plenty big enough for them both to use it one on each side.

Alas, the girl hadn't found that arrangement good enough.

'Hmm, how do I go about this…?' he wondered to himself, leaning back on his chair and looking at his notes and the pile of books to his side. Then his eyes slid to the side towards the Ophis Snake that he had in vials on the other end of the table. The infinity wardstones he'd put beside them called for some attention too.

Joshua had decided to put visual representations of stuff that he had to keep in mind. There were too many of them, after all. He'd gotten the idea when he'd considered how Ravel – and later Iryuka and Seekvaira – was helping him keep track of all the things he needed to do. Which, funnily enough, weren't many those days, since he'd kind of scrapped a lot of them from his schedule to open up time to work on Khaos Brigade things.

He might have them organizing his time in that regard too though, since there were a lot of those too.

Absently, he waved his hand and made an illusion of Ophis. After that, he started adding new illusions, one next to the other in front of him. Grendel, a shining halo for Heaven, bat wings for the devils, black wings for Grigori and so on. There were many things. It left his desk looking a little cluttered, but at least it helped him keep things in mind.

'Valerie is the most important one right now,' he mused, looking at the girl who was doodling in her own mini-desk set up next to Ravel's. She'd wanted one rather than using the couch on the side of the room and she also ignored the snacks and drinks he'd brought too. Instead, she'd wanted to "work like them" too, which was… adorable. 'Even if she does get a feeling though… that's not going to be enough…'

Having one direction to find Khaos would be good, yes, but it wouldn't be enough. For one, the terrorists could be anywhere in that "line" all the way across the world or right next to them or anywhere in between. Hell, he wasn't sure if Valerie could point him anywhere if the pull happened to come from some other plane, like the Underworld.

For another, Khaos Brigade could very well move somewhere else after the pull. They were appearing all over the world, after all. The chances of Joshua catching them were very low as they were. They were made worse by the aforementioned issue, however. Because if he had to search for them in that "line"... Well, that was more time they could use to get away, knowingly or not.

'I need something more to fix either of those issues. Preferably both,' Joshua thought, running his fingers through his hair. The problem was how. Because he'd been looking for ways to find Khaos Brigade for quite a while by then and nothing had come up. Sadly, Valerie's newly discovered "method" had been more luck than anything, which meant that he wasn't any closer to finding a way to do that.

He didn't have any clues to go off of, not even with all the knowledge and resources at his disposal. He had pieces of infinity within hand, like the wardstones or the snakes and Joshua still had no way of getting what he wanted. Ironic, in a way, he supposed. Mainly, Joshua just thought it was annoying.

'What to do, what to do…?' he wondered to himself. There were probably a thousand things that he could be working on, but they were all minor things. Little adjustments according to new data, but that wasn't going to help him with his current problems. 'I'm so close, come on,' he urged himself, knowing that it wasn't going to help.

He couldn't help it. Khaos Brigade was more dangerous than ever, but they were also almost done. Joshua could almost taste the victory. If he could just hunt down what was left of the terrorists… It was one big battle, at most two. Then he'd be safe, his family would be safe and things would finally become peaceful.

'Almost want to take one of these…' Joshua mused idly, glancing at the Ophis Snakes once more. The more lively one, the one he'd taken from Katerea, caught his eye the most, expectedly. 'Would it change anything? Would it help? I already got a bit of infinity. What would happen if I took one of these? Both?' he wondered, and those were borderline suicidal thoughts, he knew.

And yet…

The snake seemed to almost be calling him. It wiggled inside the vial like it was trying to reach for him, for anyone really. It reached for him, for Ravel, for Valerie even. If there was anyone close by, it'd wiggling against the glass like…

'Against the glass…' he thought, blinking as an image popped in his mind. Then he straightened in his seat and he saw Ravel look up. He didn't look at her though. His eyes were locked on the vial. 'I knew it looked familiar…'

Didn't the Spartos look like that, kind of? When it shifted against its prison, he'd thought it looked purposeful, but he hadn't been able to prove much. But the Ophis Snake reminded him of it… Except, the Spartoi hadn't tried to move towards him, or Athena, or anyone. It just pressed against the cage's barrier…

'What if it was purposeful?' Joshua asked himself.

"Ravel," he called and he was only vaguely aware of the "Yes?" that she answered with. "I need to go check on the Spartoi again. How soon can you make that happen?"

"You have a scheduled visit tomorrow, Mr. Davis," she informed him and he blinked. He had a question about making it that very day at the tip of his tongue. Then he paused though, because… The very next day was pretty quick and it might not be worth the hassle. Besides…

"Right… That's perfect," he muttered, leaning back on his chair and taking a deep breath in. "Thank you," he added absently, staring at the Ophis Snake once more. "Gives me time to tinker," he added, mostly to himself, suddenly filled with determination.


[}-o-{]
​

"You seem… eager," Athena commented, but Joshua was already working. He'd cast a bunch of spells as soon as he could. Which was probably very rude, but he'd gotten a greeting out beforehand. He thought that was a massive show of restraint on his part, really. "Any reason for that?"

"I have a theory," he answered, pausing to take in the feedback he was getting from his spells. Well, some of it aligned with what he predicted. Some of it didn't. He mentally went over the spells he had in mind for the second step of the process. He approved some of them and scrapped others. He'd need to replace them, tinker them on the spot. He could do that though, easi-

"What theory?" Athena asked and he felt his eye twitch.

Someone behind him cleared their throats. Not Ravel, he pretty much knew hers by heart. It was one of the other goddesses then. Gabriel was probably having fun, after all. She'd tagged along for a bit before having to go do her own thing. He wasn't sure why. She'd only said she "wanted to keep an eye on him" for some reason that she hadn't felt like sharing with him.

"I think the Spartos is still connected to the other Spartoi," he answered, taking a deep breath in and focusing back on his work. "The way it presses against the barrier. I think it's trying to reach for them."

'Maybe it's not as soul oriented as I thought? That'd be a first,' he considered, tilting his head. 'Magic then?' he wondered, casting the new arrays of spells. He went slower that time, since he had to craft them on the spot. Although, it was a little balanced out by the fact that non-soul spells were ridiculously easier than soul spells, especially since he'd already worked out the equivalen-

"We considered that already," Athena pointed out and he held back a sigh… or maybe it was a groan. "It's not reaching in a particular direction."

"It doesn't seem to be," he corrected, still staring towards the Spartos as he worked. "I'm revisiting the idea, if you will," he told the goddess, nodding as he finished another set of spells. 'I think I might be onto something,' he thought to himself. There was some kind of correlation between the soul and the magic and the shifting. He needed more information, but Joshua was starting to think that it might actually be purposeful.

"Why?" Athena asked and that time he definitely let out a sound that was somewhere between a sigh and a groan.

Which prompted a sigh from Gabriel, but he didn't care.

"Something inspired me, you could say," he answered. Then it occurred to him to check the Spartos' body. After all, if magic was more relevant than he thought, surely the physical side could be too, right? So, that's what he started working on. He had some other arrays for the next phase, but there were already a bunch of changes he'd have to make, so…

"Inspired by what?"

"Can I finish doing what I'm doing?" he asked Athena, turning to give her a flat look. He wasn't even sure why she looked that scandalized, really. She was the one that had been going crazy to have him work on the Spartos issue. Why was she asking so many questions when he was doing what she wanted? "I'm trying to work here," he added before turning to look at the cage where the Spartos was.

"She's kind of rude," Valerie commented and when had she approached them? "Is she a bad woman?"

"Excuse you?"

"No, Valerie," Joshua answered, bringing a hand up to massage the bridge of his nose. "She's just too curious for her own good. Also, shouldn't you be with Ravel?"

"She's boring though." He couldn't see her, but he knew Ravel was either glaring or pouting or both. "What are you doing?"

"Casting spells," he answered, a weary smile on his face as he went back to work. Because he really needed to get things done.

"You're always doing that," Valerie pointed out and he closed his eyes for a moment.

"Child," a new voice called softly. Surprisingly, it wasn't Gabriel. "Maybe you can talk with us while Davis works."

"Huh?" Valerie seemed distinctly confused and Joshua followed her look. 'What was she called? Thebis?' he wondered with a tilt of his head. "Who are you?" the girl asked and she was being blunt enough that even Joshua knew the goddesses wouldn't react well to it. Or so he assumed.

"I'm Themis," the goddess answered softly, a warm smile on her face. Then she pushed a lock of brown hair behind her ear. "And I'd like to talk with you."

"Really? Why?"

"Because… you seem like a nice girl," Themis answered plainly. Her expression said something very different though. It made Joshua think that he looked similar whenever he sensed Valerie's soul. There was that pity and hurt and sadness.

"Thanks!" Valerie replied with a beaming smile. "You seem like a nice woman. Not like the other one," the dhampir commented.

"Why, thank you. That's very kind of you," Themis commented, glancing towards where Athena was.

"Davis?" a voice called and he turned to see Hecate beside him. "Did you account for the shifting in those scans?"

"That's what I'll work on after I'm done setting up the basic stuff," he answered, turning back to his spells. Then he remembered that it was the goddess of magic that he was talking to. "Any suggestions?"

"But you won't ask me?" Nephthys asked, together with a bunch of other deities at the back of his mind.

'Oh, now you're talkative, huh?'


[}-o-{]
​

"I wasn't flirting with Hecate!" he protested.

Because he had never heard such blatant lies and slander.

"You kind of were." And by Gabriel of all people. To think he'd be betrayed by an angel. What had the world come to when that was something that could happen? Nothing was sacred anymore and Joshua found that deeply sad. "So much talking and flirting."

"I was just discussing spells!"

"Discussing spells," Serafall gasped exaggeratedly. "In front of Valerie and Ravel? Josh! You can't be that degenerate in front of children. And to another woman to boot!"

"We're clearly not enough for him," Yasaka commented calmly as she brought her cup of tea to her lips. "So greedy."

"... I hate you all," Joshua muttered through his teeth. "So much."

"Love you too, magic brain," Serafall commented, her act falling apart immediately. He still glared at her for a little longer though. He thought it was entirely justified for him to do so. "Never change," she added, moving closer to him and pecking his cheek. "So, did you find out anything? You seemed excited yesterday."

"I think I'm onto something, yes," he mumbled, picking up his own cup of tea and taking a sip. "Athena still has her doubts, but I definitely think I could be right, which… I really hope I am. I do think the Spartos is trying to reach for the others. It's a bit messy though, since it's… everything is so chaotic and I assume the same goes for the others. There's also the fact that Khaos is probably hopping from place to place, so it's difficult to narrow it down."

"So, what's the plan now?" Yasaka asked, which was the question, wasn't it?

"More waiting, but now with a plan, sort of," he answered bitterly. There was nothing more frustrating than that, after all. "I hate to say it, but the best I have right now is to wait until Khaos uses their Sephiroth Graal." And he truly did hate it. "I assume that's what triggers the pulls from Valerie. So, I'll keep her around the Spartos as much as possible and the pull she feels and the reaching of the Spartos go both the same way…"

"Then you can confirm both things at the same time," Yasaka finished with a nod. "Sounds like a good plan. Less than ideal, but it's better than having nothing."

"Tell me about it," Joshua mumbled, running his fingers through his hair. "In the meantime… I guess I can work on everything and anything," he added wearily. There really were entirely too many things. He would have to improve the scans around the Spartos. He would have to continue working on measures against Annihilation Maker and the Sephiroth Graal creations. He would need to continue improving on the Silence Rooms for Ophis.

And those were only the most important projects.

"Is this a bad time to say that my brothers think they have time for another meeting the day after tomorrow?" Gabriel asked, already very much aware that yes, it was a bad time for those news. Then again, there would never have been a good moment for such. Joshua felt tired just hearing about it.

"Ravel-" he called, but the girl was already writing it down. "Thanks," he added and the girl smiled at him. "Well, there's that then, I guess."

"What about Val-tan?" Serafall asked and he took a deep breath in. For once though, he didn't feel bad. All in all, things had gone well in that regard.

"Well, Athena doesn't like her much," he answered dryly, getting some raised eyebrows and a giggle from Gabriel. "But Themis definitely does. She's taken Valerie under her wing for whatever reason. Which is good, because she's even offered to keep an eye on her while she stays in Greece. Doesn't mean I won't try to spend as much time as I can there too though."

"Gabriel, Serafall?" Yasaka asked, leaving it at that like the others could fill in the blanks with just that. Surprisingly – or maybe not –, they could. Joshua would never be able to comprehend how their minds worked, he knew. Which was kind of fair, since he was pretty sure they would never do so with his either.

Kind of sad too though, in a way.

"I haven't talked to Themis or about Themis in particular, sorry," Serafall answered with a shrug.

"She's a goddess of justice and laws," Gabriel offered, getting a quiet "ah" from the devil, like that made her own statement make sense. Joshua supposed it did, which he found funny. "She probably finds it disturbing, the state Valerie is in. It's unnatural in ways that probably ripple through her domains. And the injustice of it, it likely tugs at her heartstrings."

'Huh, Themis hadn't seemed like that kind of person…' Joshua mused. When he'd talked to her, she'd seemed… Stiff, strict, no-nonsense. But with Valerie, she had looked more like Yasaka, in a way, or Gabriel. All the rough edges had smoothed and softened even.

It was why he'd felt comfortable leaving Valerie to her.

"Hm, good," Yasaka replied with a nod. "Then, what's in your mind now?" she added towards him and he shrugged.

"Nemesis gave me some nice ideas for how to fight Annihilation Maker and the Sephiroth Graal chaotic creations. I kinda wanna go over them while they are still fresh in my mind," he answered, a slightly vindictive smile tugging at his lips. That particular goddess would be fun to talk to, if only because it'd give him a lot of options whenever he finally got his hands on Khaos Brigade.

"The fact that you're not trying is what makes it worse," Serafall commented and he blinked, confused.

And why were Gabriel and Yasaka nodding?


[} Chapter End {]

#1,660
-Now We're Waiting Till It Blows-

'Provided I do find them, I need a way to reach them before they can disappear,' Joshua thought, tapping a pencil against a page with the most basic teleporting circle. Nothing like the ones he used those days, which were a little slower, but didn't have the slow appearance from top to to bottom – or the other way around – that the normal ones did. His circles also had better energy efficiency and were powered by surrounding arrays, but that was beside the point.

He also had his battle teleportation circles, which were instantaneous, but only worked at close distances. Long distances of those would require more power than he could afford to give, even by the standard of his arrays. He couldn't pour his infinite magic all at once in spells that expensive energy-wise.

And he wasn't about to go face Khaos Brigade on his own either, so it was a worthless point all the same.

Furthermore, he needed to get to a location where he wouldn't even have time to prepare a teleport to. That meant that he needed to go somewhere in a moment's notice and in an instant, with a group right there with him. That sounded like… a complicated matter to decide. Joshua was no stranger to those though.

If anything, it was kind of refreshing to have a clear goal and no weirdness in the middle. There was no strange, still half-unknown soul stuff. There were no unfathomable elements. There was no random ass nature to decipher. It was just magic and a spell that needed to do something specific. It was hard, but it was simple, and Joshua would take that.

That was much better than hard and complicated, if anyone asked him.

"That's not going to be easy, you know?" Hecate commented and he nodded. She wasn't wrong. "The spell is in balance, and your modifications are too. What you want to do is unbalanced. You want a spell that does everything for a pittance of magic power," she summarized and he acknowledged that point. "That's just not possible."

"Means I have to find a point where I can compromise," Joshua replied, running his fingers through his hair. "And I also need a way to set the coordinates quickly."

"Do you want it to give you some tea while you're at it?" Hecate asked and he sighed. It was fair of her to say that, he supposed, but it didn't make it any less frustrating. "You have a growing alliance. Surely there'll be someone that can respond if you point them at a location in their territory, right?"

"Yes," Joshua answered honestly. However, in the spirit of honesty though… "And I trust that they'll try, but I don't trust that they'll succeed. And even if they do, I don't trust that they can keep Khaos trapped until I get there. No, I have to be the one to catch them."

Because so far, Annihilation Maker had been able to make creatures to bypass any defense and barrier. So, Joshua and Friday were probably the only two with a chance of stopping them, at least long enough to try and do some damage, if not outright defeat them. Until they took out that shitty Sacred Gear cheat from the board, there was nothing else they could do.

He didn't think there was a way to stop them otherwise, except maybe… Project WWW, but he wasn't about to pull that when things were kind of looking up. The smallest setback and Joshua might just go for it, no matter how much of a mess it'd create. He'd deal with any kind of mess if it meant Khaos was no longer around to be a thorn in his side.

"That sounds kind of arrogant. You know that, right?" Athena asked him from where she was standing, off to the side and staring at her Spartos, like she did most of the time she spent there. "Are you that confident or letting your hatred get the better of you?"

"If you can think anyone else could hold them down long enough, let me know. Name one of them, even," Joshua replied, eyes on his notebook still. He knew the answer was none. He'd even checked, researched it. Had been part of his preparation for the measures to counter Annihilation Maker even. Nobody had anything even remotely flexible and adaptable enough to do the job.

"I wasn't admonishing you," Athena told him and he paused to blink at that. "Just making an observation," she added and he turned to see her watching him rather intently.

"For the record, it's actually both. I'm that confident, but I also hate them that much," he said with a slight half-smile. With that though, he turned his attention back to what he was doing, because he kind of needed to get that done and the sooner the better. The last thing he wanted was to get confirmation and a location only to not have a way to get there in time.

Even if it turned out his theories on how to find Khaos Brigade were wrong, the work on that particular project wouldn't be a waste.

'There's got to be a way to make this work,' he thought, going over every aspect of the spell he needed to craft. There had to be a way to adjust things so that it'd work the way he wanted. Unfortunately though, the more he looked at it, the more it became evident that nothing was going to suddenly change.

The spell he needed simply could not be powered by him nor his arrays. It was too much magic all at once. His spells couldn't deliver that in one go and he'd burn himself to death if he tried with his current magic output. Even if he managed not to do that, he'd definitely not be in any condition to get into a fight or do anything at all afterwards.

"The good thing is that if you somehow manage to pull it off, then you can power as many as you want, probably. So, that's two problems that can be solved at once," Hecate commented, looking about as focused as he was and he nodded. Then he paused.

"If I power one, I power all of them," he commented, speaking every word like he was savoring them, testing them. "If I power one, I power all," he sort of repeated. Then, slowly, he drew a circle on the blank side of the notebook. "If I power one," he started once more, drawing a smaller circle on one side of the previous one, overlapping a little. "I power all of them," he finished, drawing a bunch of other circles all around the first one.

"Am I missing something?" Athena asked and Joshua chuckled lowly before grinning widely. "Davis," the goddess urged impatiently.

"I think I got it," he replied, more laughter bubbling at the back of his throat. "Instead of making one super spell, I'll make a super array. Handle every bit of the spell separately, to divide the power need. Then make arrays to power each part. It's big and messy-"

"But it'd get the job done," Hecate finished, eyes narrowed. "Butchering a spell into parts like that isn't going to be easy," she pointed out. "This isn't an array with different spells working together for the same end result. You'r making an array for the job of a single spell. That's like the difference between putting together a team of people and making one single creation from different parts, like your own Talos."

"Or Frankenstein's monster, more accurately," Joshua commented, but he was still grinning. "I'll make it work. I just need to find a way to get the coordinates…" he started before trailing off. "Actually, I don't."

"You're gonna leave the destination part of the array empty and then make it when you have it, aren't you?" Hecate asked, like she was reading his mind. Maybe the thing about being a goddess of magic wasn't just because she had a lot of it or-

"You'll still need ridiculous amounts of power," Nephthys pointed out, because apparently the Egyptians were silent unless some other pantheon or god started showing them up. Petty, but if it helped him, Joshua supposed it didn't matter. "You need to get those wardstones working better and faster," she commented and the way Hecate's eyes narrowed, she probably was hearing the Egyptian goddess too.

"Well…" he started, leaning back and smiling so widely that his cheeks hurt a bit. In his defense, it'd been a while since things had just… worked for him. It felt like forever ago since he had stopped struggling and crawling through a project. "You two mind helping me out here?" he asked and he could feel Nephthys determination at the same time that he saw the same emotion appear on Hechate's face.

He liked spellcrafting, but he'd admit that it was nice to have some help for once.


[}-o-{]
​

"You've slowed down."

Those were horrible, terrifying words to hear coming from Ophis.

Immediately, he stiffened and straightened where he sat. He felt a chill run down his spine and the blood leaving his face. In seconds, Joshua was already struggling not to break down entirely.

He thought he had been progressing enough. Yes, he wasn't making as much progress as before with the Silence Rooms, but that wasn't because he was working less on them. The time always remained the same. It was just that the more he progressed, the more difficulty it became to come up with new things to add or improve on.

"I'm sorry," Joshua managed to say, surprised that he didn't choke on those words. "I've been struggling with it lately, but I'm trying to make more time for it," he added, hoping against hope that she wouldn't ask what he was trying to do. Because he didn't know what she'd do if they actually talked about the elephant in the room, which was his war against Khaos Brigade. She had said that she was leaving them to it, but then again, he hadn't really tried to talk about it much.

He didn't know what she'd do if push came to shove, and he preferred not to find out.

"Hm, I see," she mumbled as she reached for the tea he'd prepared for her. With any luck, that meant that she wasn't about to vaporize him. He didn't dare to hope that much though. "How long do you think it'll be before you can give it more time?" the dragon asked and he breathed a little easier. That meant there was a chance for him to survive and fix things. That was good.

"I don't know, but-" he started, going quickly before she could get upset. "-I don't think it'll be too long," he declared. Because, one way or another, things were going to go down soon. Khaos wasn't going to keep gathering creatures forever. Those were going to be used. And even if they did, Joshua was going to catch them eventually if they tried to stay hidden for too long.

"How much is not too long?" Ophis asked and that was kind of a question that he hadn't wanted her to voice.

"At most… about two months," he answered, giving himself a little breathing room. That was, more or less, what he expected to need for his own projects. At least, to perfect them. Chances were that they'd be working before then. Although, to be fair, there were also chances that he'd hit unexpected roadblocks that'd slow him down. "I'm sorry if that's too long."

Ophis didn't say anything after that, simply drinking her tea and picking up a pastry. The silence stretched and Joshua could do nothing but try to get a read on Ophis. Which he knew was pointless, since she was always expressionless and he could see nothing about her with his spells.

He actually had to actively have most of his spells work around Ophis. She always broke them just by existing otherwise. Not to say that he wasn't trying to get a read on her, but that was done with specific, disposable spells rather than main ones.

"That is acceptable," the dragon said, nodding as if she were making a magnanimous decision. Joshua wasn't sure he agreed, but he was happy with the decision all the same. "These are good, by the way," she added and he nodded. "I saw what you ate last night," she added and he blinked.

'Well, that's not creepy and scary at all,' he thought to himself. He was hardly surprised though. She had shown already that she could see… pretty much anything, or so he assumed, all things considered. It was another thing entirely to know that it happened. Alas, he wasn't in a position to complain to the literally infinitely strong dragon, he supposed.

She'd only spied on a meal though, apparently.

Or, at least, he hoped that was all.

"Could I try that?" Ophis asked and he paused, more processing the question rather than considering it. In hindsight, he should have seen that coming. He totally should have. And yet, it would always be strange to him that he was basically giving Ophis mini-bribes in the shape of… normal snacks.

"Sure, I'll have some ready for next time."

"Can it be fresh?" Ophis asked and he blinked. The meals he gave her were always fresh. He had them in stasis with spells that were about as overkill as it'd be to use nuclear weapons to get rid of a rat in the house. "They are fine as is, but the magic changes the food," she said and he felt a shiver run down his spine once more.

He'd assumed that was fine. He'd tested things and they tasted the same with or without the stasis. She could tell something from that? Hell, he'd made sure to drain any foreign magic from the food before presenting it to her with spells. There shouldn't be any difference between those and freshly cooked things and yet…

"I can bring fresh things," he said slowly, picking his words carefully. "It takes time to prepare them. That's why I had them ready and preserved in magic. If you want them fresh, you might have to wait a bit. Or you could let me know when you'll come out and I'll get started ahead of time," he explained, trying to be as thorough as he could. Ophis didn't seem like the kind of unreasonable that wouldn't like hearing that, but…

Well, Joshua had accepted that he would never not be terrified of the dragon.

"... Alright," she mumbled after a moment of silence and taking a sip from her tea. "I'll let you know then."

"Alright," he parroted, feeling himself relax the smallest bit. "Well, if there's anything else you want to try, let me know," he added and the dragon nodded. Then she went back to snacking and drinking tea.

And Joshua, for his part, wondered what the fuck they'd eaten the previous night.


[}-o-{]
​

Idly, Joshua contemplated the Spartos.

Beside him, Athena did much the same. Although, he was pretty sure that they were doing different things. For his part, Joshua was just analyzing what else he could do to better scan the creature in order to find out where Khaos was, or even if his current working theory was correct in that regard. On the other, he was pretty sure the goddess was just… kind of lamenting what had become of her creation.

Or something along those lines.

He wasn't sure why, but Joshua knew that she found the state of the Spartoi to be deeply unpleasant, insulting and probably worse things. Ultimately, it worked in his favor, because it motivated her and probably was the reason why she'd called for the other goddesses. She might even have pushed for the Greek to join their alliance.

Not that he was happy that had happened, but there was no denying that it was convenient and helpful to his cause.

"When you get your hands on Khaos Brigade. You'll call for reinforcement, right?" Athena commented and it was a good thing that he had been thinking about her rather than something else. It meant that he didn't have to shift the gears in his mind like he usually did. "Would it be too much to ask that you do? That you call us?"

"I hate them, I really do," Joshua replied with a slight smile on his face. "That means that I have no issue dropping the entire world and the full consequences of their actions on them," he said as an answer. He was glancing her way, which was how he saw Athena's lips pull into a vindictive smile.

"Piece of advice, don't say stuff like that around Nemesis," the goddess told him, which he wasn't sure the reason for. Nemesis was a goddess of revenge, after all. Surely she'd appreciate the way he felt in regards to Khaos, right? Maybe he was missing something. "Or Themis, for that matter," Athena added.

"Speaking of, Seekvaira," Joshua called, making the devil – who was, like usual, trying to make herself inconspicuous – stand straighter. "Make a note to do something nice for Themis when this is all over." The woman was basically a metaphorical angel, far as he was concerned. She was so good to Valerie and Joshua still didn't know why, but God if he wasn't happy with her for it.

"Will do, Mr. Davis," Seekvaira replied instantly.

"It's rather amusing," Athena said then and he was about to ask what was amusing. However, she beat him to it before he could open his mouth. "At least, looking from outside. I imagine it's very frustrating otherwise."

"I think you lost me," Joshua admitted and that only made the goddess smile.

"I know. That's what I'm talking about," she replied and he wasn't sure what to say or even think about that. "However, I think I've wasted your time enough," she added and he nodded slowly. "I believe you were thinking about something before I opened my mouth and distracted you?"

"Not much distracting to do," he said wearily. "I'm trying to come up with new ways to approach this, but I've more or less done everything I could. Trying to think if I've missed something is always frustrating. Talking and going over other things is more or less what I need to be able to get some new ideas, to be honest," he explained then, running his fingers through his hair as he considered the situation. Alas, he was as out of new ideas as he'd been before their conversation.

"I see," Athena said slowly. "I can understand that," she added after a moment with a nod. "Anything in particular that'd help to talk about?" she asked and for some reason, he found that deeply amusing. Like she was trying to accommodate a strange way of thought, which for once Joshua was pretty sure wasn't just him. He guessed her mind was plenty different from others though, at least in that sense, maybe.

"Wish I knew," he answered with a shrug and a deep breath in. For a moment, he considered commenting on how he'd been thinking about her connection to the Spartoi. He thought about asking how it felt, why it affected her so.

Then he realized that might be a slightly terrible small talk topic.

'Eh, I might not be as bad socially as I thought,' he thought wryly. He totally was though. It was just that sometimes things were obvious enough even for him. Particularly when he was having a good day in that regard.

"Is it leading you somewhere?" Athena asked then, turning her attention once more towards the Spartos.

"I think so," he answered, unsure. "It's difficult to tell without confirmation from Valerie. It does seem to reach in specific directions at times. Makes me wonder if Khaos just isn't in this plane most of the time, or if they move around a lot," he explained, but that made no sense. Why would they move around a lot? Far as Khaos was concerned, they didn't have a way to spot them. "Right now, he seems to be reaching that way, for the most part," he added, pointing over his shoulder, slightly to the right.

"... Lots of pantheons that way, but…" Athena commented, sounding and looking like she was trying to go over the entire list of pantheons. "It's pointless to wonder, isn't it?" she asked then.

"For the most part. If Khaos pulls off a stunt over there, we could maybe confirm something," he pointed out before pausing and considering that for a moment. "Or at least, might help."

"It's been days since the last attempt. Either they ran out of targets, took a break, or…"

"Or got what they wanted," he finished for the goddess. One of those was definitely more concerning than the others. None of them were good though, since they kind of relied on Khaos giving them a clue as to where to find them. If they suddenly went under the radar again, then Joshua didn't know what they'd do.

"Let's hope that's not-"

"Josh!" Valerie called and he could see Athena twitching. For whatever reason, the goddess didn't like the dhampir. Joshua wasn't sure why. The only reasons he could think of were rather petty and, beyond the initial impression, he didn't think it made sense for that to be the case, given what he'd seen of Athena. One way or another, at least the Greek goddess had refrained from acting on her obvious emotions. "I feel the cup!"

Immediately, all thoughts vanished from his mind.

In their place, only one thing stood. He turned to look at the dhampir and she was pointing in a specific direction. Just in case though, he hesitated for a moment and considered things. The teleportation spells weren't in place anyway. He was still working on that.

Valerie wasn't pointing in a wildly disconnected direction though not even a little off. The line her finger was painting for them aligned with the one he'd noticed from the Spartos. Beyond that, he wouldn't be able to tell much, considering how close they were.

All the same, he turned to look at Athena.

The goddess turned towards him.

"Thanks for telling me, Valerie," he said, a grin spreading over his lips and he didn't turn until he spoke again. "That's going to be very helpful," he added. And that was a huge understatement.

"Do I get extra dessert then?" the dhampir asked, all smiles and ironic sunshine.

"Double dessert," he answered and smiled a little wider when the girl let out a cheer. All the same, his mind was already working overdrive. He hadn't noticed a single thing with all his scans on Valerie herself. So, he either had missed something entirely, or it was impossible for him to pick up on whatever was going on…

For the moment, that is.

The Spartos also hadn't reacted, but that was hardly important. The important part was that they had a method. It was a matter of moving Valerie somewhere else and then triangulating the location. If he finished his teleportation spell in time for that moment… Then they'd have them. Khaos Brigade would be right there and he'd be able to finally get a hold of them. He'd trap them…

And he'd end them.

"We have preparations to make, evidently," Athena commented, standing a little closer to his side. When he turned, he noticed that she had a smile wider than even his. "I have plenty of ideas on how we can approach this."

"Let's call Nemesis. I'm sure between the three of us, we'll come up with good things," he replied, hardly able to wait even after he said that himself. He was so close to that single moment, the point in time that he'd been waiting for, preparing for, working towards. "We do have a lot to prepare," he agreed.

He was so eager.

'Just a little more,' Joshua told himself.
