#1,667
-Fight Like You'll Never Die-

Joshua looked at the devastation before him.

It was so extensive that he could hardly see where it ended and where the normal landscape started again, in any direction. It spread all around him, in scorched earth and foul fumes. The very magic in the air showed twisted to his senses, like a mist of corruption and aggression even. It was disturbing to witness that, but through it all, Joshua felt… hopeful.

Because they had confirmed that both the Spartoi and Valerie could help locate Khaos Brigade.

They had pointed in the right direction. Working on a way to find the precise location both of them were pointing towards would be easy. A matter of an hour or two, probably. From there, Joshua just needed to finish with the new Teleportation circles. Once that was done, the next time Khaos reared its ugly head, he'd be on them.

No more chasing ghosts and fearing at home.

He was hunting them.

"So… Can you fix this?" Serafall asked him and he blinked, his mind returning to that ruined landscape. "Gabriel is managing to calm down Altjira and Baiame, but they are still very angry," she commented and he could hardly blame the leaders of the two factions of the Australian pantheon.

He still wasn't sure how it all actually looked like, politically speaking, but that was the summary he'd gotten and it was good enough for him. Everything else he'd heard had sounded very complicated, because apparently Australia was a mess of smaller factions, but it could be sort of organized into North and South the same way the Youkai divided themselves into East and West. He didn't think about it too much, admittedly, so even that could be completely wrong.

Something that he did know though, was-

"Yeah, I can fix this," he answered, looking around. Apparently, the Spartos wasn't the only example of Khaos leaving behind a "present" for the factions that they attacked. The area around him wasn't the second either, but it was the second that he got a good look at. Second one he'd been asked to solve too. Fortunately, this one was child's play compared to the Spartos. "It might take a bit."

"Difficult?" she asked and he looked at her. "Difficult, got it," she repeated, that time with a slight smile on her face. She'd gotten what he meant, thankfully. It wasn't always inconvenient for his partners to be able to almost read his mind.

It wasn't difficult, but it'd take time.

Time that he didn't have right then and there. He needed to get everything ready to tackle Khaos Brigade. Everything else would be pushed to the side, except Ophis' Silence. Once the world was safe for him and his family again, then Joshua would be able to do other things. Hell, cleaning that area sounded downright fun, but… Alas, he wasn't allowed nice things for as long as Khaos Brigade was around.

"They slowed down," Serafall pointed out and he nodded. He'd noticed. It had gotten to the point that they had thought their enemies might have gotten what they wanted, or decided to stop even if they hadn't. "Do you think they might stop?"

"They might," he answered with a nod. Neither of them could really have any idea though. They had more than discussed that amongst themselves and with others. Nobody had any idea what Khaos was even doing, really. "If they stop, I might have to look into Valerie's piece and see if I can force a reaction somehow," he commented, although he wasn't very positive about that.

That'd set him back quite a while, since he didn't have the first idea how to go about it. To add insult to injury, since he could be delayed so much like that, Khaos was likely to do whatever they were setting out to do before he managed. The situation was less than ideal that way, which he wasn't happy with, at all.

"One more target," he said, his expression flat even as his emotions ran all over the place. "I need one more target," he added before running his fingers through his hair. Considering the intervals between attacks, he was fairly sure that his preparations would be ready for the next one. One more and that'd be that…

"Do you think we could make that happen?" Serafall asked and he blinked. "Make an attack happen?" she added and he considered that, his mind running the situation through as if it were a magic spell. He wasn't sure what Khaos was taking into account other than targeting dragons and dragon-adjacent figures. Sometimes it was just the one, sometimes it was groups, like the Spartoi.

Or the latest targets, Neitee and Yeutta.

Unfortunately, there were dragons all over the world, so that didn't really narrow it down at all. 'It's always a different faction, at least so far,' he thought to himself. So, that at least crossed off some areas, but that helped very little. The factions themselves were interesting to note though.

'There hasn't been a single small faction that's been attacked,' he noted to himself. 'Not all of them are the biggest, but none of them are small,' Joshua mused, which was interesting. Certainly something to keep in mind and also something that narrowed things down, but still…

"Thought of something?" Serafall asked and he shook his head. "Boomer," she added with an exaggerated pout. "Something for us to discuss then. Maybe we can find something." Doubtful, since they had already tried, but it couldn't hurt to check again… probably. "The Australian factions are gonna join us though, from what I'm seeing."

"That's good," he replied, although he probably didn't sound like he meant it. To be fair, factions joining their efforts as an actual alliance of any sort would have been good news months and months in the past. At that very moment, it changed almost nothing. The bigger part of Khaos had already been dealt with. It was only the core group that was still around and maybe some stragglers here and there.

The alliance was doing basically nothing, even if it might sound harsh.

They'd all come around a little too late. Maybe though, their attack power would come in handy during the final battle. Provided things went well, of course. Joshua didn't want to be too optimistic though. After all, nobody's defense had been able to hold off… Khaos…

"How likely is it that we can get the details of their defenses?" he asked and Serafall paused.

"... How detailed?" she asked back and he just stared at her and shrugged. "Oh, these conversations are going to be fun," she said then, her lackadaisical act falling a little with frustration shining through. He was about to take back the request, but she beat him to it all the same. "Don't worry. At least it's something we can do while you do your own thing."

"If you can't, you can't," he tried to reassured her, but she waved him off.

"Well, I guess I have to negotiate something. At least I don't have to do it alone," Serafall commented, standing up and squaring her shoulders before moving to join Gabriel. 'Well, that just means I have to try harder myself then, I guess,' Joshua thought, looking back towards the ruins of the area around him.

And he wondered if that's how his entire world would look like, if he failed.


[}-o-{]
​

"Hm… Mr. Davis?" Iryuka asked and he paused.

Then he looked up and at the young devil that had been quietly working to the side on a far spot at the table. There wasn't much for her – or Seekvaira or Ravel – to do those days, considering he'd cut back on most things, admittedly. Sure, they had helped him check through his library for information and they still looked through at times. However, beyond that and making sure he didn't neglect some projects for others, there was little else for them to do.

Funny how his schedule had been the busiest right before it cleared up almost completely.

Forcefully, of course, but still.

"Yeah?" he replied, taking a deep breath in and resetting his mind a little. Maybe he should ask them to interrupt him from time to time. Joshua did have a tendency to go on tangents in his own mind. Funnily enough, he also had a tendency to hyperfocus on things and get stuck. Both things weren't much of a problem, normally, but he was a little too motivated those days and that was, ironically, working against him.

A poke here and there should prevent both of those from happening.

"... Um, my family has connections with Rosenkreuzer, the magician association," Iryuka said and he nodded, urging her to continue. He didn't need the clarification, but he appreciated it all the same. She seemed very hesitant to bring up whatever it was that she wanted to though, but that only made him more curious, really. "And we got a report that someone was causing trouble for House of Water. I wasn't sure if I should… bring it up or not, since you have stepped away from that, lately."

That was decidedly not what Joshua had thought it was all about. Although, to be fair, he wasn't sure what he had expected at all. All the same, he still found himself somewhat surprised.

Also because Agnes was supposed to have enough power to just shrug off most anything. That was why she always felt so incredibly in debt with him, wasn't it? He had given her a lot of power, helped strengthen her standing and her association's. So, how was anyone giving her trouble?

"Many people are doubting how much you're actually involved," Iryuka explained and he nodded. That made some sense, but still… He took a deep breath in, and that seemed to worry the devil, for whatever reason. "Apparently, a gathering of smaller associations are working together to press that point," she added, as if more information would help.

Which it did.

So, a bunch of mosquitoes were trying to be a bother…

"Any names in particular?" he asked and Iryuka sat a little straighter.

"Adytum, it's an association from America, they-"

"Is there any way I can tell this group of associations to fuck off without taking from my time?" he asked, because he really couldn't be bothered. He had important things to do and much as he appreciated all that Agnes had done for him… He kind of needed to focus on his own things. There was a reason why he had abandoned his duties to the association, sort of.

"Lady Serafall or Gabriel could maybe do something," she mumbled, but Joshua didn't like that idea. Those two had their own stuff to work on. They were busy on good days, and with all the alliance work they had to put in… Well, he'd feel bad adding more to that for something that was technically not that important.

'I don't suppose you guys feel like helping?' he thought to himself, projecting towards the Egyptians. Those were, allegedly, supporters of House of Water, or at least Nephthys was. Hell, they were working with his apprentices, so… He got a vague sense of disinterest though, which was kind of sad and annoying. However… 'Well, I guess I could ask Hecate,' he mused. She was a goddess of magic, after all. Surely she had an association or two she could push to help House of Water's situation.

"No, you won't," Nephthys hissed in his mental ear. Joshua found himself incredibly unimpressed with how petty gods could be… again. "And don't think I don't know what you're doing."

'It's working anyway, isn't it?' Joshua asked. Although, to be fair, he did plan to ask Hecate if the Egyptians didn't bother. The lot of them were sitting on their asses doing nothing but channeling their powers through him and his apprentices, unlike his partners, or even the Greek gods. He felt no shame in poking them into action.

"You're too smug about this."

'Meh.'

He ignored the bristling in his head and nodded.

"Thanks for telling me, Iryuka. Already handled it," he commented, turning his attention back to his work. He could tell the girl was confused, but he didn't elaborate. To her credit, the devil also didn't push for an explanation. She seemed to just take his word for it and go back to work.

Although, he did make a mental note – and send a message through Friday to Ravel – regarding the connection she mentioned to a big association. One never knew, after all. He also added a little task for the Phenex girl to make a list of the resources the two new secretaries might be able to bring to the table… and her own too.

He wasn't sure why he had never asked, to be honest.

On second thought, he held back that last part. If Ravel hadn't said anything, she probably didn't have that much to offer. Maybe because she was a fourth child and a girl to boot, so she didn't have that much power through Phenex contacts. Bullshit, if anyone asked him. He'd be sure to offer her some of that power himself.

She could manage his connections better than he could anyway.


[}-o-{]
​

"Go ahead," Michael said and Joshua nodded.

However, before actually doing what he was setting out to, he glanced around. Uriel looked about as happy with the situation as he could have hoped, which was to say not at all, but there wasn't a flaming sword pointing his way. Raphael looked torn between being incredibly curious and being worried. Michael's expression, for his part, was carefully neutral, which didn't really help.

Gabriel was the only one that seemed even remotely at ease and encouraging, and even she had some twitches of unease.

"You guys know I don't have to do this, right?" Joshua asked, raising an eyebrow and using all his acting skill to camouflage how he felt saying that. Not that he expected them to fall for it, but he could try. Because he really did want to try… but he knew they felt as unsure of the course of action as Joshua himself did.

Alas, he was running out of things to try and help himself with.

The current idea, one that he'd brought to them and they had tentatively agreed to, was… Checking through Heaven's System to see if anything could be done in regards to Valerie. It wasn't a new idea at all, really, but they had stayed away from it up to that point. Raphael, for the most part, had been reviewing it ever since though.

Finally, the angel had come to the conclusion that it'd be probably fine to just try and check on it. Even that much had them feeling a little uneasy. Not that Joshua could blame them. The Sacred Gear section of the system was infamously the one that was the most… buggy, as it were, so it made sense for them to be a little wary of that part.

"No, we have to check that side of things eventually. Might as well do it for a good cause like this," Michael insisted then and Joshua stared at him for a long moment. He wished Cheshire could have joined him for that visit. Alas, it was already a stretch for him to be there, even with the system business. And that was without the fact that his familiars were… Well, some of them were such that the angels liked to pretend they didn't exist.

Fortunately, Gabriel wasn't like that, but she was kind of an exception that way.

"So, let's do this. We need the information ourselves," Michael told him and he nodded again, that time more definitely. He could understand those points, at least. So, if they were determined, he might as well just try and make the most of it.

With a thought, he called for the System once more…

And it answered immediately. Not very clearly, however, not at all. It felt like the stuttered response of someone that had been caught off guard. Half baked ideas popped in his mind, blurry pictures and vague statements. All of it flashed in his mind like one of those videos that use glitching to turn the thing into a collage-like piece, with random pictures and noises and effects…

Joshua felt a headache coming his way just trying to process that for a second.

"Alright… this is a mess," he muttered, vaguely aware that Raphael leaned forward. He raised a hand to prevent any questions from coming his way as he tried to parse through the influx of botched information. Ultimately, he gave up. "This is going to take a while," he muttered, taking a deep breath in and starting to speak.

And through it all, even Uriel started taking notes when it became evident that things were even worse than they'd thought. Michael, for his part, looked at what he could, which wasn't that much. Raphael, Michael and Joshua himself became a bit of a combination, trying to process things and rule out things, cover any gaps… And prevent any mistakes.

Because all of them knew that the slightest wrong move could be disastrous, especially after seeing how much of a disaster Heaven's System was where they were looking. Joshua had, at that point, completely given up on actually getting any work done. They were merely gathering information and would likely spend a session or ten just… looking for a way to fix things at least a little.

Because there was no way they could actually get anything done.

It was only after a long stretch that Joshua realized that the System, in its Sacred Gear area, looked like a spell. Except, it was a spell that was perpetually failing, or, maybe more accurately, a spell that was continuously on the verge of failing. It never quite did, but it was right there and that was even worse.

In a way, Joshua thought that might be the most terrifying thing he'd ever witnessed.

"That was…" Raphael commented once they decided to just… call it quits. Checking idly, Joshua realized that they'd been there for five hours and it felt like they'd barely gotten anything done. 'Fuck, Kunou's going to be sad. I better bring ice cream with me when we go back…' he thought with a grimace.

"It's going to take some time," Michael said when it became evident his brother wasn't going to finish whatever he'd started saying. Joshua, for his part, thought the Leader of Heaven had just uttered quite the understatement.

"We just can't have easy things, can we?" he lamented to himself.

Gabriel patted his shoulder comfortingly.

At least he had her.


[}-o-{]
​

'I know you're eager, girl,' Joshua thought to himself, lying down on a long bench at the training area. As usual, his group of misfits and his familiars were fighting each other for training purposes… Probably. Nagini sometimes actually tried to kill them, admittedly. Not that anyone let her succeed, but that wouldn't stop her.

"I fight," Friday insisted and he let out a mental sigh.

'I know,' he repeated, fighting not to roll his eyes. 'You'll fight Annihilation Maker when the time comes. For now, you have other things to do,' he said, with all the patience he'd learned to have dealing with as many children and childish people as he had. He had liked to think he was a patient guy to begin with, but time had definitely tested that fact, that was for sure. 'For now, can you please keep an eye on the defenses? That's fighting too.'

"I fight?" Friday asked, apparently latching onto that last point. Joshua almost wanted to roll his eyes, and also laugh, and also sigh again. The living spell was bringing a lot of emotions to his head, which he really was too tired to process fully. Alas…

The perils of being a father, he supposed.

'You fight,' he agreed and that seemed to make Friday happy. Fortunately, she did listen and go back to checking on the defenses he'd set up for people in the alliance. Annihilation Maker was the reason Khaos could get through those so easily, so the living spell was their best bet at keeping them out if they decided to visit.

From there… Well, Joshua was taking a bit of a break, if he were honest. His head still hurt whenever he thought about Heaven's System after his last visit. It also hurt whenever he tried to think about the new thing to work on – because of course he had a new thing to work on – and that was the fact that faction defenses could be the factor that attracted and/or delayed Khaos.

Because, the long pause in activity could have a reason and that could be faction defenses. They weren't targeting small factions, but he considered that might be because they didn't consider those good enough to bother. And that meant that it required some kind of effort on their part. They also were never attacking places in quick succession, so that meant that it took some preparation to get things done.

They were scouting, preparing raids…

And maybe they could crack some kind of code. Joshua considered that, if they could figure out what all of that meant, they might be able to predict a target. If nothing else, they might be able to determine if there'd be more targets at all. A lot of "ifs" were involved in the situation, but it was what they had.

They had been in a state of throwing things at the wall and seeing what stuck for quite a while, Joshua was realizing.

'Just a little more,' he told himself, closing his eyes and going over things in his head. His people were strong. His spells were coming along nicely. His allies were growing in number and strength. 'Feels like everything's coming together,' he mused.

So, why wasn't that comforting? Instead, it just made Khaos Brigade feel all the more inevitable in his head. The shadow that had long since loomed in the distance was closing in. Whether he liked it or not, Joshua knew that the clock was ticking, louder than ever before.

'One way or another…'

With a deep breath in, he pulled himself to a sitting position.

There was work to get done, after all. He still needed to wrap up the teleportation arrays. He'd need a bunch of them, but he was making progress. He was also improving on the infinity wardstone-based spells, which would be a big part of what would make the formers possible at all. From there, he needed to get some more work done in regards to sensing around the Spartos and maybe Valerie too.

And from there, he also needed to prepare some gifts for Khaos Brigade.

Lots of things to do, but he had an objective, or several, really. All the cards were on the table and Joshua just needed to see how things would play out. He just needed to continue for a little longer and then…

'Let's see,' he thought, focusing as he opened his notebook. 'Right, teleport target reading,' he noted. 'Do I need to divide that into several spells or can it be only one?' That was a thought that crossed his mind a lot in regards to the Teleportation arrays. Because breaking down the spell was kind of the point, but if he did it too much, then he was adding more work to his plate…

But if he didn't do it enough, then he ran the risk of falling short and still needing too much energy. If that happened… Well, he'd need to start over, and that was not something he wanted to happen. 'Better err on the side of caution,' he decided with a sigh. That'd be more work, but oh well. 'What's new, right?'

At least, things feeling so close to an end also kind of helped. It gave him something to latch onto in order to push a little more. After all was said and done, he'd either be able to rest or he wouldn't be there to care. One way or another, it'd all be behind him.

'Just make sure you win,' he told himself.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,671
-Fight to Stay Alive-

[Yasaka]

"It's not like you to be so… restless," she said, but the word didn't feel like it fit the situation.

"I know," Joshua replied, clearly not quite agreeing with her thoughts on the choice. Then again, he was probably too focused on his own things to really give it any thought. And he tended not to have the clearest view on certain things to begin with, so there was that. "I just thought this would help me think, maybe. It'll change things up, at least," he added and he wasn't wrong about that last part, Yasaka supposed.

So, she sat at the table with a cup of tea in her hands and another to the side where Kunou was sitting. Their daughter – she still loved just thinking that, she'd admit – seemed particularly mystified by the sight of Joshua walking around and casting illusions of what crossed his mind. In a way, it reminded Yasaka of how they'd met, with his illusions catching Kunou's attention and slowly helping him worm his way into her heart… and Yasaka's too.

"Gives me a picture of things and helps me not forget things. Ravel and the others have a list of things, if I miss something, they have to point it out," he added, waving his hand towards the Agares devil that was sitting off to the side and leaning down with her head in her notes, to make herself as inconspicuous as possible. If there weren't a precedent of Joshua turning down women too young – and immature, particularly –, she might have worried about her.

But then again, Joshua wasn't an easy target for women in general. He was too dense, for one, and he was also unwilling to consider the idea of welcoming more partners. Even if they gave him permission he'd push back against it. It was so strange, but also very very much appreciated, by her and also Serafall and Gabriel.

"Positioning is turning into a bit of a problem, too many spells…" Joshua commented then, speaking to himself as Kunou took a sip from her own tea. The man followed suit without realizing, waving his hand and making illusory circles appearing in the air. They were small, most of them the size of a thumb, but more and more started appearing, forming an array of circles the size of the way in front of him. That was, indeed, a lot of circles.

Not a lot more than what he usually set up wherever he went, but still more, which was saying something.

"And I'll need to set up several of these," Joshua pointed out and Yasaka felt her eyebrows raise. That was, indeed, a lot of space needed just to have spells set up. "I'm gonna need a ridiculous amount of space just for this, and then I'd need to set up defenses for that, which might mess with the setup, which is just…" He finished with a sigh, looking at the illusion in front of his face.

"Can't you do the thing you told me about, putting spells on top of each other?" Kunou asked and Joshua considered that for a moment before nodding slightly. Then, with a few hums and other idle sounds, he started rearranging the illusion into piles like they were chips in a casino table.

"Better, right? Looks like a mess, it's throwing off the balance something fierce," Joshua commented, but he didn't look nearly as frustrated as before. Even Kunou noticed and Yasaka saw their daughter puff up a little, clearly proud of being able to help her father. "Maybe some other kind of arrangement though, like…" Joshua continued, unaware of the look on his daughter while shifting the circles again, that time into some kind of donut-like shape-

"Kind of looks like you could make a rose, you know, with the circles as petals, like…" Kunou said then, eager to get more "points" for helping Joshua as she started gesturing with her hands. Yasaka looked at her trying to explain the way she envisioned the overlapping the circle. Which wasn't very different from what Joshua had just done, except the overlap kind of went a little diagonal about it. "Or maybe like the ratatouille, the one from the illusion story!"

"Those are… not the worst ideas," Joshua replied, sounding and looking like he meant it while making illusion displays as examples. "I have to look at the numbers, but you might be on to something here, Kunou," he added, and that time he definitely did it on purpose. He had that fond smile on his face that he always did when Kunou did something adorable.

Like looking entirely too smug about being helpful.

"I think that deserves ice cream though," Joshua said, evidently having abandoned his spellcrafting trance of sorts in favor of spoiling their daughter. Gods, Yasaka loved that man and he was only making her fall harder as time passed. "What do you say, Yasaka, you coming?" he added and he knew exactly what he was doing, because Kunou turned to look at her with wide, pleading eyes.

"Might as well wait and go out for dinner, don't you think?" she asked with a raised eyebrow that gave both of them pause. She was not at all surprised by the fact that they seemed to have lost track of what the time was. "Speaking of going out, are we bringing your other daughters?"

"You're saying that like they aren't yours," Joshua pointed out and she paused. He didn't say that accusing her of anything, just an idle observation. Like he was checking something that had crossed his mind and wanted to make sure he had the right idea of things.

"True," she replied, because she knew she was definitely going to keep Joshua and he didn't seem to be in a hurry to change his mind about her so… She guessed she'd picked up a bunch of kids from him the same way he'd picked hers. "Are we bringing them?"

"I'll tell Morag and the others," Kunou said, looking between them like she thought they might need a moment to talk… or "talk". Her daughter was very smart, indeed, but she was reading too much into things that time.

Besides, they didn't have time for that if they wanted to make it to dinner.

Afterwards, definitely.

"Are you calling Ravel and Koneko, dad?" Kunou asked, already standing up to leave.

"Yes, don't worry about it," Joshua reassured, entirely too unaware of the situation, as usual.


[}-o-{]
​

[Agnes Waterhouse]

She wasn't sure how Joshua had heard that there were minor associations trying to get uppity with her, but he had.

And subsequently, Nephthys had been more active as a patron of House of Water than she ever had before. There were even a few other gods of the Egyptian pantheon that dropped by on occasion. Additionally, his Stars were displaying a lot more of their divine given gifts and more blatantly at that.

'I didn't need the help though,' Agnes thought wryly. And that wasn't even her not wanting to increase her already nigh infinite debt with Davis. Sure, the group of associations had been annoying, but it hadn't been any worse than other things Agnes had already had to deal with before her association rose to the top of the food chain. If anything, it had been a little flattering that they had to resort to that kind of thing to even try to face her.

Yet, Joshua had apparently heard about them and decided to act in what Agnes was realizing was his usual approach. He'd taken a nuke and decided to use that to make the nail sticking out disappear. Measured and subtle, Joshua Davis was decidedly not. 'Every day, I'm given reasons to be grateful I managed to get that man on my side,' she mused to herself.

Granted, it was a bit of a double-edged sword, since she was essentially forever at the man's service, but there were worse people to owe, she supposed.

"What did you do?" Elizabeth asked as she walked in. She'd left for one of her usual "trips" where she visited her barely gray and sometimes downright Stray association contacts. She was doing a lot of that those days, but then again, she was always on the lookout for information she could offer Davis. The man had rather curious interests, after all, particularly towards soul-related magic.

Agnes would reluctantly admit that such were a lot closer to the kind of thing Elizabeth was more likely to find.

"Believe it or not, nothing," Agnes replied wearily with a half smile. "Apparently, Davis heard about the situation with the smaller associations and…" she finished that answer by simply waving her hand up in the air. There was no need to say anything else, after all. The situation spoke for itself.

"That man is a menace," Elizabeth hissed, bringing a hand up to massage her forehead. "We're never getting out of this, are we?"

"You thought we had a chance?" Agnes asked with a raised eyebrow. She'd long since given up, to be honest. Sure, sometimes she lamented the tragedy of it whenever Davis did something to pile up on her debt, but she couldn't realistically pay him back in her lifetime and that had been a fact for quite a while by then. So, she was getting better at accepting the inevitable and just seeing how she could make herself feel better by repaying parts of it.

"Fair enough," Elizabeth said with resignation and frustration in equal parts. Then she sighed and deflated. "Any luck coming up with things to do?" she asked then, moving to take a seat on a chair across her desk. "Because I've been digging everywhere and I barely find anything."

"As a matter of fact, I did," Agnes replied and that seemed to surprise Elizabeth. She couldn't blame her for the doubt, but it still annoyed her. "He seems very interested in learning new kinds of magic. I bet it's not just a thing with the Norse Runes only."

"... That sounds promising," Elizabeth replied, eyes narrowed like she was looking for a flaw in her idea. Which she probably was, since she loved to find things to criticize in her plans. Agnes did much the same for her thought. They pushed each other that way. "Not easy, but promising."

"Yeah, I guess Davis might see it as an investment. We'll use all that influence, power and resources that he gave us to give him what he wants. We just need to be smart about how we handle things so that we don't burn ourselves, but…" Agnes mused out loud, leaning back as she thought it over herself a little more. She'd kind of been waiting to discuss the idea with someone, after all. "I have a feeling that he'll appreciate it even if we get some minor systems rather than something like the Myrddin circles or the Norse runes."

"That sounds more doable and yes, like it'd be something he'd be interested in," Elizabeth replied, eyes narrowed for a completely different reason. She probably could think of at least one such magic system that she could reach for. Agnes knew better than to ask which one, because she wasn't likely to think about one that she'd want to know about herself.

The divide had never been more obvious, in regards to their roles in the association, but Agnes had never been less bothered by that. They were working as a team like they never had before. She looked at the legal factions and Elizabeth at the illegal and maybe barely legal ones. Between the two, they could get a lot more done and they kind of needed to maximize what their efforts earned.

It was imperative, considering the situation they'd both been put in by a certain magician.

"I guess I have calls to make," Elizabeth commented with a sigh. "I don't suppose there's anything I should be doing here?" she added, almost like she wanted to have work for the association rather than going back to her shady contacts. Agnes found that a little amusing, considering how before she couldn't wait to get out of the association. Alas, the situation had changed that much, she supposed.

"I guess I could use some help with this meeting," she said, throwing her only ally in that situation a bone.


[}-o-{]
​

[Penemue]

"Fascinating," Azazel commented, looking at the new batch of Sacred Gear users that Davis had sent their way.

Personally, she thought that it was kind of… sad how the man could absolutely forget about the tensions between factions. Especially all the friction that was always present between them – Azazel in particular, and almost exclusively – and the Egyptian's Pharaoh. Considering it was half the reason for the issues their faction was having, one would think he'd at least be aware of that.

Penemue counted herself grateful of the fact that Davis seemed distracted those days. Hell, most of the alliance seemed to have their minds on things other than Grigori, which was very fortunate. However, it was a fact that one day, Khaos would be dealt with and then people would be able to turn back their way. Penemue feared that day, which was why she was doing her absolute best to get some points with the alliance's factions.

"That one is even a subspecies. Where'd you get these people, Penny?" Azazel asked and she considered answering honestly for a long, vexing moment. Then she smiled her best professional smile. Because at the end of the day, she had a duty to her position and to her people and, sadly, Azazel was no longer as big a part of her decision making process as he'd once been.

"I pulled some strings when the chance presented itself," Penemue answered, which wasn't a lie. She had pulled the strings when the chance presented itself. The chance being that she'd been asked what she'd need to get some extra decision power in Grigori. "So, I take it I wasn't scammed?" As if she ever could be, but one never knew. Especially when it came to Sacred Gears and all their peculiarities.

"Not at all!" Azazel answered immediately, not even bothering to ask what she'd had to pay for his new Sacred Gear projects. She guessed that was to be expected. Once, she might have thought it was because he trusted her judgement. At that moment, Penemue wondered if he even cared. "Oh, this is going to be so good to check on some of the ideas I had!"

"Just remember that you're the Governor, Azazel," she pointed out, but she knew what her answer would be. In a way, she was expecting that answer, hoping for it even. Because it would mean that her deal with Serafall, Gabriel and Yasaka would still be good. It would also mean that things for her faction could continue to be just as good, since she'd have plenty of support from outside… and Azazel would allow her to do what she needed to do.

"Eh," was the Governor of Grigori's eloquent response as he shrugged. "You can more than cover for me. This will mean so much. I might even get some information to help the Tepes girl. Might get the others off my case."

If she had to guess, that was kind of what they wanted from Azazel. Penemue was pretty sure that was just a side-effect of things. For the most part, the alliance just seemed to want to get rid of Azazel and put Penemue in a position of power. Or, more accurately, a better position of power.

She was pretty sure that if they could make Azazel disappear and sit her in his metaphorical throne, they would.

Penemue didn't know how she felt about any of that.

"You know you have to do things other than Sacred Gear research sometimes, right?" she asked, but she knew it would get her anywhere. She wasn't even sure why she tried anymore. It did nothing for the guilt she felt for all but backstabbing her own leader. If anything, it just brought to the forefront of her mind that she was doing something questionable.

"You can handle it better than I would anyway," Azazel said, not at all helping the conflict she had to deal with on a daily basis. It was also a blatant lie. Because there was a reason why he was their leader, yet… He seemed determined not to be the Azazel that had commanded them through wars, that had turned them from lost souls and twisted minds into a proper faction, one to rival the angels and the devils.

Time had passed and Penemue could barely remember that Azazel anymore. It was like he was a completely different person at that point, had been for quite a while, really. She wasn't sure what she could do in that regard anymore. She'd tried, she had tried so hard, to bring that Azazel back at least a little bit. She'd failed and she was starting to realize that she might never have had a chance to succeed.

"I'll handle it, then," Penemue replied and, for a second, Azazel seemed to pause. He probably expected her to fight him more on that, like she always had. Penemue almost wanted him to call her out on it. She almost wanted him to question things, say something, anything.

"Great!" he exclaimed then, grinning from ear to ear.

Then he turned towards the Sacred Gear holders she'd brought… And Penemue wondered why she wasn't upset, or even disappointed. Instead, she found herself in a dull resigned state, like she had run out of other emotions to feel. Ultimately, she guessed it didn't matter how she felt in regards to Azazel, her faction or even the alliance. She was, once again, a pawn to higher powers, except it was no longer her Father nor Azazel that was pulling her strings.

Idly, she wondered if her new puppeteers would disappear on her too.

That seemed to be the trend, at least.


[}-o-{]
​

[Athena, Goddess of Wisdom]

In a flash, one Joshua Davis appeared before her for another session of studying her Spartos.

Her creation, which was still just as twisted and wrong as the first time they captured it. Athena didn't feel any better than she had that day, when she first realized there was something wrong, when she felt the sliver of her divinity connected to the Spartoi being taken and corrupted. And lying her eyes upon it only made things worse, but she couldn't look away. She knew it did nothing; she knew it wouldn't get better no matter how much she stared at the Spartos… yet she had nothing else to do, she knew not what to do.

All she could do was hope that Davis would be able to fix it.

"Sorry for the delay," the man said, rubbing the back of his neck, stretching it and his back awkwardly. 'He was with one of his lovers,' Athena deduced immediately with some annoyance. Alas, she didn't see a point in talking about it. She wouldn't achieve anything other than making things uncomfortable for everyone involved.

And probably make Hecate jealous.

"That was instant teleportation," the aforementioned magic goddess pointed out. "Were you close by?" she asked then. Apparently, she hadn't picked up on what Athena had, which was good. Interestingly, it seemed to be because she had hyperfocused on that detail… Which, admittedly, was rather interesting. It made sense considering the project that Davis seemed to be working on in order to be able to ambush Khaos Brigade.

"I wasn't," the man said, a satisfied, confident smirk on his face that probably did something for his partners… and Athena's gathering of goddesses. It was such misfortune that she hadn't been able to find a god agreeable to her cause. But then again, it helped to have such… motivated allies, she supposed. It was annoying, but also helpful.

"You cracked it?" Hecate asked, eyes wide with shock that gave Athena pause. "Already?" her fellow goddess had to add. Disbelief was clear in her expression and her voice for which she couldn't really be blamed. The goddess of magic had given Athena an estimate based on what she'd seen of Davis and that estimate had already seemed crazy even to Hecate herself.

Yet there they were, with the man apparently having worked things out way faster than expected.

"Sort of," the man said with a so-so wave of his hand. "I made it work, but it's really not space efficient and there's a few things to work out still. I need to work out a tighter arrangement for the circles, which I already have ideas for. I actually wanted to run things by you, Hecate. Nephthys is busy with something and I need a second opinion on a few things," the man explained and Hecate straightened, clearly pleased by the "compliment" that the man's words carried.

Athena looked to the side to share a look with Themis and Nemesis, but she only found the exasperated eyes of the latter. The former, instead, had moved forward. Athena even caught a slightly disappointed look on her face, sad even. Something that even Davis picked up on, if the way he turned towards the goddess was any indication.

He even knew what that was about.

"Sorry, Valerie stayed back today," he said as an answer to an unasked question.

"Makes sense," Athena replied, even as Themis deflated a little. "It'd make it easier to triangulate the location if the dhampir and the Spartos are in different places," she added, although she wasn't sure why Themis was making a big deal out of it. Honestly, the Tepes girl was a distraction at best and a hindrance at worst. She literally couldn't do anything. Athena wasn't sure why Themis had even grown so fond of the girl and so suddenly at that.

"It does make sense," Themis mused grudgingly, which made Athena roll her eyes.

"She was asking after you yesterday, you know?" Davis commented, focusing on Themis and Athena told herself that pressing to get to work would only make everyone annoyed with her and not actually accomplish what she wanted. It was still frustrating though. "You must have made quite the impression on her. It usually takes her longer to remember people, let alone think of them when they're not in front of her."

"Really?" Themis replied with a bright smile, clearly pleased. "Hopefully we can see each other soon."

"Well, like Athena said, that's not very… efficient," Davis said, seeing reason for once. Themis seemed deeply sad about that though. "But you could visit us if you want. We try to keep her company all the time, but it can't hurt for her to have more friends around," he added.

"Truly? It won't be an issue?"

"Not at all," Davis replied, waving off Themis' worries. "I'm sure Yasaka will be fine with it and if not, I can convince her. So long as you don't mind some more company than just Valerie."

"I don't, not at all," Themis replied instantly. Did she realize that Davis probably included his sisters and maybe Yasaka's daughter into that equation? Did she realize she was volunteering for babysitting duties? Surely she did. She wasn't dumb. There was a reason Athena had reached for her to help them, and it wasn't just because of her domain of laws, which helped figure out how much of a mess had been made of her Spartos and the justice that needed to be delivered upon Khaos Brigade.

Admittedly, she might have overestimated how much Themis would do in the latter case.

"Maybe we can focus on the matter at hand?" Athena asked and both Themis and Davis turned towards her like they'd just remembered she was there. 'The audacity of these two…' she thought as her eye twitched. None of that was helped by the fact that Nemesis was giggling behind her.

"Right," Davis said all the same. "So, Hecate, about the arrangements I had in mind, do you think it'd affect anything if we give it the actual shape of something? Because what gave me the idea was Kunou mentioning the circles being arranged as rose petals. Do you think it might have some unintended effects? Maybe if we use the shape of something else?"

Well, they were back to talking business, so that was good.

Hecate even seemed particularly motivated after the goēs' words.


[} Chapter End {]

#1,679
-Fight to Raise the Crown-

Joshua had experienced lucky moments a lot when spellcrafting.

They usually came in the shape of some kind of eureka situation. He would be having a conversation that's unrelated or someone would make an idle comment and it would spark an idea. He had kind of gotten used to it. It even happened with his own thoughts on occasion.

Other times, it'd come in the shape of a conveniently easy time during testing. He'd set up a spell prototype and it'd work right away, or even just surprisingly well very quickly. Those always caught him off guard, no matter how many times they happened. Joshua had gotten used to things taking time. Everything was a process that he had to go through a bunch of times. Even when it helped him, it also always made him pause, because it messed with the process unexpectedly… But he never complained, obviously.

Joshua had stumbled upon a different kind of lucky moment when spellcrafting the Teleportation Arrays. Well, some of the previous ones were also involved, but there was one in particular that had just… been new for him. And that was that a mistake actually worked for the better.

He'd been working on one of the targeting circles in particular, the one that would pick up what – or who, more specifically – would need to be teleported. Joshua wasn't sure what he'd messed up, if the part that read distances, or the part that read position, but somehow the approach he'd used worked wonders for the thing. The thing could somehow pick someone up from double the distance Joshua had expected and five times what he'd been working towards. That was a lot.

He had expected to get himself – and get everyone else that would need to use the things, for that matter – trapped at home and under the range of the target spell, to be able to use the things effectively. After all, what was the point of working out fast teleport if he would need to take his sweet time getting in position to get teleported at all. So, he thought he'd need to wait out the end of things before being able to be truly free again and he'd get a taste of how Yasaka lived her life for a bit.

"You look happy," Koneko commented, in between nibbles on a pastry he'd cooked while thinking about the spells. "Did something happen?" she asked, peering at him curiously with her golden eyes. "Spellcrafting went well?"

"A spell I've been working on sort of… does, better than I thought even," he answered with a nod before taking a sip from his tea. His thoughts drifted a little back to the spell in question for a moment and then he managed to get his mind back on track. He needed a break and Koneko was right there so… He wanted to give her the attention she deserved. "How about you? Things going well?"

"Struggling," she answered and that certainly helped him focus on her more. "Nothing bad, just…" she hurried to clarify, somewhat. Then she went silent, slowly finishing the pastry while visibly gathering her thoughts. Joshua waited for her to speak again, mostly because Koneko was easily spooked and sometimes had a hard time communicating things. "... Working with Kuroka is hard."

"I thought you guys were getting along," he pointed out and the girl grimaced, somewhat bothered. Maybe he'd been wrong, apparently. Or maybe he hadn't understood her.

"... I meant, working on Senjutsu with her," she explained and he nodded. That made a little more sense. Maybe she'd hit a wall or something. That happened. Even he struggled with certain projects, no matter how much people thought he was a monster. "And her too, yes," she added, almost like an afterthought and Joshua was getting a little dizzy trying to keep up with the twists and turns of the conversation already.

"Did she do anything?" he asked. "Should I talk to her?"

"You don't have to," she answered quickly, shaking her head.

"But I want to," he sort of argued, making the girl pause. He let that sink in for a second before adding: "Do you want me to?" That seemed to give the girl even more to think about, and he waited for her to speak once more. Things seemed to be fine though, so the silence didn't feel heavy or anything. He was finding himself curious, he'd admit.

"... No," she replied in the end and he nodded. "Thanks for offering though." He gave her a smile at that, one that she returned, even if hers was barely visible. He'd take what he could get and from Koneko, that was already plenty.

"Tell me if you change your mind," he told her and she nodded. "For now… You wanna talk about anything else?" he asked and she blinked at him and he could almost see the gears shifting in her mind. It was a little humorous, he'd admit.

"... You went to Jeanne's meeting with the teachers last year, right? The one that parents are supposed to go to," the girl asked and whatever he thought she might want to talk about, that hadn't been it.

"I did, siblings can go to those too. I think Rias' brother went for her and Serafall went for Sona. I remember something like that," he pointed out, but Koneko quickly shook her head.

"Their parents went too," she told him and he nodded. He'd take her word for it. That wasn't something he remembered overly well, really. Not something that'd stick to his mind, that. "... Do you think you could go for me?" she asked and he blinked.

"Me? Not Kuroka?" he asked her, more curious than anything. Everyone and their mothers knew that he had all but adopted the lil' reincarnated nekoshou, after all. However, there always seemed to be this thin veil between what was there and confirmation. Like they all had plausible deniability if they wanted it.

"Yes, you," she said then, and Joshua felt that veil disappear a little more.

"Sure, I can do that."

The reactions to him being there as the "parent" to two students that clearly weren't related were going to be fun, if nothing else.

But if his kid wanted that, then… How could he say no?


[}-o-{]
​

His fingers tapped on the desk impatiently.

Starting from the pinky followed by the others up to his index finger and then again, Joshua knew that he was distracting himself more than anything. He couldn't quite bring himself to stop though, because it felt like it made no difference. He'd been staring at the files in front of him for hours by then and he had learned almost nothing.

He had finally gotten his hands on the defenses of their allied factions. Some of them, he'd already had, since he'd needed that to build his own defenses for them. However, the ones that had rejected his offering had fought them a lot more on that. It took some negotiating, a few favors here and there and Joshua improving their defenses, but they had shared things with him eventually. He thanked his partners for most of it, because he couldn't be bothered to do all that politicking. And besides, he would have failed anyway, most probably…

Or he would have given too much, which would have counted as failing, he supposed.

"Having trouble?" Aika asked and he nodded. "Same," she mumbled, not quite pouting but almost. "I don't know where else to look," she admitted and Joshua debated with himself telling her that he was surprised she'd gotten as much as she had. He had a feeling that she wouldn't like hearing that, even though it was a complement. He knew he wouldn't have, at least.

"Guess that makes two of us," he replied, because he was in much the same situation, sort of. He had looked over all the defense details he had and he'd found nothing. No patterns that stood out, no signs of something that might have made Khaos choose them. All the common points between defenses were from basic things. Nothing that other factions wouldn't have. If there was a "standard defense" package, those were exactly the spells that all factions had in common.

"I'm starting to think about just looking at the same things and see if I can come up with a different way to do so," Aika admitted and he hummed. If she had no ideas, that wasn't the worst decision, he supposed. For that matter…

"I guess I could do that too," he replied, running his fingers through his hair.

'How though?' he asked himself. He'd already looked through the list and tried to find identical spells and even spells that did roughly the same thing. Nothing had really stood out to him. 'What other similarities am I supposed to find then?' he wondered, because he wasn't even sure there were any to begin with. He'd looked at the effects, for the most part, but if he started dissecting every part of the spells, that'd take forever. If there even was a pattern, he would never find it in time.

There were probably at least a handful of different elements he could consider worth looking out per spell. Joshua simply didn't have the time to look through all the lists like that in detail. Even if he tried to shorten the process by simply taking two lists and going through them as a partial filter of sorts… That wouldn't work.

Going through all the spells just to see if one or two things…

'One or two things,' he repeated in his mind, his eyes narrowing. 'If I can look for one or two things before dissecting all the spells, that'd lower the time needed a lot,' he thought, but that was kind of obvious. The difficult part was finding that element or two to look for before going through the spells. That was going to be more difficult.

'Or will it?' he wondered, because there was one thing that came to mind. 'Khaos is obsessed with dragons, right? And so is this verse as a whole…' It'd be a gamble to just go with that, but then again, Joshua didn't have that many ideas on what to do other than that.

"Iryuka," he commented, turning to the side and seeing the girl straighten stiffly immediately. It was a little humorous how she always acted like he'd caught her with her hands in the cookie jar. Suspicious too, but he'd done his best to check if she was actually up to something and she'd come out clean. Even his partners, much better at reading people than he was, had waved off any worries.

The girl was just very tense when working for him, apparently.

"Can you make a note to use my time analyzing the defenses into two things, analyzing and brainstorming analysis criteria," he commented and the girl nodded quickly, muttering an acknowledgement while writing down the note for herself. Nodding to himself, Joshua turned back towards the list.

He already had an idea, even if it was suboptimal, so-

"When should we start the divide, Mr. Davis?" Iryuka asked, looking very much like she hadn't wanted to do so when he turned to look at her. It took him a moment to realize that she'd kind of interrupted him and she realized. "Should I have waited to ask?" she added nervously.

"... It's no problem," he reassured first of all, because the girl was already on edge enough as it was. "But next time let's start from the next related slot unless I tell you something else, alright?" he suggested and she nodded quickly, scribbling another note down and he ran his fingers through his hair.

'Alright, now let's see how I can do this,' he thought, finding the first spell and getting to work. He had a lot of things to go through, even if he'd reduced the time needed a lot just deciding to focus on dragon-related elements.

'No rest for the wicked, indeed.'


[}-o-{]
​

The peak of Mount Everest on a cloudy day was beautiful, Joshua learned.

Granted, it required some prep, mainly to make sure the winds, the temperature and a few other things didn't make things troublesome, but still. Fortunately, all that made it less troublesome in a different way, and that was the fact that nobody was climbing the thing in that weather, obviously. So, Joshua knew they'd be by themselves unless someone supernatural interrupted.

And that was what he had a bunch of other spells for and if anyone had a problem with it, then he would deal with that too.

Back to the point though, the view from that spot in that weather was breathtaking, and not because of the lack of oxygen. He'd taken care of that, after all. No, the view was just outstanding because it was like standing on a wispy sea. In a way, Joshua was reminded of Heaven, but less… extra. Heaven was supernaturally – obviously – beautiful, it shone even without light and everything was always perfect and nice.

The view from the Everest was more natural though, imperfect. There were darker spots here and there, maybe hints of a storm that he might have to stop. The imperfections made it a different kind of beautiful. Not better than Heaven, not at all, but maybe still just as good. He wasn't sure it was safe to admit, but he kind of liked the sight before him more. The perfection of Heaven could be overwhelming.

It made him feel out of place, like an Uncanny Valley situation, but centered around himself, because he was the one throwing things off.

"It's beautiful, right?" Gabriel asked, leaning sideways onto his shoulder. "It's not home, but it's a close second," she commented, although she sounded like she was still taking in the sights. "Would you believe me if I said I haven't seen this before?"

"No." How could he? They never brought it up – because it was awkward and also… Well, even he knew that'd be a terrible thing to do –, but she was laughably old. It didn't show in a lot of things, but it definitely showed in the things she'd seen.

"I haven't," she admitted and his eyebrows shut up. "Most of the time, when we're not home, we stay closer to the ground, ironically," she explained, likely sensing his surprise and skepticism. "The few times we'd be above the clouds, we didn't usually have time to take in the view," she added and he nodded slowly.

It was still hard to believe, but he had no reason to not trust her word for it, really.

"Well, I know it's not really your thing, but I was looking for places to go and found this one," he admitted, feeling a little self-conscious even despite her initial comment. Natural spots were more his thing, after all. Not to say that she didn't like them, but it usually took a lot more than it did for him to make her enjoy herself with natural things.

Then again, the peak of Mount Everest was no small thing, he supposed.

"You know I have exceptions," she replied and he could almost hear the smile on her face. It made him smile in turn. "I think I'd like to come back here some other time," she added and Joshua was glad to hear that.

"Well, I guess we'll be coming back," he decided, because sure, there wasn't much to look at, but what was there was just… incredible, even in its simplicity. Joshua was struggling to put it into words, why he liked it so much. But he did, so he wouldn't mind seeing more of it. Just maybe not too soon, since he tended to get tired of things if he took in too much of them.

"I'm choosing the next spot though," Gabriel commented and he chuckled. That was more what he'd expected to hear, if less playful. He'd take it with no problems whatsoever.

"Sure thing," he readily agreed. If anything, he preferred for his partners to pick their date spots. He didn't always know where it would be good to go and he always felt nervous that they wouldn't like it. Admittedly, he was growing a little more confident in that – and Cheshire usually helped him when he was particularly unsure, since she had never steered him wrong –, but all in all, he would rather not have to deal with any of that.

"Josh?" Gabriel started then and he turned towards her. Not because of the questioning tone, but because she sounded unsure and he'd felt her tense a little bit beside him. Apparently, there was something bothering her all of a sudden. He'd thought things were good. "You said you'd work on a spell for us once Khaos is done, right?" she asked and he blinked.

"I did," he answered calmly, not sure why that was something that made her behave like that. They had talked about that a bunch of times – awkward and kind of worrying as it could be, what with her being an angel – and she'd never sounded like that. "Changed your mind?"

"No," she denied firmly, grabbing her hand in hers. "I just… You have a lot of children, you know?" she asked and it almost seemed like she was holding back a pout to him. That was kind of funny. Although, the fact that he could finally guess where she was going kind of took away from that a little.

"Do you want children?" he asked her and Gabriel seemed taken aback, maybe by the fact that she hadn't had to spell it out to him. That was entirely fair, really.

"... I think so," she mumbled, pressing more into him, like she was trying to hide by his side.

"Alright," he replied calmly and that seemed to surprise her once more. "I have no problem with that," he told her with a grin. "I love having a big family. I don't love how busy I am and the fact that I can't see them or spend time with them as much as I'd like to, but…" he explained and Gabriel giggled, pulling him down a little to kiss him before he could continue. "You always tell me I worry too much, I know, but still, I think we could…" he was interrupted by another kiss, that time very deliberately.

He wasn't complaining.


[}-o-{]
​

"Do I really have to do this?" Jeanne asked, pouting even as she continued pushing around plants and pulling out weeds.

"You don't have to," Asia answered, all patience and kindness. "I'm sure you have other things you'd rather do," she added, smiling like the pseudo-angel that she was. Far as Joshua was concerned, she was more of an angel than some actual angels, to be honest. And he didn't say that just because Uriel still hated his guts… although it was definitely part of it. "I appreciate the help you've already given me."

"Not helping, Asia…" Jeanne mumbled, confusing the lil' nun.

"Asia stuck to the kendo practice you suggested the other day, Jeanne," Joshua pointed out and the girl flinched. "So, you're gonna stick to this and you're gonna stop complaining," he added and the girl did as she was told. She sulked all throughout, but he didn't care for that.

He had finished setting up the first design of the teleportation arrays that sort of worked two days before and he'd decided to spend time with his family while he worked on improving them. For the moment, the range of the spells was limited, at least in regards to where they could be, but he was working on increasing that. One day, with the infinite wardstones as foundation, he was sure he could make them limitless.

That'd take way too long though, but he could hope.

"I don't wanna force you to do this if you don't want to," Asia said, worrying her lip as she glanced at Jeanne. Joshua had to hold back a sigh at that. Instead, he took a deep breath in, pulled away from the plants he was caring for and then approached the nun.

"Asia," he started, snapping his fingers to wash the dirt off his hands before placing them on her shoulders. "It's fine to want to share things that you like with others. And people that love you should be able to share that with you even if they don't like it. You don't like kendo, but you still did it for Jeanne. And you don't like magic, but you hear me anytime I ramble about those."

"It's not bothersome for me though," the girl mumbled, wringing her hands and looking away. She had a slight smile on her face though. Unfortunately, it was lost the next second. "I don't want you two to do this if it's bothersome for you."

"It's not bothersome for you because you appreciate the two of us more than you dislike those things," he explained, and he wasn't even guessing. He knew that, she'd told him as much already. "Jeanne should learn to appreciate you more than she dislikes getting her hands dirty on some grass and dirt."

"Now you're just making me feel like a bitch," Jeanne grumbled behind him and he nodded.

"Exactly," he said, making the girl sputter. "Maybe I've spoiled you too much," he added, sighing and shaking his head. "I remember when you were all well behaved and eager to help. I miss those days." He really didn't. Those days had been like that because Jeanne had been afraid he'd abandon her to her fate, literally.

Admittedly, he might have gone overboard trying to help her relax.

He was dealing with the consequences of that.

"Shut up," Jeanne mumbled, but she was working, so Joshua guessed she wasn't too upset. "I'm… I guess I've gotten used to things being good," she added then, and both Joshua and Asia looked at her. There was something serious in her tone even as she kept pulling out weeds, firm, steely even. "I forget how bad things were… before, or a part of me does. I should be more grateful."

"It's not a bad thing, Jeanne," he told her and he saw her stop. "I'm actually glad about that. It means you've healed," he added and Jeanne turned towards him, equal parts surprised and hopeful. "Why do you look like that?" he asked, a little amused. "Sure, you might be a brat, but it's fine. It's my job to get you to be better, but it's certainly an improvement from before."

"I don't know if that's sweet or insulting," Jeanne replied.

"I guess it's supposed to be a bit of both," he told her with a half smile, making her scoff. At least she seemed to have relaxed a little. Seriously, why did he have to be the mature one all the time? Being an adult was exhausting. "Either way you're my sister, Jeanne," he added and the girl paused again. "You're stuck with me," he told her with a smile before looking at Asia. "And we're stuck with you."

"Why do I still feel like you're half insulting me?" Jeanne cried out.

"That's kind of what I have to do as the big brother, pretty sure," he answered, getting a roll of eyes from Jeanne and a giggle from Asia. Things were much more calm after that. They focused back on what they were doing after that, which was working on the garden. Fortunately, not all of it was taking out weeds, although the other parts were more complex.

That is, until he felt the alarm he'd set up, both through his own spells and Friday. It blared like a siren in his mind, except it made his entire magic twitch and then shiver. He wasted precisely a second to snap his mind to action though. He'd been preparing for that moment for months after all…

'Everyone get ready,' he ordered through his bond with his familiars. 'Friday,' was all he had to think before the living spell started sending messages that he'd had ready for way too long. That was all he needed to do before getting to work on the location, following the lines drawn by the Spartos and Valerie…

Because their enemies had done something once more, drawing a reaction from the dhampir.

'Let's do this then, Khaos Brigade.'


[} Chapter End {]
