#1,688
-Fight to Take Them Down-

'Like a charm,' he thought, appearing immediately in his destination, somewhere in West Africa.

Joshua wasn't sure who's territory that was or what factions were around… And he also didn't care, admittedly. He could deal with any ruffled feathers afterwards. He had already talked to his partners, who had then communicated it to their allies, that as soon as they could get Khaos Brigade, they would, consequences be damned.

Joshua wasn't about to let them get away from him just because some god would feel slighted.

He'd give them something to actually be upset about if they got in his way.

'Hello,' he said, after appearing in the area and turning around. Beside him, his familiars gave a much more overt greeting. Nagini reared up and glared with the full force of her disastrous gaze. Cheshire dashed, lightning at her paws while she grew to her biggest form. Margalo flew up, her cry rippling through the area in a way that he could almost see. Morag scurried away, hidden by the impressive displays of her sisters and likely already working on a web.

And Friday… Friday worked with him.

With a snap of his fingers, foci appeared behind him, infinity wardstones, yes, but also a few others. He was still studying Ophis' gifts, which meant that some traditional foci worked better in some cases, but that was beside the point. As their resources appeared, both Joshua and Friday started casting. Lockdown, defense, draining, all the foundation spells were laid down in a second, almost as fast as they'd appeared there.

All of that, happening in the span of a second, because that's what he'd practiced for, what he'd been preparing for.

The following second brought even more.

Behind him, he heard the crackling of Incinerate Anthem as Raynare took to the sky. He saw the purple mist of Dimension Lost spreading from the corner of his eyes. He sensed the life energy that Kuroka was starting to channel already. He would have brought Kokabiel too, but… He didn't trust that one nearly as much as he did the others, and even Georg had been a stretch.

In front of him, much the same way, he saw several things happen.

There were dragons and serpents and… creatures all around. He knew what most of those were supposed to be, or he could at least guess. Joshua had memorized what Khaos had been so busy bringing back to life or kidnapping and twisting. They were as similar as the Spartos was to its original form, yes, but still. All of them turned towards them. There were growls and roars and hisses. One of them even breathed something that seemed like a cross between flame and toxic green gas.

A presence of magic rose and shapes seemed to take form from the ground. Lucifuge and Annihilation Maker, he'd bet. He welcomed those, especially the latter one. They had been a thorn on Joshua's side for so long that he wanted to get his hands on them almost as much as he wanted Khaos Brigade gone.

And then there was the last one.

"How?!" he shouted and Joshua listened to the shock mixed with anger and a tinge of what he hoped was fear. He watched the silver-haired devil's expression twist with much the same emotions. He took in that like a man enjoys his last meal; Joshua savoured that like it was a gift… Because it was.

Rizevim Lucifer was right there.

He was in front of Joshua.

'I caught you, you piece of shit,' he growled in his mind as he slammed another spell down in the third second after their arrival. The allies Joshua had brought were already moving forward then. Annihilation Maker's creations and the corrupted dragons did much the same, if in the opposite direction.

He cast more spells, layering more and more with every passing second. Domain Authority, that was what people called him and that was what his system called him. It was awkward, to hear others use it, and he had never given his titles all that much attention beyond their effects after he got them. However, at that moment, he found a corner of his mind wishing to honor those two words.

He was an oblivious man, but Joshua wasn't blind. He'd seen how people looked at him. He'd seen how many of them did. He'd seen how his Stars felt very indebted to him. He'd seen House of Water would do whatever he asked of them. He'd seen youkai waiting for him to start acting like a co-leader to Yasaka. He'd seen how Rias was still looking at him a certain way still.

He didn't understand most of that, yes, and he didn't get why they felt like that, or why they didn't realize that he was just a massive magic nerd.

But he had seen all that.

And at that moment, Joshua pushed aside all the awkwardness he'd usually feel, the doubts and justifications. Instead, he found himself wanting to be that person that people respected, feared even, to be that grand mage that the world saw him as. He wanted Khaos to find themselves facing that. He wanted them to look at him and know that they were done. He wanted to be for them what Trihexa had been for him for so long, the shadow of death looming over, hanging above their heads like a Sword of Damocles.

Raynare's flames hit a twisted creature that had once been a dragon at the same time that Cheshire's fangs wrapped around the neck of what had once been a Spartos. The conflict started like that, with roars and fire and lightning. And Joshua ignored all that, throwing more spells and hoping that their magical presence made Khaos realize that they were trapped, that there was no hope for them and that he was going to kill them all.

He hoped against hope that they would feel a sliver of the fear that had gripped at his heart all that time.

And if they weren't feeling that, then… he was going to make sure of it in time.

[Divide!]

'Even better,' he thought, grinning widely as a new presence appeared under his wards. Because he'd been thinking about it for so long… What if he didn't catch all of Khaos? What if he got there but there was only Rizevim and not the others? What'd he do then?

And he'd just reached a rather easy solution.

Let the others come in.

The only thing he needed was for them to not leave. For all he cared, anyone was allowed to join the battle. His allies would come, any second. And Khaos… Khaos would die in its entirety if they came and he wanted that. Anyone else would either be allies or enemies, no in between. Joshua didn't have it in him to care about anything else anymore.

Khaos needed to disappear and anyone that wasn't helping was getting in his way.

'Welcome, Vali,' he thought to himself, so very pleased to recognize those presences. Bikou, Arthur, Le Fay and some other strange creature, not a corrupted one. He didn't care. His spells shifted to target them all the same, he adjusted everything to do so with a thought. He'd been working on combat spells for so long too…

And when Leonardo tried to craft a creature or three that would help with that, Friday made her appearance. Because the living spell was all too eager to prove herself and she did so by performing the task for which he'd created her, back when he didn't even know what he was actually doing, what he'd achieve. She did so by facing Annihilation Maker and holding it back.

Every effect that the Longinus crafted, she countered, their clash was the biggest as far as Joshua was aware. Ironic, since it was also the least noticeable, the least flashy. Georg had teleported Vali's team around, dropping Bikou in front of Raynare and the Pendragon siblings with Kuroka. Flames met senjutsu. Senjutsu met magic and swordsmanship. Nagini was fighting against a serpentine corrupted dragon. Margalo was clawing at a Spartos while her song persisted. Morag had trapped the remaining two of those while trying to web down a dragon…

And as all that happened, Leonardo and Friday had what amounted to a stare contest.

Far as Joshua was concerned, it was the most epic staring contest ever.

Just the first few seconds painted a picture that only he could see, he was pretty sure. Not because he was special, but because he was the only one that had any spare awareness to notice and the deep sense of magic required to see most of it. He felt it, the magic all over the place, the magic of the Sacred Gear creatures, the magic of the living spell. They shifted and twisted and turned in the same way that he imagined a wave of water and a wave of oil hitting each other would, mixing together yet repelling the other at the same time. It was a mess and downright dangerous feeling… yet Joshua found himself oddly fascinated by it.

For the split second that he could pay that any mind, that is.

"Georg, keep moving them, we need to buy time," he said and the Dimension Lost holder did just that. It took a lot of energy to do, but he kept teleporting creatures around, at least those that weren't already in a fight that was at least semi-stable. There were too many dragons and other monsters that Khaos had gotten their hands on, after all. Worse, those creatures were too strong.

Joshua's group was too small to handle all that.

The chaotic beings that Rizevim seemed to have put together during his raids were more difficult to move around than normal ones. Joshua could tell by the way the mist seemed to struggle to wrap around them, and the stifled nature of the teleport. He'd seen enough of the Sacred Gear being used to notice. Instead of an instantaneous shift, there was a stutter to it, like the things glitched halfway through the teleport before properly appearing where it was sent. And the Sacred Gear seemed to struggle for whole seconds before being able to move them again.

He also could tell that Georg was bleeding energy the same way an inflated balloon loses air when the neck isn't tied. Not that the rest of them were doing much better. Most of his allies were facing at least two enemies each and they were managing, but that was all. They managed and not that well, even if it was better than barely doing so. They were at least keeping themselves somewhat safe, but that was about it.

Joshua himself was still casting spells creating the fortress for the fight… But it was taking time. His spells were already in effect, sure. Some of them were weighing on their opponents, some of them draining their energy and there were many more, but… The enemies were too strong, he was slowing them down, weakening them, but not nearly fast enough to make up for the disadvantage that they were in from the start.

However-

One particularly big dragon was hit with magic and a quarter of the battlefield that Joshua was turning into his domain froze entirely with it right in the middle. He heard the distant voice of Serafall announcing her arrival cheerfully, like she would as Levia-tan in her show. He smiled despite himself and kept on casting.

The cavalry was arriving and Khaos would soon be surrounded.

But he knew it wouldn't be that easy. They'd just gotten there and it was a small miracle that Serafall had made it there so fast. Everyone else… They were busy people. And they had to organize their faction forces. Serafall must have been with one of her fellow Satans or something, and she'd still taken a risk by getting there so fast.

He didn't hold that against her though, hardly.

There were too many monsters created by the broken Grail and the dragon remains of dead creatures and – worse – living ones. Georg was still trying to keep things somewhat controlled by disturbing Khaos' fighting force. Everyone else was still fighting, pushing and- 'Fuck off,' he thought, summoning neutral magic to slap away a twisted "dragon" head before they could try to bite at Margalo. It didn't do any damage, but there was enough energy in it to knock it off course.

The perks of having infinite magic, even if his output was limited.

It might not be infinite, but his output wasn't negligible.

"No! You won't stop me!" he heard Rizevim cry out and it was music to his ears to hear his frustration, his anger. Joshua grinned even as he felt the spike of magic. "You won't!" the devil shouted, a challenge and a curse at the same time. And then Joshua felt other presences, humans and other beings that he'd felt but had been insignificant in the grand scheme of things.

Those had been more than held down by his spells and it'd only been getting worse by the second. Besides, little that they did reached his familiars or his allies. George's mist usually took care of anything, but Raynare was all but immune to their spells, burning them before they touched her. Not everyone had spells specially designed to avoid Incinerate Anthem's bullshit meta-burning, after all.

So, Joshua was unsurprised – annoyed and disgusted, but not surprised – when he felt Sephiroth Graal being used on them.

Maybe he should have done something to stop that… but he didn't think so. He was busy laying down more layers to his spells that were overall lowering the attack power of Khaos and they needed that to keep cornering them like the rabid dogs that they were so that they could be put down. Besides, as long as he was making his corrupted, chaotic minions, Rizevim wasn't taking to the battlefield and Joshua preferred things that way.

The guy was his to deal with and, besides, it wasn't like he cared if the devil turned all his little gathering of… whatever those were, maybe Stray magicians, maybe mercenaries, ultimately they didn't matter. They'd all chosen to put themselves in that position and Joshua didn't have enough in him to care about them. What he did care about was that Rizevim needed time to twist them into properly dangerous creatures, and that meant more time for him and his allies.

Specifically, it meant more time for the factions that wanted Khaos gone to make an appearance.

Serafall and Georg were doing a great job keeping the corrupted dragons from actually being too dangerous, between freezing them and teleporting them, but they couldn't make that last forever. Several of those dragons had once been forced to be reckoned with, after all, even before Rizevim Grail'd them. Not even Serafall could just shrug them off. 'Everyone's burning energy like crazy just keeping this balance,' Joshua thought with a slight grimace and pursed his lips. Nagini was struggling to wrap around enemies while glaring at anything and everything. Margalo kept her song going, but that was getting in her way a little. Cheshire and Raynare occasionally sent attacks away from their own fights. Kuroka kept weaving illusions all around while dancing between creatures.

He had spells that could turn their enemy's energy into energy for their allies, a modification to draining spells that he'd worked out, but… That'd mean stopping casting the other spells that he needed to set up. Spells that would make sure no one from Khaos escaped, and that they got weaker, more manageable. He didn't know how long it'd take their allies to get there from wherever they were. Not everyone had instant teleportation ready like he did. It'd been only him, his familiars, his gathering of enemies turned allies, Serafall and…

'Just a little longer…' Joshua told himself before his expression relaxed the smallest bit when light shone down on several creatures, like the sun had decided to be particularly mean to them. If particularly mean meant getting blasted and slammed down by holy light like they'd been hit by an invisible hammer twice their size. 'Just a little…' he repeated, more confident than wary that time.

Gabriel had made an appearance already, which was faster than Joshua imagined, if slower than he'd have liked.

Then again, his perception of time was a little skewed at that moment. He wondered how long it'd actually been since the fight started, because it felt like it'd been an hour already even if it'd probably been a few minutes, if that. Every second counted at that moment, with so many monsters on the other side. There was a small army of beings in front of them that had already been strong – some of them ridiculously so – before Rizevim gave them a chaotic boost with the Grail. His group wasn't supposed to beat them and it showed. They had to buy time. He trapped them, his group entertained them and, from there, they waited.

And through it all, Joshua focused on his own thing, because he had a job to do just like everyone else.

He wanted nothing more than to jump in, take out True Longinus or his daggers or even Ascalon and start stabbing things. He'd have been so happy to take out some of the aggression that bubbled in his chest on their opponent. However, he could leave that for later. He could wait and then enjoy himself unleashing some of the things he'd tinkered up to that point, or the things he'd tinkered for that moment.

"How did you find us?!" Rizevim screamed and if anger alone were enough to do damage, Joshua would have been worried. Instead, he was worried about the particularly high spike of energy that followed and- 'You damned crazy piece of shit,' he cursed in his mind, eyes widening when he saw that Rizevim was going to turn someone else into one of his chaotic creatures…

And that someone was Euclid Lucifuge.

The others had taken a second or two to start shifting, to start being corrupted. The devil, however, took longer but he also remained conscious. The power surged and the energy twisted, and through it all Euclid kept shooting attacks. Attacks that were getting stronger by the second.

'They are crazier than I thought,' Joshua thought to himself, splitting his attention a little to summon shields in front of said attacks before they caused damage and tilted the scales against them. 'And that's fucking saying something.'

And then, the precarious balance got even worse.

Or maybe he just realized that it'd been getting worse, for a while by then. Because when Joshua blocked another attack by Euclid, he noticed something out of the corner of his eyes. The biggest creature got frozen and broke through the ice faster than before. Two creatures managed to get an attack out before Georg teleported them with his mist. A flying serpent dove straight at Nagini despite her glare barely twitching. A drake of some sort pushed through Gabriel's light to spit some kind of attack at her.

'Are they growing resistant?' he thought, dread drilling a hole at the pit of his stomach. He knew they shifted, but so far all he'd seen in the Spartos was that it was random. 'Didn't have a reason to change any particular way?' he wondered, summoning a shield and a blast at two different spots and grimacing. If he was going to be more involved in the fights, then he would slow down his own casting and that-

A gigantic sword was thrust forward and through a creature.

'Jeanne?' Joshua thought, blinking at the La Pucelle armor and the sword it held, looming over Jeanne and her chosen enemy. 'How did she get here so fast?' he wondered.

[Boost! Boost! Boost!]

[Divide! Divide! Divide!]

He paused again, watching a shiny red spot hitting a shiny white spot off to the side. 'Issei?' he wondered, but the fights were still going. Things were still bad and that was without Euclid somehow still going through the process of turning into a monster. One that was going to be remarkably troublesome, just like the dragons that had been turned into weapons

He slapped another area spell down.

'Come on,' Joshua told himself, taking a deep breath in. 'We can last long enough, I know we can,' he told himself. They were holding well enough. And soon enough, the cavalry would arrive and-

And-

'Are they getting stronger too? No way, right?' Except, that seemed to be exactly what was going on. It showed in the way that a creature broke out of Nagini's hold. It showed in the way another clawed Cheshire away. It showed in the way a Spartos tore itself out of Morag's web. 'What the fuck did Rizevim do with them?' he wondered to himself. 'This is getting kind of frustrating…'

Maybe it was hypocritical of him, but Joshua was getting tired of feeling like things were fine and then immediately having them crumble. They were running out of energy quickly, their enemies had the number advantage and the power advantage, since they were holding back Serafall and Gabriel with sheer numbers and their chaotic nature, and they were also just less flexible than creatures that were apparently adapting to them.

'This is some bullshit,' he thought, casting more spells as quickly as he could. He was nowhere near done with his set up, but he needed to be quick about it or he'd run out of time. When that happened – when, not if – he'd have to get involved and that would definitely lower their chances of lasting longer. Because sure, he could do a lot, but if he didn't finish creating his own battlezone, then the effect of his spells wouldn't be as good and they might get overwhelmed eventually, especially considering what he was learning about the Grail creations.

He didn't know if he could outgrow them, but he was stalling them some. And if they were pushing against their forces as it was, then he could only imagine how much more dangerous they could get if they were allowed to grow unrestrained. With any luck, his spells would pick up speed and catch up, maybe even push back, but Joshua wasn't holding his breath for that.

Because he was just cursed to run into problems infinitely, it seemed.

'No matter,' he thought, pushing through and covering some attacks at the same time that he placed more spells. A few more and he'd manage the main cluster. Not the end, not even close, but he could do it. 'Just a little more. The other pantheons are on their way,' he told himself, taking in the battlefield as best he could and continuing to cast.

Serafall and Gabriel were taking on more, trying to smack down the aberrations and prevent Euclid from doing much of anything… Especially considering his Grail transformation had finished. Joshua couldn't see what had actually been done to him, there were no outward changes that he could see, but there was very much something wrong there. Especially with the way his power had spiked and was by then all over the place.

His observation was cut short though, as a random twisted dragon roared and threw itself at him rather than flew. The creature surged through the battlefield, making an arch over Cheshire even when the feline shot it with her lightning. Then it charged through Serafall's Ice Magic, barely losing some of its skin and scales and fur. When Gabriel pushed it to the ground with her light, however… it was still not done.

A claw was raised and Joshua was about to dismiss it as a concern. That is, up until the limb grew and then grew and then grew more. In a second or maybe two, the twisted thing had grown bigger than the biggest creature on that field and then it started going down towards Joshua. 'Man, fuck my luck, I guess…' he thought a half resigned and half annoyed expression taking over his face.

With a deep breath in, he prepared himself to summon a succession of shield spells, one after the other, to try and take from the power of the attack. He'd have teleported, but the field was a mess and he needed to keep casting so-

A presence appeared behind him and, less than a second later, a huge creature lunged from behind him and caught the corrupted limb in its maw.

Then he blinked, because that was a gigantic, golden fox and he could see several tails swishing around from the corner of his eyes…

'Yasaka?'


[} Chapter End {]
